themes.name: Engine behaviour and contract fixes outside render
themes.desc:
Real behaviour defects and unenforced contracts in non-render engine code:
- ThreadPool ignores the result of SetThreadpoolThreadMinimum.
- add_child dereferences null.
- refresh_style is const yet writes.
- ByteReader accepts temporaries.
- read_file_bytes misreports open failures and omits documented exceptions.
- Broad-phase cell arithmetic is undefined for nonfinite boxes.
- JSON numbers narrow to float silently.
- Sound-bank keys are ignored silently.
- XAudio2 handles streaming banks and out-of-range play_wave differently from null and Web Audio.
- XInput does not report suspended slots as disconnected.
- Window guards are uneven, and window_ is dereferenced without a check.
- Viewport out-of-range returns fullscreen.
- Colour 0/0 gives NaN.
- Partitioner, sprite_world_bounds and getBoundingClientRect do avoidable per-frame work.
themes.story: Several small behaviour commits, each with a behavioural test and a CHANGES.md entry where the change is consumer-visible. Keep them separate from any mechanical moves. Start with cross-backend agreement (audio play_wave and streaming banks, gamepad suspend), then input validation (ThreadPool, broad phase, JSON, Colour, sound-bank keys), then the guard and const-correctness fixes, and finally the measured per-frame allocation and trig work.

findings.title: Sound-bank definitions silently ignore unknown keys, unlike the manifest and sprite-sheet loaders
findings.evidence: read_sound_bank_definition reads root.array("waves"), root.boolean("create_effect_instance_for_each_wave"), root.array("sound_effect_instances") and effect.identifier("name"/"wave") with no reject_unknown_keys call. By contrast, asset_manifest_loader.cpp:16 and sprite_sheet_loader.cpp:137 call "asset_details::reject_unknown_keys(root, { ... })".
findings.why: All three are hand-edited, fixed-schema content files. A typo'd extra field in an effect instance, such as a misspelled volume or looping key a person expects to work, is accepted silently. That is the quiet disagreement T6 forbids, and the sibling loaders and their headers argue against it explicitly.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply reject_unknown_keys to the definition root and to each effect instance, document it in sound_bank_loader.h's throw contract, update json_object_keys.h's and published.ts's 'manifest and sprite-sheet loaders' wording, and add tests to match the other two loaders.
findings.verify_reason: sound_bank_loader.cpp reads waves, create_effect_instance_for_each_wave, sound_effect_instances and name/wave, and never calls reject_unknown_keys. json_object_keys.h:11 says the check is private to the manifest and sprite-sheet loaders. BACKLOG PI-20 (done) was scoped to 'a manifest or sprite sheet', and STORIES records no decision to exempt sound banks. content.md frames rejecting unknown keys in 'the engine's loaders' as a T6 defect. Not tracked in TODO or code-hygiene.md.

findings.title: Null play_voice ignores DirectXTK's Play transitions it claims to transcribe
findings.why: Suppose a voice is paused (or playing) without a loop and play_effect(effect, true) is called. The null backend then reports is_effect_looping()==true, while XAudio2 and Web Audio report false. The null backend exists so headless tests can assert what a real backend would do, so this divergence can pass a test that a real device would fail.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the web/DirectXTK branches. Paused goes to playing with looping unchanged. Playing is left unchanged. Only stopped goes to playing with looping = loop. Keep recording the call, and add a null test for play_voice on a paused looping/non-looping voice.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: null play_voice (null/audio_device.cpp:167-173) sets state=playing and looping=loop unconditionally. Web Audio (webaudio/audio_device.cpp:719-732) and the XAudio2 path through DirectXTK's SoundEffectInstance::Play (xaudio2/audio_device.cpp:195) change the loop flag only from stopped. The null model's 'transcribed from DirectXTK' claim at line 35 is therefore false for this transition. It is a divergence in the test model with no shipped-behaviour impact, so medium, not high.

findings.title: One-shots during suspension are dropped on Web Audio but queued by XAudio2; the seam says nothing
findings.why: Application keeps ticking updates while minimised. Native one-shots fired then are started on a stopped XAudio2 engine and plausibly all play together at resume, which is the 'plays late plays wrong' outcome the seam rejects elsewhere. The browser drops them instead. Callers get different audible behaviour per backend, and nothing documents it.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide the rule in audio_device.h (most likely: a one-shot asked for while suspended is dropped) and implement it in XAudio2 with a suspended flag, which DeviceRecovery already tracks. Then document it beside the gesture paragraph and in SoundBank::play_wave.
findings.verify_reason: Web play_wave returns early when device.suspended (webaudio/audio_device.cpp:297-299). XAudio2 play_wave (xaudio2/audio_device.cpp:181-186) calls WaveBank::Play with no suspension check while AudioEngine::Suspend has stopped the engine, so the voice would start at resume. Null records the call. The seam documents dropping only before the first gesture and during recovery. The behaviour per backend is undocumented and differs.

findings.title: XAudio2 accepts a streaming wave bank at load and later fails with an anonymous error
findings.why: audio_device.h promises that a container this backend can read but not play fails at open_wave_bank with a runtime_error naming the file or wave (T6). A streaming bank (xwb_file.h says the engine's reader accepts 'in-memory or streaming') opens without error on XAudio2. It then throws std::runtime_error("WaveBank::CreateInstance") from create_voice, or "WaveBank::Play" from the const play_wave path, during gameplay. Neither message names the bank or the wave. The Web Audio backend plays the same file, so the backends also disagree on the same content.
findings.suggested_fix: After constructing the WaveBank, check bank->IsStreamingBank() and throw std::runtime_error("Failed to open wave bank: " + path + " is a streaming bank; re-pack it in-memory"), or whatever the decided policy is. Add an XAudio2-only test with a streaming fixture.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed in xaudio2/audio_device.cpp:120-164. open_wave_bank constructs the WaveBank, checks names with Find and stores it, with no IsStreamingBank check. The vcpkg build tree's DirectXTK WaveBank.cpp sets mStreaming at Initialize, throws runtime_error("WaveBank::Play") in Play and runtime_error("WaveBank::CreateInstance") in CreateInstance for a streaming bank. audio_device.h:102 promises that a container the backend can read but not play throws at open, naming the wave, and xwb_file.h:76 says the engine reader accepts streaming banks. The contract break is real, but it only happens with content explicitly packed as streaming (the shipped samples use in-memory banks), so medium rather than high.

findings.title: play_wave out of range is silently dropped on XAudio2 but throws on null and Web Audio; the null comment says otherwise
findings.why: SoundBank::play_wave validates only handle.valid(), not that the index belongs to this bank. A WaveHandle resolved from a larger bank and passed to a smaller one throws std::out_of_range under null audio (CI) and Web Audio, but plays nothing with no error on the shipping Windows backend. This is exactly the 'silence with no error' that sound_bank.h says the engine exists to prevent. The null backend's comment justifying its throw describes the real backend wrongly.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the XAudio2 play_wave (and create_voice, before the unsigned cast) the same bounds check and std::out_of_range message the other two backends use, for example by checking against WaveBank's entry count. Correct the null comment to say the check is the seam's, not the API's.
findings.verify_reason: xaudio2 play_wave (audio_device.cpp:181-186) forwards straight to WaveBank::Play, which DebugTraces and returns when the index is out of range (WaveBank.cpp). null (audio_device.cpp:143-155) and webaudio (693-702) throw std::out_of_range. SoundBank::play_wave (sound_bank.cpp:132-147) checks only wave.valid(). The null comment 'The bounds check a real backend's Play would have done' is false for DirectXTK.

findings.title: Grid cell arithmetic is undefined for nonfinite or very large boxes
findings.why: Converting a NaN or out-of-range float to int32_t is undefined behaviour. The subtraction max_x - min_x + 1 is also done in int32 and can overflow before the widening cast. narrow_phase.h makes nonfinite coordinates report no contact, and the all-pairs sweep (the specification) handles them that way. The grid, which is supposed to reproduce exactly the same pairs, has no defined behaviour for such a box. Nothing in tests/collision/broad_phase_tests.cpp covers NaN, infinity or huge coordinates.
findings.suggested_fix: In collect_candidates, skip boxes with nonfinite fields (they can produce no contact anyway). Do the cell division in double and clamp it to the int32 range, or route out-of-range boxes to large_. Widen to int64 before subtracting. Add a randomised agreement case that includes NaN and huge coordinates.
findings.verify_reason: broad_phase.cpp:47-50 cell_of does static_cast<int32_t>(std::floor(value / cell_size)) with no finite or range guard. index_cells computes max_x - min_x + 1 in int32 before widening it. choose_cell_size's std::max(min_cell_size, NaN) returns min_cell_size, so a NaN box reaches the cast. narrow_phase.h:71-84 explicitly defines nonfinite as no contact. Grepping broad_phase_tests.cpp for nan, infinity or numeric_limits finds nothing, and nothing in TODO.md or code-hygiene.md tracks this.

findings.title: read_file_bytes reports any failure to open as 'No file at', which contradicts its documented split between a missing file and an unreadable one
findings.why: An existing file that cannot be opened (access denied, locked, or a directory) throws out_of_range with "No file at". That is exactly the 'content bug' classification the header says is reserved for a missing name. The callers are dds_file, png_file, sprite_font_file and xwb_file, so a disk or permission problem gets misreported as a missing asset.
findings.suggested_fix: After the open fails, test std::filesystem::exists(path_from_utf8(path)) with an error_code: throw out_of_range only when the file does not exist, and runtime_error ("Could not open ...") otherwise. Add a test that opens a directory or a locked file.
findings.verify_reason: byte_reader.cpp:75-79 throws std::out_of_range('No file at ...') for any failed open. byte_reader.h:56-59 promises out_of_range only when there is no file, and runtime_error when a file exists but cannot be read. A permission-denied file or a directory path breaks that documented contract. Confirmed as stated.

findings.title: ThreadPool ignores SetThreadpoolThreadMinimum's failure and never validates its min/max arguments
findings.evidence:
SetThreadpoolThreadMaximum(pool,
			static_cast<DWORD>(maximum)); // Set maximum number of threads

		SetThreadpoolThreadMinimum(pool,
			static_cast<DWORD>(minimum)); // Set minimum number of threads

The ThreadPool(int, int) constructor in thread_pool.h:36 has no range check. Only ApplicationOptions::validate (application.cpp:45-48) requires min_threads >= 1 and max_threads >= min_threads. ThreadPool is published as game code (website/src/lib/published.ts:119), and bench/fanout_bench_null.cpp:287 and the tests construct it directly.
findings.why: SetThreadpoolThreadMinimum returns a BOOL that is FALSE when it fails, for example when it cannot create the minimum number of threads. That failure is silently lost. A direct caller passing ThreadPool(0, 0), ThreadPool(-1, 2) or ThreadPool(4, 2) gets negative values cast to huge DWORDs, or an inconsistent floor and ceiling, with no diagnostic. The wasm Impl stores the values unchecked, and the problem only shows up later, as Partitioner::partition's throw when max_num_threads() is below 1. The engine's other public constructors (FocusGroup, Partitioner, StateContext) throw std::invalid_argument at the boundary, so this one breaks the pattern.
findings.suggested_fix: In ThreadPool::ThreadPool, before either Impl is built, throw std::invalid_argument unless 1 <= min_num_threads <= max_num_threads. That covers the Win32 and serial builds alike. In the Win32 Impl, check SetThreadpoolThreadMinimum's BOOL, and on failure close the pool and throw, as the CreateThreadpoolCleanupGroup failure path already does. Drop the restating end-of-line comments.
findings.verify_reason: thread_pool.cpp:65-76 shows SetThreadpoolThreadMaximum/Minimum called with unchecked static_cast<DWORD> and the Minimum BOOL ignored; ThreadPool::ThreadPool (line 221-224) forwards straight to Impl with no range check. Direct constructions exist in tests/bench; validation only lives in ApplicationOptions. Neither code-hygiene docs nor TODO track it.

findings.title: The seam promises suspended slots read disconnected, but XInput does nothing on suspend
findings.why: The published contract states a guarantee and then disclaims it. The web backend keeps it with a `suspended` flag that blanks states in sample(). The XInput backend has no flag, and on Windows 10+ DirectXTK's Suspend is a no-op, so read() keeps reporting connected pads with live buttons while suspended. Even XInputEnable(FALSE) yields neutral-but-connected data, not disconnected. Callers cannot rely on the stated sentence, and the two backends diverge on observable behaviour.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the web backend: add `bool suspended` to the XInput Impl, set it in suspend()/resume(), and have sample() write default GamepadStates while suspended. Then cut the disclaiming paragraph so the header states one true contract. Alternatively, file it as a behavioural decision per code-hygiene.md's rule for false contracts.
findings.verify_reason: gamepad_reader.h:51-63 states that a suspended reader answers disconnected, then disclaims it. xinput/gamepad_reader.cpp:90-96 forwards only to vibration.suspend() and gamepad.Suspend(), and its own comment admits DirectXTK's XInput Suspend sends nothing on Windows 10+. No XInput suspended flag exists. Not tracked: SM-45 is closed, and TODO.md and the ledgers do not mention it.

findings.title: FocusGroup::refresh_style is const but writes every registered widget's colour
findings.why: In this engine, const signals a read that is safe to make from draw() on several render workers at once (game_object.h, state.h). This function mutates the borrowed widgets that those draws read. A page's const draw() could call it and race with other views without the compiler objecting. It compiles only because const does not propagate through the stored raw pointers. Its only callers are FocusGroup's own non-const mutators (focus.cpp:36,75,133,155), and git grep finds no caller outside focus.cpp, so the const qualifier enables nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the const qualifier: refresh_style() is a mutation of what the group paints. No caller changes, because every existing call site is already non-const.
findings.verify_reason: focus.h:159 declares refresh_style() const; focus.cpp:158-180 calls visual()->set_colour on every widget. git grep finds callers only at focus.cpp:36,75,133,155 (all non-const), and nothing in ColourWars/game calls it, so dropping const breaks no caller. The const-means-draw-safe contract makes the lie meaningful.

findings.title: ~Application calls CoUninitialize before the audio device, renderer and window members are destroyed
findings.why: The XAudio2 engine (opened under the COM apartment this class initialised) and the other Windows services are released after COM is uninitialised on this thread. That order is unsupported. The browser on_closed path (lines 566-578) already resets each service explicitly in reverse order, so Windows teardown is less strict than the browser's. Impact is plausible rather than observed.
findings.suggested_fix: Before CoUninitialize on Windows, reset the service members in the same reverse order the on_closed path uses (sharing one helper), or move COM initialisation into an RAII member declared before the services so it is torn down after them.
findings.verify_reason: application.cpp:97-102: after clear() and suspend(), CoUninitialize runs in the destructor body. The unique_ptr members (audio_device_ at application.h:372, renderer_, render_resources_, window_) are destroyed after it. The comment covers only the states. No failure has been observed, so low as stated.

findings.title: window(), quit(), set_resolution and set_fullscreen dereference window_ unguarded, while set_cursor_* guard it
findings.why: Before initialize(), window_ is null. The header says every service accessor answers null until then, but window() (and quit()) crash instead. Sibling setters on the same class handle the pre-initialize case deliberately ("a call before the window exists is the option it would have been"), so the class is inconsistent about calls made before initialize.
findings.suggested_fix: Return nullptr from window() when window_ is null, and make quit() a no-op then. Alternatively, state in application.h that these members require initialize().
findings.verify_reason: window() (application.cpp ~813) and quit() (249-252) dereference window_ without a check. set_cursor_visible (321-328) guards it. application.h:315 says every service accessor is null until initialize(), and window() is declared in that block at line 363. The class is inconsistent, though calling these before initialize is an unlikely misuse.

findings.title: Two getBoundingClientRect calls per mouse or pointer event, including page-wide mousemove
findings.why: client_position runs for every mousemove on the page's window (the listener is on EMSCRIPTEN_EVENT_TARGET_WINDOW, line 395), every mouse down/up and every touch pointer event. Each call makes two JS calls, and each of those builds a DOMRect and may force a layout. This engine targets low-end hardware, and the doubled layout query on the busiest input path is avoidable.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the two EM_JS functions with one that writes left and top through out-pointers, or returns both in a single call, so each event does one getBoundingClientRect.
findings.verify_reason: web/window.cpp:481-482 calls labrador_canvas_left() and labrador_canvas_top() (EM_JS at 46 and 50), each doing getBoundingClientRect; client_position is called from window-level mousemove/mouseup (395-397) and pointer paths (630, 648, 673, 811). The second call only reflows if layout is dirty, so the cost is mostly an extra JS crossing and DOMRect; still a trivial real fix.

findings.title: Closed-window guards are uneven across Window's methods
findings.why: enter_fullscreen and set_cursor_visible return early on a closed window. resize_client and leave_fullscreen do not: they still measure the canvas and call notify->on_window_size_changed. APPLICATION.md section 7 says the closed window "listens to nothing", but these calls go on reporting into the owner between close() and on_closed. The Win32 window has the same split: set_cursor_visible and set_cursor_confined check `handle != nullptr` (win32/window.cpp:576, 585), while resize_client, enter_fullscreen and leave_fullscreen (501-571) pass a possibly null handle to SetWindowPos, IsWindowVisible and MonitorFromWindow.
findings.suggested_fix: Give every mutating Window method the same early return: `if (closed) return;` on the web, `if (handle == nullptr) return;` on Win32. Then state in window.h that every call after close() does nothing, as close() already says of a second close.
findings.verify_reason: web/window.cpp:881-917: enter_fullscreen and set_cursor_visible check impl_->closed, resize_client and leave_fullscreen call report_size() (464-469), which calls notify->on_window_size_changed unconditionally. Win32 set_cursor_* check handle != nullptr while resize_client/enter/leave_fullscreen do not. Win32 calls with a null HWND fail harmlessly rather than crash, so impact is small; low stands.

findings.title: JsonValue::number narrows any JSON number to float with no range check
findings.evidence:
`if (!raw.IsNumber()) { value.fail("is not a number"); }
return raw.GetFloat();`  (rapidjson GetFloat is static_cast<float>(GetDouble()))
findings.why: json.h promises that every read is checked and that a content mistake throws naming the file and key (T6). A hand-typed value such as `"frame_time": 1e40` passes IsNumber, then becomes +inf, which is formally undefined for an out-of-range double-to-float conversion, with no diagnostic. It then reaches AnimationStrip and sprite origins. The narrow phase works hard to keep nonfinite values out of positions, while this reader produces them.
findings.suggested_fix: Read GetDouble(), and fail("is out of range for a float") when the result is not finite or exceeds FLT_MAX. Document this next to `number` in json.h.
findings.verify_reason: json.cpp:227-236 JsonValue::number checks IsNumber() and then returns raw.GetFloat() with no range or finite check, so 1e40 narrows to inf or out-of-range. json.h:34 promises checked accessors. The cited lines 789-798 were wrong; the code is at line 235.

findings.title: read_json_file's documented exceptions omit the null-path std::invalid_argument
findings.evidence: Header: "Throws std::runtime_error naming the path if the file cannot be opened, cannot be read, or does not parse." Implementation json.cpp:633-636: `if (path == nullptr) { throw std::invalid_argument("read_json_file - null path"); }`
findings.why: The neighbouring parse_json documents its std::invalid_argument precondition, and this one does not. A caller catching std::runtime_error, as ResourceLoader's optional-bank path does, would get an exception type the contract never mentioned.
findings.suggested_fix: Add "Throws std::invalid_argument for a null path" to the header comment, matching parse_json.
findings.verify_reason: json.h:16-18 documents only std::runtime_error for read_json_file, while json.cpp:73 throws std::invalid_argument('read_json_file - null path'). parse_json's comment at json.h:28 does document its invalid_argument. The cited lines were wrong; the comment is at json.h:13-19.

findings.title: reload_device_resources and the load_* helpers are const but fill the stores
findings.evidence: `void reload_device_resources() const;` ... `void load_texture(const std::string& directory, const std::string& name) const;` ... `void load_sound_bank(bool optional, const std::string& directory, const std::string& name) const;` Each one writes through `render_resources_` / `audio_resources_`, for example resource_loader.cpp:1029 `this->render_resources_->add_sprite_sheet(name, ...)`.
findings.why: The engine uses const to mean 'no observable writes': draw() is const all the way down, and concurrent const calls are assumed safe. A const method that rebuilds every GPU texture in the registry advertises a safety it does not have. It compiles only because the stores are held through non-const pointers, which is shallow const.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop const from reload_device_resources and the four private load_* helpers. Callers already hold a non-const ResourceLoader.
findings.verify_reason: resource_loader.h:113 declares 'void reload_device_resources() const;' and lines 129-136 declare the four load_* helpers const. resource_loader.cpp:134 load_sprite_sheet calls this->render_resources_->add_sprite_sheet. That is shallow const over non-const pointers. The cited line numbers (392-415) were wrong because the header is 138 lines.

findings.title: Empty JS catch in detach() swallows every source.stop() error without saying which one it expects
findings.why: The expected case is an InvalidStateError from stopping a source that was never started, but the catch also hides any other failure from stop(). Its neighbour at line 275 (`catch (refused)`) explains itself; this one has no comment.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line reason, and if practical rethrow anything other than InvalidStateError (`if (ignored.name !== 'InvalidStateError') throw ignored;`).
findings.verify_reason: webaudio/audio_device.cpp:131-132 has `catch (ignored) {}` with no reason, unlike the commented `catch (refused)` near line 275. Minor, low.

findings.title: Both wave-bank opens turn every std::exception, bad_alloc included, into the runtime_error that triggers silent optional-bank substitution
findings.evidence: xaudio2: `catch (const std::exception&) { ... throw std::runtime_error("Failed to open wave bank: " + path); }`. webaudio/audio_device.cpp:610: `catch (const std::exception& unread) { ... throw std::runtime_error("Failed to open wave bank: " + std::string(unread.what())); }`. assets/resource_loader.cpp:157 then catches `const std::runtime_error& missing` and, for an optional bank, substitutes SoundBank::silent with only a warning.
findings.why: An out-of-memory (std::bad_alloc) or any other non-file failure while opening an optional bank is relabelled as 'container missing' and handled as a stated-optional asset. It shows up as a warning and silent audio instead of stopping the game. The XAudio2 path also drops the original what() entirely. resource_loader.cpp says only a missing, unreadable or unplayable container may be substituted, which these catches do not enforce.
findings.suggested_fix: Catch only the reader's or DirectXTK's file and format failures (std::runtime_error and the reader's out_of_range for 'no file'), or rethrow std::bad_alloc unchanged before the catch-all conversion. Keep the original what() on the XAudio2 path as well.
findings.verify_reason: Both catches convert any std::exception, so a bad_alloc on an optional bank would become a silent-bank warning. That part is real but narrow. Part of the claim is wrong: the XAudio2 path drops what() deliberately, and its comment says why (DirectXTK's what() is just "WaveBank", and T6 wants the path), so that is not a defect. What remains is bad_alloc during an optional bank open: an unlikely input, and the result is a warning plus silent audio, not corruption.

findings.title: partition() returns a fresh vector, so Scene::draw allocates on the heap every frame
findings.evidence: `std::vector<std::pair<int, int>> Partitioner::partition(int num_elements, int num_partitions) const { ... std::vector<std::pair<int, int>> result; ... result.push_back(std::make_pair(start, end));` used per frame at engine/scene/scene.cpp:238-240 `const std::vector<std::pair<int, int>> ranges = this->partitioner_->partition(count, this->thread_pool_->max_num_threads());`
findings.why: broad_phase.h cites PHILOSOPHY: "per-frame code performs no heap allocation", and the collision module goes out of its way to reuse buffers (find_contacts, BroadPhase::pairs_buffer). The fan-out helper in the same folder returns by value and is called once per Scene::draw with more than one view, so every split-screen frame allocates. It also never calls reserve.
findings.suggested_fix: Have partition fill a caller-owned vector (clear, then push) that Scene keeps as a member, or return a fixed-capacity range array. The count is bounded by the view capacity.
findings.verify_reason: The cited lines 378-406 do not exist: partitioner.cpp is 54 lines, and the vector is built at lines 22-37. The allocation per multi-view draw is real (scene.cpp:238-240). But the same loop calls ThreadPool::add_task(std::function<void()>) with a lambda capturing five values, which almost certainly heap-allocates per task anyway. Removing this one vector would not make the fan-out allocation-free, and the path runs only for more than one view with a pool.

findings.title: ByteReader borrows its buffer by const reference but accepts temporaries
findings.why: `ByteReader reader(read_file_bytes(path), path);` compiles and leaves bytes_ dangling as soon as the statement ends. That is exactly the read-past-a-heap-allocation this class exists to prevent. Every current caller (xwb_file.cpp:348, dds_file.cpp:147, sprite_font_file.cpp:54 and the tests) passes an lvalue, so the contract currently holds only by convention. The header is published as game code (published.ts:120).
findings.suggested_fix: Add `ByteReader(std::vector<unsigned char>&&, const std::string&) = delete;` so the compiler enforces the lifetime rule.
findings.verify_reason: byte_reader.h:29-30 takes const std::vector<unsigned char>& and stores const ref bytes_ (line ~50); no rvalue overload is deleted, so a temporary binds and dangles. Current callers pass lvalues.

findings.title: read_file_bytes' documented exceptions omit the std::invalid_argument that path_from_utf8 throws
findings.why: A caller that catches the two documented types, for example to report a missing asset, is not told about a third type that escapes from the same call. The published contract is incomplete.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the comment that a path containing an embedded NUL throws std::invalid_argument (file_path.h).
findings.verify_reason: byte_reader.h read_file_bytes comment lists only out_of_range and runtime_error; file_path.cpp:9-12 path_from_utf8 throws std::invalid_argument on embedded NUL, and read_file_bytes calls it.

findings.title: 0/0 in Colour division yields NaN, which clamp01 passes through, breaking the [0,1] invariant
findings.evidence:
this->r /= other.r; ... this->clamp_colours();
clamp01 (colour.h:15-18): `return value < 0.0f ? 0.0f : (value > 1.0f ? 1.0f : value);` NaN fails both comparisons and is returned unchanged. operator/(Colour, Colour) at line 156 and operator/(Colour, float) share the problem.
findings.why: The header promises 'each channel clamped to [0, 1]'. Colour::black / Colour::black, or any zero-channel divisor, produces a NaN channel that reaches vertex colours on every backend. Under /fp:precise the NaN propagates, and its effect on the pixel is backend-defined.
findings.suggested_fix: Make clamp01 map NaN to 0, for example `!(value > 0.0f) ? 0.0f : ...`. Alternatively, document and test that division by a zero channel is undefined, or remove the Colour-by-Colour division operators if nothing uses them.
findings.verify_reason: colour.h:15-18 has clamp01 return value < 0 ? 0 : (value > 1 ? 1 : value). NaN fails both comparisons and passes through unchanged. operator/= (colour.cpp:86-93) divides channel by channel, so 0/0 gives NaN and the [0,1] invariant breaks. Low severity, an edge case.

findings.title: sprite_world_bounds always calls cos/sin, unlike quad_bounds, although it runs per object per view
findings.why: The file's own stated T8 rationale is ignored on the path that actually serves the cull. It is a small, needless cost per widget per view per frame.
findings.suggested_fix: Short-circuit rotation == 0.0f (cosine = 1, sine = 0), matching quad_bounds.
findings.verify_reason: sprite_geometry.cpp:251-252 calls std::cos and std::sin unconditionally in sprite_world_bounds, while quad_bounds (lines 125-132) short-circuits rotation == 0 'because this runs on the cull path, per object per view'. It is a minor cost.

findings.title: Out-of-range player index silently returns a fullscreen viewport; dividers throw for the same class of mistake
findings.why: renderer.h:379-380 rejects exactly this: 'asking for a view nobody set up must not quietly return a fullscreen pane and draw a whole extra pass (T6)'. ViewportManager::player_viewport does it anyway, and viewport_manager.h never says so. The fallback is pinned by tests/render/viewport_manager_tests.cpp:124-141, which only checks that it is not the next layout's answer. all_viewports() takes no argument, so the '*4*' comment describes a call that cannot be made.
findings.suggested_fix: Throw std::out_of_range for an index outside viewport_count_from_layout. Update the test to CHECK_THROWS, document the throw in the header, and delete the stale all_viewports comment.
findings.verify_reason: The fullscreen fallback in calculate_viewport is real, and the all_viewports '*4*' wording is confusing. But tests/render/viewport_manager_tests.cpp:126-141 deliberately pins the fallback (CHECK is_fullscreen for index 9 and -1), so this is tested, intended behaviour. renderer.h:376-380 is about Renderer view indices, not ViewportManager. ColourWars calls player_viewport from several places (player_builder.cpp:60, level.cpp, seat_commands.cpp), so switching to a throw is a behaviour and API decision, not hygiene.

findings.title: FocusGroup's throw on an out-of-range slot is stated only in the .cpp, and set_focused applies it inconsistently
findings.why: CONVENTIONS requires a contract to live at the declaration. focus.h's focused/set_focused/move/activate say nothing about std::out_of_range for a bad slot. set_focused checks the widget first, so a bad slot with a foreign widget returns false while the same bad slot with a held widget throws. The same caller mistake gets two different answers.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the slot first in set_focused, as focused() effectively does. In focus.h, add one line to the slot-taking members: "Throws std::out_of_range if slot is outside [0, slot_count())." Move the .cpp rationale there.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed. focus.cpp:58-62 holds the throw-not-clamp rationale, and focus.h:100-123 says nothing about out_of_range on focused, set_focused, move or activate. set_focused (:67-74) checks index_of(widget) before slot.at(), so a bad slot with a foreign widget returns false while a bad slot with a held widget throws. A bad slot is a programming error caught by .at() either way, so low.

findings.title: UiContainer::add_child states a non-null precondition but dereferences null immediately
findings.why: Passing nullptr is undefined behaviour (a null dereference inside child->name()). There is no named diagnostic. The sibling registration API in the same module, FocusGroup::add, rejects null with std::invalid_argument (focus.cpp:26-29), as do Scene::remove and StateContext::push. T6-style loud failure is the module's norm, and this public entry point is the exception.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `if (child == nullptr) throw std::invalid_argument("UiContainer::add_child: null child");`, change the header comment to say it throws, and add a widget_tests case for it.
findings.verify_reason: widget.cpp:65-68 dereferences child unchecked, and widget.h:72 states non-null as a precondition. But docs/code-hygiene-public-headers.md (UI objects and containers, SM-45) records 'Non-null children are a precondition' and 'No new exception or null-recovery policy is introduced', so it is a documented precondition rather than a missed contract; the inconsistency with FocusGroup::add (focus.cpp:28) is real but minor.

themes.name: Untrusted input and exception safety
themes.desc: Readers of external bytes and code that crosses C callbacks. JSON parses recursively, so deep nesting overflows the stack instead of throwing; an animation strip's frame_count is unbounded; read_file_bytes narrows the file size unchecked. Win32 window_proc lets game and renderer exceptions escape into user32 against window.h's promise, and a throwing notify handler during construction leaves an HWND pointing at freed state.
themes.story: Behaviour commits with negative tests: a nesting limit or iterative parse for JSON, a bound on authored counts named with the file, checked size narrowing, and an exception barrier in window_proc that hands the failure to pump_until_quit as window.h states. Each consumer-visible refusal gets a CHANGES entry.

findings.title: window_proc lets game and renderer exceptions escape into user32, against window.h's promise that they come out of pump_until_quit
findings.evidence: window_proc has no try/catch, yet on_size_message calls `this->notify->tick();` (line 694, WM_PAINT during a size/move drag) and `this->notify->on_window_size_changed(...)` (lines 750, 757, 777), which reach Renderer::window_size_changed and ResolutionManager::set_resolution_exactly (both throw). app/window.h:262-263 promises: "An exception out of tick() or out of a handler comes out of this call." The backends say the opposite: render/d3d12/device_resources.cpp:331 "unwound into DispatchMessage instead, where the shell has nowhere to catch it"; render/d3d11/renderer.cpp:769 "the throw comes out of a window message where the shell has nowhere to catch it"; render/vulkan/device_resources.cpp:1389 the same. Vulkan's create_window_size_dependent_resources still throws on that path through create_colour_target's check_vk and through handle_device_lost -> create_device_resources.
findings.why: Messages sent by the system (ShowWindow/SetWindowPos in resize_client, and DefWindowProc's modal size/move loop dispatching WM_PAINT) call window_proc through user32 and kernel callback frames. A C++ exception unwinding through them is either silently swallowed or ends the process, depending on the process's callback-exception policy. So a device loss or a state's update() throwing during a window drag is lost or crashes the game instead of reaching main's handler. The public contract is false for exactly the cases the backends try to avoid.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the web window's guarded(): wrap the body of window_proc (or each notify call) in try/catch, store the first std::exception_ptr in Impl, call DestroyWindow/PostQuitMessage, and std::rethrow_exception it from pump_until_quit after the loop ends. Then the backend comments' 'nowhere to catch it' becomes false and can be removed or reworded.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: window_proc (window.cpp:1099) has no try/catch, and on_size_message calls notify->tick() on WM_PAINT during a drag (694) and on_window_size_changed (750/757/777). window.h's pump_until_quit says an exception out of tick() or a handler comes out of that call, while the d3d12, d3d11 and vulkan comments say such a throw has nowhere to be caught. It is not tracked anywhere. Severity is inflated: the exception has to happen during a modal drag or a SetWindowPos/ShowWindow-sent message, and a throw is already fatal under T6. What goes wrong is how the game stops (a crash or a swallowed error instead of an on-screen reason), not the game state.

findings.title: JSON is parsed with rapidjson's recursive parser, so deep nesting overflows the stack instead of throwing
findings.evidence: document.Parse(text, length);
findings.why: With the default flags, rapidjson recurses once per nesting level (ParseValue -> ParseArray/ParseObject). A small file of about 100,000 '[' characters overflows the 1 MB native stack, and wasm uses -sSTACK_SIZE=1048576 (cmake/settings.cpp:82 is settings.cmake). The process crashes. json.h promises std::runtime_error naming the source for text that does not parse, and the loaders exist so that a hand-edited content file never crashes (T6). Both read_json_file and the public parse_json pass through this line.
findings.suggested_fix: Parse with document.Parse<rapidjson::kParseIterativeFlag>(text, length), which uses a heap stack and reports errors normally. Optionally add a depth limit. Add a json_tests case that feeds 100,000 nested '[' to both entry points and expects runtime_error.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed at json.cpp:56: document.Parse(text, length) uses default flags, no RAPIDJSON_PARSE_DEFAULT_FLAGS override anywhere, so the recursive parser runs; wasm stack is 1 MB (settings.cmake:82). Deep nesting crashes instead of the runtime_error json.h promises. However the input is the game's own content file or caller text, not untrusted network data, so medium rather than high.

findings.title: An animation strip's frame_count is unbounded, so one JSON number allocates up to 32 GB and fails without the path
findings.why: Only negative counts are refused. Input: {"name":"a","first_frame":{"x":0,"y":0,"w":0,"h":0},"frame_count":2147483647,"frame_time":0.1,"looping":false}. With w = 0 every x stays in range, so calculate_frame passes. animation_strip.cpp:79 then runs rects.reserve(2^31) of 16-byte RectangleI, which is 32 GB, and loops 2^31 times. The result is std::bad_alloc natively, or std::length_error on wasm32, neither of them the runtime_error naming path and strip that sprite_sheet_loader.h promises. The catch above it handles only out_of_range. byte_reader.h names exactly this shape ('the one place a corrupt file can ask for gigabytes'), and the binary readers guard against it.
findings.suggested_fix: Bound frame_count by something the content can justify, such as a named maximum or the frame width against the atlas. Alternatively, stop caching every rect and compute frames on demand. Add a loader test with frame_count 2147483647 and w 0.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: only frame_count < 0 is refused (sprite_sheet_loader.cpp:107); AnimationStrip ctor calls calculate_all_frame_rects which reserves frame_count RectangleI (animation_strip.cpp:79). Even w=1,x=0 keeps the last x in int range, so INT_MAX passes the pre-check and the reserve throws bad_alloc/length_error, which the out_of_range catch does not convert to a path-naming runtime_error. Developer-authored content only, so medium not high.

findings.title: A notify handler throwing during the constructor's SetWindowPos/ShowWindow leaves a live HWND whose user data points at freed Impl
findings.evidence: After CreateWindowExW succeeds (and WM_CREATE has stored `this` in GWLP_USERDATA), the constructor calls `SetWindowPos(this->handle, nullptr, 0, 0, corrected.x, corrected.y, ...)` (line 403) and `ShowWindow(this->handle, ...)` (line 407). Both synchronously send WM_SIZE / WM_ACTIVATE to window_proc -> notify->on_window_size_changed / on_activated. Cleanup exists only for the CreateWindowExW failure: "The destructor does not run for an object whose constructor threw, so the registration above is this line's to undo."
findings.why: WindowNotify is a public interface, and Application's on_window_size_changed throws std::invalid_argument for a non-positive size. If a handler throws and the exception makes it back out of ShowWindow, ~Impl never runs. The window is not destroyed, the class stays registered, and every later message to that window dereferences a dangling Impl*. The constructor's own comment shows the author knew ~Impl does not run, but the cleanup covers only one throw site.
findings.suggested_fix: After CreateWindowExW succeeds, wrap the rest of the constructor in try/catch: clear GWLP_USERDATA, DestroyWindow, UnregisterClassW, then rethrow. Alternatively, defer notify delivery until construction completes, or rely on the guard from the window_proc finding.
findings.verify_reason: The code shape is real: only CreateWindowExW's failure is cleaned up, and the SetWindowPos (403) and ShowWindow (407) that follow synchronously deliver WM_SIZE/WM_ACTIVATE to notify. But the throw the finding names needs a non-positive client size. WM_SIZE with SIZE_MINIMIZED is diverted, and the size here comes from validated ApplicationOptions, so the concrete input is hard to produce. Even then the exception has to get back out through a kernel callback, which is finding 0's problem. A latent robustness gap, low.

findings.title: Fixed-schema loaders reject unknown keys but silently accept duplicate ones; the first value wins
findings.evidence:
inline void reject_unknown_keys(const JsonValue& object,
		std::initializer_list<std::string_view> allowed)
findings.why: keys() keeps duplicates, as json_tests.cpp:209 pins, and the accessors use FindMember, which returns the first. {"position":{"x":1,"x":2,"y":0}} in a sprite sheet or a repeated "optional" in a manifest group therefore loads using the first value, with no message. That is the 'quiet disagreement with a content file' sprite_sheet_loader.cpp:55-64 argues against. Unknown keys are refused, so a duplicate is the remaining silent hand-edit mistake.
findings.suggested_fix: In reject_unknown_keys, also fail with where() + " repeats key '<k>'" when a name appears twice. Add sprite-sheet and manifest tests.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: reject_unknown_keys (json_object_keys.h:38-49) only checks membership; keys() keeps duplicates (json_tests.cpp:209 pins it) and accessors take the first match, so a repeated key silently loads one value.

findings.title: The file size is narrowed to size_t unchecked, then the full streamoff is read into the possibly smaller buffer
findings.why: On a 32-bit size_t (wasm32), a file of 4 GiB + N bytes gives an N-byte vector, and file.read is then asked for the full 64-bit size. That is a heap overrun, and the only reader in the engine without a checked bound. MEMFS makes such a file unlikely in the browser, but NODEFS and NODERAWFS test runs and any future 32-bit port do not.
findings.suggested_fix: Throw runtime_error naming the path when size > max of size_t (or above a named content limit), and pass the vector's own size to read().
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed at byte_reader.cpp:87-91: static_cast<size_t>(size) then file.read(..., size) with the unnarrowed streamoff; on wasm32 with NODERAWFS (used by Node test runs) a >4 GiB file would overrun. Practically unreachable; low is right.

findings.title: A PNG is decoded with no size limit, and the dimension check after decoding cannot fire
findings.why: lodepng allocates width*height*4 from the IHDR before the engine looks at the dimensions. A zero-filled 30000x30000 PNG compresses to about 1-2 MB and asks for 3.6 GB, which is a decompression bomb. The result is bad_alloc or lodepng error 83 on wasm, after a long inflate. The width > INT_MAX test at line 38 runs only after a successful decode of that size, so it is effectively dead. The .dds and .spritefont readers check declared sizes against the file before allocating; this reader does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Call lodepng_inspect first, or use a lodepng::State with decoder.zlibsettings.max_output_size set. Refuse dimensions above a named texture limit before decoding, naming the path. Add a hostile-IHDR test to png_file_tests.cpp.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: lodepng::decode is called with default settings (max_output_size = 0, unlimited) before any dimension check, and lodepng itself rejects width/height 0 (error 93), so the engine's post-decode check is largely unreachable. Real decompression-bomb hardening gap, but PNGs are the game's own assets; low.

findings.title: Hostile-JSON shapes (deep nesting, out-of-float-range numbers) and the PNG size bomb are untested
findings.evidence: TEST_CASE("a parse error names the file and where in it")
findings.why: json_tests.cpp covers NULs, BOMs, types and positions. It has no case for nesting depth or for a number outside float range, the two inputs that crash or produce non-finite values above. png_file_tests.cpp:154 tests only non-PNG bytes, not a valid PNG declaring huge dimensions. Without these tests, fixing the findings above would not be pinned.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a deep-nesting case through parse_json and read_json_file, a number("x") case with 1e39, and a png_file_tests case with a crafted IHDR (for example 40000x40000) expecting runtime_error before allocation.
findings.verify_reason: True that json_tests.cpp has no nesting-depth or float-range case and png_file_tests has no huge-IHDR case, but this restates the test parts already in the fixes of findings 0, 1 and 3; low and redundant.

findings.title: Several .xwb header refusals have no test
findings.evidence: TEST_CASE("a bank this engine cannot play says which way")
findings.why: xwb_file.cpp refuses these by name, and no subcase covers them: bank data shorter than 96 bytes (line 92), entry_size < 24 (line 111), a name table too small for entry_count*name_size or a zero name_size (line 431), zero channels or zero sample rate (line 239), and 8-bit or 16-bit PCM whose length is not whole frames (line 262). These are the header fields a hostile bank controls; a later edit could drop any one of them silently.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a subcase per check using the existing build_bank and poke helpers, each asserting the message fragment.
findings.verify_reason: Subcases in the TEST_CASE at xwb_file_tests.cpp:433 do not cover entry_size < 24 (actually xwb_file.cpp:411, not 111), the name-table check (431), zero channels/sample rate (239) or PCM data not whole blocks (262). Some cited engine line numbers (92, 111) point at helpers, but the untested refusals exist.

findings.title: Most of the .dds reader's named refusals are untested
findings.evidence: TEST_CASE("a file that is not a texture this engine draws says which way")
findings.why: dds_file.h promises named throws for volume textures, the DX10 header and unknown fourCCs. Only the cube map, no-alpha, too-many-mips and large-width cases are exercised. These have no test: the DX10 throw (dds_file.cpp:94), an unknown fourCC, a volume texture via caps2 or depth > 1, a header_size other than 124, a pixel_format_size other than 32, zero width or height, a file truncated inside the header, and the DXT2->BC2 and DXT4->BC3 collapse the header documents. A regression in any of them would pass CI.
findings.suggested_fix: Add poke-based subcases on quad_bytes() for each listed field, each checking runtime_error and that the message names the path. Add mapping checks for DXT2 and DXT4 fourCCs.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed that dds_file_tests.cpp has no DX10, unknown fourCC, volume, header-size, pixel-format-size, zero-dimension or DXT2/DXT4 subcases (grep of tests finds no DX10/DXT2/DXT4). Missing negative-path tests for a reader of the game's own assets; low, not medium.

findings.title: The spritefont reader's unknown-DXGI-format and stride/rows-mismatch refusals are untested
findings.evidence: TEST_CASE("a file that is not a font says which way it is not one")
findings.why: sprite_font_file.cpp refuses an atlas format other than 28, 74 or 115 (to_texture_format) and an atlas whose stated stride or rows disagree with texture_level. The second is the check its comment calls worth 'a message rather than a texture full of noise'. Neither path appears in the tests; only overflowed layouts, glyph count, glyph extents and metric finiteness are covered.
findings.suggested_fix: Add two cases: patch the DXGI format field to an unsupported value, and change the stride to expected+4. Each expects runtime_error naming the path.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: the overflow test's widths all fail inside texture_level or positive_field before the stride/rows comparison at sprite_font_file.cpp:162-170, and no test feeds an unsupported DXGI format to to_texture_format (line 44).

themes.name: Render backend error handling and resource ownership
themes.desc:
Format switches whose default case silently maps unknown formats to RGBA or DXT5 in D3D11, D3D12 and GL. Other items:
- block_until discards the wait result.
- D3D12 holds a raw fence HANDLE.
- Vulkan writes failed-create outputs into owned members, ignores vkResetCommandPool failures and has no RAII for its buffers.
- GL fetches wglCreateContextAttribsARB without the sentinel filter, leaks the bootstrap context, shader and program objects, and gives TextureOwner implicit copy operations.
- A SetPixelFormat failure reuses another message.
- D3D11 add_texture_asset breaks the seam's naming contract.
- D3D HRESULT failures carry no operation context.
themes.story: Fix this per backend in behaviour commits: exhaustive format switches that throw on unknown values, RAII for the D3D12 fence event, GL objects and Vulkan buffers, propagated wait and reset results, and an operation-named ThrowIfFailed overload. Verify across the five native Debug presets plus wasm-debug GL, and re-run the Vulkan validate_sync procedure for the Vulkan changes.

findings.title: D3D11 add_texture_asset breaks the seam's 'names the texture and format' contract; the other four backends keep it
findings.evidence:
engine/render/d3d11/texture_factory.cpp:106-112:
		ComPtr<ID3D11Texture2D> texture_2d;
		ThrowIfFailed(device_of(renderer)->CreateTexture2D(&description,
			initial.data(), texture_2d.GetAddressOf()));
		...
		ThrowIfFailed(device_of(renderer)->CreateShaderResourceView(

Contract, engine/render/resource_factory.h:88-91: "Throws std::runtime_error naming `name` and the format if the device will not take it".
Siblings: d3d12/texture_factory.cpp:201 `throw std::runtime_error("Texture '" + name + "' is " + format_name(texture.format) + " at " ... + hresult_name(created) + ").");`, vulkan/texture_factory.cpp:185, gl/texture_factory.cpp:62/219 all name the texture.
Also false: engine/render/throw_if_failed.h:41-45 "both Direct3D backends reach this class instead, and deriving from std::runtime_error here is what holds every ThrowIfFailed site to that contract at once."
findings.why: When a D3D11 device rejects a format, for example optional B4G4R4A4 support, the thrown message is only "Failure with HRESULT of 80070057". It gives no texture name and no format, which is the eight-digit-HRESULT outcome resource_factory.h's own comment (lines 43-45) calls unacceptable under T6. D3D12 fixed this for the same call, but D3D11 did not. throw_if_failed.h then claims the exception type alone meets the contract, but the contract is about the message content, not just the type.
findings.suggested_fix: Do what d3d12/texture_factory.cpp does: capture the HRESULT from CreateTexture2D and CreateShaderResourceView and throw std::runtime_error naming the texture, format, size and HRESULT. Share format_name (see the separate finding). Then correct throw_if_failed.h:41-45 so it claims only the exception type, not the message contract.
findings.verify_reason: d3d11/texture_factory.cpp:106-112 calls bare ThrowIfFailed on CreateTexture2D/CreateShaderResourceView, and com_exception formats only 'Failure with HRESULT of %08X'. resource_factory.h says add_texture_asset 'Throws std::runtime_error naming `name` and the format'. d3d12:202 and vulkan:186/197 do name them. throw_if_failed.h:41-45 claims the base type 'holds every ThrowIfFailed site to that contract', which is false about the message content. The problem is real, but it only makes a device-refusal diagnostic less useful. It does not cause a functional bug, so medium is the right severity, not high.

findings.title: wglCreateContextAttribsARB is fetched with raw wglGetProcAddress, bypassing the sentinel filter
findings.why: load_entry_point (line 36-43) exists because 'ICDs may use these failure sentinels instead of a null pointer' (1, 2, 3, -1). On the one lookup that decides whether a 3.3 context can be made at all, a sentinel passes the null check and gets called, which crashes instead of producing the intended 'no WGL_ARB_create_context' message. The file also uses two inconsistent fetch paths.
findings.suggested_fix: Use load_entry_point("wglCreateContextAttribsARB") here.
findings.verify_reason: wgl_context.cpp:36-43 defines load_entry_point, which filters the 1/2/3/-1 sentinels 'ICDs may use'. Lines :349-352 fetch wglCreateContextAttribsARB with raw wglGetProcAddress and check only for nullptr, so a sentinel would be called as a function pointer instead of producing the named refusal. The quote and the inconsistency are both real.

findings.title: D3D HRESULT failures carry no context, while Vulkan's check_vk names the failing operation
findings.why: These are the same concept with two reporting styles. A Vulkan failure says which call failed and with what result name. A D3D11/D3D12 failure at any of roughly 50 ThrowIfFailed sites, such as swap chain or PSO creation, is just a hex code, which is what T6 objects to. D3D12 has started writing its own one-off formatter (hresult_name) to get around it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an engine-styled `check_hr(HRESULT, const char* what)`, or a ThrowIfFailed overload taking `what`, that produces the check_vk message shape. Use it at the engine-written D3D call sites. The upstream-adopted d3d11/device_resources.cpp can keep its ThrowIfFailed calls.
findings.verify_reason: throw_if_failed.h:64-70 throws com_exception(hr), which carries only the hex value. check_vk names the operation, and d3d12 has its own hresult_name for the texture throw. The inconsistency is real, and this file is not tracked in code-hygiene.md. It overlaps with finding 0 for texture upload.

findings.title: Format switch default silently treats any unlisted format as RGBA
findings.why: texture_format.h promises that an unsupported format is 'rejected by name ... rather than passed through to fail as a device error'. If an enumerator is added to TextureFormat, this backend compiles without warning and uploads its bytes as RGBA. That is wrong pixels, or a size-mismatch device error, with no name attached.
findings.suggested_fix: List every enumerator without a default, and after the switch throw std::invalid_argument naming the format. MSVC's /W4 then reaches the throw only for values outside the enum.
findings.verify_reason: texture_factory.cpp:53-57 has 'case r8g8b8a8_unorm: default: return DXGI_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM;'. The enum has six values, all listed, so this is latent only, and texture_format.h:26's 'rejected by name' promise is about files, which the parser enforces. The same pattern exists in d3d12/texture_factory.cpp:72-74, so it is not D3D11-only. Removing the default would let an added enumerator reach the compiler's warnings. A valid low-severity robustness point.

findings.title: New size is committed before a rebuild that can throw, so a retry at the same size becomes a no-op over released back buffers
findings.why: output_size_ is updated first. create_window_size_dependent_resources then resets every back buffer (line 362) before ResizeBuffers or GetBuffer can fail with something other than removal, such as E_OUTOFMEMORY or INVALID_CALL. If the exception is caught and the same size is requested again, both DeviceResources::window_size_changed (line 463) and Renderer::window_size_changed (renderer.cpp:979) treat it as unchanged and return false. back_buffer() is then null and back_buffer_size() reports a size the swap chain never reached. On the line-357 throw the back buffers survive, but output_size_ and screen_viewport_ disagree. Renderer::window_size_changed has also already called abandon_recording, so frame_begun stays true while no view is reopened.
findings.suggested_fix: Commit output_size_ only after the rebuild succeeds: pass width and height into create_window_size_dependent_resources, or restore the previous RECT on failure. Alternatively, leave the size marked dirty so the next call rebuilds.
findings.verify_reason: The ordering is as described: device_resources.cpp:469-474 commits output_size_ and then calls create_window_size_dependent_resources, which resets back buffers at 360-364 before ResizeBuffers (385) or GetBuffer (441) can throw. A same-size retry would then hit the early return at 463 and at renderer.cpp's comparison. The failure needs a caught non-removal exception followed by a retry at the same size. The file's own comment at 329-331 says a throw on this path unwinds into DispatchMessage, where the shell has nowhere to catch it, so it is effectively fatal. That makes this a latent robustness issue, not a medium bug.

findings.title: block_until ignores WaitForSingleObjectEx's result and reports S_OK even when the wait failed
findings.evidence:
WaitForSingleObjectEx(this->fence_event_, INFINITE, FALSE);
		return S_OK;
findings.why: block_until carries the HRESULT for both wait_for_frame (throwing) and try_wait_for_gpu (bool). If the wait returns WAIT_FAILED (for example, an invalid or closed event handle), the function reports completion although the fence was never reached. Its callers then reset allocators and overwrite vertex pages, or release staging buffers, that the GPU may still be reading. This is exactly the hazard the fence exists to prevent, and nothing reports it.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the return value. On anything other than WAIT_OBJECT_0, return HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(GetLastError()) (or E_FAIL), so wait_for_frame throws and try_wait_for_gpu answers false.
findings.verify_reason: device_resources.cpp:567-568 does call WaitForSingleObjectEx(fence_event_, INFINITE, FALSE) and then return S_OK without checking the result, so the unchecked return is real. The failure the finding describes is not realistic, though. The event is created and owned by this class (lines 303-311), and the only place that closes it is the destructor (82-86). try_wait_for_gpu also returns true early when the event is null. A wait on that handle can only fail through misuse, so this is a hygiene gap rather than a likely hazard. Neither docs/code-hygiene.md nor TODO.md tracks it.

findings.title: Fence event is a raw HANDLE closed manually in the destructor
findings.evidence: HANDLE fence_event_ = nullptr;
findings.why: Every other resource DeviceResources owns is a ComPtr. The event is created at device_resources.cpp:305 and closed by hand at :82-86. RAII would remove the manual cleanup, and the lazy-creation branch becomes the only place that touches it.
findings.suggested_fix: Hold it in Microsoft::WRL::Wrappers::Event (from <wrl/event.h>), or in a small unique_ptr with a CloseHandle deleter, and delete the destructor's CloseHandle block.
findings.verify_reason: device_resources.h:148 declares HANDLE fence_event_ = nullptr. It is closed in the destructor at device_resources.cpp:82-86, and that cleanup is correct. CONVENTIONS has no RAII or wrapper rule, and the Vulkan backend's backend.h also holds raw VK handles. Using an Event wrapper would be an optional style improvement; nothing is wrong with the current code.

findings.title: `default:` in format switches silently maps any future TextureFormat to RGBA8
findings.evidence:
case TextureFormat::r8g8b8a8_unorm:
default:
	return DXGI_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM;
(also format_name at 88-89)
findings.why: Every current TextureFormat enumerator is listed, so the default only catches a future one. It would then create an RGBA8 resource and copy rows sized by RGBA8 footprints from data laid out for another format, with no error. Without the default, a switch-coverage warning would flag the missing case.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the `default:` labels, add a throw after the switch for out-of-range values, and make the same change in the sibling backends that share the pattern.
findings.verify_reason: texture_factory.cpp:72-74 and 88-89 do fall through default: to RGBA8. The 'why' is wrong for this backend: it builds only under MSVC, where C4061/C4062 are off by default even at /W4, so removing default gives no coverage warning. TextureFormat is an enum class with every enumerator listed, so the risk applies only to a future format. A throw after the switch would still help.

findings.title: Shader/program objects leak when compile or link fails
findings.why: A fragment-compile failure leaves vertex_shader undeleted. A link failure leaves both shaders and the program. compile_shader carefully deletes its own shader on failure, so the cleanup contract is half-kept. restore_device rethrows on a live context, so these objects can stay on a context that remains in use.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the shaders and program before throwing on link failure, and delete vertex_shader if the fragment compile throws. A scoped shader-name owner like texture_factory's TextureOwner would handle both.
findings.verify_reason: renderer.cpp:285-312: if the fragment compile throws, vertex_shader is never deleted. A link failure throws before glDeleteShader on both shaders, and program is left behind. restore_device (renderer.cpp:454-463) calls create_gl_resources inside a try and rethrows. Leaks only on a failure path.

findings.title: compressed_format's default case silently maps any format to DXT5
findings.evidence:
case TextureFormat::bc3_unorm:
			default:                       return COMPRESSED_RGBA_S3TC_DXT5;
findings.why: A future block-compressed TextureFormat (for example BC7) that is_block_compressed accepts would upload as DXT5 and draw garbage, where the uncompressed path refuses unknown formats by name. The default case also turns off the compiler's switch-coverage warning.
findings.suggested_fix: List the three cases explicitly and throw a named refusal after the switch, matching check_uncompressed.
findings.verify_reason: texture_factory.cpp:30-39: `case bc3_unorm: default: return DXT5`. Today TextureFormat has only bc1/bc2/bc3 as block formats, so nothing is wrong yet. The point is hardening for a future format and restoring the switch-coverage warning: low.

findings.title: TextureOwner has a destructor but implicit copy operations
findings.why: An accidental copy would delete the same GL name twice. Every other owner in the folder (GlTexture, both Context structs) deletes its copy constructor and copy assignment.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the copy constructor and copy assignment, as GlTexture does.
findings.verify_reason: texture_factory.cpp:100-104: TextureOwner has a user destructor and implicit copy operations. GlTexture deletes both (backend.h:90-91). It is used once, as a local (`TextureOwner pending;` :168), so the double delete is hypothetical.

findings.title: SetPixelFormat failure reuses the ChoosePixelFormat message
findings.why: By this point a suitable format was found and described (l.306-328); SetPixelFormat typically fails because the window already has a format or for a GetLastError reason. The copied message misdirects diagnosis.
findings.suggested_fix: Say SetPixelFormat failed and include GetLastError(), as configure_swap_interval does at l.102-105.
findings.verify_reason: l.331-335: the SetPixelFormat failure throws a 'cannot be given a 32-bit double-buffered pixel format' message after the format was already chosen and validated (l.306-329), and it gives no GetLastError.

findings.title: Bootstrap legacy context leaks when wglMakeCurrent fails
findings.why: When legacy is non-null and wglMakeCurrent fails, the throw drops the HGLRC. Context's destructor owns only gl_context, and the next failure branch (line 352-358) deletes legacy by hand. This is manual cleanup that RAII should own, and one path misses it.
findings.suggested_fix: Hold the bootstrap context in a small scoped owner, or a unique_ptr with a deleter that calls wglMakeCurrent(dc, nullptr) and wglDeleteContext, so every exit releases it. That also removes the two hand-written cleanups.
findings.verify_reason: wgl_context.cpp:341-347: when legacy is non-null and wglMakeCurrent fails, the throw drops the HGLRC. The next branch (:352-358) deletes legacy by hand, and Context's destructor (:156-161) owns only gl_context. This is a real leak on a one-shot failure path.

findings.title: unit_bytes' `default:` silently sizes any future TextureFormat as 4 bytes, and block_decode's `default:` decodes it as BC3
findings.why: texture_level is the single layout authority for the .dds reader, the .spritefont check and block_decode. With a default label, /W4 and -Wswitch cannot flag a new enumerator, so adding a format such as BC4 or R8 yields a wrong stride and size with no diagnostic. block_decode.cpp:167 has the same shape ('case TextureFormat::bc3_unorm: default:'). It is guarded only by a separate hand-kept list in is_block_compressed, and block_bytes there is also a 'bc1 ? 8 : 16' ternary.
findings.suggested_fix: List every enumerator and drop `default:` so the compiler enforces exhaustiveness. Put a throw after the switch for out-of-range values. Do the same in block_decode's decode_block and block_bytes.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: texture_data.cpp:21-23 groups the RGBA cases with default: returning 4, and block_decode.cpp:167 has a default:. TextureFormat currently has six enumerators all handled, so this is only future-proofing; low. Not in known.json (those entries are backend texture_factory files).

findings.title: Failed-create outputs are written straight into owned members, against the file's own rule
findings.evidence: create_vulkan_buffer (323-328): "A failed API output is not an owned allocation or mapping. Publish each to the cleanup record only after its call reports success." Elsewhere the outputs go directly into members: 540-541 "std::ignore = create(this->owner_->instance, &messenger, nullptr, &this->owner_->messenger);" (result ignored, then ~VulkanDevice at 250-258 destroys it if non-null); 980-981 "check_vk(vkAllocateMemory(device, &allocation, nullptr, &this->colour_memory_)"; 965 "&this->colour_image_"; 738-739 "&frame.command_pool"; 925-926 "&this->timeline_"; texture_factory.cpp:245 "vkAllocateMemory(device, &allocation, nullptr, &memory)" and 343 "&view", which the catch then frees if non-null.
findings.why: The Vulkan spec leaves a failed command's output parameters undefined. The destroy paths treat any non-null value in these members as owned, so a failed create can hand an indeterminate handle to vkDestroy*/vkFreeMemory. The debug messenger case is the most direct: its VkResult is discarded and the handle is still destroyed later. The rule is stated and followed in one function and ignored in the others.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the create_vulkan_buffer pattern everywhere: create into a local VK_NULL_HANDLE and assign it to the member or cleanup variable only after VK_SUCCESS. For the messenger, check the result and store the handle only on success.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed. create_vulkan_buffer (323-328) states the publish-after-success rule. Line 540-541 discards the messenger create result and writes straight into owner_->messenger, which ~VulkanDevice (250-258) later destroys if non-null. 965/980 (colour_image_/colour_memory_) and 738 (frame.command_pool) write directly into members. The device review (2026-10-28-device-ownership.md:105) says only that it 'does not inject failed Vulkan creation outputs', so this is not tracked. The hazard depends on a driver leaving a non-null garbage handle after a failed create. The messenger case is _DEBUG-only. Low.

findings.title: vkResetCommandPool failures are discarded before the buffer is begun again
findings.why: vkResetCommandPool can return VK_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY. When that is ignored, the state flags claim the buffer is in the initial state while it may still be executable. The next vkBeginCommandBuffer on a pool without RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER_BIT is then invalid usage, where the backend's T6 convention would give a named throw. Every other API result on the frame path goes through check_vk.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap both calls in check_vk with an engine-worded message, such as "The frame's command pool could not be reset", before the flags are cleared. Keep std::ignore only for vkResetDescriptorPool, which the spec defines as always returning VK_SUCCESS.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed at 1496-1497 and 1619-1620: both are std::ignore = vkResetCommandPool, with the flags cleared afterward. Only vkResetDescriptorPool (1629) is defined to always succeed. The finding is real, but it needs an OOM on a pool reset, and the consequence is invalid usage instead of a named throw. Low.

findings.title: VulkanBuffer has no RAII, so every temporary buffer needs a hand-written try/catch
findings.evidence: "Pairing them in one struct is what stops the second from being forgotten.\n\tstruct VulkanBuffer { VkBuffer buffer ...; VkDeviceMemory memory ...; ... }\n\tvoid destroy_vulkan_buffer(VkDevice device, VulkanBuffer& buffer);". Manual release blocks: renderer.cpp:572-614 (index staging, catch + duplicate destroy), renderer.cpp:1288-1376 (read-back, catch + duplicate destroy, comment "VulkanBuffer has no destructor"), texture_factory.cpp:231/330/366 (staging), device_resources.cpp:311-349 (create_vulkan_buffer itself).
findings.why: The struct pairs the handles but does not own them. Each of the four temporary-buffer sites repeats the same destroy in a catch and again on the success path, and SM-56's read-back fix was exactly this kind of hand-written cleanup going wrong. A move-only owner holding the creating device's shared_ptr would remove all four try/catch blocks. SM-56 deliberately ruled a general owner framework out of its own scope, so this needs its own story.
findings.suggested_fix: Open a separate story for a move-only scoped owner of a local staging or read-back VulkanBuffer. It would hold the shared_ptr<VulkanDevice> and call destroy_vulkan_buffer in a noexcept destructor. Long-lived Frame and Renderer::Impl members can stay as they are. Keep the SM-56 regression tests as the acceptance.
findings.verify_reason: The sites exist: renderer.cpp:569 and 1286 have 'VulkanBuffer has no destructor' comments with catch blocks at 608/1370, and there are texture_factory staging catches. SM-56 excluded 'a general owner framework' from its own scope only. SM-53 gave a keep verdict on file placement and did not decide against RAII, so a new story is legitimate. It is a design proposal. The four sites are currently correct and covered by SM-56's regression tests, so medium is inflated.

themes.name: Build, CI and remaining tools
themes.desc:
Problems in CMake, workflows and non-Python tools:
- CMake: probe hashes are computed at configure time, input backends are not validated, CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS does not travel with labrador_settings, content-copy and page-test commands repeat, shader helpers duplicate, and PHILOSOPHY.md is re-read per token.
- Workflows: the NVDA step can hide npm failures and is unpinned, setup steps are copied into five jobs, timeouts are missing or too short (master-watch), and comments are stale or historical, including the WIC claims, the null preset labels and the whitespace scope.
- Tool scripts: flash_check's verdict contradicts its recorded decision, PNG reads are unchecked, check_live crashes, PowerShell paths and GDI disposal are wrong, and pacing literals and the geometry test are duplicated.
themes.story: Make the CI and workflow correctness fixes first (NVDA step, timeouts, a composite setup action). Any job rename needs the owner's branch-protection update. Then fix the CMake build behaviour (probe hashes, input backend refusal, extensions on the target, with a CHANGES entry for settings.cmake). Then fix the tool bugs (flash_check verdict, PNG size, check_live, hold_key). The comment corrections, including the WIC to lodepng ones, go last. Run the standalone lint checks and the Node flash, pacing and bundle suites.

findings.title: The NVDA install step can hide a failed npm ci or npm install, and its packages are unpinned
findings.evidence:
- name: Install Guidepup and NVDA
        run: |
          npm ci
          npm install --no-save @guidepup/guidepup @guidepup/setup
          npx guidepup setup --ci
          npx guidepup install nvda
findings.why: On windows-latest this run block uses pwsh, and pwsh only returns the last native command's exit code. A failing `npm ci` or `npm install` is therefore ignored whenever the later commands succeed. ci.yml handles the same problem by checking `$LASTEXITCODE` explicitly between commands (lines 207-216). The `--no-save` install also takes whatever Guidepup versions are newest, so the screen-reader job can change behaviour with no change to the repository. That is the drift the rest of CI avoids by pinning versions and SHA-256 digests.
findings.suggested_fix: Put `if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }` after each command, or split them into separate steps. Pin exact versions, for example @guidepup/guidepup@x.y.z and @guidepup/setup@x.y.z.
findings.verify_reason: website.yml:237-263 is the acceptance-screen-reader job on windows-latest with the default pwsh shell. The run block chains npm ci, npm install --no-save @guidepup/guidepup @guidepup/setup and two npx commands with no $LASTEXITCODE checks, so only the last exit code counts. guidepup is not in website/package.json, so the versions are unpinned.

findings.title: Flash check's verdict and exit status use the concurrent count, but the recorded decision says the pixel bound is the verdict
findings.evidence: flash_check.mjs:53 "- The concurrent count is the definition, and is the verdict." and :63 "This rule is the one the result rests on"; :458 `passes: concurrent.transitions <= 2 * MAX_FLASHES,`; :519 `passes: general.passes && red.passes,`; :597-599 prints "Passes WCAG 2.3.1: no window has more than ${MAX_FLASHES} concurrent flashes." and :600 `return result.passes ? 0 : 1;`. Against that, samples/linesweeper/README.md:796 "they are held to its strict reading: any pixels in the field flickering at any time in the second count together. That is the owner's decision of 2026-10-13", :810 "The strict reading is the one taken." and :887 "the tool reports the concurrent count beside the pixel bound; the pixel bound is the verdict." flash_check.test.mjs:72-90, 'flashes that are not concurrent fail the pixel bound and not the count', asserts `result.passes === true` with `bound.transitions === 8`.
findings.why: The tool's exit code, its final verdict line and its header contract all follow the loose reading that the owner rejected. A frame sequence that fails the pixel bound but passes the concurrent count (the test fixture at :72 is one) exits 0 and prints "Passes WCAG 2.3.1". A maintainer or CI step that trusts the exit status would accept bursts the documented policy refuses, and the header tells a reviewer to argue with the wrong rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Base `passes` and the exit status on the pixel bound (`bound.transitions <= 2 * MAX_FLASHES`) and report the concurrent count as the diagnostic. Rewrite the TWO COUNTS header so the pixel bound is the verdict, matching samples/linesweeper/README.md. Update the test at :72 so it expects `passes === false`.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed contradiction: flash_check.mjs:53 says the concurrent count is the verdict, :458 bases `passes` on concurrent.transitions, and :597-600 print 'Passes WCAG 2.3.1' and return 0 on that basis. The flash_check.test.mjs:72-90 fixture asserts passes===true with bound.transitions===8. samples/linesweeper/README.md says 'The strict reading is the one taken' and 'the pixel bound is the verdict'. git log shows the README wording came from 8c69272 'Calm LineSweeper's top-out by default, on the strict reading', a later commit than the tool's 1677547, and the tool was not updated. This is not in docs/code-hygiene.md, which only lists the file as a size 'keep', or in TODO. I lowered the severity because nothing automated uses the exit code: no CI or tools script calls flash_check.mjs except its own test suite. The harm is a misleading verdict line and header for a human operator, not accepted bursts in CI.

findings.title: Comments claim golden_image.cpp / RenderPixelTests use WIC; they use lodepng
findings.evidence: png_file.cpp:80-81 "handed a bitmap that says what it holds and WIC converts if it has to - the same arrangement golden_image.cpp makes, for its reason." tools/linesweeper_capture/CMakeLists.txt:33 "# The in-box PNG codec, as RenderPixelTests links it for its golden set." But tests/render/golden_image.cpp:4 has `#include <lodepng.h>` and :214 `lodepng::encode(...)`. A repo-wide grep finds `windowscodecs` only in samples/collision, samples/local_multiplayer and this target, not in tests/render/CMakeLists.txt.
findings.why: Both comments use a precedent that no longer exists to justify a design choice. Anyone following the cross-reference to golden_image.cpp finds a different codec and no SetPixelFormat arrangement at all.
