findings.suggested_fix: Drop the references to golden_image.cpp and RenderPixelTests and state the WIC behaviour on its own terms, or resolve this together with the png_file.h finding by moving the tool to lodepng.
findings.verify_reason: png_file.cpp:80-81 says 'the same arrangement golden_image.cpp makes', but golden_image.cpp:209-215 encodes with lodepng::encode and has no WIC SetPixelFormat arrangement. tools/linesweeper_capture/CMakeLists.txt:33 says windowscodecs is linked 'as RenderPixelTests links it'. tests/render/CMakeLists.txt links lodepng, and outside out/ a grep finds windowscodecs only in samples/collision, samples/local_multiplayer and this tool. Both cross-references are false.

findings.title: emsdk manager is cloned from the head of its default branch although the comment calls the toolchain pinned
findings.evidence:
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/emscripten-core/emsdk.git C:\emsdk
... (line 6-11) "the tools to do it are git and the SDK itself, and a build that can be done with those should not add a supply chain to do it. The version is pinned because it is the one this build was proven on"
findings.why: Only EMSDK_VERSION is pinned. The emsdk.py/emsdk.bat scripts that run with the job's permissions, and their release-tag table, are whatever the default branch holds on the day the cache misses. The same commit can therefore install differently, or break, on two runs, and the comment's claim that nothing outside git and the SDK is trusted to move is false. Because the cache key is emsdk-<version>-<os>, the change surfaces only when the key misses.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin the manager: clone and then `git -C C:\emsdk checkout <sha>` (or fetch the emsdk tag matching EMSDK_VERSION), with the commit in ci.yml's env beside EMSDK_VERSION, and put it in the cache key.
findings.verify_reason: Line 55 does clone emsdk at --depth 1 with no commit pin, so the manager scripts and their tag table can drift. But the comment never says the manager is pinned. It says the tools are 'git and the SDK itself' and that the compiler version is pinned, and both are true: emsdk is the SDK's own manager from the same upstream. That makes this a reproducibility gap that only shows on a cache miss, not a false claim or a new supply chain.

findings.title: ccache cache path hard-codes C:\ccache instead of reading the CCACHE_DIR it says it shares with ci.yml
findings.evidence: path: C:\ccache   (comment, lines 2-3: "share its pins (EMSDK_VERSION, CCACHE_VERSION, CCACHE_SHA256, CCACHE_DIR and CCACHE_MAXSIZE in that workflow's env)"); ci.yml line 64: CCACHE_DIR: C:\ccache
findings.why: The directory ccache writes to (env CCACHE_DIR) and the directory the cache saves are two separate literals. If CCACHE_DIR in ci.yml changes, every run silently caches an empty folder and the documented minutes of savings disappear without any failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `path: ${{ env.CCACHE_DIR }}`, as the steps above already do with env.EMSDK_VERSION.
findings.verify_reason: The action's 'Cache compiled objects' step uses the literal path C:\ccache, while ci.yml:64 sets CCACHE_DIR: C:\ccache, and the header comment says CCACHE_DIR is a shared pin. The step should use env.CCACHE_DIR the way the other steps use env.EMSDK_VERSION. A change today would silently cache an empty folder.

findings.title: Workflow comments narrate history rather than current behaviour
findings.evidence:
# ARCHITECTURE said ctest runs "on a contributor's machine or in CI" while
# there was no .github/ at all. This is the CI half made true.
(also :262-263 "WHICH THIS FILE SAID UNTIL ONE JOB LOG WAS READ"; :304 "since the audio seam landed"; :308-310 "That second half is what a runner could never check before"; :386-392 "so a failed install was a green step ...")
findings.why: CONVENTIONS keeps history out of comments. These passages tell how the file came to be rather than what it does. SM-47 cleaned build-comment archaeology in compile_shaders.cmake and check_doc_citations.cmake but did not cover ci.yml.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite each passage as present-tense rationale. For example, line 386 becomes '-PassThru makes the installer's exit code observable, so a failed install fails here rather than as a misattributed VULKAN_SDK error later.' Drop the origin narratives.
findings.verify_reason: ci.yml:3-4 ('ARCHITECTURE said ... This is the CI half made true'), 262-263 ('WHICH THIS FILE SAID UNTIL ONE JOB LOG WAS READ') and 386-392 ('so a failed install was a green step') are present. They are history narrative. SM-47's targets (code-hygiene.md:150-152) do not include ci.yml.

findings.title: The env-block comment is ragged and describes only part of the block it heads
findings.evidence:
# The three browser jobs share one compiler, so they share its pins. ccache is
# ...cache shortens. Emscripten compiles every file through a Python driver and
# clang. .github/actions/emscripten installs
# both.
env:
  # Windows SDK installer and SHA-256 published at vulkan.lunarg.com/sdk/home.
  VULKAN_SDK_VERSION: ...
findings.why: The comment is about EMSDK and ccache pins but sits above an env block that starts with the Vulkan SDK and Mesa pins used by the windows matrix. The broken wrap ('installs / both') suggests an edit left half-done.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the browser paragraph down beside EMSDK_VERSION, CCACHE_* and CCACHE_DIR, rewrap it, and give the block a one-line header saying it holds the pinned tool versions and digests for all jobs.
findings.verify_reason: ci.yml:38-44: the browser/ccache paragraph wraps raggedly ('installs' / 'both.') and sits above an env block that opens with the Vulkan SDK and Mesa pins. EMSDK_VERSION and CCACHE_* come only at lines 51-54.

findings.title: Windows job comment says GL and Vulkan get no device, contradicting the same block's llvmpipe and SwiftShader paragraphs
findings.evidence:
# checkable shape is what the matrix rests on and it is unchanged: Direct3D
# gets a device on this machine, GL and Vulkan do not.

The same comment block (lines 253-260 and 281-286) says 'THE GL PRESET DRAWS ON MESA'S LLVMPIPE' and 'THE VULKAN PRESET DRAWS ON SWIFTSHADER', and RenderPixelTests is registered and required for x64-debug-gl and x64-debug-vulkan in tests/ctest_inventory.json.
findings.why: The sentence predates the software-rasteriser setup. It now states the opposite of what the job does, inside the comment that documents that job.
findings.suggested_fix: Rephrase: Direct3D gets an adapter from the runner image; GL and Vulkan get one only from the Mesa and SwiftShader drivers the steps below provide.
findings.verify_reason: ci.yml:272-274 says 'Direct3D gets a device on this machine, GL and Vulkan do not.' A reader can take it to mean natively, before the following Mesa and SwiftShader steps, which the surrounding paragraphs explain. It still sits awkwardly beside 'THE GL PRESET DRAWS ON MESA'S LLVMPIPE' in the same block, so the wording is worth fixing. It does not state the opposite of what the job does, so low.

findings.title: vswhere/vcvars and VCPKG_ROOT steps are copy-pasted into five jobs
findings.evidence:
for /f "usebackq tokens=*" %%i in (`"%ProgramFiles(x86)%\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer\vswhere.exe" -latest -products * -requires Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.x86.x64 -property installationPath`) do echo VCVARS=%%i\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat>> %GITHUB_ENV%
(identical at lines 444, 638, 866, 950, 1073; the 'Point at the runner's vcpkg' step is repeated at 358-363, 612-616, 846-850, 915-919, 1053-1057)
findings.why: The repository already uses a local composite action (.github/actions/emscripten) for shared setup. The vcvars lookup is a 200-character one-liner duplicated five times, and a change to the required component or path has to be made in five places.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a composite action, for example .github/actions/msvc-env, that exports VCPKG_ROOT, IMAGE_VERSION and VCVARS, and use it from the five Windows jobs.
findings.verify_reason: The same vswhere one-liner is at ci.yml lines 444, 638, 866, 950 and 1073, and 'Point at the runner's vcpkg' at 358, 612, 846, 915 and 1053. .github/actions/emscripten shows the composite-action precedent. code-hygiene.md's 'Keep' verdict on ci.yml is about file length, not about this duplication. The copies are stable, so low.

findings.title: master-watch's 45-minute bound is shorter than the CI jobs whose rerun it waits for
findings.evidence:
# Long enough to wait out a rerun of the slowest workflow.
    timeout-minutes: 45
(ci.yml: windows/wasm/wasm-null/wasm-consumer/consumer all `timeout-minutes: 90`, safari `needs: [changes, wasm]` adds 30 more; tools/master_watch.py wait_for_rerun loops `while True: sleep(interval)` until the rerun completes)
findings.why: master_watch.py blocks on the rerun it started, because a token-started rerun raises no workflow_run event of its own. A rerun of a failed windows or wasm job may legitimately run up to 90 minutes (cold vcpkg cache), and longer for wasm followed by safari. The watch job is then cancelled at 45 minutes, so no issue is opened or commented: the second failure goes unreported. The comment's claim is false against ci.yml's own bounds.
findings.suggested_fix: Raise timeout-minutes above the slowest rerun chain (for example 150: wasm 90 plus safari 30 plus margin). Alternatively, give wait_for_rerun its own deadline that reports 'rerun still running' as an issue comment rather than dying silently. Make the comment state the arithmetic.
findings.verify_reason: master-watch.yml:28-29 does say 45 minutes, ci.yml has several 90-minute jobs, and master_watch.py:63 wait_for_rerun loops with no deadline. But 90 is a cold-cache upper bound. A `--failed` rerun normally runs on a warm cache and takes far less. A watch job cut off at its timeout also fails as a visible red run, so the failure is not silent. The mismatch is real; 'unreported' is overstated.

findings.title: The versions:verify base expression is copied into two steps, and the job has no timeout
findings.evidence: BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/master' && !github.event.forced && github.event.before) || '' }}
findings.why: The same non-trivial expression appears at lines 114 and 135. Both steps must agree on the base, and the header comment (lines 38-43) describes it once. Separately, the `website` job (line 66) has no timeout-minutes, while every ci.yml job and the other website.yml jobs set one. ci.yml line 245 gives the reason: a stalled step should fail the check instead of holding pull requests for six hours.
findings.suggested_fix: Move BASE into the job's env (or one step's output) and reference it from both steps. Add a timeout-minutes to the website job.
findings.verify_reason: website.yml repeats the identical BASE expression in the 'Verify published versions' and 'Verify appended errata links' steps. The website job (line 66) has no timeout-minutes, while the other jobs set 45, 30 and 30 (lines 155, 192, 241).

findings.title: Build comments tell the history of earlier wording instead of the current contract
findings.evidence:
# AND EVERY REAL TARGET DEPENDS ON IT, which ALL alone did not give. ... none of those is the default build, and every one of them skipped the
# check while this file said "runs on every build"
# (docs/review/gpt6/README.md, G6-10).
findings.why: CONVENTIONS calls for removing archaeology, and SM-47 covered only five files. Narratives about earlier wording remain here and in .github/workflows/ci.yml:3-4 ('ARCHITECTURE said ctest runs ... while there was no .github/ at all. This is the CI half made true.') and ci.yml:262-263 ('WHICH THIS FILE SAID UNTIL ONE JOB LOG WAS READ'). The constraint is worth keeping; the account of what the file used to say is not.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite each comment as the present-tense reason (e.g. 'ALL alone covers only the default build; this dependency covers targeted and consumer builds') and drop the earlier-wording narrative and review citation.
findings.verify_reason: CMakeLists.txt:30-35 says 'skipped the check while this file said "runs on every build" (docs/review/gpt6/README.md, G6-10)'. ci.yml:3-4 says 'ARCHITECTURE said ctest runs ... This is the CI half made true', and ci.yml:262-263 says 'WHICH THIS FILE SAID UNTIL ONE JOB LOG WAS READ'. CONVENTIONS.md:161 defines archaeology for removal. SM-47's closed target list (code-hygiene.md:150-152) covers neither file, so the finding is not already tracked.

findings.title: Citation-check rationale omits engine/, which the check reads and a consumer builds
findings.evidence:
# build failure for a section number this repository moved, and the files
    # it reads are tests/, samples/, bench/ and tools/, none of which a
    # consumer builds.
(cmake/check_doc_citations.cmake:17-22 globs "${REPO_DIR}/engine/*.h" "${REPO_DIR}/engine/*.cpp" first)
findings.why: The argument for keeping the check top-level only rests on a file list that leaves out engine/. engine/ is the one folder the check reads that a consumer does compile, so the stated rationale is false. The real reason is that the check guards this repository's prose, not the consumer's build.
findings.suggested_fix: List engine/ among the folders read, and restate the reason without the 'none of which a consumer builds' claim. For example: a consumer should not fail its build over this repository's document renames.
findings.verify_reason: CMakeLists.txt:59-61 lists only tests/, samples/, bench/ and tools/. cmake/check_doc_citations.cmake:17-18 globs engine/*.h and engine/*.cpp first, and engine/ is built by consumers. The rationale is false as written, but the decision itself (top-level only) still stands, so low.

findings.title: Presets repeat blocks that inheritance could hold once: wasm-base copies base's fields, and 12 test presets repeat the same output block
findings.evidence: "name": "wasm-base", "hidden": true, "generator": "Ninja", "binaryDir": "${sourceDir}/out/build/${presetName}", "installDir": "${sourceDir}/out/install/${presetName}", "toolchainFile": "$env{VCPKG_ROOT}/scripts/buildsystems/vcpkg.cmake" ... and twelve times: "output": { "outputOnFailure": true }
findings.why: The generator, binaryDir, installDir and vcpkg toolchain lines are written twice, in base and wasm-base. The output block is written in all 12 test presets, and the backend cacheVariables are repeated in each Debug/Release pair. A change to the build layout or the toolchain must be made in two places, and a new test preset can silently lose outputOnFailure.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a hidden `common` configure preset (generator, binaryDir, installDir, toolchainFile) that both base (adding the Windows condition and architecture) and wasm-base inherit. Add a hidden test preset carrying `output` that the others inherit. Optionally add hidden backend mixins (d3d12, gl, vulkan, null) combined with debug/release through multiple `inherits`.
findings.verify_reason: The duplication is real: wasm-base repeats base's generator, binaryDir, installDir and toolchainFile, and outputOnFailure appears 12 times. It is four declarative lines in one JSON file, though, and the copies sit beside each other. That is a cosmetic config tidy-up, not medium.

findings.title: D3D12 probe source hashes are computed at configure time and go stale after an edit
findings.evidence:
file(SHA256 "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../engine/render/d3d12/renderer.cpp"
            descriptor_renderer_sha256)
...
                LABRADOR_DESCRIPTOR_RENDERER_SHA256="${descriptor_renderer_sha256}"
                LABRADOR_DESCRIPTOR_DEVICE_SHA256="${descriptor_device_sha256}"
findings.why: bench/d3d12_descriptor_count_main.cpp:165 and bench/d3d12_descriptor_query_probe.cpp:106-108 print these values as provenance for the source that was measured. file(SHA256) runs only at configure, and neither file is registered as a configure dependency (git grep CMAKE_CONFIGURE_DEPENDS finds nothing in the repo). So if renderer.cpp or device_resources.cpp is edited and then rebuilt without a reconfigure, the probe compiles the new code but still prints the old hash. That is false evidence.
findings.suggested_fix: Add both files with set_property(DIRECTORY APPEND PROPERTY CMAKE_CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ...) so an edit triggers a reconfigure. Alternatively, compute the hashes in a build-time custom command that writes a generated header.
findings.verify_reason: bench/CMakeLists.txt:121-132 has file(SHA256) on d3d12 renderer.cpp/device_resources.cpp feeding compile definitions, and git grep finds CONFIGURE_DEPENDS only in tests/render/CMakeLists.txt:272 (a GLOB), so an edit without a reconfigure leaves the printed hash stale. The defect is real. It affects only the optional D3D12 investigation probes, which the comment just above says are 'outside ALL and ctest', so it is low, not medium.

findings.title: PHILOSOPHY.md is re-read for every T-number token on every build
findings.evidence:
if(word MATCHES "^T([0-9]+)$")
                set(number "${CMAKE_MATCH_1}")
                file(STRINGS "${REPO_DIR}/docs/design/PHILOSOPHY.md" heading
                    REGEX "^### T${number}\\. ")
findings.why: This script is an ALL target and a dependency of labrador_settings (root CMakeLists.txt:62-72), so it runs on every top-level build. For each T-token in a comment line of every engine/sample/test/bench/tools source, it reads the whole of PHILOSOPHY.md from disk again. The set of valid T headings is constant and could be read once.
findings.suggested_fix: Before the source loop, read the '^### T[0-9]+\. ' headings once into a list of valid numbers, then test each token with `if(number IN_LIST valid_tradeoffs)`.
findings.verify_reason: cmake/check_doc_citations.cmake, in the trade-offs loop (about 114-125), calls file(STRINGS PHILOSOPHY.md REGEX "^### T${number}\. ") inside the per-word loop for every T-token. It is a real but trivial inefficiency.

findings.title: CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS is a directory variable, not part of labrador_settings, so consumer targets don't get it
findings.evidence:
# The standard language, not a vendor's dialect of it: CMake otherwise asks
# clang for gnu++20. MSVC has no dialect to ask for, and /permissive- below is
# the same refusal in its spelling.
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)
findings.why: The file header says 'every real target links labrador_settings, so compiler strictness lives in exactly one place'. This setting, though, is a variable in the engine's directory scope. A game that uses add_subdirectory (website/src/walkthrough/root-CMakeLists.txt) and links labrador_settings still compiles its own targets as gnu++20 under clang/Emscripten. CHANGES.md:959 records this, but the source comment presents it as part of the shared settings.
findings.suggested_fix: Say in the comment that this applies only to targets in this tree and that a consumer has to set it itself. Alternatively, add it to the walkthrough's root CMakeLists so the template carries the same rule.
findings.verify_reason: cmake/settings.cmake:9-12 sets CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF as a directory-scope variable. The file's header says strictness lives in labrador_settings. CHANGES.md:959 records that an add_subdirectory consumer does not inherit it, but the source comment does not say so. The point is real and minor.

findings.title: Configure never refuses the input backend on the wrong platform, unlike render and audio
findings.evidence:
# The input backend, a third axis chosen the same way.
...
if(LABRADOR_INPUT_BACKEND STREQUAL "xinput")
    target_sources(LabradorEngine PRIVATE
        input/xinput/gamepad_reader.cpp
findings.why: The render block (lines 137-142) and the audio block (lines 324-332) both refuse a backend on a platform that lacks its API, by name at configure time. Line 313 says why: 'Each platform API is refused where it does not exist'. The input block claims to be 'chosen the same way' but has no such guard. With LABRADOR_INPUT_BACKEND=xinput under Emscripten, the first error is an unnamed find_package(directxtk) failure (vcpkg.json limits directxtk to windows). With web on native, the first error is a missing emscripten header at compile time. Both are the late, misattributed failures that T5/T6 and the neighbouring blocks exist to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the matching guard: if(EMSCRIPTEN AND LABRADOR_INPUT_BACKEND STREQUAL "xinput") FATAL_ERROR naming web, and if(NOT EMSCRIPTEN AND LABRADOR_INPUT_BACKEND STREQUAL "web") FATAL_ERROR naming xinput. Update AGENTS.md's list of what configure refuses.
findings.verify_reason: engine/CMakeLists.txt does refuse render (EMSCRIPTEN + d3d11/d3d12/vulkan) and audio (xaudio2 in a browser, webaudio on native), and the input block (about lines 339-370) has only the unknown-name FATAL_ERROR, so the asymmetry is real. It only matters when someone explicitly sets a wrong cache value: the defaults are right, and a later failure still stops the build. AGENTS.md lists only render and audio refusals, so no doc is made false. Low.

findings.title: The comment over PROJECT_NAME lists the engine's packages but omits directxtk

Every package the engine` / `# names: lodepng decodes PNG textures and doctest runs the game's own tests.` / `PROJECT_NAME = "mygame"`. vcpkg.json's dependencies are `directxtk` (feature xaudio2redist, windows), `doctest` and `lodepng`, and derived_manifest (:87) copies all of them.

findings.title: readPng does not check the inflated size, so a short image stream reads as black pixels
findings.why: If the decompressed data is shorter than height * (stride + 1), `raw[source + x]` is undefined. `undefined + n` is NaN, and `NaN & 0xff` is 0, so missing rows become zeros with no error. A PNG without IHDR gives width = height = 0 and an empty frame, which the analyser then refuses only by its size check. For a tool whose verdict is an accessibility claim, a malformed frame should be refused (exit 2), not analysed as dark.
findings.suggested_fix: After inflating, throw when `width === 0` or when `raw.length !== height * (stride + 1)`, naming the file, in the same way the IHDR format check does.
findings.verify_reason: flash_check.mjs:137-166: after inflateSync there is no check of raw.length against height*(stride+1), and no check for a missing IHDR (width=height=0). A short but well-formed zlib stream would read undefined bytes as 0. A truncated zlib stream would already throw in inflateSync, so the silent case needs a malformed encoder. Low.

findings.title: Save-Client's GDI objects are disposed only on the success path
findings.evidence:
$bitmap = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap $rect.Right, $rect.Bottom
    $graphics = [System.Drawing.Graphics]::FromImage($bitmap)
    $graphics.CopyFromScreen($origin.X, $origin.Y, 0, 0, $bitmap.Size)
    $bitmap.Save($path, [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png)
    $graphics.Dispose()
    $bitmap.Dispose()
findings.why: With $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop', a failure in CopyFromScreen or Save skips both Dispose calls. The GetClientRect and ClientToScreen return values are also discarded with [void]. A failed GetClientRect produces a 0x0 Bitmap, and the constructor throws an unhelpful 'Parameter is not valid' instead of naming the window problem.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the body in try/finally and dispose there. Check GetClientRect's result and throw 'Could not read the game window's client area' when it is false.
findings.verify_reason: Lines 97-108 are as quoted: Dispose is on the success path only, and GetClientRect/ClientToScreen are voided. But with ErrorActionPreference Stop, a failure ends this one-shot script, so the leaked GDI handles are moot. Only the unhelpful 0x0 'Parameter is not valid' message has any value. Minor.

findings.title: Bitmap.Save receives a path relative to PowerShell's location, but .NET resolves it against the process directory
findings.evidence: $bitmap.Save($path, [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png)  -- with $path = (Join-Path $OutDirectory 'before.png') and $OutDirectory defaulting to 'out\input-drive'
findings.why: New-Item creates the folder relative to PowerShell's current location. Bitmap.Save resolves the same relative path against [Environment]::CurrentDirectory, which PowerShell does not update on Set-Location. If the script is invoked with `&` or dot-sourced from a session that has changed directory, the folder is created in one place and Save then fails with a generic GDI+ error or writes elsewhere. The documented `powershell -File` form works only because it starts a fresh process.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the output folder once after creating it, with `$OutDirectory = (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $OutDirectory).Path`, and pass absolute paths to Save-Client.
findings.verify_reason: hold_key.ps1:24 defaults to the relative 'out\input-drive'. Line 110 creates it with New-Item (PowerShell's location), and lines 105/133/139 pass the relative Join-Path to .NET Bitmap.Save (the process directory). This is a known PowerShell pitfall, and the documented -File usage avoids it. Low.

findings.title: The capture tool's comment says RenderPixelTests links WIC, but it uses lodepng
findings.evidence:
# The in-box PNG codec, as RenderPixelTests links it for its golden set.
        windowscodecs
findings.why: tests/render/CMakeLists.txt:102-104 says 'lodepng is the golden set's codec, on every platform', and RenderPixelTests links lodepng, not windowscodecs. A git grep for windowscodecs/wincodec in tests/render finds nothing. So the comment justifies a dependency by pointing at a precedent that no longer exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the comparison and state only the current reason: the capture writes PNGs through WIC (png_file.cpp).
findings.verify_reason: The file is only 63 lines long. The comment is at tools/linesweeper_capture/CMakeLists.txt:33-34, not 168-169, and it reads 'The in-box PNG codec, as RenderPixelTests links it for its golden set.' followed by windowscodecs. tests/render/CMakeLists.txt links lodepng and calls it the golden set's codec, and no windowscodecs is linked there, so the comment is stale. Severity is low for a stale comment. png_file.h:20 should also be checked for the same stale comparison.

findings.title: The rationale for WIC over lodepng is false now that the engine itself links lodepng
findings.evidence: "THROUGH WIC, the codec Windows already has, so this costs no dependency (T9): the tool is Windows-only, which is why it does not take the lodepng tests/render/golden_image.cpp needs to read the golden set in a browser as well." But vcpkg.json lists "lodepng", engine/CMakeLists.txt:407 has `find_package(lodepng CONFIG REQUIRED)` with `PRIVATE labrador_settings lodepng`, and engine/render/png_file.h already provides engine-side PNG decoding, which tests/render/golden_image.cpp:186-187 cites as "the same port".
findings.why: The comment justifies a second, Windows-only PNG writer plus a `windowscodecs` link by avoiding a dependency the build already pays for through LabradorEngine. A maintainer cannot tell whether the WIC writer is still deliberate, or whether it could share lodepng and drop the platform-specific code. The paragraph is also wrapped mid-sentence: "Lossless" sits alone at the end of line 24.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-justify or retire the WIC writer. Either state the real reason it stays (for example, the engine links lodepng PRIVATE and the tool should not reach into it), or encode with lodepng and remove `windowscodecs` from the target. Rewrap the paragraph.
findings.verify_reason: png_file.h:18-26 says WIC 'costs no dependency (T9)', and that is still true: the tool would have to add its own find_package and link to use lodepng, because engine/CMakeLists.txt:411 links lodepng PRIVATE and the engine's png_file.h only decodes. The comment does not claim the build lacks lodepng. It says lodepng is what golden_image.cpp needs for the browser, which is accurate. The rationale is weaker than it was but not false. The mid-sentence wrap ('Lossless' alone at the end of line 24) is real and cosmetic.

findings.title: camelCase and snake_case identifiers mixed in one file; one-use temporaries
findings.evidence: Functions and options are snake_case (`parse_arguments`, `verify_bundle`, `brotli_size`, `notice_text`, `options['build-type']`, `build_type`), but :219-227 use camelCase: `const gitRoot = ...`, `const sameRoot = ...`, `const sourceCommit = git('rev-parse', '--verify', 'HEAD');`, `const sourceDirty = ...;` then `commit = sourceCommit; dirty = sourceDirty;`. The sibling check_live.mjs is snake_case throughout (`page_url`, `build_response`, `expect_commit`).
findings.why: Within one script and its sibling, the same kind of local is named two ways. sourceCommit and sourceDirty exist only to be copied into the outer variables on the next line.
findings.suggested_fix: Use snake_case (`git_root`, `same_root`) to match the rest of the file and check_live.mjs, and assign `commit` and `dirty` directly from the git calls.
findings.verify_reason: The camelCase locals at bundle.mjs:219-225 (gitRoot, sameRoot, sourceCommit, sourceDirty) are real, and the file's other locals are snake_case, so the naming inconsistency stands. The 'one-use temporaries' part and its fix are wrong. Computing both git results before assigning commit and dirty means a throw from the second call, caught at :229, leaves both at 'unknown'/null instead of a commit with no dirty flag. Assigning directly would lose that. Only the rename is valid.

findings.title: The bare catch drops the reason a checkout's commit could not be read
findings.why: The try also covers cases that are not 'not a checkout': `.git` exists and is the same root, but git is missing from PATH, the repository is corrupt, or HEAD is unborn. In each case BUILD.json silently records `commit: "unknown", dirty: null`. The failure only shows up later, when `--verify` or check_live refuses the bundle with 'commit must be a full Git revision', and the cause is gone. A non-checkout is already handled without an exception by the `existsSync(join(repository, '.git'))` branch.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the unknown fallback, but write the error to stderr: `catch (error) { process.stderr.write(`bundle: commit unknown: ${error.message}\n`); }`. Alternatively, narrow the try to the cases that are expected.
findings.verify_reason: bundle.mjs:229-232 has a bare catch around realpathSync and git rev-parse/status. A missing git or a corrupt or unborn repository silently gives commit 'unknown'. The non-checkout case is handled by the existsSync branch. The effect is lost diagnostics only, since --verify and check_live still refuse the bundle later. Low.

findings.title: An unknown Content-Encoding on an identity fetch crashes the run instead of failing one check
findings.evidence: get(): `: coding === 'identity' ? wire : null;` then answers with body null. In the SERVED loop, outside any attempt(): `served[name] = plain.body;` ... `check(..., brotli.body?.equals(plain.body) === true, `${brotli.body?.length ?? 'undecodable'} against ${plain.body.length} bytes`)` and `const digest = sha256(plain.body);`
findings.why: The header says "A request that cannot be made at all is a FAIL of that check, not a crash", and every check runs. If a server answers the Accept-Encoding: identity request with a coding get() does not decode (for example zstd), plain.body is null. `plain.body.length` and `sha256(null)` then throw a TypeError at top level, so the run dies with a stack trace and writes no dated record. The page path already guards with `page.body?.`, but this loop does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Have get() refuse (reject) an unrecognised coding, so attempt() records it as a FAIL. Alternatively, treat `plain.body === null` in the loop as a failed check and `continue`.
findings.verify_reason: check_live.mjs is 256 lines, so 358-479 is wrong. The code is real: get() line 98 sets body null for an unknown coding, and lines 204-225 use plain.body.length and sha256(plain.body) outside attempt(), so a null body would throw at top level. It only happens when a server answers an explicit Accept-Encoding: identity request with an undecodable coding, which is a protocol violation and unlikely from the live host. Real, but low.

findings.title: `width` names the row stride of the sample buffer, in a function that also uses canvas.width and box.width
findings.evidence: page.js:18 `const width = 15;`, used as `const base = index * width;` (:82) and `const base = count++ * width;` (:169), while the same closure compares `canvas.width`, `box.width` and `geometry.drawing_buffer[0]`.
findings.why: Inside a geometry-tracking closure, `width` reads as a pixel width. It is actually the number of float fields per engine row, and the 15 must match the field offsets written at :170-184 and read at :83-91.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename it to `row_fields` (or `fields_per_row`) and note that it counts the offsets written in labradorPacingFrame.
findings.verify_reason: page.js:18 `const width = 15;` is the number of fields per row, used at :82 and :169 as `index * width`. The same closure compares canvas.width, box.width and drawing_buffer at :63-75, so the name is easy to misread. This is a minor naming issue.

findings.title: updateGeometry repeats its unchanged-geometry comparison twice
findings.evidence:
if (!geometryDirty && geometry && canvas.width === geometry.drawing_buffer[0] &&
			canvas.height === geometry.drawing_buffer[1] && devicePixelRatio === geometry.dpr &&
			innerWidth === geometry.viewport_css[0] && innerHeight === geometry.viewport_css[1]) return;
...
		if (geometry && canvas.width === geometry.drawing_buffer[0] &&
			canvas.height === geometry.drawing_buffer[1] && devicePixelRatio === geometry.dpr &&
			innerWidth === geometry.viewport_css[0] && innerHeight === geometry.viewport_css[1] &&
findings.why: The second test is the first one plus the canvas box. Adding a field to the geometry record means editing both expressions identically. If they drift apart, a geometry change can stop starting a new segment, which corrupts what analyse.mjs counts as contiguous.
findings.suggested_fix: Factor out `const sameBuffer = () => geometry && canvas.width === ... && innerHeight === geometry.viewport_css[1];` and use `sameBuffer() && box.width === ... && box.height === ...` for the second test.
findings.verify_reason: page.js is 203 lines. updateGeometry at lines 63-71 repeats the five-field comparison, and the second test only adds the canvas box. Low duplication as described, at the corrected line.

findings.title: The 9,600-particle fixture count is hard-coded throughout the JS instruments
findings.evidence: page_input.mjs:352 `snapshot[10] === 9600 && snapshot[11] === 0`, :409 `burst.live_particles === 9600`, :414 `progress.marked.elements >= 9600 * 6`, :419; tools/web_pacing/page.js:229 `counts_match: marked.live_particles === 9600 && marked.dropped_particles === 0`
findings.why: C++ names this value once, as `pacing_particle_count` (samples/linesweeper/web/pacing_fixture.h:12) and `expected_particles` (bench/linesweeper_frame_result.h:14). The JS side repeats the literal six times across two files, together with positional snapshot indices 9/10/11 that must match the argument order in page.js. If the fixture changes, the JS checks silently become wrong unless every literal is found.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare `const FIXTURE_PARTICLES = 9600; // pacing_fixture.h pacing_particle_count` once in each file, and name the snapshot indices (for example `const MARKER = 9, LIVE = 10, DROPPED = 11`), so the C++ owner is cited in one place.
findings.verify_reason: page_input.mjs is about 130 lines, so the cited 352-419 is wrong. The literal 9600 appears at page_input.mjs:26 (with snapshot[9]/[10]/[11]), 83, 88, 93 and 124, and at page.js:106 (not 229). Repeated magic literal, low.

findings.title: Three page drivers each retry the same navigation race with a different regex
findings.evidence: tools/web_pacing/page_input.mjs:112 `/Execution context was destroyed|Cannot find context with specified id/`; tools/save_check/reload.mjs:15 `/Execution context was destroyed|Cannot find context|Inspected target navigated/`; tests/render/web/bundle_page.mjs:189 `/Execution context was destroyed|Cannot find (?:default execution context|context with specified id)/`
findings.why: All three drivers handle the same DevTools errors around a navigation, but they disagree on which messages are benign. page_input.mjs does not tolerate 'Cannot find default execution context' or 'Inspected target navigated', which the other two accept. A Chrome that reports the race with one of those messages fails the Release LineSweeperPacingPageTests intermittently. The next driver will copy one of the three regexes at random.
findings.suggested_fix: Export one `is_navigation_race(error)` predicate, or a `poll_across_navigation(evaluate, expression)` helper, from run_page.mjs, or pass it in through page_api. Use it in all three drivers.
findings.verify_reason: The three regexes are present as quoted and do differ (page_input.mjs:112, reload.mjs:15, bundle_page.mjs:189). The claim that page_input fails the Release pacing test intermittently is speculation: no failure is cited. A shared predicate is a fair low-severity cleanup.

themes.name: Python tooling hygiene
themes.desc: There are six git subprocess wrappers with different hardening, and a commit walk copied between checkers. Two JUnit parsers and preset executors apply different acceptance rules, and the wasm registration lists diverge from ci_gap_report and ctest_inventory. Bugs: master_watch has an unreachable rerun branch, analyze returns the wrong exit status, and DPI scans miscount. Other problems: private imports across modules, positional parallel tuples, repeated literals and nvidia-smi queries, unused exports and imports, test loader boilerplate copied 14 times, and incident history in docstrings.
themes.story: Add a single tools/_git.py and a single JUnit/preset-sweep helper. Derive verify_changes' wasm entries from ctest_inventory.json. Fix master_watch, the analyze exit code and the DPI scan as behaviour commits with tests. Then do the tools/tests loader consolidation and docstring cleanup. Run the offline Python suites.

findings.title: The 'rerun did not record a new attempt' branch can never run, and the case it names spins until the job times out
findings.why: wait_for_rerun returns only when the attempt number has risen above the first one. decide() returns "rerun" only for attempt 1, so lines 77-78 can never run. A rerun that never records a new attempt is exactly what that branch describes. In that case the unbounded `while True` loop keeps polling `gh run view` every 30 s until master-watch.yml's 45-minute timeout kills the job, with no message. The code claims to handle a failure it actually turns into a silent timeout.
findings.suggested_fix: Bound wait_for_rerun with a deadline or a maximum number of polls. On expiry, return the run unchanged or raise a clear error, so the 'did not record a new attempt' outcome can actually happen. Then add a FakeGh case where the views never show a higher attempt.
findings.verify_reason: master_watch.py:60-78: wait_for_rerun loops `while True` and only returns when state['attempt'] > run_attempt, so the returned run has attempt>=2 and decide() cannot return 'rerun'; lines 77-78 are unreachable, and a rerun that never records a new attempt polls until the workflow timeout.

findings.title: Required wasm browser registrations are listed separately from ci_gap_report and ctest_inventory.json, and the lists already differ
findings.evidence:
verify_changes.py:239 `browser_tests = (["RenderPixelTests", "RenderPixelTestsWithoutS3tc", "RenderContextLossTests",
                          "WebWindowTests", *pages, "LineSweeperBundlePageTests"] if wasm and render == "gl" else [])` where `pages` only matches `labrador_sample_page_test(` calls. ci_gap_report.py:41 `BROWSER_TESTS = (... "ComponentsPageTests", "ComponentsPointerPageTests", ...)`. CMakeLists.txt:242 registers ComponentsPointerPageTests with a plain `add_test(NAME ComponentsPointerPageTests`, so the planner never requires it. Neither tool reads tests/ctest_inventory.json, which AGENTS.md names as the list each configuration must register.
findings.why: There are three owners of one fact: which browser tests a Chromium-equipped wasm build must register. The planner already omits ComponentsPointerPageTests, so `verify_changes --execute` would accept a wasm-debug sweep that silently dropped it. ci_gap_report's tuple has no drift test against CMakeLists or the inventory.
findings.suggested_fix: Make one owner. Either derive both lists from tests/ctest_inventory.json (adding a wasm-debug or Chromium-required grouping there if needed), or have both tools share one module-level list with a test that checks it against the inventory and CMakeLists.txt's add_test/labrador_sample_page_test names.
findings.verify_reason: verify_changes.py:153 takes pages only from `labrador_sample_page_test(` calls, and line 240 builds browser_tests from those pages. CMakeLists.txt:242 registers ComponentsPointerPageTests with a plain add_test, so the planner never requires it. ci_gap_report.py:40-45 keeps its own BROWSER_TESTS, which does include it. Neither tool reads ctest_inventory.json, and test_ci_gap_report only feeds BROWSER_TESTS back to itself, with no drift check.

findings.title: Commit-walk and diff-tree code copied from check_golden_reviews even though the module already imports it
findings.evidence:
check_changes_rule.py:53 `def changed_paths(repository, commit, parents):
    if len(parents) > 1:
        raise CheckError(f"{commit} is a merge commit; merge diffs are unsupported, not treated as empty")
    revisions = [parents[0], commit] if parents else ["--root", commit]` and lines 70-75 `contents = golden.git(repository, "cat-file", "commit", commit)
        headers, separator, message_bytes = contents.partition(b"\n\n")
        ... parents = [line[len(b"parent "):].decode("ascii") ...]`. Both are near-verbatim copies of check_golden_reviews.py:79-82 (changed_goldens) and 95-101 (missing_reviews).
findings.why: The commit-parent parsing and the merge-commit refusal are a policy that both lint checks must apply identically. With two copies, a fix to one (say, a signed-commit header edge case or the error wording) will not reach the other.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `commit_parts(repository, commit) -> (parents, message_bytes)` and `changed_paths(repository, commit, parents, *pathspec)` to check_golden_reviews (or the shared Git helper suggested above), and call them from both checkers.
findings.verify_reason: check_changes_rule.py:53-58 (changed_paths) and 70-75 (cat-file parent parsing) are near-verbatim copies of check_golden_reviews.py:79-82 and 95-101, and the module already imports golden. Confirmed, but the copies are about ten lines and stable, so this is low.

findings.title: A folder scan counts a malformed GUI program as a skipped console program
findings.why: CI runs `python tools\check_dpi_manifest.py out\build\<preset>\samples`. If a sample .exe is truncated or otherwise unreadable as a PE image, its error is swallowed and it is reported as "console programs skipped". The check still passes as long as one other GUI program is found. In the same loop, an OSError from read_bytes is not caught and ends the run with a traceback instead of a named failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Return unparsable images separately (for example `found, skipped, unreadable`) and have check_paths report each one through `complain` and fail. Catch OSError at the same point so it produces a named failure.
findings.verify_reason: check_dpi_manifest.py:144-157 catches ManifestError, sets subsystem None and counts the file as skipped; an OSError from read_bytes propagates as a traceback. Both claims hold. A truncated sample exe in CI's build output would also fail the smoke and page tests, so silent harm is unlikely. Low.

findings.title: Six separate git subprocess wrappers in tools/ with inconsistent hardening
findings.evidence: tools/check_golden_reviews.py:25 `def git(repository, *arguments) -> bytes` (sets GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS/GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT, `--no-lazy-fetch --no-replace-objects`, keeps ambient GIT_* env); tools/check_demo_lag.py:27 `def git(repository, *arguments, accepted=...)` (strips every GIT_* variable, nulls global/system config and grafts: "Ambient Git routing/configuration must not substitute another checkout..."); tools/ci_tested_tree.py:141 `def run_git(*arguments)` (plain `["git", *arguments]`); tools/cloud_performance/release.py:32 `def _git(root, *arguments)`; tools/consumer_check/starter_zip.py:47 `def git(engine, *arguments)`; tools/ci_gap_report.py:135 `git_state` with its own lambda runner. tools/consumer_check/assemble.py:48 `tree_files` and cloud_performance/release.py:52 `source_files` both run the same `ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard` listing.
findings.why: check_demo_lag decided that ambient GIT_DIR/GIT_* variables and replace refs must not redirect a check. check_golden_reviews (a required CI lint) and check_changes_rule (which reuses it) still honour ambient GIT_* routing. The hardening policy depends on which script you read, and each new tool picks a pattern at random.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a tools/git_local.py with one hardened `git(repository, *args, accepted=(0,), text=False)` (check_demo_lag's environment scrubbing plus golden's flags) and a `tree_files(root)` listing. Have the six call sites use it. Keep the injectable runners in tests by passing the function.
findings.verify_reason: Wrappers confirmed at check_golden_reviews.py:25, check_demo_lag.py:27 (scrubs GIT_* and nulls global/system config and grafts), ci_tested_tree.py:141, cloud_performance/release.py:32, starter_zip.py:47 and ci_gap_report.py:135, plus duplicate ls-files listings in assemble.py:48 and release.py:52. The hardening is inconsistent, but the tools have different needs: release and consumer scripts run against the local checkout, and CI sets no ambient GIT_DIR. The 'random pattern' framing is exaggerated, so low.

findings.title: Two independent ctest-JUnit parsers and two preset-sweep executors with different acceptance rules
findings.evidence: tools/ci_gap_report.py:79 `def junit_summary(text)` and tools/verification_runner.py:98 `def junit_results(text, names)` both parse the same ctest `--output-junit` file. Both use `ElementTree.fromstring`, unwrap a single `testsuites`, reject empty/duplicate names and map `status`. ci_gap_report silently skips unknown suite children (`if case.tag != "testcase": continue`), while verification_runner raises `unsupported JUnit suite child`. Only verification_runner checks aggregate counts. Each file also has its own sweep loop: ci_gap_report.py:149 `run_command` / :159 `execute` vs verification_runner.py:144 `run_command` / :149 `execute_plan`, both running configure/build/ctest argv lists serially with `shell=False, check=False`.
findings.why: Two tools that both report "these presets passed" judge the same JUnit output differently. A ctest JUnit shape change can be accepted by one and rejected by the other, and docs/verification.md owns only one of the two contracts.
findings.suggested_fix: Make verification_runner's parser the single JUnit reader, returning per-case outcomes without raising on failure, with a strict mode for the planner. Have ci_gap_report group its output. Consider building ci_gap_report's execute on verification_runner's runner so logs and failures are handled one way.
findings.verify_reason: ci_gap_report.py:79 junit_summary and verification_runner.py:98 junit_results both exist, and the claimed differences (skipping versus raising on unknown children, aggregate checks) are real. They differ by design: junit_summary groups failures without rejecting them, for a report, while junit_results is a strict all-must-pass gate that also checks the inventory. The claim that docs/verification.md owns only one contract is false: verification.md:251-264 documents ci_gap_report's execute and its JUnit use. Shared parsing would be a modest cleanup: low.

findings.title: --forced takes any string and treats everything except the exact text "true" as not forced
findings.evidence: `parser.add_argument("--forced", default="false")` ... `forced=arguments.forced == "true",`
findings.why: "True", "1" or a typo silently means 'not a forced push'. A forced push could then be judged already tested, and the CI build that should run would be skipped. Every other boolean in tools/ uses store_true or choices.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `choices=["true", "false"]` so argparse refuses anything else, which still matches what the workflow passes.
findings.verify_reason: ci_tested_tree.py:165 `add_argument("--forced", default="false")` and :175 `forced=arguments.forced == "true"`, as quoted. ci.yml:107-111 passes github.event.forced only on push-to-master, where GitHub sends true/false. Branch protection also blocks force pushes, so the risk is theoretical, but argparse choices would make it fail closed.

findings.title: Package re-exports that nothing imports
findings.evidence:
from .common import canonical, digest, load_config, validate_config

__all__ = ["canonical", "digest", "load_config", "validate_config"]
findings.why: `git grep -E "cloud_performance import (canonical|digest|load_config|validate_config)|cloud_performance\.(canonical|digest|load_config|validate_config)\b"` across the repo, excluding docs/review, finds no user. Every caller (the __main__, analysis and infrastructure modules and the tools/tests files) imports from `.common` directly. The re-export adds a second public spelling with no consumer.
findings.suggested_fix: Reduce __init__.py to its docstring, or add a comment if the package-level API is intentional.
findings.verify_reason: __init__.py re-exports canonical, digest, load_config and validate_config. Every import I found uses `from tools.cloud_performance import __main__/analysis/infrastructure/release` or `.common`, and none uses the package-level names.

findings.title: _stack_instance repeats _validated_runner's Runner lookup with weaker checks
findings.evidence:
_stack_instance: `pages = cloudformation.get_paginator("list_stack_resources").paginate(StackName=stack["StackId"])
    matches = [resource["PhysicalResourceId"] for page in pages ... if resource["LogicalResourceId"] == "Runner" ...]` versus _validated_runner lines 91-100, which also checks ResourceType == "AWS::EC2::Instance" and that it agrees with the RunnerInstanceId output. The namespace prefix is also spelled twice: line 54 `return "labrador-performance-" + run_id` and line 79 `prefix = "labrador-performance-"`.
findings.why: Two functions resolve the same Runner instance under different rules. `launch` trusts the output without checking the resource type, while `status`, `collect` and `stop` check both.
findings.suggested_fix: In _launch, use _validated_runner(cloudformation, stack_name) after the create waiter and delete _stack_instance. Hoist the stack-name prefix into one constant used by _stack_name and _validated_runner.

The prefix is spelled at 54 and 79. Only _launch (337) uses _stack_instance, on a stack it just created, so the weaker check is low risk.

findings.title: Stack-name prefix, launch-record key and default Region are repeated as literals
findings.evidence:
54:    return "labrador-performance-" + run_id
79:    prefix = "labrador-performance-"
388:            Key=outputs["RunPrefix"] + "/control/launch.json",
485/488/492:    ....add_argument("--region", default="ap-southeast-2")
(common.py:118 already defines "launch": f"{prefix}/control/launch.json")

The Region default is written three times. If one copy changes, the stop, status or collect commands quietly stop matching the stacks that launch creates.

findings.title: worker_dispatch's docstring narrates incident history instead of stating the contract
findings.evidence:
Kept whole in one place so the offline suite can assert on what the agent
    will parse. The first launch idled its runner for an hour because the
    worker's location was written as an s3:// URI and nothing before the
    agent looked at it; the second did the same because the corrected form
    existed as a function nobody called.
findings.why: The first sentence is rationale. The rest is a story of past launches, which belongs in the dated performance records or git history. worker_source_info in common.py already states the s3:// rule in present tense.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the first sentence. Replace the narrative with a pointer to worker_source_info's docstring, or with the present-tense rule that the dispatch must use the HTTPS sourceInfo.
findings.verify_reason: __main__.py:208-214's worker_dispatch docstring narrates the first and second launch incidents exactly as quoted.

findings.title: `analyze` exits 0 when analysis is withheld; `analyze-local` exits 1
findings.evidence:
else:
        result = analysis.analyze(args.input)
        _write_new(args.out, json.dumps(result, indent=2).encode("utf-8") + b"\n")
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2, default=str))
    return 0

versus line 508 for analyze-local: `return 0 if result["complete"] else 1`
findings.why: analysis.analyze returns `_withheld(...)` with `complete: False` for a worker failure, a missing marker, manifest drift, identity mismatch and so on. The CLI still exits 0, so a script or shell that checks `$LASTEXITCODE` cannot tell refused evidence from a valid analysis. The sibling subcommand already uses the opposite contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Handle `analyze` the same way as `analyze-local`: after writing and printing, return 0 if result["complete"] else 1 (or return the value from one shared helper used by both branches).
findings.verify_reason: __main__.py:525-529 does `return 0` after analysis.analyze, while line 508 returns `0 if result["complete"] else 1` for analyze-local, and a test (test_command_reports_a_refusal_and_exits_nonzero) pins the nonzero exit for analyze-local only. analysis._withheld sets complete False. So the inconsistency is real. But analyze is a manual one-shot EC2 command, the README shows it run by hand, and the printed JSON carries analysis_withheld. Nothing scripts it, so this is low rather than medium.

findings.title: analysis imports the private `_integer` validator from common
findings.evidence: from .common import _integer, canonical, deadline, digest, safe_relative, validate_config
findings.why: `_integer` is underscore-private in common.py, yet analysis.py uses it to validate every raw sample (`_integer(sample.get(phase), f"sample.{phase}")`) and vendor IDs. It is really part of the module's shared contract, so the underscore misleads anyone changing it.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename it to `integer` (or `require_integer`) in common.py and update both modules.
findings.verify_reason: analysis.py:13 imports `_integer` from .common, and common.py:86 defines `def _integer`. This is a cross-module use of an underscore-private name.

findings.title: Bundle-manifest scope, bundled-worker path and power-plan GUID are unnamed literals repeated across modules
findings.evidence:
analysis.py:333  or release.get("scope") != "labrador-cloud-performance-payload"):
release.py:130   "scope": "labrador-cloud-performance-payload",
release.py:185   or manifest.get("scope") != "labrador-cloud-performance-payload"
analysis.py:366  release_files.get("source/tools/cloud_performance/worker.ps1")
__main__.py:267  "source/tools/cloud_performance/worker.ps1", {}).get("sha256")

findings.title: Null check on Process.ExitCode can never be true
findings.evidence: if ($null -eq $process.ExitCode) { throw "$Name has no exit code" }
findings.why: System.Diagnostics.Process.ExitCode is an Int32. Once the process has exited it never returns null, and reading it before exit throws rather than returning null. The branch suggests a failure mode that cannot happen. The line 73 `$processHandle = $process.Handle` read, which is what actually keeps ExitCode available, has no comment.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the null check, and add a one-line comment at line 73 saying why the handle is read.
findings.verify_reason: trace_benchmark.ps1:83 checks `$null -eq $process.ExitCode` after WaitForExit succeeded. Process.ExitCode is Int32, so this never returns null. Line 73 `$processHandle = $process.Handle` has no comment.

test_ci_tested_tree.py:13 from tools import ci_tested_tree as checker
test_verification_runner.py:15 import test_verify_changes as fixtures

findings.title: Each configuration's backend is matched to it only by position in a parallel tuple; tool requirements use bare slices
findings.evidence:
25: CONFIGURATIONS = (*NATIVE, "wasm-debug", "wasm-release-null")
26: BACKENDS = ("d3d11", "d3d12", "gl", "vulkan", "null", "gl", "null")
184:    for name, render in zip(CONFIGURATIONS, BACKENDS):
311:                      ("cl", NATIVE), ("fxc", NATIVE[:2])):
319:                    ("EMSDK", "upstream/emscripten/cmake/Modules/Platform/Emscripten.cmake", CONFIGURATIONS[-2:]),
338:            for variable, suffix in (("VCPKG_ROOT", "scripts/buildsystems/vcpkg.cmake"),):
findings.why: The backend for each configuration is known only by its position in a second tuple, and zip() silently truncates if a configuration is added to one tuple and not the other. NATIVE[:2] means 'the Direct3D presets' and CONFIGURATIONS[-2:] means 'the wasm configurations', but nothing names them, so reordering either tuple breaks the fxc/EMSDK requirements without an error. Line 338 loops over a one-element tuple. The file also runs many lines past 150 characters, unlike its sibling tools, which makes these rules harder to read.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the two tuples with one mapping, e.g. CONFIGURATIONS = {"x64-debug": "d3d11", ...}, or zip(..., strict=True) with an assertion. Name the subsets (D3D_PRESETS, WASM_CONFIGURATIONS), replace the one-element loop with a plain if, and wrap lines to match the sibling tools.
findings.verify_reason: verify_changes.py:25-26 parallel CONFIGURATIONS/BACKENDS tuples are zipped at :184. NATIVE[:2] for fxc and CONFIGURATIONS[-2:] for EMSDK are at :311/:319, and the one-element loop is at :338. The file has 11 lines over 150 characters while the sibling tools have 0. All of this is accurate, but it is a readability and fragility issue with no current defect, so low.

findings.title: An unreadable cache is followed by a mismatch for every expected key
findings.why: After the read fails, `values` stays `{}`, and the comparison loop then adds a `mismatch` check for CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY, the generator, each backend and so on. Those checks report "does not match plan: actual=None" when the real problem is that the cache could not be read. The single-element `for variable, suffix in ((...),):` loop is also needless indirection.
findings.suggested_fix: After adding the cache-read failure, `continue` past the comparisons (or put them in an else). Replace the one-item loop with a plain `if environment.get("VCPKG_ROOT"):`.
findings.verify_reason: verify_changes.py:331-341: after the except adds the cache-missing check, the code falls through to the expected/mismatch comparisons with values={}. The one-element `for variable, suffix in ((...),):` loop is present as quoted.

themes.name: Browser test runner consolidation
themes.desc: run_safari.mjs forks run_firefox.mjs's server, file list, bundle translation, sample hook and frame wait, and also forks website/acceptance's WebDriver client, now missing its port-race retry. Other duplication: five MIME tables, quit keys kept in both CMake and SAMPLES, deadline and listener boilerplate, two stderr tails, and the module-hook copies. There are small bugs too: usage validation happens after launch, teardown waits on an exit that has already happened, and DevTools.send leaks its waiter. WebDriver key tables use invisible private-use literals.
themes.story: Extract shared modules for serving, MIME types, the sample hook and frame wait, bundle steps, and the WebDriver client, used by the Chromium, Firefox and Safari runners and by website acceptance. Have CMake and SAMPLES read one quit-key source. Fix the three runner bugs separately. Verify with BrowserProtocolTests, wasm-debug page tests and the CI safari job.

findings.title: Second classic-WebDriver client, Safari tab-to-links probe and driver launcher, forked from website/acceptance and already missing its port-race retry
findings.evidence: run_safari.mjs:89 `export class WebDriverError extends Error` and :96 `export async function webdriver_command(base, method, path, body, ...)` duplicate website/acceptance/webdriver.mjs:34 `export class WebDriverError` and :56 `export async function command(baseUrl, method, commandPath, body, ...)`. run_safari.mjs:258 `export async function safari_tabs_to_links(...)` and :275 `read_default` are line-for-line website/acceptance/browsers.mjs:261 `safariTabsToLinks` / :279 `readDefault`. The comment at run_safari.mjs:255 even says "The same reading as the website's acceptance suite (website/acceptance/browsers.mjs)". run_safari.mjs:534 `free_port` duplicates browsers.mjs:288 `freePort`, and :542 `driver_arguments` duplicates browsers.mjs:102 `driverArguments`. Divergence: browsers.mjs:339 `startDriver` retries `DRIVER_START_ATTEMPTS` times because "Only an early exit can be a port taken between choosing and binding it", and accepts only `value?.ready === true` (:365). run_safari.mjs:551 `start_driver` makes one attempt and accepts `status?.ready !== false` (:568).
findings.why: Safari and iOS driving is the flakiest part of CI, and recent commits keep hardening it. Hardening that lands in website/acceptance (port-race retry, a stricter readiness check, richer error context) does not reach the Safari sample runner, and the reverse is also true.
findings.suggested_fix: Have run_safari.mjs import WebDriverError/command, safariTabsToLinks, freePort, driverArguments and startDriver from website/acceptance (both are plain Node ESM with no npm dependencies), or move them into a shared tools/webdriver module that both import. Keep only the sample-specific drive_sample/drive_bundle logic in run_safari.
findings.verify_reason: run_safari.mjs:89 WebDriverError, :96 webdriver_command, :258 safari_tabs_to_links, :275 read_default, :534 free_port, :542 driver_arguments, :551 start_driver all present. website/acceptance/webdriver.mjs:34/56 and browsers.mjs safariTabsToLinks/readDefault/freePort/driverArguments/startDriver are near-identical; the comment at run_safari.mjs:255 names the website copy. The claimed divergence is real: startDriver loops DRIVER_START_ATTEMPTS and requires `value?.ready === true`, while start_driver makes one attempt and accepts `status?.ready !== false`. The website's WebDriverError also carries richer context (status, method, cause). Not tracked.

(sample_key.mjs, the same rule\n	// for the development pages).` and line 254 `if (++seen >= 2 && timestamp - started >= 100)`. sample_key.mjs:9 uses `timestamp - started >= 150`, and its test is named 'fast frames preserve the existing 150 ms minimum'.
