findings.title: DevTools.send leaves a pending waiter when socket.send throws, unlike FirefoxProtocol.command
findings.why: A send on a closing or closed socket throws inside the executor. The promise rejects with a bare InvalidStateError that does not name the method, and the entry stays in `pending` until refuse_all. firefox_protocol.mjs:267-273 catches this case, clears the waiter and prefixes the method. The message handler at :12 also runs JSON.parse and the listeners unguarded, so a listener's throw escapes into socket dispatch. FirefoxProtocol.receive guards against both (:300-311).
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap socket.send in try/catch, delete the pending id and refuse with `${method}: ${error.message}`, as FirefoxProtocol does. Optionally guard listener calls the same way.
findings.verify_reason: The cited firefox_protocol.mjs lines are wrong: the file is 190 lines long. The send try/catch is at :88-97 and the guarded receive is at :100-135. The mechanism is also partly wrong. Under the WHATWG WebSocket send (Node's WebSocket), send throws only while CONNECTING and silently drops data on a closing or closed socket. A throw in the executor already rejects the promise, so the leftover pending entry is harmless. DevTools.send's real gap is that it has no readyState or failure check. FirefoxProtocol.command has one (:73-74). DevTools' message handler (devtools.mjs:12-28) is unguarded, as the finding says.

findings.title: Each sample's quit keys and target names are kept in both CMake and SAMPLES, unchecked
findings.evidence: run_firefox.mjs:42 `linesweeper: { target: 'LineSweeperSample', keys: ['Escape', 'ArrowDown', 'ArrowDown', 'ArrowDown', 'Enter'] }` and :49-50 `components: { target: 'ComponentsGallery', keys: ['ArrowDown', 'ArrowDown', 'ArrowLeft', 'ArrowUp', 'ArrowRight', 'KeyR', 'Escape', 'Escape'] }` repeat CMakeLists.txt:200-230 (`labrador_sample_page_test(LineSweeperPageTests LineSweeperSample "Escape,ArrowDown,ArrowDown,ArrowDown,Enter"`, `ComponentsPageTests ComponentsGallery "ArrowDown,ArrowDown,ArrowLeft,ArrowUp,ArrowRight,KeyR,Escape,Escape"`) and the 'The pause menu: RESUME, RESTART, COLOURS, QUIT.' comment. The CMake sample list is repeated at CMakeLists.txt:317-320. run_safari.mjs:41 imports this table from the Firefox runner (`import { SAMPLES } from './run_firefox.mjs';`). I grepped tests/render/web/*.test.mjs for CMakeLists/quit_keys and found no check that the two agree.
findings.why: If a sample's menu changes, for example a new pause-menu row, the Chromium entry must be updated in CMake and the Firefox and Safari entries in run_firefox.mjs. A missed copy makes one browser's entry time out. Separately, the Safari runner depends on the Firefox runner module only to get this table.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the sample table (target, quit keys, why) in one place, for example a small samples.json or samples.mjs beside the runners that run_firefox and run_safari import. Have CMake read it, or add a Node test that parses the labrador_sample_page_test calls in CMakeLists.txt and asserts they match.
findings.verify_reason: run_firefox.mjs:40-51 SAMPLES repeats the quit keys at CMakeLists.txt:201-238, and run_safari.mjs:41 imports SAMPLES from run_firefox.mjs. firefox_protocol.test.mjs:233 checks only the key set, not that it agrees with CMake. Real, but a missed copy fails loudly with a timeout, so low.

findings.title: Three copies of the deadline, complaint-listener and context-destroyed boilerplate in one file
findings.evidence: drive_sample (177-202), drive_window_page (336-364) and drive_bundle (431-457) each open with `const deadline = Date.now() + timeout_ms; const remaining = () => { const duration = deadline - Date.now(); if (duration <= 0) throw new Error('Firefox ... deadline expired.'); return Math.min(duration, 10000); };` followed by the same `protocol.on((message) => { if (message.method === 'log.entryAdded') { ... complaints.push(`${entry.level}: ${entry.text}`) } else if (message.method === 'browsingContext.contextDestroyed' && message.params.context === context) { protocol.fail('the tested Firefox context was destroyed'); } })`, and each subscribes with the same `session.subscribe` / `script.addPreloadScript` / `browsingContext.activate` / `browsingContext.navigate` sequence.
findings.why: These three entries must apply the same failure policy, yet the copies have already diverged: only drive_window_page honours expected_complaint. A fix to the logging, the 10 s per-call cap or the complaint format has to be made three times.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract a `watched_context(protocol, context, { timeout_ms, log, expected_complaint, what })` helper that returns { remaining, complaints, assert_healthy, unsubscribe }, plus an `open_page(protocol, context, url, preload)` for the subscribe/preload/activate/navigate sequence, and use them in all three drivers.
findings.verify_reason: drive_sample (177-202), drive_window_page (336-364) and drive_bundle (431-457) carry the same deadline/remaining and log/contextDestroyed listener; only the messages differ. The expected_complaint difference is deliberate: the comment above drive_window_page says the sequence's last step causes an error on purpose. The duplication is within one test file.

findings.title: WebDriver key tables hold invisible private-use characters instead of \uE0xx escapes
findings.evidence: run_firefox.mjs:399 `const BUNDLE_KEYS = Object.freeze({ Escape: '', Enter: '', Tab: '', KeyA: 'a',` (od -c shows bytes 356 200 214 = U+E00C etc. inside the quotes). Same in run_safari.mjs:45-47 `const KEY_VALUES = Object.freeze({ Escape: '', Enter: '', Tab: '', ...` and `const OPTION_KEY = '';`, and in safari_protocol.test.mjs:68 `{ type: 'keyDown', value: '' }`. The same file's line 53 writes `Escape: '', Enter: ''`, and line 239 writes `Tab: ''`.
findings.why: In any editor or diff these values look like empty strings, so a reader cannot tell which WebDriver key each one is. A 'cleanup' that really empties them would still look like no change. The same file and its tests already use explicit escapes for the same values, so the inconsistency is within one module.
findings.suggested_fix: Spell every WebDriver key as a \uE0xx escape, as KEY_VALUES at run_firefox.mjs:53 does, in run_firefox.mjs BUNDLE_KEYS, run_safari.mjs KEY_VALUES/OPTION_KEY and the safari_protocol.test.mjs expectations. Better still, keep one shared, named WebDriver key table that both runners import.
findings.verify_reason: cat -A confirms raw U+E0xx bytes in run_firefox.mjs:399-400 BUNDLE_KEYS, run_safari.mjs:45-47 KEY_VALUES/OPTION_KEY and safari_protocol.test.mjs:68,322, while run_firefox.mjs:53-54 and 239-240 use \uE0xx escapes. Real inconsistency, but in test runners whose tests pin the values, so low rather than medium.

findings.title: Usage errors exit 1 (with a stack trace) in some runners and tools, and 2 in others
findings.evidence: run_firefox.mjs:687 and run_safari.mjs:651 `catch (error) { console.error(`run_firefox: ${error.stack ?? error}`); process.exitCode = 1; }`. Their parse_options throws for bad arguments, so a usage error exits 1 and prints a stack. run_page.mjs:202 `process.exit(2);`, tools/web_bundle/bundle.mjs:100 `process.exit(2);`, check_live.mjs:66, flash_check.mjs:608 and web_pacing/analyse.mjs:121 exit 2, as do the Python check_* tools (`return 2`) and tools/linesweeper_capture/main.cpp:343 `return 2;`. bench/linesweeper_frame_bench.cpp:517, bench/d3d12_descriptor_query_probe.cpp:82/152 (`throw std::invalid_argument("Usage: ...")` then `return 1;`) and tools/consumer_check/*.py (`raise SystemExit(f"...")`, exit 1 for operational errors) exit 1.
findings.why: Most of the repo uses 2 for 'could not run or bad invocation' and 1 for 'ran and failed'. Callers and CI steps cannot rely on that split while some runners treat a mistyped flag as a test failure and print an irrelevant stack trace.
findings.suggested_fix: Have run_firefox and run_safari catch argument errors separately: print the message without the stack and exit 2. Make the bench and probe usage paths and consumer_check's operational refusals exit 2 as well. Write the convention down in CONTRIBUTING or docs/verification.md.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: run_firefox.mjs:686-687 and run_safari.mjs:650-651 catch parse_options' throw, print error.stack and set exitCode 1, while run_page.mjs:202 calls process.exit(2) on a usage error. ctest and CI treat any non-zero exit as failure, and no caller reads the difference between 1 and 2 for these runners, so this is cosmetic consistency.

findings.title: Five separate extension-to-MIME tables for serving the same wasm pages
findings.evidence: tests/render/web/run_page.mjs:135 `const MEDIA_TYPES = { '.html': 'text/html; charset=utf-8', '.js': 'text/javascript; charset=utf-8', ... '.wasm': 'application/wasm', ...}`; tests/render/web/run_firefox.mjs:498 and tests/render/web/run_safari.mjs:462 `CONTENT_TYPES` ('.js': 'text/javascript' without charset); website/acceptance/server.mjs:18 `export const CONTENT_TYPES = {...}`; tools/lan_serve.py:27 `TYPES = { ".wasm": "application/wasm", ".js": "text/javascript", ... }`.
findings.why: These servers all serve the same Emscripten outputs and already disagree on the charset parameter for .js. Adding an asset type (a .data or .woff2 file a sample starts loading) means finding every table.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the three Node test runners import website/acceptance/server.mjs's exported CONTENT_TYPES, or a shared one in tests/render/web, and drop their local tables. lan_serve.py can stay separate (Python), but its header could name the canonical table.
findings.verify_reason: run_page.mjs:135 MEDIA_TYPES ('.js' with charset), run_firefox/run_safari CONTENT_TYPES ('.js' without charset), website/acceptance/server.mjs:18 exported CONTENT_TYPES, and tools/lan_serve.py:27 TYPES. All exist and disagree on the charset. The practical risk is small, because the Firefox and Safari servers also allow-list exact files and a new asset type needs that list changed too. This overlaps finding 0. Low.

findings.title: The usage message leaves out options the header says either form accepts
findings.evidence:
The header (lines 14-15) says `// Either form also takes [--emulate-media <feature>=<value>],
// [--expect-console <text>] and [--root <folder>].`, but fail_usage prints `'[--input <script.mjs>] [--root <folder>]
' + ... '--quit-keys <code,...> [--frames <n>] [--timeout <seconds>] ' + '[--sample-input fixed-step]
'`. That never shows --emulate-media or --expect-console, and shows --root for the first form only.
findings.why: The usage text is what someone sees after a typo, and it does not show options that ctest entries use, such as --emulate-media and --expect-console on LineSweeperPageTests. parse_arguments also never rejects unknown option names, so a misspelt --expect-consol is silently ignored instead of reaching this message.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the options shared by both forms to fail_usage. Consider having parse_arguments reject unknown names, as run_firefox/run_safari parse_options already do with an allowed set.
findings.verify_reason: run_page.mjs:14-15 says both forms take --emulate-media/--expect-console/--root, but fail_usage (193-203) omits the first two and shows --root only for the first form. parse_arguments (149-156) stores any --name without rejecting unknown names.

findings.title: Two stderr listeners keep identical 16 KiB tails of the browser's output
findings.why: `seen` and `stderr_tail` hold the same text. One listener that appends once and then tests for the DevTools line would do, and the early-exit message at :297-298 and diagnostics() would report the same buffer.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a single `stderr_tail` updated in one 'data' listener that also runs the `DevTools listening on` match, and use it in both the refusal message and diagnostics().
findings.verify_reason: run_page.mjs:280-291 has two stderr 'data' listeners keeping identical 16 KiB tails (stderr_tail and seen). One is used by diagnostics() and the other by the endpoint match and its early-exit message. This is trivial redundancy.

findings.title: Module-callback hook written three times, with diverging order of flag and original call
findings.why: All three hooks intercept window.Module assignment and wrap onRuntimeInitialized, onQuit and onError, but they disagree on semantics. Chromium's records quit before the page's onQuit runs, so the run counts as quit even if the page's own onQuit throws. The Firefox and Safari hooks record it only after the callback returns. The same sample can therefore pass in one runner and fail in another for reasons unrelated to the browser.
findings.suggested_fix: Export one hook builder (for example module_hook(global_name, extra) returning the source text) from a shared module. Have the three runners compose it with their runner-specific counters (WebGL draw counting, input protocol), and pick one ordering for the flag.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed that the order differs. run_page.mjs:426-428 sets heard.quit before calling the original. run_firefox.mjs:124-127 and run_safari.mjs:191-195 call the original first and set the flag afterwards. The divergence only changes an outcome if a page's own onQuit throws, which no sample is shown to do. The 'pass in one runner, fail in another' consequence is hypothetical.

findings.title: --emulate-media is validated after the browser is launched; fail_usage's process.exit skips teardown
findings.why: process.exit never runs the finally block at lines 779-798. A malformed --emulate-media therefore leaves the headless Chrome running, the HTTP server listening and the labrador-browser-* temporary profile on disk. All other argument checks run in parse_arguments before anything starts. This is the only usage error that leaks resources.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the --emulate-media split and check into parse_arguments, storing the parsed name and value on `parsed` (for example parsed.media = { name, value }). run() then only sends Emulation.setEmulatedMedia.
findings.verify_reason: run_page.mjs:631-635 matches: the emulate-media split and fail_usage (process.exit(2) at :203) run inside run()'s try, after launch at :544, so the finally at :779 never runs. The leak only happens when someone types a malformed flag by hand. The only callers are CMakeLists.txt:204/209, which pass well-formed literals, so no ctest run can hit it. Real, but low.

findings.title: Teardown waits the full 5 s for an 'exit' event that has already fired
findings.why: If the browser has already exited (a crash, or the endpoint promise refused because it exited early), child.once('exit') is registered after the event and never fires. Every such run then stalls 5 s in teardown. run_firefox.mjs:585-594 `exited()` checks `child.exitCode !== null || child.signalCode !== null` first for this reason.
findings.suggested_fix: Return early when child.exitCode !== null || child.signalCode !== null before waiting, as run_firefox's exited() does, or reuse that helper.
findings.verify_reason: run_page.mjs:783-786 registers child.once('exit') with no prior exitCode/signalCode check. If the browser has already exited (for example the endpoint refused on early exit, so devtools is unset), teardown waits the full 5 s. run_firefox.mjs:585-594 exited() checks first.

findings.title: WebDriver key table duplicated between runners; Safari's copy uses invisible Private Use Area literals
findings.evidence: run_safari.mjs:45 `const KEY_VALUES = Object.freeze({ Escape: '', Enter: '', Tab: '', KeyS: 's', ...` where each blank-looking value is a raw U+E00C/U+E007/U+E004 character (bytes EE 80 8C), and `const OPTION_KEY = '';` is U+E00A. run_firefox.mjs:53 defines the same table with escapes: `Escape: '', Enter: '', ... ArrowDown: ''`. run_safari already imports SAMPLES from run_firefox.mjs.
findings.why: In review, in diffs and in most editors, Safari's values look like empty strings. A mistyped or stripped code point cannot be seen. Keeping two tables means a key added to one runner (Tab, KeyA) is missing from the other.
findings.suggested_fix: Export one escaped KEY_VALUES (a superset with Tab, KeyA and the Option key) from a shared module, or from run_firefox.mjs next to SAMPLES. Import it in run_safari.mjs and write every code point as \uE0xx.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed byte-wise: in run_safari.mjs:45-47, KEY_VALUES and OPTION_KEY are raw U+E00C/E007/E004/E012-E015/E00A characters (bytes EE 80 xx), while run_firefox.mjs:53 uses \uE0xx escapes, and the two tables differ (Safari adds Tab and KeyA). Readability and duplication in test tooling; a wrong code point would fail the test visibly. Low.

findings.title: run_safari.mjs re-implements run_firefox.mjs's server, file list, bundle substitute, key actions and sample hook although it already imports SAMPLES from it
findings.evidence: run_safari.mjs:41 `import { SAMPLES } from './run_firefox.mjs';` yet still defines its own copies of: `async function serve(options, files)` (run_safari.mjs:487) vs `async function serve(files, substitute = () => null)` (run_firefox.mjs:501), with near-identical bodies (`const allowed = new Map(files.map((file) => ['/' + basename(file), file]));`, favicon 204, substitute, `fatal(new Error(...))`, `server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', ready)`); `const CONTENT_TYPES = Object.freeze({ '.wasm': 'application/wasm', '.js': 'text/javascript', '.png': 'image/png', '.html': 'text/html; charset=utf-8' });` verbatim at run_safari.mjs:462 and run_firefox.mjs:498; `BUNDLE_FILES` + `artifact_files` (run_safari.mjs:461/465 vs run_firefox.mjs:481/483); `substitute(options, url)` (run_safari.mjs:480) vs `bundle_substitute(url)` (run_firefox.mjs:493), both returning `{ type: 'text/javascript; charset=utf-8', body: Buffer.from(FACTORY_WRAPPER) }`; `key_actions` (run_safari.mjs:246 vs run_firefox.mjs:158); `frames_expression` verbatim (run_safari.mjs:321, run_firefox.mjs:168; a third variant at run_page.mjs:447); and the `SAMPLE_HOOK` Module accessor wrapper (run_safari.mjs:172 vs run_firefox.mjs:106, and a third shape at run_page.mjs:405). The hooks have already diverged: Safari's counts clears/draws only when `!this.isContextLost()` and tracks lost/restored; Firefox's counts every call.
findings.why: The three runners are meant to enforce one page contract across Chromium, Firefox and Safari. Three hand-synced copies of the hook and server drift silently, and they already disagree on whether a draw on a lost context counts as a draw. A fix to request policy or hook semantics has to be made three times.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the page server (allow-list, substitute, content types), BUNDLE_FILES/artifact_files, frames_expression, key_actions and one parameterised SAMPLE_HOOK (with a global name and an optional context-loss block) into a shared module beside bundle_page.mjs, e.g. tests/render/web/page_harness.mjs. Import it from run_firefox, run_safari and, where the shapes fit, run_page.
findings.verify_reason: Re-read run_safari.mjs:41 (imports SAMPLES from run_firefox), :172 SAMPLE_HOOK, :246 key_actions, :321 frames_expression, :461-532 BUNDLE_FILES/CONTENT_TYPES/artifact_files/substitute/serve, and run_firefox.mjs:106-170, :481-540. The copies are real: CONTENT_TYPES, BUNDLE_FILES and frames_expression are verbatim, and serve and the hook are near-copies. Not tracked in docs/code-hygiene.md. The drift claim is overstated. Safari's hook counts loss and restore because its sample run forces a context loss (header lines 13-16); the Firefox sample run does not. The servers differ on purpose: Safari injects the hooks into the HTML because classic WebDriver has no preload script, and Firefox uses BiDi addPreloadScript and keeps a `denied` latch. The hooks also differ in shape (an IIFE string versus a function string), so sharing them takes more than one import. This is test-harness duplication, so low.

findings.title: One comment line runs past the wrap width of the rest of the block
findings.evidence: `// for every case past the sixteenth. WEBGL_lose_context is the one call that releases one now, and` (about 100 columns). The surrounding lines 35-41 wrap at about 78.
findings.why: This looks like an edit that was not re-wrapped. The whitespace lint does not catch it, and it stands out against the file's consistent wrapping.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-wrap lines 38-41 to the block's width.
findings.verify_reason: test_window.cpp:40 is 99 characters, against about 70-79 for lines 35-39. A trivial wrap inconsistency.

themes.name: Test flakiness and runner robustness
themes.desc: Fixed sleeps used as synchronisation, polls without deadlines, timeouts that differ for the same operation across runners, start_driver leaking a safaridriver or geckodriver that never becomes ready, and temporary folders left behind.
themes.story: Replace sleeps with condition waits under one deadline helper shared with the runner consolidation, kill the driver on every failure path, and clean temporary folders. Verify with BrowserProtocolTests and the page tests.

findings.title: Vibration cases rely on no pad being plugged in; with a pad in slot 0 they fail and rumble it
findings.why: On the XInput build GamepadReader::vibrate calls DirectX::GamePad::SetVibration (engine/input/xinput/gamepad_reader.cpp:21-25). That call returns true for a connected slot, so on a developer machine with a pad in slot 0 the CHECK_FALSE at line 307 fails and the motors run at 0.75/0.25 until the reader is destroyed. The case at line 275 has the same problem: `REQUIRE_FALSE(pads.connected(0))` aborts it whenever a pad is present. The file preamble at lines 16-19 says "No case here turns a motor", which is false on that machine. InputTests becomes hardware-dependent, so it passes on CI and fails on the owner's desktop.
findings.suggested_fix: Drive the suspend/resume and Gamepads::vibrate paths through VibrationOutput<RecordingTransport> or an injectable reader, as the other cases in this file do. If the real reader must be exercised, use a slot index that is out of range, or skip the cases (doctest::skip) when sample() reports a connected pad, and say so in the preamble.
findings.verify_reason: Real. GamepadReader::vibrate goes through XInputVibration::send, which calls DirectX::GamePad::SetVibration. That returns true for a connected slot, so CHECK_FALSE at line 307 fails with a pad in slot 0, and REQUIRE_FALSE(pads.connected(0)) at line 282 aborts the earlier case. The test's own comment at lines 277-278 only covers CI. TODO.md confirms the owner has a physical XInput pad, and the preamble's 'No case here turns a motor' is false on that machine. It is not tracked anywhere. Still, this is a test that depends on the environment, not a defect in shipped code, and any rumble ends when the reader is destroyed. Medium, not high.

findings.title: start_driver leaks the spawned safaridriver/geckodriver when it never becomes ready
findings.why: The child is spawned at line 554, but both throws leave start_driver before it returns { stop }. main() assigns `driver = await start_driver(options)`, so `driver` stays undefined. The finally block's `if (driver) await driver.stop()` therefore never kills the process. A driver that is slow to answer /status is left running on the runner or developer machine, holding its port and possibly a Safari automation session for the next run. website/acceptance/browsers.mjs startDriver calls killDriver on the same failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Kill the child (with the same tree/SIGKILL escalation as killDriver) before every throw after spawn. Better, reuse website/acceptance/browsers.mjs startDriver/killDriver instead of a second implementation.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed at run_safari.mjs:551-575. Both throws leave start_driver before { stop } exists, and main()'s finally (line 638) only stops a driver it was given, so a driver that never becomes ready keeps running. browsers.mjs startDriver calls killDriver in the same case. It is not high: the safari CI job runs on an ephemeral macos-latest runner, the leak happens only on a failure that already fails the run, and an early exit (the other throw) leaves no process behind.

findings.title: Waits are bounded by attempt counts, so their real timeout varies with each runner's evaluate latency; three copies with diverging error filters
findings.why: The deadline is attempts x (20 ms + one evaluate round trip). Under CDP an evaluate is fast. Under Safari it is two WebDriver HTTP calls (run_safari.mjs:144-145 sets timeouts before every execute_async). So the same step has very different real deadlines per runner. The 750-attempt wait at line 518 must outlast the page's ten-second context timer, yet nowhere is it expressed in milliseconds. The same hand-rolled loop is in tools/save_check/reload.mjs:10-22 (250 x 20 ms) and tools/web_pacing/page_input.mjs:108-116 (1200 x 25 ms). Each tolerates a different set of navigation errors: 'Cannot find (?:default execution context|context with specified id)', 'Cannot find context|Inspected target navigated', and 'Cannot find context with specified id'.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the attempt counts with a deadline in milliseconds, like webdriver.mjs waitUntil, and state the 10 s + margin explicitly for the context-timeout case. Export one shared until/navigation-error predicate from bundle_page.mjs and use it in reload.mjs and page_input.mjs.
findings.verify_reason: The loops are counted in attempts, but each attempt waits at least 20 ms, so the 750-attempt wait at line 518 lasts at least 15 s on any runner, longer than the page's 10 s timer. A slower Safari evaluate only makes the deadline longer. The claimed flakiness does not follow. What remains is clarity: the deadline is implicit, and three loops filter navigation errors differently (reload.mjs:10-22, page_input.mjs:108-116).

findings.title: Firefox profile cleanup fails the run on a transient Windows lock, where run_page retries
findings.why: run_page.mjs:788-797 explains that 'The profile can stay locked for a moment after the browser exits on Windows' and retries ten times, 200 ms apart. The Firefox runner, used locally on Windows for the Firefox* entries, makes one attempt and turns an EBUSY/EPERM into a test failure. Separately, whenever the BiDi session never connected (line 677-679), the profile is deliberately retained in %TEMP% on every such failure and nothing ever removes it.
findings.suggested_fix: Use rmSync's maxRetries/retryDelay (as website/acceptance/fixture.mjs:93 does), or share run_page's retry loop. Also give retained profiles a cleanup path, such as removing stale labrador-firefox-* directories on start.
findings.verify_reason: Cleanup makes one rmSync attempt, and only after exited() has confirmed that the owned process exited (`closed`). run_page.mjs retries instead. A lingering Firefox content process on Windows could still hold a lock, so the gap is real in principle. Keeping the profile when no session was established is deliberate and already counts as a failure. The Firefox* entries run locally or need a GPU, and CI runs only FirefoxWebWindowTests on Linux.

findings.title: Chromium runner's DevTools commands have no deadline, and setup runs outside the page timeout
findings.why: DevTools.send (devtools.mjs:39) registers no timer. Only the endpoint (30 s), Browser.getVersion (10 s) and the later Promise.race with timeout_ms are bounded. If the browser stops answering during attach/enable/prepare/navigate, the run hangs until ctest's default 1500 s timeout kills node. The finally block's Browser.close, profile removal and child.kill then never run. firefox_protocol.mjs times out every command (default 10 s), and run_safari.mjs's webdriver_command defaults to 30 s.
findings.suggested_fix: Give DevTools.send an optional per-command timeout, as FirefoxProtocol.command has. Alternatively, start the timeout_ms deadline before Target.getTargets so setup is covered by the same race.
findings.verify_reason: DevTools.send (devtools.mjs:38-45) sets no timer, and attach, enable, prepare and navigate (run_page.mjs:568-654) run before the timeout_ms race. But devtools.mjs:10 refuses every pending command when the socket closes, so a crashed or exited browser does not hang the run. Only a browser that is alive but silent hangs, and then ctest's timeout ends it. This is a robustness gap, not an observed flake.

findings.title: Fixed 5-second sleep used as 'Safari is ready' after restarting the simulator's Safari
findings.why: restartSimulatorSafari is the recovery path for the flaky iOS retry (suite.mjs:1699). It always costs 5 s, yet the sleep proves nothing about readiness. A failed launch is only logged, then the code sleeps and proceeds anyway. The first-boot path at line 218 launches the same app with no sleep at all, so the two paths assume different readiness.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the sleep with a readiness condition, such as polling the driver's /status or retrying newSession with a deadline. If a settle time is really needed, name it as a constant with its reason and use it on both launch paths.
findings.verify_reason: The fixed 5 s sleep exists, at browsers.mjs:224-230. It runs only on the retry and recovery paths (browsers.mjs:418, suite.mjs:1699), and newSession's own retry loop with SESSION_ATTEMPTS follows it. So the sleep does not decide readiness. It is a magic number with no comment, not a flakiness source.

findings.title: Waiting for typed text into the search box uses 5 s in one check and 3 s in another
findings.evidence: await waitUntil(() => context.script('return arguments[0].value;', [input]), { timeoutMs: 5_000, message: 'the typed text' });
findings.why: search() at line 1165 waits for exactly the same condition with `{ timeoutMs: 3_000, message: 'the typed text' }` and then retypes. searchSubmission has no retry and a different allowance. The two literals will drift independently, and searchSubmission fails on the dropped-first-text simulator behaviour that search() documents and works around.
findings.suggested_fix: Share one named constant and one 'type and confirm it arrived, retyping once' helper between search() and searchSubmission().
findings.verify_reason: suite.mjs:1284 waits 5 s with no retype. search() at line 1165 waits 3 s and retypes, because the simulator can drop the first text. searchSubmission therefore lacks a workaround that is documented a hundred lines earlier.

themes.name: Core, math, scene, app, audio and input test hygiene
themes.desc:
Comments in these suites cite ColourWars files and counts that are not in this repository, give stale configuration censuses, or tell history. Some fixtures sit off the boundaries their names claim, and the shape-edge test skips slots. Rng, CollisionObject stubs and null-renderer harnesses are duplicated, and three tests hand-roll a file reader. Other items:
- Cases sit outside their TEST_SUITE.
- Namespaces are PascalCase, public members carry trailing underscores, and include groups are wrong.
- Temporary folders are not cleaned up.
- The XAudio2 recovery assertion tests the fake's own field.
- Test files are laid out inconsistently.
themes.story: First, fix weak tests (shape edge order, boundary fixtures, the tunnelling constants, the recovery assertion) as test-behaviour changes. Second, consolidate fixtures into shared test-support headers (engine Random, byte_reader, null harness). Third, rewrite the comments. If case names change, update ctest_inventory.json; keep doctest case names otherwise.

findings.title: Test name and comment are defined by history ("already here", "before view_capacity joined")
findings.why: A test name is permanent output in every failure report, and this one describes the order in which code was written, not behaviour. CONVENTIONS: "a sentence about what it was belongs to the history." "The split" refers to a past change the reader cannot see.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename it to the behaviour, for example "a zero frame rate, thread count, window minimum or class name is rejected". Reword the comments in present tense ("each of these reaches a divisor"; "the thread ceiling is a property of the machine, not of the view capacity").
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed at application_options_tests.cpp:70: TEST_CASE("the checks that were already here still hold"). The comment there refers to 'before view_capacity joined them', and line 26 says 'The whole point of the split'. The test name is historical rather than behavioural and appears in every failure report.

findings.title: dom_events_tests.cpp says it is browser-only, but it is compiled on every platform
findings.evidence: dom_events_tests.cpp:17 "// directly. Compiled into the browser build only, beside the file it tests."  tests/app/CMakeLists.txt lists dom_events_tests.cpp in the unconditional AppTests SOURCES and, if NOT EMSCRIPTEN, adds "../../engine/app/web/dom_events.cpp". Its header comment says "including the pure DOM-event translator on every platform". tests/input/standard_gamepad_tests.cpp:13-14 repeats the error: "Compiled into the browser build only, beside the file it tests, as dom_events_tests.cpp is."
findings.why: The comment states the opposite of the build. A maintainer could guard browser-only code in this file on that belief and break the native AppTests build, or overlook that native CI already covers the translator.
findings.suggested_fix: Say that the file is compiled into AppTests everywhere and that native builds compile engine/app/web/dom_events.cpp into the test target. Remove 'as dom_events_tests.cpp is' from standard_gamepad_tests.cpp:14. Line 14 should also name keyboard_input_tests.cpp, beside window_tests.cpp, as the Win32 half.
findings.verify_reason: dom_events_tests.cpp:17 says 'Compiled into the browser build only', but tests/app/CMakeLists.txt:1 says 'on every platform', line 10 lists it unconditionally, and lines 14-21 add engine/app/web/dom_events.cpp when NOT EMSCRIPTEN. standard_gamepad_tests.cpp:13-14 repeats 'as dom_events_tests.cpp is'.

findings.title: "names the path" / "names itself" / "says so" cases assert only the exception type
findings.why: The case name promises a T6 diagnostic (the path in the message), but only the type is checked. A loader that threw `runtime_error("")` would pass. The same pattern appears in tests/assets/json_tests.cpp:75 ("a file that is not there names itself", CHECK_THROWS_AS only), tests/assets/sound_bank_loader_tests.cpp:388 ("a definition that is not there names itself") and sound_bank_loader_tests.cpp:331 ("...is a content bug, and it says so", whose comment adds "The throw names the file"). Sibling cases in these same files already use CHECK_THROWS_WITH_AS / doctest::Contains for exactly this purpose.
findings.suggested_fix: Use CHECK_THROWS_WITH_AS(..., doctest::Contains("no_such_manifest.json"), std::runtime_error) and the equivalent for the other three. For the duplicate-effect case, also check that the message contains 'bang' and the definition's path.
findings.verify_reason: asset_manifest_loader_tests.cpp:94-99 and json_tests.cpp:75 use CHECK_THROWS_AS only, under case names that promise the path appears in the message. The sound_bank_loader cites are mislined because the file is 159 lines: the duplicate-effect case is at 98-116, and its comment 'The throw names the file' is unverified. The 'names itself' case is at 155-159. Sibling files use CHECK_THROWS_WITH_AS. Substance holds.

findings.title: Audio test preambles narrate the survey that produced them and the state before the null backend existed
findings.why: CONVENTIONS: "Archaeology ... is never a comment." These passages describe what the code used to be and which survey asked for it, and "only implementation was DirectXTK's" is no longer true (null and webaudio backends exist). The census numbers ("eight of thirteen", "five sites") can go stale.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the contract and rationale (which side of the seam the clamp is on, what the null model cannot assert). Delete the survey provenance, the "now" and "had never executed" narrative and the thirteen/eight/five census.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed in null_tests.cpp:19-29, 136-137 and 183-185, sound_bank_tests.cpp:65-67 and 164-166, and tests/audio/CMakeLists.txt:51-54. findings.title: Line-number citation into PHILOSOPHY.md points at the wrong text
findings.why: The citation sends a reader to an unrelated section. check_doc_citations.cmake only checks document and section names, so it cannot catch a line number that has drifted. CONVENTIONS asks for a citation a machine can check.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the trade-off by its T-number or section, or quote the sentence without a line range. Drop the `:632-637` suffix.
findings.verify_reason: null_tests.cpp:27 does cite PHILOSOPHY.md:632-637. That range is now the UI/components text, and the quoted sentence is at PHILOSOPHY.md:856. So the citation is wrong. It is still one stale pointer inside a test comment, which is not high severity, and the same preamble is also covered by finding 5.

findings.title: Sniper test cites ColourWars files that are not in this repo and claims a failure mode it cannot have
findings.why: The comment says its numbers come "from the tree", but none of the four cited files is in this repository. It also says the test "will fail the moment the content is corrected". It cannot: the four values are hard-coded `constexpr` literals and nothing reads game content. So the test is a permanent arithmetic fact about another project's tuning, and its own reminder to delete it can never fire. The test name and comment present it as a live record of 'the shipping' game, which is false here.
findings.suggested_fix: Either delete the case (the decision belongs to ColourWars), or rewrite it as a neutral worked example of max_safe_speed with made-up numbers. Remove the file citations and the claim that it fails when content changes.
findings.verify_reason: tunnelling_tests.cpp is 103 lines; the case is at line 46-85. The comment cites weapon_consts.h/projectile_consts.h/main.cpp/close_quarters.json 'from the tree' (none in this repo) and says it 'will fail the moment the content is corrected', yet the values are constexpr literals, so that can never happen. Real, but a stale test comment, not high severity. Not tracked in TODO/code-hygiene.

findings.title: Rationale cites a SpriteFrame RECT* that no longer exists, and the test checks handles, not references
findings.why: The comment's premise is false today: sprite_frame.h explicitly says it hands out a RectangleI, not a RECT*. The test name promises reference stability, but the body holds a `Handle` and re-reads through `get()`, which is index stability. A reference taken before the adds would dangle on reallocation, which is the opposite of the name. "64 reallocations" is also wrong: 64 push_backs do not cause 64 reallocations.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename it to "a resolved handle stays valid as the table is filled". Drop the RECT* paragraph and the reallocation count. If reference stability after loading is the contract, cite name_table.h's own statement instead.
findings.verify_reason: name_table_tests.cpp is 146 lines; lines 120-135 carry the 'SpriteFrame hands out a RECT*' comment, TEST_CASE 'references stay valid as the table is filled', holds a Handle and re-reads via get(), and says 'Resolved before 64 reallocations'. sprite_frame.h:30 says 'A RectangleI, and not a RECT*'.

findings.title: Comments cite ColourWars call-site counts, story IDs and game content that do not exist in the engine repo
findings.evidence:
// The statement the ten live call sites do not have. If the

The same file at 695-696 has "it is the one thing about C3 that cannot be driven from a keyboard - the paint-shooter reaches it only through a gamepad." findings.title: Test comments narrate history: past bugs, prior implementations, and the commit that added them
findings.why: CONVENTIONS#comments: archaeology 'is never a comment'. Past-tense accounts of what the code used to do can only age, and several already have. SM-47 cleaned implementation and build comments but did not cover tests. A short sentence in the present tense saying what each case pins would carry the same value.
findings.suggested_fix: Run a comments-only pass over the unit's tests in SM-47's style. Keep the present-tense contract each case pins ("a degenerate triangle contains nothing") and drop the narratives of what was, was replaced, or was deleted.
findings.verify_reason: thread_pool_tests.cpp:10-14 'THERE WERE NO TESTS HERE UNTIL THE HEADER WAS RESHAPED...' (file is 144 lines, so the cited 512 is wrong). Verified the past-tense narratives at triangle_tests.cpp:17, vector2_tests.cpp:88, contacts_tests.cpp:113, ericson_math_tests.cpp:202, widget_tests.cpp:153, narrow_phase_tests.cpp:138 and inflate_tests.cpp:75. CONVENTIONS 'Archaeology... This is never a comment.' SM-47's targets are only engine/cmake files, so this is not tracked.

findings.title: 'Just touching' and 'just not touching' fixtures do not sit at the boundary their comments name
findings.why: Circle a has radius 10 at the origin and b has radius 5 at (10,5). The centres are about 11.18 apart against a radius sum of 15, so b overlaps by about 3.8 units. That is not 'just touching'. In the circle-triangle and circle-quad cases, the 'just not touching' shapes have their nearest point at (10,10), about 14.1 from the centre and over 4 units clear. Their 'touching' siblings sit on y=0. The y offset moved these fixtures away from the boundary, so the boundary these comments describe is never tested.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the fixtures on the boundary: Circle(15.0f - epsilon_f, 0.0f, 5.0f) for touching. For the triangle and quad 'not touching' cases, use y=0 to match their touching siblings, e.g. Triangle((10+eps,0),(20,0),(10+eps,20)) and RectangleF(10+eps, 0, 10, 10).
findings.verify_reason: shape_intersect_tests.cpp:271-272 has 'just touching' b = Circle(10-eps, 5, 5) against a=Circle(0,0,10): the distance is about 11.18 against a radius sum of 15, a deep overlap. Lines 319-321 have a 'just not touching' triangle at y=10 while its touching sibling (313-315) is at y=0, so it is far from the boundary. The circle-quad case follows the same pattern.

findings.title: Edge-order test claims every slot matches its accessor but skips Quad and RectangleRotated slots 1 and 2
findings.evidence: "These checks are the contract: each slot is the matching named accessor." ... "CHECK(quad_edges[0] == quad.edge_0());\n\t\tCHECK(quad_edges[3] == quad.edge_3());" ... "CHECK(rr_edges[0] == rr.edge_0());\n\t\tCHECK(rr_edges[3] == rr.edge_3());" (quad.h:43-44 and rectangle_rotated.h:70-71 declare edge_1()/edge_2())
findings.why: The comment says order mistakes once put three of four faces on the wrong side, yet the test leaves edge_1/edge_2 unchecked for two of the four shapes. A swap of the middle two edges in Quad::edges() or RectangleRotated::edges() would pass while the test claims to pin the contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Add CHECK(quad_edges[1] == quad.edge_1()); CHECK(quad_edges[2] == quad.edge_2()); and the same two checks for rr_edges.
findings.verify_reason: shape_tests.cpp:51-52 and 58-59 check only slots 0 and 3 for Quad and RectangleRotated. quad.h:43-44 and rectangle_rotated.h:70-71 declare edge_1() and edge_2(), and the comment at lines 24-31 claims every slot is checked.

findings.title: Public data members carry the private trailing underscore
findings.why: CONVENTIONS: private members end in `_` and public fields are bare. Here the suffix wrongly marks these as private while the cases read them directly.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename them to capture_before, capture_after and steps (public, bare), or make them private with noun accessors.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: application_loop_tests.cpp:92-96 declares capture_before_, capture_after_ and steps_ in the public section before 'private:'. CONVENTIONS reserves the trailing _ for private members. This is a cosmetic naming slip in one test fixture.

findings.title: Hidden-Application option setup is copy-pasted into eight cases
findings.why: Every new live-Application case copies four lines, and a change to the headless recipe (for example a new option every hidden test needs) has to be made eight times.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `hidden_options(const wchar_t* class_name)` helper in each file's unnamed namespace, as join_state_tests.cpp does.
findings.verify_reason: window_class_name, visible, view_capacity and max_threads are repeated at application_loop_tests.cpp:170, 200, 263, 326 and 375, and at application_resize_tests.cpp:76, 108 and 146. join_state_tests.cpp:21-29 factors the same setup into options(). This is minor test duplication.

findings.title: StepTimer cases sit in the app options test and rely on a transitive include
findings.evidence: "TEST_CASE(\"accepted frame rates always produce an advancing timer period\")" uses StepTimer::TicksPerSecond, SetTargetElapsedTicks and Tick (lines 320-352). The file includes only engine/app/application.h and engine/math/vector2i.h. StepTimer is engine/core/step_timer.h, which arrives only through application.h. tests/core/step_position_tests.cpp is the other StepTimer test file.
findings.why: About half the case tests core's StepTimer rejecting zero, negative, infinite and NaN periods. It sits in an app test file and compiles only because of an indirect include. Removing step_timer.h from application.h would break it, and the core module's own coverage is split.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the options-validation half here. Move the SetTargetElapsed*/Tick assertions to a tests/core StepTimer test that includes engine/core/step_timer.h directly, or at least include it here.
findings.verify_reason: The case is at lines 103-135, not 320-352, because the file has 175 lines. It uses StepTimer::TicksPerSecond, SetTargetElapsed*, and Tick. The file includes only application.h and vector2i.h, and StepTimer arrives through application.h:11. The case also legitimately ties target_fps validation to the timer, so its placement is partly justified.

findings.title: Fixed-name temp folders are never cleaned up after a failure and can read leftovers from a crashed run
findings.why: A failing REQUIRE skips remove_all, and the next run reuses the same folder. That is the failure mode the shared ScratchFile helper was written to prevent, so these cases bypass the suite's own fixture policy.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a small RAII scratch-directory helper beside ScratchFile in tests/scratch_file.h (unique name, removal in its destructor) and use it in both cases.
findings.verify_reason: Both cases use fixed temp-folder names, and REQUIRE precedes remove_all (content_root_tests.cpp:154-185 and 191-211). However, each run rewrites the manifest and binary file with ofstream before reading, so a leftover from a crashed run is overwritten rather than read as input. The only real cost is a stray temp folder after a failure.

findings.title: The child names window_tests.cpp as its launcher; startup_info_tests.cpp launches it, and the exit codes are defined twice under different names
findings.why: Both comments name the wrong file. That file has no names for these codes. The protocol is two unrelated sets of literals with different identifiers, and the failure code (30) is not named at all on the reading side, so the two sides can drift apart silently.
findings.suggested_fix: Change both comments to name startup_info_tests.cpp. Put the three codes in one small shared header under tests/app/ that both translation units include, or at least use the same names on both sides.
findings.verify_reason: startup_child.cpp:17 says 'The child window_tests.cpp launches' and line 50 says 'window_tests.cpp's names'. Both are wrong: only startup_info_tests.cpp uses LABRADOR_STARTUP_CHILD (line 30), and window_tests.cpp never mentions it. The CMakeLists comment at line 24, 'The child startup_info_tests.cpp launches', is correct, so that part of the claim is refuted. The reading-side constants are at startup_info_tests.cpp:17-18, not 95-97. The duplicated literals 10/20 are minor: if they drift, the CHECK at lines 53 and 59 fails loudly.

findings.title: The startup child copies Application::create_window's option mapping by hand
findings.evidence: startup_child.cpp:58-68 "const ApplicationOptions defaults; WindowOptions options; options.window_class_name = defaults.window_class_name; options.window_title = defaults.window_title; ... options.min_window_height = defaults.min_window_height;" duplicates engine/app/application.cpp:182-192 "WindowOptions window_options; window_options.window_class_name = this->options_.window_class_name; ... window_options.min_window_height = this->options_.min_window_height;"
findings.why: The test claims to make 'a window made as Application makes one from default ApplicationOptions'. Nothing ties the two lists together: a field added to WindowOptions and forwarded by Application would be left out here, and the STARTUPINFO test would keep passing on a different window from the one games get.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the ApplicationOptions-to-WindowOptions mapping into one function, for example a free `window_options_from(const ApplicationOptions&, Vector2I client)` in the app module. Have Application::create_window and the child both call it.
findings.verify_reason: startup_child.cpp:58-68 does mirror application.cpp create_window's field-by-field mapping, and nothing ties the two together. The drift risk is real but narrow: one STARTUPINFO visibility test whose deciding fields are visible and fullscreen. Adding a new engine function only to serve a test is a heavy fix for that risk.

findings.title: Window and content-root tests narrate the review probes they came from
findings.why: How the tests came about belongs in git history. docs/review/ is frozen, so these comments tie live tests to a historical ledger.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the present-tense statements of what each case pins. Delete the provenance sentences ("were probes", "the probe the review ran", "the restore fix", "The review's reproduction").
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: window_tests.cpp:23-24 says 'Both were probes against a hidden window before they were tests', and content_root_tests.cpp:20-21 says 'The review's reproduction was...'. Both are provenance narratives. The G6 IDs are partly useful as a pointer, but the 'were probes' sentences are archaeology.

findings.title: Win32 lParam bits are spelled inline repeatedly, and the Loss table is defined twice
findings.why: Magic shift counts (24 = extended, 30 = previous state, 31 = transition) are unexplained at each use. The duplicated table means a new focus-loss message has to be added in two places.
findings.suggested_fix: Hoist one `focus_losses` array and `key_down_lparam` / `key_up_lparam` helpers (named for the extended/previous/transition bits) into the file's unnamed namespace.
findings.verify_reason: window_tests.cpp:374 and 455 both define 'struct Loss { UINT message; WPARAM parameter; }' with a table starting at WM_KILLFOCUS. The inline lParam bit shifts appear at 326, 425, 473 and 475. keyboard_input_tests.cpp:22 already has key_position().

findings.title: size_entry duplicates RecordingNotify's size format, and client_of ignores the Win32 result
findings.evidence: Lines 52-55 in RecordingNotify: "this->log.push_back(\"size \" + std::to_string(width) + \"x\" + std::to_string(height));". Lines 713-716: "std::string size_entry(LONG width, LONG height) { return \"size \" + std::to_string(width) + \"x\" + std::to_string(height); }". Lines 727-731: "RECT client_of(HWND handle) { RECT client = {}; GetClientRect(handle, &client); return client; }", whereas application_resize_tests.cpp:26 does "REQUIRE(GetClientRect(window, &client) != FALSE);". window_extent at line 970 is unchecked as well.
findings.why: The log format is defined twice, so a change to one breaks comparisons without the cause being obvious. An unchecked GetClientRect turns a failed call into a 0x0 size, and the case then fails on an unrelated size mismatch.
findings.suggested_fix: Move size_entry above RecordingNotify and have on_window_size_changed call it. REQUIRE the BOOL results in client_of and window_extent.
findings.verify_reason: window_tests.cpp:51-55 (RecordingNotify) and 713-716 (size_entry) build the same 'size WxH' string. client_of at 727-731 and window_extent at about 968-972 ignore the BOOL results, while monitor_of right beside them REQUIREs its result.

findings.title: PerMonitorAware ignores a failed SetThreadDpiAwarenessContext
findings.evidence: "explicit PerMonitorAware(DPI_AWARENESS_CONTEXT context = DPI_AWARENESS_CONTEXT_PER_MONITOR_AWARE_V2) : previous_(SetThreadDpiAwarenessContext(context)) {}". The destructor restores previous_ unconditionally. Only two of the five DPI cases REQUIRE the window's awareness. The WM_GETDPISCALEDSIZE, WM_DPICHANGED and full-screen DPI cases do not.
findings.why: If the call fails, it returns NULL. The guard then 'restores' NULL, and three cases run on an unaware thread while appearing to test per-monitor behaviour.
findings.suggested_fix: REQUIRE(previous_ != nullptr) in the constructor, or move the existing AreDpiAwarenessContextsEqual REQUIRE into the guard so that every case gets it.
findings.verify_reason: PerMonitorAware (about lines 945-963) never checks the result of SetThreadDpiAwarenessContext. AreDpiAwarenessContextsEqual is REQUIREd only at lines 1007 and 1098, so the cases at 1022, 1045 and 1072 rely on the guard. On a supported Windows 10+ system the call is very unlikely to fail.

findings.title: Include groups are run together in some files, and others rely on transitive standard headers
findings.why: This is inconsistent with sibling files and with CONVENTIONS' grouped order (own/doctest, engine, external, standard). Leaning on transitive includes breaks when an engine header stops pulling them in.
findings.suggested_fix: Separate the groups with blank lines as the other tests do, and add the missing <vector>/<array> includes.
findings.verify_reason: asset_manifest_loader_tests.cpp:1-7 runs its include groups together. content_root_tests.cpp uses std::vector at line 208 without including <vector>; draw_tests.cpp uses std::vector at line 50 without it; arena_tests.cpp uses std::array at line 21 without <array>. All rely on transitive includes.

findings.title: Later cases sit outside the file's TEST_SUITE
findings.why: Running the suite by name (`-ts=AssetManifestLoaderTests`, `-ts=JsonTests`) silently skips these cases. That membership is accidental, the result of appending cases rather than a choice.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the appended cases inside the existing TEST_SUITE blocks, or drop TEST_SUITE from these files consistently.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: the AssetManifestLoaderTests namespace and suite close at line 184 of asset_manifest_loader_tests.cpp, and cases follow at 187-260. In json_tests.cpp the suites close at 664 and a case follows. Nothing in CI selects tests by -ts, so the effect is only on a manual suite filter.

findings.title: Configuration counts in test preambles are stale ("ALL FOUR", "all six")
findings.why: These counts are fragile census claims that are already wrong, the same kind SM-47 removed elsewhere. The point being made is that the file runs everywhere, not a particular number.
findings.suggested_fix: Write "in every configuration" (as sprite_sheet_loader_tests.cpp and sound_bank_loader_tests.cpp already do) and drop the number.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: resource_loader_tests.cpp:20 says 'IT RUNS IN ALL FOUR CONFIGURATIONS' and audio_resources_tests.cpp:25 says 'all six configurations'. AGENTS.md lists more preset configurations than either number. These are stale census claims in comments, with no functional effect.

findings.title: Comment about pinning wave order sits on the source_path assertion
findings.why: The rationale belongs to the `definition.waves == waves` check at line 275. Attached to the source_path check, it misdirects the reader, and source_path itself gets no stated reason.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the comment above line 274/275, and give the source_path check its own one-line reason, or none.
findings.verify_reason: The comment is real but mislined. sound_bank_loader_tests.cpp is 159 lines; the wave-order comment is at lines 47-49, sitting on CHECK(definition.source_path == ...) at line 50. The waves == check it describes is at line 41.

findings.title: Five cases repeat the hook and warning-mode bookkeeping
findings.evidence: Five cases capture "const _CRT_ALLOC_HOOK initial_hook = _CrtGetAllocHook(); const int initial_mode = _CrtSetReportMode(_CRT_WARN, _CRTDBG_REPORT_MODE);" (lines 174, 236, 309, 363, 471). Each follows its scope with "REQUIRE_FALSE(sample.hook_conflict); REQUIRE(_CrtGetAllocHook() == initial_hook); REQUIRE(_CrtSetReportMode(_CRT_WARN, _CRTDBG_REPORT_MODE) == initial_mode);". The first case runs that block twice, once more for its unwind probe (lines 213-215).
findings.why: The restoration contract is the core safety property of this fixture, and it is written out six times. A change to what a scope restores, such as a new CRT setting, has to be made in every copy.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a helper, for example `struct CrtBaseline { hook; mode; void require_restored(const AllocationFailureSample&) const; }`, or a function that runs one refusal and checks restoration. Have each case call it once.
findings.verify_reason: The capture/restore triple appears at lines 174-175/192-194, 213-215, 236-256, 309-329, 363-386 and 471-490 as described. These are three-line test assertions, and a missed copy in a future change would weaken one case, not break the engine. The duplication is real but low.

findings.title: 'compiles in all six configurations' matches no current census
findings.evidence:
// no content needs no device and compiles in all six configurations, and none

AudioTests is built in every preset (12 named presets, 8 CI configurations in tests/ctest_inventory.json, 3 audio backends).
findings.why: The count matches neither presets, CI configurations nor backends, so a reader cannot check it. The claim intended is 'every configuration'.
findings.suggested_fix: Change it to 'compiles in every configuration'.
findings.verify_reason: audio_resources_tests.cpp:25 says 'compiles in all six configurations', which matches no current census of presets, CI configurations or backends.

findings.title: WAV chunk walker silently truncates a chunk that runs past the end of the file
findings.evidence:
tag, size = data[at:at + 4], struct.unpack_from("<I", data, at + 4)[0]
        found[tag] = data[at + 8:at + 8 + size]
findings.why: Python slicing clamps silently, so a truncated or corrupt ping_adpcm.wav produces a short chunk instead of an error. A data chunk cut at a block boundary still passes `len(payload) % block_align == 0`, and the fact-chunk duration (which is not checked against the payload) would then describe more samples than the bank holds. The result is a fixture whose decode silently differs from the pinned msacm32 hash. A repeated chunk tag is also silently overwritten by the last one.
findings.suggested_fix: Raise if `at + 8 + size > len(data)` or if a tag repeats. Check `duration <= (len(payload) // block_align) * samples_per_block`.
findings.verify_reason: Lines 36-44 match exactly: slices clamp silently, a repeated tag overwrites, and fact duration (line 59) is never compared with len(payload)//block_align*samples_per_block. Because a regenerated bank's hash is re-derived from msacm32 decoding that same bank (docstring 21-24), a truncated input would be pinned rather than caught. The known item at :37 is about using assert for validation, which is a different problem.

findings.title: Fixture generator writes unnamed format constants and validates input with assert
findings.evidence:
struct.pack_into("<3I", out, 0, 0x444E4257, 46, 44)
...
struct.pack_into("<II64sIIIIQ", out, header_size,
                 0x00010000, 1, b"adpcm", entry_size, 64, 4, 0, 0)
and line 51: assert (tag, channels, bits) == (2, 1, 4), "expected mono MS-ADPCM"
findings.why: The WBND signature, tool and header versions, and bank flags are bare literals, while the script names other layout sizes (header_size, bank_size, entry_size). The input checks use `assert`, which `python -O` removes, so a wrong WAV would then produce a corrupt fixture without any error.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the signature and version constants next to STANDARD_COEFFICIENTS. Raise SystemExit or ValueError for the input checks instead of using assert.
findings.verify_reason: make_adpcm_bank.py:71 has 'struct.pack_into("<3I", out, 0, 0x444E4257, 46, 44)' with unnamed constants, and line 77 has 0x00010000. Lines 51-60 validate the input with assert, which python -O strips. This is a fixture generator, so the impact is small.

findings.title: Backend-specific tests are filed inconsistently: subfolders for render, flat files for audio, input and render/null
findings.evidence: render: tests/render/d3d12/*.cpp, tests/render/vulkan/*.cpp, tests/render/gl/texture_tests.cpp, tests/render/web/, tests/render/win32/. But tests/render/null_tests.cpp, tests/render/null_resource_tests.cpp and tests/render/null_test_harness.h are flat. audio: tests/audio/null_tests.cpp, tests/audio/webaudio_tests.cpp, tests/audio/xaudio2_recovery_tests.cpp are all flat. input: tests/input/xinput_gamepad_tests.cpp, tests/input/standard_gamepad_tests.cpp, tests/input/web_vibration_tests.cpp are flat. app: tests/app/dom_events_tests.cpp is flat but tests/app/web/window_page.cpp is in a subfolder.
findings.why: Finding a backend's tests needs a different rule in each module, and the null render backend is the only render backend whose tests are not in a backend folder. Two files are also both named null_tests.cpp, in different modules.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose one rule, such as tests/<module>/<backend>/ for backend-only sources, and apply it when these files are next changed. Keep names and ctest registration the same.
findings.verify_reason: The layout is as described: tests/render/d3d12, vulkan and gl are subfolders, while null_tests.cpp, null_resource_tests.cpp and null_test_harness.h are flat. Audio and input backend tests are also flat. code-hygiene.md:589 records the null_tests split but not a folder rule. No convention requires a layout, so this is only a minor organizational inconsistency.

findings.title: Comment says every recorded call names the effect's voice; only one pair is compared
findings.why: Calls 2-7 (stop, stop, pause, resume, set_volume, set_pitch) are never checked for the voice they target. A SoundBank that forwarded one of those verbs to the wrong voice index would pass, which defeats the check the comment describes.
findings.suggested_fix: Loop over played[1..8] and CHECK(played[i].voice == played[1].voice).
findings.verify_reason: null_tests.cpp:205-209: the comment says 'every one of them names the voice', but only played[1].voice == played[8].voice is checked. Calls 2-7 are unchecked.

findings.title: "resumes at it" is claimed but resume is never exercised
findings.evidence:
// The paused effect took the level now, and resumes at it.
CHECK(fixture.second->effect_state(second_theme) == SoundState::paused);
findings.why: The comment promises that the paused effect resumes at the new level, but the case only checks that it is still paused. No resume_effect call is made, so nothing confirms a resume would not reapply a stale level.
findings.suggested_fix: Call fixture.second->resume_effect(second_theme), then assert that no further set_voice_volume with the old level is recorded and the state is playing. Otherwise trim the comment to "took the level while paused".
findings.verify_reason: null_tests.cpp:416-417: the comment says 'and resumes at it', but the case never calls resume_effect. It only checks that the effect is paused. The recorded set_voice_volume at before+2 shows the level was taken while paused, but not that the effect resumes at it.

findings.title: "still runs the arithmetic it owns" cannot observe the arithmetic and repeats the previous case
findings.why: Its own comment says "A bank with nothing behind it still cannot show you the result". The case asserts only that out-of-range levels do not throw, which the "plays nothing, and every verb still runs" case at line 92 already covers. The name promises more than the case can check, and the clamp is really pinned in null_tests.cpp.
findings.suggested_fix: Fold the out-of-range arguments into the line-92 case as "nonsense levels are accepted", and drop the claim about arithmetic. Leave the clamp to null_tests.cpp.
findings.verify_reason: The case's own long comment explicitly says it cannot see the clamp and defers to null_tests.cpp. 'Repeats the previous case' is partly false: the line-92 case passes in-range levels only, while this one passes out-of-range ones. The only real issue is that the name overpromises. Trivial.

findings.title: "a group's volume reaches this device as plain level calls" asserts no level
findings.why: The name claims the group product reaches the Web Audio device, but every assertion is CHECK_NOTHROW or a play/pause state. No volume is read back, so a backend that dropped or mis-multiplied the level would pass. As written, the case only shows that the calls do not throw.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename it to what it shows (group calls are accepted and do not disturb voice state), or expose the backend's last-set voice gain to tests and assert the products (0.25, 0.125, then 0.5).
findings.verify_reason: Accurate: every group-volume step is CHECK_NOTHROW, and the only state reads are paused and playing. The case's own comment says the arithmetic is SoundBank's, above the seam, and null_tests.cpp pins the products. So this is a test name that overclaims, not missing coverage. Low.

findings.title: The critical_error assertions check the fake's own field, which DeviceRecovery never reads
findings.evidence: RecoveryEngine has "bool critical_error = false;" (line 19), and its Reset() sets "this->critical_error = false;" (line 33). The case "XAudio2 keeps retrying after reset clears the critical error" sets engine.critical_error = true and then asserts "CHECK_FALSE(engine.critical_error);" (lines 81-83). Line 62 does the same. grep for 'critical' in engine/audio/xaudio2/device_recovery.h finds only the comment on line 7. The template calls only engine.Update() and engine.Reset().
findings.why: These checks can only fail if the test's own fake changes. They test nothing in the engine, but the case name suggests the recovery policy handles a critical-error flag. A reader would take it as cover for behaviour the code does not have.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the critical_error field and its assertions. Rename the case to the behaviour it actually covers, for example 'keeps retrying a reset that finds no output, and a fresh loss starts a new interval'. If the DirectXTK quirk needs recording, keep the comment in device_recovery.h only.
findings.verify_reason: The fake's critical_error field and its CHECK_FALSE assertions (lines 19, 33, 62, 81-83) are tautological, and device_recovery.h mentions critical only in a comment at line 7. However, the case does cover real policy: repeated retries, success, and a fresh loss that does not inherit the old delay (resets==4). The fake records the DirectXTK quirk the header comment describes. Only the naming and the self-checks are hygiene noise.

findings.title: Three tests hand-roll the whole-file reader that engine/core/byte_reader.h already exports
findings.evidence: Identical bodies `std::ifstream file(path, std::ios::binary | std::ios::ate); REQUIRE(file.good()); const std::streamoff size = file.tellg(); std::vector<unsigned char> bytes(static_cast<size_t>(size)); file.seekg(0, std::ios::beg); file.read(...); return bytes;` at tests/audio/xwb_file_tests.cpp:33 `file_bytes`, tests/render/dds_file_tests.cpp:36 `quad_bytes` and tests/render/sprite_font_file_tests.cpp:42 `whole_font`. engine/core/byte_reader.h:60 declares `std::vector<unsigned char> read_file_bytes(const std::string& path);`, which tests/app/content_root_tests.cpp:208 already calls. The same files also hand-roll little-endian pokes (`put_u32` xwb_file_tests.cpp:52, `poke` dds_file_tests.cpp:48). engine/assets/json.cpp:78 reads with its own chunked ifstream loop instead of read_file_bytes.
findings.why: Three copies of an unchecked read (no check after `file.read`) sit beside a tested engine helper that reports short reads. The engine's own JSON loader also reads files a second way, with different exception types for a missing file (runtime_error vs read_file_bytes' out_of_range).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the three test helpers with `labrador::read_file_bytes(...)`, and move a `put_u32_le` into the shared tests helper header next to ScratchFile. Decide whether read_json_file should use read_file_bytes, and align the missing-file exception type if it does.
findings.verify_reason: The bodies are identical at xwb_file_tests.cpp:33 file_bytes, dds_file_tests.cpp:36 quad_bytes and sprite_font_file_tests.cpp:42 whole_font, none checking the read. byte_reader.h:60 declares read_file_bytes with out_of_range/runtime_error semantics. json.cpp:78ff reads with its own chunked ifstream and throws runtime_error on a missing file. Accurate, and low.

findings.title: Hand-rolled xorshift Rng duplicates engine/core/random.h, which exists for exactly this reason
findings.evidence:
"// A deterministic scatter. std::rand's sequence is not specified across implementations, and a test that only reproduces on one library is not a regression test.
	struct Rng
	{
		uint32_t state = 0x9e3779b9u;" ... "this->state ^= this->state << 13;". engine/core/random.h: "A stream of pseudo-random numbers that is the same on every platform" with uniform_float(min,max). tests/collision/narrow_phase_tests.cpp:537 already uses labrador::Random for the same purpose. grep '<< 13;' across engine/samples/tests/bench finds only this file.
findings.why: There are two sources of cross-platform deterministic randomness in one test directory. The engine's Random states the same rationale and has the same API shape (uniform_float plays the role of Rng::in). The local copy also uses unqualified uint32_t, where the engine spells std::uint32_t.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace Rng with labrador::Random (seeded), and Rng::in(low, high) with Random::uniform_float(low, high). Delete the struct and its comment.
findings.verify_reason: broad_phase_tests.cpp:69-90 does hand-roll a xorshift Rng with unqualified uint32_t. engine/core/random.h gives the same cross-platform rationale and has uniform_float, and narrow_phase_tests.cpp:537/659 already uses labrador::Random. The duplication is real, but it is a 20-line test-local helper, so low severity.

findings.title: Scenario behaviour keyed on a string comparison of its display name
findings.evidence: "if (std::string(scenario.name) == \"with a giant\")\n\t\t\t{\n\t\t\t\tboxes.push_back(std::make_unique<Box>("
findings.why: The Scenario struct is the table that drives the loop, yet one behaviour is hidden behind matching its CAPTURE label. Renaming the label silently drops the giant, and with it the large-object coverage the comment says the scenario exists for. This is also the only reason <string> is included.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `bool with_giant` field to Scenario, set it in the table, and test the field.
findings.verify_reason: broad_phase_tests.cpp:193 reads `if (std::string(scenario.name) == "with a giant")`. The Scenario struct (162-169) has no flag, and <string> (line 12) is used only for this comparison.

findings.title: const object declared only to be const_cast back for find_contacts
findings.evidence: "const Box only(RectangleF(0.0f, 0.0f, 10.0f, 10.0f), world_layer, mover_layer);\n\t\tstd::vector<CollisionObject*> one{ const_cast<Box*>(&only) };"
findings.why: find_contacts takes non-const CollisionObject* (dispatch may mutate). Declaring the object const and casting it away is the only const_cast in the unit. It gains nothing and would be undefined behaviour if the callee ever wrote through the pointer.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare `Box only(...)` without const and push `&only`.
findings.verify_reason: broad_phase_tests.cpp:229-230 declares `const Box only(...)` and then does `const_cast<Box*>(&only)`, exactly as quoted.

findings.title: Rectangle CollisionObject stub is written four times across collision and scene tests
findings.evidence: tests/collision/broad_phase_tests.cpp:30 "class Box final : public CollisionObject"; tests/collision/contacts_tests.cpp:31 "class TestObject : public CollisionObject"; tests/scene/scene_tests.cpp:55 "class TestCollider : public CollisionObject"; tests/scene/order_tests.cpp:60 "class Collider final : public CollisionObject". Each holds a RectangleF, layer_/mask_/tag_ and for_deletion_, and repeats the same eight overrides (update, draw, bounds, shape, layer, mask, tag, on_contact, for_deletion, set_for_deletion).
findings.why: CollisionObject's pure-virtual surface is duplicated four times, so any change to that interface (a new pure virtual, a signature change) must be made in four test files. tests/ui/stub_widget.h already solves the same problem for UiWidget with one shared stub header.
findings.suggested_fix: Add tests/collision/stub_collider.h (alongside stub_widget.h's pattern): a rectangle collider with layer/mask/tag, for_deletion and a contact log. Have the four files use or derive from it, keeping file-specific extras (draw markers, make_fixed, retire_on_contact) as small subclasses.
findings.verify_reason: The four CollisionObject subclasses exist, but the evidence is inaccurate. order_tests' Collider has no layer_, mask_ or tag_ (it returns 0) and draws markers. broad_phase's Box has no tag_. Each on_contact does something different: a received log with retire/separate, a contact counter with last_other and make_fixed, or nothing. What they share is the pure-virtual boilerplate. That is ordinary test-double repetition, not one stub copied four times.

findings.title: std::min/std::max and std::is_same_v used without their headers
findings.why: Both files rely on transitive includes. contacts_tests.cpp and state_context_tests.cpp include <algorithm> explicitly for the same purpose. A change to partitioner.h or registry.h could break these tests for an unrelated reason.
findings.suggested_fix: Add #include <algorithm> to partitioner_tests.cpp and #include <type_traits> to registry_tests.cpp.
findings.verify_reason: partitioner_tests.cpp includes only partitioner.h, <stdexcept> and <vector>, and uses std::min/std::max at 92-93. partitioner.h includes only <utility> and <vector>. registry_tests.cpp:221 uses std::is_same_v without <type_traits>, and registry.h does not include it.

findings.title: PascalCase wrapper namespaces violate the one-lowercase-word namespace rule
findings.evidence:
namespace NameTableTests
{
	TEST_SUITE("NameTableTests")

Also: tests/core/registry_tests.cpp:214 `namespace RegistryTests`, tests/core/thread_pool_tests.cpp:525 `namespace ThreadPoolTests`.
findings.why: CONVENTIONS#namespaces: 'Namespaces | one lowercase word'. These namespaces also add nothing, because each one wraps a TEST_SUITE of the same name. No sibling test file uses the pattern.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the namespace wrappers and keep the TEST_SUITE, as the other files do.
findings.verify_reason: name_table_tests.cpp:37, registry_tests.cpp:50 and thread_pool_tests.cpp:23 have PascalCase wrapper namespaces. But 'No sibling test file uses the pattern' is false: asset_manifest_loader_tests, json_tests, resource_loader_tests, deadzone_tests, direction_tests, gamepad_tests, keyboard_tests and others use it too. It is a widespread test pattern, not three outliers, and the CONVENTIONS namespace rule is written about engine/game namespaces.

findings.title: Compile-time type identity checked with a runtime CHECK, without <type_traits>
findings.why: The comment itself says this is a compile-time property. Checking it at runtime only reports a mismatch when the test runs instead of failing the build, and the file relies on a transitive include for std::is_same_v.
findings.suggested_fix: Use static_assert(std::is_same_v<...>) at namespace scope (or keep it in the case), and #include <type_traits>.
findings.verify_reason: registry_tests.cpp:221 has `CHECK(std::is_same_v<...>)`. The includes (lines 1-6) are doctest, registry.h, memory, stdexcept, string and utility, with no <type_traits>, and the nearby comment calls it a compile-time property.

findings.title: Five copies of a comment, each claiming its own test is 'the first thing in the tree' to depend on a deviceless Renderer
findings.why: A claim of being 'the first' can be true of at most one place, and here it is pasted five times. It is also stale: null render tests, cull/fanout/order tests and text_widget_tests now all depend on a deviceless Renderer. This is copy-paste noise that turns census archaeology into five false sentences.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the comment from all five sites, or keep one neutral line once, near a shared helper (e.g. "a Renderer needs no device to be constructed").
findings.verify_reason: state_context_tests.cpp lines 194-195, 212-213, 243-244, 273-274 and 298-299 each say 'is the first thing in the tree to depend on it'. That is real copy-paste and a false census claim, but it is harmless comment noise, not medium.

findings.title: Two cases build the same throwing-init drain and differ only in how the context ends
findings.why: These are the same fixture with two endings (scope exit and clear()). The setup lambda is duplicated verbatim, so a change to the failing-drain scenario has to be made twice.
findings.suggested_fix: Fold both into one TEST_CASE with SUBCASE("clear()") and SUBCASE("leaving scope"), or extract a helper that arms the failing drain on a given state.
findings.verify_reason: state_context_tests.cpp:590-618 ('leaving scope drops a queued state') and the later 'clear drops a queued state that never became live' build the same level/on_update lambda with bad (throwing on_init) and never. The setup is essentially verbatim; only the ending (scope exit vs clear()) and the log.clear placement differ.

findings.title: Comment claims Scene::draw waits on the pool unconditionally; it returns early before touching it
findings.why: The comment is false: with one view or fewer, Scene::draw returns before reaching the pool. With two or more it always submits at least one range. No caller performs the empty wait this comment cites as the reason for the test.
findings.suggested_fix: Justify the case on the pool's own contract (an empty wait returns), or delete the Scene::draw sentence.
findings.verify_reason: thread_pool_tests.cpp:128-129 says Scene::draw waits unconditionally even when nothing was submitted. scene.cpp:230-235 returns early when count<=1 or there is no pool or partitioner, and otherwise submits ranges before waiting. The comment is false, but the test itself (an empty wait returns) is valid pool contract, so only a rationale sentence is wrong.

findings.title: Test namespaces are PascalCase, against the one-lowercase-word namespace rule
findings.evidence:
namespace DeadzoneTests
