In this unit also: tests/assets/asset_manifest_loader_tests.cpp:22 `namespace AssetManifestLoaderTests`, json_tests.cpp:71 `namespace JsonTests`, resource_loader_tests.cpp:92 `namespace ResourceLoaderTests`, direction_tests.cpp:55 `namespace DirectionTests`, gamepad_tests.cpp:36 `namespace GamepadTests`, keyboard_tests.cpp:71 `namespace KeyboardTests`, mouse_tests.cpp:42 `namespace MouseTests`, touch_tests.cpp:51 `namespace TouchTests` (git grep '^namespace [A-Z]' over tests/samples/engine: 13 hits, 9 here).
findings.why: CONVENTIONS: "PascalCase names a type ... Namespaces: one lowercase word." Newer siblings in the same folders (vibration_tests.cpp, standard_gamepad_tests.cpp, null_tests.cpp) use only an unnamed namespace, so there are now two styles. The TEST_SUITE string already groups the cases.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the named namespace wrappers. The TEST_SUITE names stay, and helpers go in the existing unnamed namespace.
findings.verify_reason: git grep finds 13 PascalCase test namespaces, including core/ and render/ beyond those listed. Each wraps a TEST_SUITE of the same name. CONVENTIONS' naming table does say 'Namespaces: one lowercase word', so the inconsistency is real. It is limited to test-file organisation and has no effect on behaviour.

findings.title: Input test comments recount defects in former client code
findings.why: Each states what was or what someone once did, not what the code requires. The webaudio comment depends outright on git history, which is the archaeology CONVENTIONS rules out.
findings.suggested_fix: Restate each as the present contract ("rescaled so the live range starts at 0, not offset by the threshold"; "a button held across a transition is not a press"). Remove the defect and commit references.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: deadzone_tests.cpp:23-26 ('the defect it was written for: the paint-shooter...'), gamepad_tests.cpp:99 ('the bug the two hand-primed edge detectors kept having') and webaudio_tests.cpp:24-25 ('the commit that added this file says how it was checked'). The sprite_sheet_loader comment is weaker, closer to rationale. Low.

findings.title: File preamble tells the history of a header's false claim instead of what the file tests
findings.why: This describes what a previous version of another file wrongly said, which CONVENTIONS names as archaeology ("a sentence narrating what this very comment used to say"). A reader of the current file learns nothing about pad_direction or DirectionRepeat from it.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace it with one present-tense line, for example "pad_direction and DirectionRepeat: the stick-to-menu-direction producer; hold-to-repeat gets the most cases because it is the part that goes wrong."
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed at direction_tests.cpp:12-19: 'The producer engine/ui/navigation.h spent its whole life claiming existed... That header said...' narrates what another file used to say, which is archaeology. The rest of the preamble, from line 20 ('NO DEVICE...'), is present-tense rationale. Comment-only, so low.

findings.title: Repeat-rate test states an exact rhythm but accepts anything from 2 to 9 moves
findings.why: The default rhythm over 60 frames gives a fixed count of about 7. A regression that halved the repeat rate, or dropped the long first delay, would still land inside (1, 10). The comment gives the expected count but the check is loose.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert the exact count that the default intervals produce (computed from the DirectionRepeat defaults), or at least the moves seen before 0.4 s and after it.
findings.verify_reason: direction_tests.cpp:191-193: the bounds are 1 < moves < 10 while the comment states an exact rhythm. Halving the default rate would still pass. Other cases pin the rhythm, but only with explicit (0.4, 0.1) constructor arguments, so the defaults are not pinned. The case's stated aim, 'far fewer than sixty', limits the impact.

findings.title: Long-frame comment's arithmetic does not match the 0.65 step
findings.evidence:
// A quarter of a second in one frame, which is four repeats' worth.
CHECK(repeat.update(Direction::up, 0.65f) == Direction::up);
findings.why: The step is 0.65 s. Past the 0.4 s first delay that leaves 0.25 s, which is two and a half repeats at the 0.1 s interval, not four. Neither "a quarter of a second in one frame" nor "four repeats' worth" describes the value passed, so a reader checking the no-burst rule against the comment gets confused.
findings.suggested_fix: Say "0.65 s in one frame: past the first delay by 0.25 s, two repeats' worth", or pick a step that matches the existing wording.
findings.verify_reason: direction_tests.cpp:234-235: the step is 0.65 s with a 0.4 s first delay and a 0.1 s interval. 0.65 is not a quarter second, and the 0.25 s past the delay is 2.5 repeats, not four. The comment's arithmetic does not match the value.

findings.title: Cases repeat assertions already made earlier in the same file
findings.why: This is line 81 verbatim. "an edge between two occupied frames is unaffected" (line 140) likewise repeats lines 80 and 91. In tests/input/deadzone_tests.cpp:399, `apply_deadzone(0.5f, 0.5f) == 0` repeats line 390. Duplicate cases inflate the suite without covering anything new, and they read as if they test something distinct.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the duplicate cases, or move their explanatory comments onto the original assertions.
findings.verify_reason: gamepad_tests.cpp:97-106 repeats line 81's CHECK_FALSE(pressed(down,down,a)), and line 140's case repeats the press and release edges. The deadzone duplicate is real, but the lines are wrong because the file is 83 lines: apply_deadzone(0.5f,0.5f)==0 appears at both 18 and 27. Minor, and the duplicate cases mostly exist as documentation.

findings.title: Comment starts mid-sentence, and its "BEFORE doctest" ordering claim is contradicted by siblings
findings.why: The subject of the first sentence is missing; the file has started with "// BEFORE" since it was created. Other files include <ostream> after doctest and build, so the ordering claim is wrong: the type only has to be complete where the assertion is instantiated. The comment also breaks CONVENTIONS' rule that a test opens with doctest.
findings.suggested_fix: Move <ostream> into the standard-library group after doctest and reword: "<ostream> is needed wherever an assertion compares std::string_view: doctest only forward-declares basic_ostream."
findings.verify_reason: keyboard_tests.cpp line 1 begins '// BEFORE doctest, and it is not a stray include' with no subject, and it is the first line of the file. dom_events_tests.cpp includes <ostream> after doctest and uses std::string_view (line 9). block_decode_tests.cpp also includes it after doctest. So the 'BEFORE' ordering claim is contradicted by sibling files that build.

findings.title: Bounds guard tests cannot fail: the bits they read are never set
findings.why: KeyboardState::is_down guards with `if (!is_key(key)) return false;` (engine/input/keyboard.cpp:79). The test only sets Key::a's bit, so bit 0 (none) and bit `count` are zero whether or not the guard exists. Remove the guard and the test still passes. tests/input/mouse_tests.cpp:57-65 ("the bounds are not buttons") has the same flaw with `at(0, 0, { MouseButton::left })`. The comment says the answer must be "no rather than a read of whatever bit they would index", but the test cannot tell those two apart.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the state with every bit set (keys[0] = keys[1] = ~0ull; buttons = 0xFF) and then assert that is_down(none) and is_down(count) are false. Only the guard can produce that answer.
findings.verify_reason: Correct. board({Key::a}) never sets bit 0 or bit Key::count, and count is at most 128 per the static_assert, so it falls within keys[2]. at(0,0,{left}) likewise never sets bit 0 or bit 6 of buttons. Both tests would pass with the is_key/is_button guard removed. This is a weak test of a two-line guard, so low.

findings.title: Says dom_events_tests.cpp is compiled into the browser build only, but it is built on every platform
findings.why: The comparison is false and misstates how dom_events is built, which is the opposite pattern.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the comparison: "Compiled into the browser build only, beside the file it tests."
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: tests/app/CMakeLists.txt lists dom_events_tests.cpp in the unconditional SOURCES and adds engine/app/web/dom_events.cpp for native builds. Its header comment says 'on every platform'. The comparison in standard_gamepad_tests.cpp:13-14 is therefore false. It is a one-clause comment error.

findings.title: "The guide button is not read" is never asserted with the guide button pressed
findings.why: Only the button count is varied. No case presses W3C index 16 (or 6/7 as digital) and checks that `buttons` stays 0. "every named button has its own index" covers indices 0-5 and 8-15 only. A translation that mapped index 16 onto some engine bit would pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: standard_pad(0) with digitalButton[16] = true gives state.buttons == 0.
findings.verify_reason: This is at standard_gamepad_tests.cpp:142-145; the cited line 447 is past the end of the 201-line file. Only numButtons=16 is tested. Index 16 (guide) is never pressed with buttons asserted 0, and 'every named button' covers indices 0-5 and 8-15 only. The implementation skips index 16 through its table, but nothing asserts that.

findings.title: Comment says gamepad_tests.cpp needs Node to have no Gamepad API; vibration_tests.cpp is the file that does
findings.why: The comment points a maintainer at the wrong file as the dependent. Someone changing the fake-pad lifetime would check the wrong case.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the comment to name vibration_tests.cpp (its GamepadReader/Gamepads cases that expect empty slots).
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: web_vibration_tests.cpp:97-98 names gamepad_tests.cpp, which has no Node or Gamepad API mention. vibration_tests.cpp:278 is the file that relies on Node having no Gamepad API. It is a wrong filename in a comment, so low.

findings.title: Test hard-codes the arena's landmark colour copied from the sample source
findings.evidence:
if (sprite.corners[0].colour == Colour(129, 103, 186))
samples/local_multiplayer/arena.cpp:87-88: rectangle(RectangleF(880.0f, 490.0f, 40.0f, 100.0f), Colour(129, 103, 186));
findings.why: If the sample's palette changes, this test fails with no clue why, or matches some other sprite by chance. Arena already exposes `player_colour(i)` for the same purpose in draw_tests.cpp, but the landmark colour is an anonymous literal in two places.
findings.suggested_fix: Expose the landmark colour as a named Arena constant (for example `Arena::landmark_colour`), use it in arena.cpp, and compare against it here.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: join_state_tests.cpp:152 compares against Colour(129, 103, 186), copied from arena.cpp:87-88. If the palette changes, the test fails with landmarks == 0, so it is not silent. Low.

findings.title: Single-capital-letter constants X and Y break the snake_case constant rule
findings.evidence:
constexpr float X = 6232.75f;
constexpr float Y = 5408.46f;
findings.why: CONVENTIONS: constants follow value naming (snake_case), and uppercase is reserved for macros. 'X' and 'Y' read as macros and do not say what they are. `side` on the next line follows the rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to `origin_x`/`origin_y` (or `left`/`top`).
findings.verify_reason: ericson_math_tests.cpp:109-110 constexpr float X / Y. CONVENTIONS#constants: value naming, and screaming is reserved for macros.

findings.title: Legacy snake_case 'test_...' case names mixed with sentence names, including a doubled 'test_test_'
findings.evidence:
TEST_CASE("test_test_2D_segment_segment")

Others in the same style: "test_closest_pt_point_AABB" (22), "test_signed_2D_tri_area" (348); 22 such names in tests/math/shape_intersect_tests.cpp (e.g. line 82 "test_rectangle_circle_intersect"); tests/math/rectangle_rotated_tests.cpp:95,131,151. The rest of the unit uses sentences, e.g. "a zero-length segment is its own closest point, not a NaN".
findings.why: Doctest names are the test's documentation, and the unit has two naming schemes. The old names repeat the 'test_' prefix that TEST_CASE already implies (doubled in 'test_test_') and say nothing about the property checked. quad_tests.cpp:15 cites one of them by name, which keeps the old style in place.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the legacy cases to sentences that state the property, e.g. "test_2D_segment_segment reports the crossing point and parameter". Update quad_tests.cpp:15 in the same change.
findings.verify_reason: ericson_math_tests.cpp:363 TEST_CASE("test_test_2D_segment_segment"), :22 and :348 confirmed. 35 'test_' case names across tests/. quad_tests.cpp:15 cites "test_rectangle_rotated_setters_are_transactional" by name.

findings.title: Last case sits outside the file's TEST_SUITE
findings.why: Every other case in the file is in TEST_SUITE("EricsonMath"). This one is appended after the suite's closing brace, so `-ts=EricsonMath` filtering skips it and the grouping is inconsistent. The same appended-after-the-fact pattern shows in its compressed style.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the case inside the TEST_SUITE block.
findings.verify_reason: ericson_math_tests.cpp: TEST_SUITE("EricsonMath") opens at line 20 and closes at 563, and the TEST_CASE at 565 sits outside it.

findings.title: Unused standard includes in three test files
findings.evidence: tests/math/matrix3x2f_tests.cpp:7 "#include <cmath>" (no std:: math call; rotations come from Matrix3x2F::rotation(pi_over_2)); tests/scene/cull_tests.cpp:27 "#include <string>" (only the word 'string' in a comment at line 199); tests/ui/text_widget_tests.cpp:17 "#include <string>" (no std::string/wstring use; text() is compared with a wide literal).
findings.why: Includes that serve nothing widen each translation unit's dependencies and mislead about what the file uses. This was checked by grepping each file for every std:: name the header provides.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the three includes.
findings.verify_reason: matrix3x2f_tests.cpp has no sqrt, abs, sin, cos, isnan or isfinite call, so <cmath> at line 7 is unused. cull_tests.cpp mentions 'string' only in the include at 27 and a comment at 199 (its std::cos/sin come from <cmath>). text_widget_tests.cpp mentions 'string' only in the include at 17 and a comment at 32.

findings.title: Stray space after the tabs in one test body, and an '00.0f' literal
findings.why: Each body line in test_segment_rectangle_rotated_intersect has tab+tab+space indentation, unlike the rest of the file. `00.0f` is a typo-looking literal. The whitespace lint misses both.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the extra space on lines 663-675 and write `0.0f` on line 433.
findings.verify_reason: cat -A shows '^I^I ' (tab tab space) on the body lines of test_segment_rectangle_rotated_intersect, about lines 663-675. Line 433 has Point2F(10.0f + epsilon_f, 00.0f) and Point2F(20.0f, 00.0f).

findings.title: Harness comment says 'a two-texel texture' but the harness builds an 8x8 one
findings.why: The comment contradicts the code below it. It looks copied from fanout_tests.cpp's 2x2 harness. The 8x8 size is load-bearing here: the later rotated-visual test's '40/8 or 20/8 world units' arithmetic depends on it. A reader who trusts the comment gets that arithmetic wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'an eight-texel-square texture', or drop the size from the comment.
findings.verify_reason: cull_tests.cpp:49 says 'a two-texel texture', and lines 61-64 build 8x8 with an 8x8 frame. The contradiction is real, but it is a one-word comment slip, so low.

findings.title: Four per-file null-renderer Harness classes repeat the device/table/texture setup that tests/render/null_test_harness.h already shares
findings.evidence: cull_tests.cpp:59 "this->renderer_.create_device(nullptr, 1280, 720, 1);\n\t\t\tthis->renderer_.set_resources(&this->resources_);" then a hand-built TextureData of 0xFF. fanout_tests.cpp:70, order_tests.cpp:102 and text_widget_tests.cpp:54 repeat the same create_device + set_resources. fanout and text_widget also repeat the TextureData/texture_level/add_texture_asset block, and cull_tests.cpp:82-92 and text_widget_tests.cpp:66-71 build the same two-glyph 'A'/'B' 10x10 font on a 20-tall line. Each carries its own copy of the 'table before the renderer' member-order rationale.
findings.why: The same seam-ordering rule (resources before renderer, create_device before set_resources before content) and the same synthetic atlas/font are restated in four places. null_test_harness.h deliberately loads from ./content, so a second shared, file-free fixture is what is missing. The duplication drifts: canvas sizes, texture sizes and accessor shapes already differ for no stated reason.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one file-free null fixture header (for example tests/render/null_synthetic_harness.h) that owns the resources-then-renderer members, a white or quad texture made from bytes, and the optional two-glyph font. Have cull, fanout, order and text_widget tests compose it, keeping only their scene/draw helpers.
findings.verify_reason: The create_device + set_resources pair is repeated in cull, fanout, order and text_widget. However, order_tests already uses the shared add_white_texture helper, and the others use the shared add_texture_asset/texture_level helpers. The 'table before the renderer' comment appears only in fanout_tests:102 and text_widget_tests:86, not in all four. Each harness builds different content (sheets with a pinned origin, view capacity, a glyph atlas), so the shared remainder is small.

findings.title: Hand-typed pi literals where labrador::pi and pi_over_2 exist
findings.evidence:
const float half_turn = 3.14159265f;

Also cull_tests.cpp:162 `3.14159265f`, :260 `1.57079633f`, :282 `{ 0.0f, 1.57079633f, 0.7f, -0.7f }`; tests/collision/narrow_phase_tests.cpp:569 `random.uniform_float(0.0f, 3.14159265f)`.
findings.why: engine/math/scalar.h defines `pi` and `pi_over_2`, and the math tests use them. The literals truncate pi, so they differ from the engine's constants in the last bits, and they repeat a value the reader must recognise by eye.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `pi` and `pi_over_2` (both files already `using namespace labrador`).
findings.verify_reason: The literals exist (cull_tests.cpp:147,162,260,282; narrow_phase_tests.cpp:569), and scalar.h:10-11 defines pi and pi_over_2. But the claim that they 'differ in the last bits' is wrong: 3.14159265f and 1.57079633f round to the same float as pi and pi/2. It is purely a readability nit.

findings.title: StateContext composition case sits in the fan-out file, has no thread pool, and drops the file's style
findings.why: The file header says the file covers the per-view fan-out, but this case builds only Scene(nullptr, nullptr) and tests StateContext draw order. Its style also differs from every other class in the file: no `this->`, an unnamed `float` parameter instead of `/*dt*/`, integer literals passed to float constructors, and no comment saying what it pins.
findings.suggested_fix: Move it beside order_tests.cpp's layering contracts (or into a state-composition file). Match the file's style and add a one-line statement of the contract it pins.
findings.verify_reason: fanout_tests.cpp:389-431 has the StateContext composition case with Scene(nullptr,nullptr), unnamed float, no this->, integer literals and no contract comment. It does check view_count offsets, which is loosely draw-related, but the placement and style inconsistency are real.

findings.title: Local SceneState departs from the unit's member-access and parameter style
findings.evidence: "void update(float) override {}" ... "bool covers_screen() const override { return covers_; }\n\t\tvoid draw(Renderer& renderer) const override { scene_->draw(renderer); }" ... "bool covers_;" (no initializer)
findings.why: Every other test double in the unit writes `this->member_`, comments out unused parameter names (`float /*dt*/`) and default-initialises bool members (`bool covers_screen_ = true;`). This one class does none of the three, so it reads as pasted from elsewhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Write `this->covers_` and `this->scene_`, use `float /*dt*/`, and give `covers_` a default initializer (or make it const).
findings.verify_reason: fanout_tests.cpp:393-404's SceneState uses `void update(float)`, accesses bare `covers_` and `scene_`, and leaves `bool covers_;` uninitialised. The other doubles in the same file use `float /*dt*/` (lines 116, 137, 311) and `this->` access. CONVENTIONS.md has no explicit `this->` rule, but the inconsistency within the file is real.

findings.title: Pointer to 'the closing comment in this file' lands on a comment in the middle of the file
findings.why: Tests appended later left the cross-reference wrong, so a reader scrolling to the end of the file finds nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the pointer to name the content ("see the note above the end_tick contact test"), or move the line-360 note to the end of the file.
findings.verify_reason: scene_tests.cpp:159-161 points to 'the closing comment in this file'. The note is at lines 359-361, and eight TEST_CASEs (364-480+) follow it in a 503-line file.

findings.title: Standard header placed before engine headers, and some files have no blank lines between include groups
findings.why: CONVENTIONS#files: a test 'opens with <doctest/doctest.h> and then follows the same order' (engine, external, standard). navigation_tests puts <vector> before the engine headers. The ungrouped files break the blank-line layout every sibling uses.
findings.suggested_fix: Move <vector> below the engine/test includes, and add the group-separating blank lines to the three core files.
findings.verify_reason: navigation_tests.cpp:1-6 has <vector> right after doctest and before the engine headers, against CONVENTIONS line 138-141 (doctest, then engine, external, standard). The blank-line grouping part is style only; CONVENTIONS does not require blank lines.

themes.name: Native render test hygiene
themes.desc:
Problems in tests/render (excluding the web runners):
- Stale comments from before the SM-49 split, plus history in seam and viewport comments.
- Probe Watchdog, fail_fast and loader_function scaffolding copied across D3D12 and Vulkan.
- Hand-built 2x2 textures and a copied 4097-sprite loop.
- The harness assumes 64x64 frames, and ink_bounds' comment disagrees with its code.
- Golden-directory errors are discarded.
- DeviceFixture has a teardown-order problem.
- Include order, namespaces and pi literals do not follow conventions.
themes.story: Make one shared test-support header for probe scaffolding and flat textures, preserving test names and registration. Make the harness follow the reported buffer size. Fix the fixture teardown order and the golden-directory error. Then rewrite the stale and archaeology comments. Confirm with RenderPixelTests on D3D11, D3D12 and null; no golden image should change.

findings.title: Watchdog, fail_fast and loader_function are copy-pasted across the D3D12/Vulkan probes and tests
findings.evidence: Near-identical `class Watchdog` with `std::chrono::seconds(10)`, a `finished_` flag and `check_deadline()` at d3d12/presented_slots_probe.cpp L46, d3d12/destruction_probe.cpp L156, vulkan/presented_slots_probe.cpp L44 and vulkan/destruction_probe.cpp L213. `template<typename Function> Function loader_function(const char* name)` appears in vulkan/pending_submission_tests.cpp L43, vulkan/presented_slots_probe.cpp L87 and vulkan/destruction_probe.cpp L121. `class Event` appears in d3d12/pending_submission_tests.cpp L39 and d3d12/presented_slots_probe.cpp L87.
findings.why: The four watchdogs have already drifted: the Vulkan presented-slots copy reorders members, starts the thread in the constructor body and uses different messages. Each one hard-codes "ten-second" in a string next to a literal `seconds(10)`. A fix to one bounded-termination path (the safety net that keeps these probes from hanging) will not reach the others.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract a small tests/render/probe_watchdog.h that takes a deadline and a [[noreturn]] failure callback, and a tests/render/vulkan/loader_function.h. Have each probe include them and keep only its own fail_fast message.
findings.verify_reason: There are four Watchdog classes with seconds(10) and 'ten-second' strings (d3d12/destruction_probe L156, d3d12/presented_slots_probe L46, vulkan/destruction_probe L213, vulkan/presented_slots_probe L44), and d3d12/destruction_probe uses fputs instead of fail_fast. loader_function is copied in six Vulkan files (more than the three claimed). class Event is copied in two D3D12 files. No probe comment declares the copies deliberate.

findings.title: pixel_tests.cpp preamble and case comments still describe the pre-split single file
findings.evidence: L44 "A backend is correct when this file passes against it"; L62 "Because the text cases below are relationships (see two paragraphs down)"; L89 "text. Each case below names the term it fixes."; L159 "Presented, unlike every other case here"; L306 "The one frame here that is not held against a golden image"; L325 "ONE OF TWO CASES HERE THAT ARE NOT ABOUT A PIXEL"
findings.why: Since SM-49 the text cases are in text_pixel_tests.cpp, and this file holds only the lifecycle cases. Here, "below" points at nothing. Two later cases also present ("read back and then presented", "submitted and never presented"). The file calls end_not_comparable three times (L309, L370, L433), not once. Of the cases here, the device-info and vsync ones are the two not about a pixel, and the resize case that claims the label checks pixels. A reader trusting these sentences gets this file's own scope and coverage wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the preamble to cover what pixel_tests.cpp now holds (lifecycle/readback) and move the text-relationship paragraphs to text_pixel_tests.cpp. Correct or delete the per-case "only/one/every other case here" claims at L159, L306 and L325.
findings.verify_reason: pixel_tests.cpp L44 'A backend is correct when this file passes', L62 'text cases below are relationships', L89 'Each case below names the term' are present though L72 already says text lives in text_pixel_tests.cpp. L159 'Presented, unlike every other case here' while L444/L497 cases present; end_not_comparable is called at L309, L370, L433 despite L306 'The one frame here'. L325 'ONE OF TWO CASES HERE THAT ARE NOT ABOUT A PIXEL'. SM-49 in docs/code-hygiene.md is closed and does not track these.

findings.title: "RenderTests is otherwise identical in every configuration" is contradicted nine lines later
findings.evidence: L63-64 "RenderTests is otherwise identical in every configuration." followed by L71-73 "if(WIN32)\n    target_sources(RenderTests PRIVATE throw_if_failed_tests.cpp)\nendif()"
findings.why: The WIN32-only source makes RenderTests differ between native and wasm builds as well, so the sentence is false.
findings.suggested_fix: Say "RenderTests is otherwise identical in every configuration except for the Windows-only HRESULT test below", or move the sentence below both conditionals.
findings.verify_reason: tests/render/CMakeLists.txt says 'RenderTests is otherwise identical in every configuration', and the if(WIN32) target_sources for throw_if_failed_tests.cpp follows a few lines later.

findings.title: Calls RenderPixelTests 'the one entry in ctest' that can fail for reasons outside the repo; MinimalSmokeTests and D3D12SynchronizationTests also need a device
findings.evidence:
# A separate executable from RenderTests, which is pure arithmetic and wants no
# device. This one creates a device and a hidden window, so it is the one entry
# in ctest that can fail for a reason outside the repository

samples/minimal/CMakeLists.txt:85-86: 'It needs a graphics device, so a machine without one fails it'. tests/ctest_inventory.json registers MinimalSmokeTests and D3D12SynchronizationTests too, and ci.yml:258 says 'RenderPixelTests and MinimalSample, the two tests that make a device'.
findings.why: The uniqueness claim is false and conflicts with ci.yml and the minimal sample's CMake comment.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'one of the ctest entries that need a device (with MinimalSmokeTests)', or drop 'the one'.
findings.verify_reason: tests/render/CMakeLists.txt:77-79 says 'the one entry in ctest that can fail for a reason outside the repository'. ci.yml:258 itself names RenderPixelTests and MinimalSample as the two tests that make a device, and D3D12SynchronizationTests is in ctest_inventory.json. The uniqueness claim is false.

findings.title: Hand-built 2x2 RGBA textures duplicate flat_texture about a dozen times in the same executable
findings.why: pixel_test_harness.cpp:32 already defines `render_tests::pixel::flat_texture(r, g, b)`, and it is linked into the same RenderPixelTests binary. `solid_texture` is a byte-for-byte copy of it. `git grep 'texture_level(.*2, 2, 0)' tests/render` finds about 14 more inline or helper copies of a white 2x2 texture: presentation_lifecycle_tests.cpp:32 white_texture, d3d12/presentation_diagnostics_tests.cpp:133, d3d12/submit_allocation_tests.cpp:39, d3d12/pending_submission_tests.cpp:204, vulkan/cleanup_failure_tests.cpp:180, vulkan/submit_failure_tests.cpp:92, vulkan/pending_submission_tests.cpp:334, vulkan/submit_allocation_tests.cpp:36, and the four probes. Some set the format and some rely on the default, which is already a silent difference between copies.
findings.suggested_fix: Move flat_texture out of the pixel harness into a tiny shared test header, for example tests/render/test_textures.h, that every RenderPixelTests source and probe can include. Replace the copies with flat_texture(255, 255, 255) or flat_texture(r, g, b).
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: d3d12/texture_replacement_tests.cpp:31 solid_texture is the same function as pixel_test_harness.cpp:32 flat_texture, and both are in RenderPixelTests. 16 files match texture_level(...2, 2, 0). Some copies, such as presentation_lifecycle_tests.cpp:32 white_texture, rely on the default format and fill every byte with 255, so they are near-copies rather than exact ones. This is small test-helper duplication, so low.

findings.title: Test code reopens the engine namespace as labrador::d3d12_wait_test
findings.why: CONVENTIONS (Namespaces) allows no nesting under labrador except detail, and says code outside the engine never reopens the engine's namespace. Every other test helper in this unit lives in render_tests (test_window.h, device_fixture.h, submit_loss.h, allocation_scope.h). This is also the only test symbol a reader could take for engine API.
findings.suggested_fix: Move it to render_tests::d3d12_wait (or render_tests) and update the macro in instrumented_device_resources.cpp L20 and the definitions in pending_submission_tests.cpp L233 and presented_slots_probe.cpp L468.
findings.verify_reason: wait_observer.h declares namespace labrador::d3d12_wait_test, and it is reopened in pending_submission_tests.cpp L233 and presented_slots_probe.cpp L468. CONVENTIONS L94-98 allows no nesting except detail. The macro is fully qualified (::labrador::...), so render_tests would work equally. (CONVENTIONS' 'never reopens' line speaks of game code, not tests, but the nesting rule applies.)

findings.title: DeviceFixture releases textures on a live device before the renderer's teardown wait
findings.why: The members are declared so the table outlives the renderer, which is the seam's constraint. render_resources.h:112-129 says a shell that releases textures ahead of ~Renderer::Impl, the only GPU wait, is what D3D12 reports as OBJECT_DELETED_WHILE_STILL_IN_USE. The destructor body runs before ~Renderer, so it does exactly that, on a live device. render_resources.h:97-102 also says the call is meant for device loss, "the one moment nothing is reading". Today it is safe only because each of the seven users (gl/d3d12/vulkan texture, replacement, cleanup and submit-failure cases) happens to drain or read back before the fixture goes out of scope. The fixture shown to backend-specific tests teaches the opposite of pixel_test_harness.h and null_test_harness.h.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the user-declared destructor and let member order handle teardown, as Harness does. If the Vulkan cleanup case needs teardown observed in a particular order, do that explicitly inside that case after renderer teardown.
findings.verify_reason: device_fixture.h:21 does call resources.release_device_resources() in the destructor body. That body runs before ~Renderer, so it goes against the constraint in render_resources.h:112-129 and the device-loss-only note at :97-102. git log shows it has been there since the fixture was added in 4cefb68, with no comment saying why. GL needs no early release, because gl/render_resources.cpp:22-38 handles names released after the context is gone. The fix is right. But this is a test-only fixture, and its seven users drain or read back before teardown, so the risk is hypothetical. Low, not medium.

findings.title: Test name claims "no allocated object" but asserts only that the caller's binding is preserved
findings.why: Nothing checks that no GL texture object was created. The assertion is that GL_TEXTURE_BINDING_2D still names the sentinel, which the inline comment states correctly ("preserving the caller's object"). The name overstates the coverage.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to "GL texture refusal leaves the caller's binding untouched and permits retry", or add an assertion that actually observes allocation (for example glIsTexture on the next generated name).
findings.verify_reason: gl/texture_tests.cpp L17 is named 'leaves no allocated object' but asserts only GL_TEXTURE_BINDING_2D == sentinel. The inline comment describes this as a proxy (an upload would bind). The name overstates.

findings.title: A failure to create the golden or actual directory is discarded and reported as "could not write it"
findings.why: On a regeneration, or when a mismatch writes golden-actual/, a directory-creation failure such as a permission or path problem is thrown away. The user then sees only the generic "could not write it", and for the actual frame (line 526-530) nothing at all, because that report is also ignored. The cause of a failed dump is the one thing the developer needs.
findings.suggested_fix: If create_directories sets the error_code, put error_code.message() into `error` and return false. When writing the actual frame fails, append a note to the report instead of silently omitting the frame path.
findings.verify_reason: golden_image.cpp:221-222 discards the create_directories error_code (named 'ignored') and reports only 'could not write it'. At :524-528 the error string from writing the actual frame is also 'ignored', and the frame path is silently left out of the report.

findings.title: Census "the set of sixty" no longer matches the golden set
findings.evidence:
// MEASURED, NOT GUESSED, with this number set to zero, against the set of
	// sixty.
findings.why: tests/render/golden/ holds 64 PNGs (git ls-files tests/render/golden/*.png | wc -l). The measurement record that justifies allowed_channel_drift now cites a set size that is no longer true, and a census in a comment does not update itself.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the count ("against the whole set") or date the measurement ("against the 60-image set at <commit>").
findings.verify_reason: golden_image.cpp L342-343 says 'against the set of sixty'. git ls-files tests/render/golden/*.png | wc -l returns 64.

findings.title: Null tests point at a viewport section and filter case in pixel_tests.cpp that moved to other files
findings.why: After the SM-49 split, the viewport cases are in view_pixel_tests.cpp and "a filter change mid-list applies to what follows it" is in sprite_pixel_tests.cpp. pixel_tests.cpp has neither. The whole point of the comment is to send the reader to that coverage, and it sends them to the wrong file.
findings.suggested_fix: Name view_pixel_tests.cpp for the viewport cases and sprite_pixel_tests.cpp for the filter case.
findings.verify_reason: null_tests.cpp:283-285 points at pixel_tests.cpp for the viewport section and the mid-list filter case. git grep finds 'a filter change mid-list' at sprite_pixel_tests.cpp:572, and the viewport cases are in view_pixel_tests.cpp (pixel_tests.cpp:21 says so itself). The pointer names the wrong file.

findings.title: snapshot, ink_bounds and row_has_ink assume a 64x64 frame while at() follows the reported size
findings.why: pixel_test_harness.h:103-106 says at() goes through the reported width "so that the three which do not [match buffer_side] can be written in the same vocabulary as the rest". The three whole-frame helpers (snapshot :175, ink_bounds :189, row_has_ink :220) still iterate the constant buffer_side. After a resize to 32x32 they would hit at()'s REQUIRE_MESSAGE "outside the back buffer" instead of describing the frame. No case does this yet, but the header invites it.
findings.suggested_fix: Iterate over static_cast<int>(buffer_.x) and buffer_.y in all three helpers, matching at().
findings.verify_reason: pixel_test_harness.cpp:175-229: snapshot, ink_bounds and row_has_ink all loop to the constant buffer_side. at() addresses pixels through the reported width and REQUIREs that the offset is inside the buffer. pixel_test_harness.h:101-103 invites the resize cases to use the same vocabulary. On a 32x32 frame the loops would trip at()'s out-of-buffer REQUIRE. No case does this today, so it is latent.

findings.title: ink_bounds comment calls right/bottom exclusive while the code treats them as inclusive
findings.why: `right` and `bottom` are the last inked column and row (L206-207 assign `right = x`), which is why the code adds 1. The comment says the opposite of what the variables hold, and "everywhere else in this file" no longer has a referent after the split.
findings.suggested_fix: Say: "right and bottom are the last inked column and row (inclusive); RectangleI is (x, y, width, height), hence the +1."
findings.verify_reason: The comment at L215-216 is ambiguous rather than flatly wrong. The returned RectangleI's right edge (x+width) is exclusive, which is what the +1 produces. The local variables are inclusive. 'everywhere else in this file' is stale after the split. Worth a reword, but not the inversion claimed.

findings.title: Harness comments point to cases "below" that live in other files, and golden_image.cpp names the wrong harness file
findings.evidence: pixel_test_harness.h L78 "The read-then-present case below walks the far end of the interval"; L113 "black, and the vocabulary every text case below is written in."; pixel_test_harness.cpp L78 "pixels, so the advance cases below can be exact"; L99-100 "by the BC2 / case below"; golden_image.cpp L361 "pixel_tests.cpp's harness takes it out"; view_pixel_tests.cpp L428-429 "it is the one file with a device on all four rasterising backends"; view_pixel_tests.cpp L53 "The harness above builds one integral 64x64 view"
findings.why: The harness is now its own header/.cpp pair, and the cases are split across five group files. No case follows these comments, the decoding harness is pixel_test_harness.cpp rather than pixel_tests.cpp, and five files share the device rather than one. The SM-49 movement kept these comments byte for byte, so they are false now.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace each "below"/"above"/"this file" with the file that owns the case (pixel_tests.cpp, text_pixel_tests.cpp, resource_pixel_tests.cpp). In golden_image.cpp say pixel_test_harness.cpp. In view_pixel_tests.cpp say "RenderPixelTests has a device on all four...".
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: harness.h L78/L113 and harness.cpp L78/L100 say 'below' with no cases following, golden_image.cpp L361 says 'pixel_tests.cpp's harness', view_pixel_tests.cpp L53 'The harness above' and L428 'the one file with a device'. These are real, but they are comment pointers in test code, so low severity.

findings.title: Pixel group files and null_tests.cpp break CONVENTIONS' test include order
findings.evidence: pixel_tests.cpp, sprite_pixel_tests.cpp, text_pixel_tests.cpp, view_pixel_tests.cpp and resource_pixel_tests.cpp all open with `#include "tests/render/pixel_test_harness.h"` and put `<doctest/doctest.h>` after the engine headers. null_tests.cpp L3-15 orders `engine/render/null/recording.h`, then `engine/core/name_table.h`, ... `engine/render/viewport.h`, then `engine/math/rectanglef.h`.
findings.why: CONVENTIONS (Files) says a test "opens with <doctest/doctest.h> and then follows the same order". Every other test in this unit does, including null_resource_tests.cpp, which shares a harness. null_tests.cpp's engine headers are unsorted, unlike its sibling null_resource_tests.cpp.
findings.suggested_fix: Open each pixel group file with <doctest/doctest.h>, then the engine headers, then the tests/ harness header, as null_resource_tests.cpp does. Sort null_tests.cpp's engine includes alphabetically.
findings.verify_reason: pixel_tests.cpp opens with tests/render/pixel_test_harness.h and doctest comes after the engine headers, against CONVENTIONS L138-141. null_tests.cpp does put doctest first, though. Its engine headers are unsorted, but CONVENTIONS orders by group, not alphabetically, so that half is not a rule.

findings.title: Case comments narrate history and give a stale count
findings.why: "Added a day after this comment" is history, not contract, which AGENTS.md rules out. Line 325 says "ONE OF TWO CASES HERE THAT ARE NOT ABOUT A PIXEL", but the file now has at least four non-pixel cases: device info, vsync policy, and the two resize-restart cases. Line 334 says "ALL THREE BACKENDS ANSWERED DIFFERENTLY" in a five-backend tree. These counts and anecdotes go stale whenever cases move, as SM-49 just showed.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite as present-tense contract: "Harness::read_frame calls back_buffer_size on every frame; this case is the only one that asserts on it." Drop the case count and the three-backend history, or move them to the review ledger they came from.
findings.verify_reason: pixel_tests.cpp:263-264 contains 'added a day after this comment', which is history. :325 says 'ONE OF TWO CASES HERE THAT ARE NOT ABOUT A PIXEL' and :334 'ALL THREE BACKENDS ANSWERED DIFFERENTLY', both narrative counts that go stale. This conflicts with AGENTS.md's contract-not-history rule.

findings.title: The 4097-sprite presented-frame loop is copied into the D3D12 diagnostics test
findings.why: d3d12/presentation_diagnostics_tests.cpp:143-172 (present_frames) repeats the same two-view, 4097-sprite, position and colour arithmetic, with the same "two full vertex pages and a partial third" rationale, and adds only the slot counting. Both files are in RenderPixelTests. If the vertex-page size changes from 2048, 4097 has to be updated in two places or one test stops exercising the boundary it claims to.
findings.suggested_fix: Share one `record_vertex_page_crossing_frame(renderer, texture, frame)` helper, with the 4097 derived from a named constant, and have the D3D12 diagnostics test wrap it with its slot bookkeeping.
findings.verify_reason: present_frame is at presentation_lifecycle_tests.cpp:43, not :258, with the 4097 loop at :53. d3d12/presentation_diagnostics_tests.cpp present_frames repeats the two-view 4097-sprite loop with the same arithmetic. Both are in RenderPixelTests; the diagnostics file is Debug only (CMakeLists.txt:141). The magic number is duplicated.

findings.title: 4097 sprites restates the engine's 2048-sprite page size as a literal
findings.why: The comment makes the count depend on the backends' page size (sprite_geometry.h `max_run_sprites = 2048`, d3d12/backend.h `max_page_sprites = 2048`). If the page size changes, the literal quietly stops crossing pages and the case loses its purpose with no build or test failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Name it from the shared constant, for example `constexpr int sprites_per_view = 2 * SpriteGeometry::max_run_sprites + 1;` (or whichever public spelling sprite_geometry.h exposes), and reference it in the comment.
findings.verify_reason: presentation_lifecycle_tests.cpp L50-53 comment says 'two full 2048-sprite vertex pages' with literal 4097. Page sizes are sprite_geometry.h max_run_sprites=2048, d3d11 max_batch_sprites=2048 and d3d12 max_page_sprites=2048, so the coupling is unenforced. Note the fix's single constant may not be every backend's page.

findings.title: Seam-test preamble and cases tell what the backends used to do
findings.evidence: L19-21 "but something else does now, and this file was the only mechanism that could when this was written"; L73-75 "Left to the backends: gl throws, d3d11 dereferences a null device ... and null ... succeeds"; L174-175 "four of the five backends answered that by walking a path with a null device in it"; L193-196 "that is exactly what begin_marker did on d3d11 ... The other four discarded the call."
findings.why: The comments describe past backend behaviour and the comment's own history ("when this was written"), which CONVENTIONS forbids. Readers may also take them as current behaviour.
findings.suggested_fix: State the rule each case holds in the present tense (the seam requires X on every backend) and delete the past-behaviour clauses. The TEST-GAP.md citations already point at the history.
findings.verify_reason: renderer_seam_tests.cpp L20-21 'when this was written', L73-75 'Left to the backends: gl throws, d3d11 dereferences...', L174 'four of the five backends answered' and L193-196 'exactly what begin_marker did on d3d11' are present and narrate past behaviour, which CONVENTIONS forbids.

findings.title: The coercion test says the Vector2I overload picks the nearest preset, but it only matches exactly
findings.evidence: `// This overload has always meant "pick the preset nearest this" and answers`. convert_ivec_to_resolution (resolution_manager.cpp:196-218) matches the four sizes exactly and otherwise returns `ScreenResolution::s_1280_720`. 1600x900 therefore becomes 720p rather than the nearer 1080p. This overload is also called only by this test, in Labrador and ColourWars alike.
findings.why: The comment states a behaviour the code does not have, and the test exists to protect it from being 'unified by accident'.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword it to 'exact preset match, otherwise 1280x720'. Also consider whether a test-only coercing overload should remain public at all.
findings.verify_reason: resolution_manager_tests.cpp:93 says 'pick the preset nearest this', but convert_ivec_to_resolution (resolution_manager.cpp:196-218) matches exactly and otherwise returns s_1280_720. Application::set_resolution(Vector2I) calls set_resolution_exactly (application.cpp:276), so ResolutionManager::set_resolution(const Vector2I&) is called only by this test in Labrador, and ColourWars has its own converter in save.cpp.

findings.title: Hand-typed pi literals at differing precision instead of labrador::pi / pi_over_2
findings.evidence: sprite_geometry_tests.cpp L178 "const float quarter_turn = 1.57079633f;"; sprite_pixel_tests.cpp L188 "const float quarter_turn = 1.5707963f;"; visual_tests.cpp L113 "const float half_turn = 3.14159265f;"; draw_object_tests.cpp L99 "turned(3.14159265f / 2.0f)"; label_tests.cpp L145/L287
findings.why: engine/math/scalar.h L10-11 defines `constexpr float pi` and `pi_over_2`. At least 15 sites across six files restate them, and one (sprite_pixel_tests.cpp) uses a different digit count from the rest. The tests then assert rotation against a constant the engine does not use.
findings.suggested_fix: Include engine/math/scalar.h and write `const float quarter_turn = labrador::pi_over_2;` / `labrador::pi` throughout the unit.
findings.verify_reason: There are 14 hand-typed 1.5707963x/3.14159265 sites across draw_object, label, sprite_geometry, sprite_pixel and visual tests. sprite_pixel_tests L188 uses 1.5707963f. engine/math/scalar.h L10-11 defines pi and pi_over_2. The float values round identically, so the 'differing precision' point is cosmetic.

findings.title: 'Both clients' and 'a second backend' wording in render tests and geometry predates the split and the five backends
findings.evidence:
tests/render/text_pixel_tests.cpp:38 "// THIS IS THE TERM EVERY LAYOUT IN BOTH CLIENTS RESTS ON."
tests/render/null_tests.cpp:296 "// Default first, asserted rather than assumed - point is what both clients"
tests/render/sprite_font_file_tests.cpp:94 "// BC2, WHICH IS THE ONE TO KNOW ABOUT BEFORE A SECOND BACKEND." and :97 "would have every glyph in both clients"
tests/render/font_tests.cpp:26 "// A SECOND BACKEND INHERITS ALL OF THIS AND RE-RUNS NONE OF IT"
tests/scene/order_tests.cpp:21 "// both clients build their layers out of it."
engine/render/sprite_geometry.cpp:83 "// majority of sprites in both clients are unrotated"
engine/render/vulkan/renderer.cpp:438-439 "every opaque sprite in both\n// samples renders identically either way"
findings.why: Since the split, this repository has one external client (ColourWars) and six samples, and all five backends exist. 'Both clients', 'both samples' and 'before a second backend' name a set the reader cannot identify and state facts that no longer hold.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with 'every sample and client', 'LineSweeper and ColourWars' or 'every backend', as each claim means. Recast 'before a second backend' as the current GL/WebGL2 BC2 constraint.
findings.verify_reason: Grep confirms each quote: text_pixel_tests.cpp:38, null_tests.cpp:296, sprite_font_file_tests.cpp:94/97, font_tests.cpp:26, order_tests.cpp:21, sprite_geometry.cpp:83 and vulkan/renderer.cpp:437-438 ('both samples'). More instances exist, such as d3d12/texture_factory.cpp:213 'both clients' and several 'second backend' lines in d3d11 and font.h. This is a real pattern, not tracked, and low.

findings.title: Comments claim the contract test runs in every configuration; CMake builds it only on WIN32, and the D3D11 count is wrong
findings.evidence: L22-23 "RenderTests is built in every configuration, so the assertions below run in all five."; L40-42 "in every configuration - including the two where no D3D11 file is built at all"; L46 "ThrowIfFailed is how the D3D11 backend keeps that promise"; tests/render/CMakeLists.txt L71-72 "if(WIN32)\n    target_sources(RenderTests PRIVATE throw_if_failed_tests.cpp)"
findings.why: The file is gated on WIN32, so the wasm configurations never compile it. Among native configurations, four build no D3D11 file (d3d12, gl, vulkan, null; engine/CMakeLists.txt L146-149 lists d3d11/ sources for one backend only), not two. engine/render/d3d12/*.cpp also includes throw_if_failed.h, so the static_assert message names one backend where there are two. Because this test calls itself a CONTRACT test, these are claims about its own reach.
findings.suggested_fix: Say the file compiles in every Windows configuration (the five native presets). Delete or correct the "two where no D3D11 file is built" clause. Change the static_assert message to "how the Direct3D backends keep that promise".
findings.verify_reason: L22-23 'run in all five' and L40-42 'the two where no D3D11 file is built' are present. CMakeLists L71-72 gates the file on WIN32. throw_if_failed.h is included by four d3d12 .cpp files, so the 'D3D11 backend' message is stale. It is real, but it is a comment and message string in a test, so low.

findings.title: PascalCase namespace ThrowIfFailedTests, unlike every other file in the unit
findings.why: CONVENTIONS: "Namespaces | one lowercase word" and "PascalCase names a type". Every other file in tests/render uses an anonymous namespace or render_tests. The same pattern exists in tests/assets, tests/core and tests/input (for example `namespace JsonTests`), so it may be worth one sweep, but within this unit it is the odd one out.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the wrapping namespace (the TEST_SUITE already groups the cases) or use an anonymous namespace like the sibling files.
findings.verify_reason: throw_if_failed_tests.cpp L34 'namespace ThrowIfFailedTests' is present, but the PascalCase test-namespace pattern is common across tests (AssetManifestLoaderTests, JsonTests, NameTableTests, RegistryTests, ThreadPoolTests, DeadzoneTests, GamepadTests, KeyboardTests...). It is a repo-wide test idiom, not a lone outlier, so it is a cross-unit consistency question at most.

findings.title: Viewport section header is history ("UNTIL NOW", "when this was written")
findings.evidence: "NOTHING HERE CALLED set_viewport UNTIL NOW, which is why the two device backends were able to disagree about a pane for as long as they did. ... which no test reached when this was written. ... One test reaches that call site now -"
findings.why: This is a changelog in a comment. "UNTIL NOW" and "when this was written" are archaeology, and "the harness above" (L53) is also stale after the split. Similar history appears in visual_tests.cpp L100-104 ("It reported the destination rectangle ... was culled") and throw_if_failed_tests.cpp L25-30 and L60-62 ("would not have compiled as a catch of the old type").
findings.suggested_fix: Reduce the section header to what the viewport cases pin and where the production caller is covered (tests/scene/fanout_tests.cpp). Do the same for the visual_tests.cpp and throw_if_failed_tests.cpp history paragraphs.
findings.verify_reason: view_pixel_tests.cpp L52-60 has 'NOTHING HERE CALLED set_viewport UNTIL NOW', 'when this was written' and 'The harness above'. The visual_tests.cpp history text is at L24-26, not L100-104, but the main citation is accurate.

findings.title: Scene-overlay case ignores the file's helper, buffer_side and naming conventions
findings.evidence: "Harness h;" ... "RectangleF(0, 0, 32, 64)" ... "// This new composition contract is asserted at every pixel" ... "for (int y = 0; y < 64; ++y)\n\tfor (int x = 0; x < 64; ++x)\n\t\tCHECK(h.at(x, y) == ((x >= 16 && x < 48 && y >= 16 && y < 48) ? blue_pixel : red_pixel));"
findings.why: `h` is an abbreviation outside CONVENTIONS' closed allowlist. The literal 64s and 32s restate buffer_side. The unbraced nested loops and integer literals for float parameters break the style of every sibling case. "new" is a temporal word that will go stale. The file already has check_red_and_blue_frame (L22) for this analytic red/blue comparison, and it reports the failing pixel's coordinates. The open-coded CHECK gives a bare mismatch, and it is the per-pixel assertion pattern pixel_test_harness.cpp L162-164 says it avoids.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to `harness`, derive sizes from buffer_side, and replace the loop with `check_red_and_blue_frame(harness, RectangleI(0, 0, buffer_side, buffer_side), RectangleI(16, 16, 32, 32))` (blue painted over red). Drop "new" from the comment.
findings.verify_reason: view_pixel_tests.cpp ~L484-504 uses 'Harness h', literal 64/32, unbraced nested loops, 'This new composition contract' and a bare CHECK, while check_red_and_blue_frame (L22) exists with CHECK_MESSAGE coordinates. 'h' is off CONVENTIONS' closed allowlist (L59-61). check_red_and_blue_frame(harness, (0,0,64,64), (16,16,32,32)) would be equivalent because blue overrides red. Real, but a style issue, so low.

themes.name: Bench harness hygiene
themes.desc: bench/: the render-cull row no longer mirrors Scene::draw_views, main.cpp silently skips the complexity assertion of any phase with fewer than two results (so a renamed case drops its check), the D3D12 descriptor probes rename tokens with macros over included engine sources, and comments carry stale history.
themes.story: Make a missing phase fail except the two fan-out names in non-null builds; mirror the real cull or rename the row; give the frame bench a seam instead of macro-renamed includes; then the comments. Run the null and D3D11 bench entries.

findings.title: A linear_phases entry with no results is skipped silently, so a renamed case drops its assertion
findings.why: The complexity-class assertions match the strings in linear_phases against the names passed to bench::run in three other files. Renaming or mistyping 'Scene::resolve (broad phase)' (or any of the other phases) on either side turns that assertion off with no output and keeps ctest green. The skip exists only so the two fan-out names pass in non-null builds (fanout_bench_absent.cpp says so), yet it applies to every phase.
findings.suggested_fix: Fail, or at least print a 'skipped' line, when a phase has fewer than two results. Exempt only the two fan-out names in non-null builds, for example with a flag returned by run_fanout_benchmarks or a per-phase 'optional' marker.
findings.verify_reason: bench/main.cpp:88-91 skips any phase with fewer than two results and prints nothing. fanout_bench_absent.cpp gives the skip as the reason the two fan-out names may stay listed, but the same skip covers every linear_phases entry. A renamed or mistyped case name therefore turns its assertion off with no output and ctest stays green.

findings.title: 'render cull' stand-in no longer matches Scene::draw_views' cull, but its comment says it is the same loop
findings.evidence:
// The render cull, lifted out of Scene::draw_views. ... The loop is the two lines that matter -
	// bounds() against the visible rectangle ... for (CollisionObject* const object : scene.collision_objects()) { if (object->bounds().intersects(visible))
findings.why: engine/scene/scene.cpp:291-306 now culls both objects_ and collision_objects_ with object->cull_bounds(1.0f / view.camera.scale).intersects(visible), which is a virtual call with a scale argument. The benchmark row named 'render cull (one view)' times a different, cheaper loop over half the objects and calls it the engine's cull. A regression in cull_bounds (for example a drawable whose extent grows with n) would not appear in the one cull row that builds under all five backends.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the real loop: iterate both scene.objects() and scene.collision_objects() and test cull_bounds(1.0f / scale) with a stated scale. Alternatively, rename the row and comment to say it is a bounds()-only proxy. Either way, drop the claim that it is 'lifted out of' draw_views.
findings.verify_reason: bench/scene_bench.cpp:144-171 says the loop is 'lifted out of Scene::draw_views' and that 'bounds() against the visible rectangle' is what matters. It iterates only collision_objects() and calls bounds(). engine/scene/scene.cpp:291-306 culls both objects_ and collision_objects_ with cull_bounds(1.0f / view.camera.scale). Round 1's known entry (scene_bench.cpp:159, about the preset count) is a different defect.

findings.title: Redundant add_dependencies on a target already linked
findings.why: target_link_libraries(D3D12DescriptorCountProbe PRIVATE LineSweeperRules LabradorEngine ...) already orders LabradorEngine first. Listing it again implies a non-link dependency (such as the generated shader headers) that the reader then looks for. Only linesweeper_frame_bench_content is needed.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop LabradorEngine from the add_dependencies call.
findings.verify_reason: bench/CMakeLists.txt:111-120 links LabradorEngine PRIVATE, which already orders the build, so listing LabradorEngine again in add_dependencies is redundant. Only linesweeper_frame_bench_content needs it. The effect is harmless noise.

findings.title: check_scaling passes silently when the small case measured zero
findings.why: A zero median, from clock granularity or a body the optimiser removed, makes the complexity assertion vacuously pass with no message. The 'ok ... stays linear' line is then printed for a check that compared nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Return a failure sentence such as 'small case measured 0 ns; cannot judge scaling' instead of an empty string, or have main.cpp print it as skipped.
findings.verify_reason: bench/bench.cpp:106-109 returns an empty string when small_cost <= 0. main.cpp treats an empty string as success and prints 'ok ... stays linear' for a comparison that was never made.

findings.title: Token-renaming macros span a whole sample-linked .cpp and every header it includes for the first time
findings.evidence:
#define wmain descriptor_count_workload_main
#define result_json instrumented_result_json
#define Window DescriptorCountWindow
#include "bench/linesweeper_frame_bench.cpp"
findings.why: linesweeper_frame_bench.cpp includes about 14 headers for the first time under these macros (scene.h, label.h, resource_factory.h, board_view.h, particles.h, top_out_banner.h, world.h and others). A future header that mentions the identifier Window (for example a Window* parameter) or result_json is silently rewritten in this one TU, which diverges from the engine's layout, an ODR violation that may not be diagnosed. The included file's namespace-scope 'using namespace labrador; using namespace linesweeper;' (lines 37-38) also leaks into the probe's own wmain. The renamed workload still reports 'LineSweeperFrameBench refused:' and prints the untagged measurement_class on success (linesweeper_frame_bench.cpp:508-516), so the census output mislabels itself. This is separate from round 1's d3d12_descriptor_count_renderer.cpp macro finding: this one covers the workload include in count_main.
findings.suggested_fix: Give linesweeper_frame_bench.cpp a real seam instead. Move FrameBenchmark into a header or library with a window factory and a result-labelling hook, and let both mains call it. At minimum, include every header linesweeper_frame_bench.cpp uses before the #defines, as d3d12_descriptor_count_renderer.cpp does.
findings.verify_reason: The macros are real, and count_main does include engine/app/window.h before them (line 4), so the existing Window class is not renamed. The ODR risk depends on a hypothetical future header that names Window or result_json. The using-namespace leak and the success line's untagged measurement_class (linesweeper_frame_bench.cpp:508-516) are real but cosmetic, and the code is an EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL instrumentation probe. This is a low maintainability note, not medium.

findings.title: Probe comment says renderer.cpp includes the FXC shader headers; sprite_pipeline.cpp does, and the preload list has drifted
findings.evidence:
// FXC's unguarded byte-array headers are included only once, by renderer.cpp;
// they contain no declarations using these method names.
findings.why: engine/render/d3d12/renderer.cpp includes no shader header; sprite_pipeline.cpp:9-10 includes sprite_pixel_shader.h and sprite_vertex_shader.h. The comment's safety argument is therefore about nothing, and bench/CMakeLists.txt:114 adds "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/generated" to the probe for a reason that does not exist. Line 1 also claims to 'Preload renderer.cpp's declaration headers', but the list omits engine/render/text_encoding.h (renderer.cpp:8). That header is first included inside the macro scope, which is exactly the hazard the preload is meant to prevent. Nothing keeps the list in sync with renderer.cpp's includes.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the comment. Remove the generated include directory from D3D12DescriptorCountProbe unless something needs it. Add text_encoding.h to the preload, and either assert the preload matches (for example a configure-time diff of renderer.cpp's #include lines) or state that it must be updated with renderer.cpp.
findings.verify_reason: The comment is false. d3d12/renderer.cpp includes no shader header, and sprite_pipeline.cpp:9-10 includes sprite_pixel_shader.h and sprite_vertex_shader.h. The generated include directory (compile_shaders.cmake:38) is therefore unneeded by the probe. The preload omits text_encoding.h, but that header includes only <string> and <string_view> and contains none of the four macro names, so there is no current hazard. This is a stale comment and dead include path with no behavioural effect, so medium is inflated.

findings.title: Probe repetition count and iteration ceiling are unnamed literals
findings.evidence: for (int repetition = 0; repetition < 7; ++repetition)
findings.why: warmup_iterations is a named constant and printed in the header, but the 7 repetitions, the default of 1000000 and the 100000000 ceiling (lines 78/91-92) are bare literals and the repetition count is not written to the output. Anyone analysing the CSV has to infer how many repetitions it holds.
findings.suggested_fix: Name repetitions, default_iterations and max_iterations as constexpr beside warmup_iterations, and print repetitions in the header block.
findings.verify_reason: The literal 7, the default 1000000 and the 100000000 ceiling are bare literals (lines 78, 91-92 and 138, not 116). However, the CSV header 'method,repetition,iterations,...' writes the repetition index and the iteration count on every row, so a reader does not have to infer them. Only the naming nit remains.

findings.title: Run-id length limit of 96 is an unnamed literal and its rejection gives the wrong reason
findings.why: A valid but 97-character --run is refused with a message about character classes, and the limit appears nowhere in print_usage or the message. The operator cannot tell what to change.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the limit (constexpr std::size_t max_run_length = 96) and report empty, too long and bad characters separately.
findings.verify_reason: ascii_token at linesweeper_frame_result.cpp:29 rejects empty or longer-than-96 values. narrow_ascii (line 54) then reports only the character-class rule. The 96 limit is unnamed and appears in neither the usage text nor the error message.

findings.title: Two ratio notes divide without the zero guard the neighbouring notes use
findings.why: The rotated-sprite and fan-out notes skip a zero denominator (lines 153 and 180), but these two do not. The sweep/broad-phase note also pairs rows by index on the assumption that both cases recorded the same counts in the same order. It checks only that the sizes are equal, so the printed n can belong to only one of the two rows.
findings.suggested_fix: Factor one helper that pairs results by n and skips non-positive denominators, and use it for all four notes.
findings.verify_reason: The missing zero guard is real, but it is a double division in a printed note, so the worst case prints inf and nothing crashes. The n^2 sweep's median at n=64 is not plausibly 0. The pairing worry does not hold: both cases are recorded by the same loop over counts[] = {64,256,1024,4096} (scene_bench.cpp:178-180), so index i is the same n in both. What remains is a consistency nit.

findings.title: 'Half of what PHILOSOPHY asks for is still unmeasured after this file' is outdated history
findings.why: bench/linesweeper_frame_bench.cpp now measures begin/record+submit/present on every real backend, and fanout_bench_null.cpp measures Scene::draw. The sentence, and the opening 'which nothing measured until this file' at line 13 and the 'were ... four phases' account at lines 15-18, narrate history rather than state what this file measures. A reader is told the backend half is unmeasured when it is not.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the 'floor, not a frame time' contract. Replace the history with a pointer: backend cost is LineSweeperFrameBench's record_submit_ns/present_ns.
findings.verify_reason: render_bench.cpp:13-31 narrates history ('nothing measured until this file', 'were ... four phases', 'Half ... is still unmeasured after this file'). The backend half is now measured by LineSweeperFrameBench, and Scene::draw is measured by fanout_bench_null.cpp.

findings.title: BenchCollider's contacts_ and both classes' age_ are written and never read
findings.why: The comment says contacts are 'Counted rather than acted on', but nothing reads the count, so it is a dead store, as are age_ in BenchObject (line 51/57) and BenchCollider (line 69/98). If they exist to keep the virtual calls from being trivial, the comment should say so. Otherwise they are noise that suggests a check the bench does not make.
findings.suggested_fix: Either sum contacts into a volatile sink after the resolve case and say why, or make update/on_contact empty and drop the members.
findings.verify_reason: contacts_ (incremented at line 89) and age_ in both classes (lines 51 and 69) are written and never read anywhere. The 'Counted rather than acted on' comment suggests a count that nothing uses.

themes.name: Unused public engine API: remove or test
themes.desc: Public declarations with no caller and no test, or used only by tests. These include Vector2F clamp/lerp/unit_vector/angle spellings, RectangleF::set_position_from_top_right, the unused Ericson functions, and Camera's three extra calculate_view_rectangle overloads. ResolutionManager's string and Vector2F setters silently coerce to 720p. The list continues with Colour::brighten/clamp_colours, sprite_quad_bounds, SpriteFrame's Vector2F constructor, the name form of set_sprite_sheet, UiContainer::children, UiTexture::set_height, FocusGroup::refresh_style, Quad::triangle_0/1, the D3D11 texture(name) overload, and untested scalar contracts.
themes.story: A single consumer-visible API-trim commit. For each symbol, decide between deletion and making it private or internal, and add behavioural tests for anything kept, such as the scalar clamp/lerp contracts. The commit needs a CHANGES.md entry naming the old and new spellings. Update website/published.ts and any quoting pages, and run website gate plus all presets.

findings.title: Public math functions with no caller and no test anywhere
findings.evidence:
float sq_dist_point_AABB(const Point2F& p, const RectangleF& b)   // ericson_math.h:50
void clamp(const Vector2F& min, const Vector2F& max);             // vector2f.h:57
Vector2F clamped(const Vector2F& min, const Vector2F& max) const; // vector2f.h:58
static float angle(const Vector2F& vec);                          // vector2f.h:61
void set_position_from_top_right(const Vector2F& position);       // rectanglef.h:73-74
findings.why: I ran git grep for `sq_dist_point_AABB`, `.clamp(`, `.clamped(`, `Vector2F::angle(` and `set_position_from_top_right(` across Labrador (engine, samples, tests, bench, tools, website) and across C:/Projects/ColourWars excluding external/. The only hits are the definitions in engine/math. None of these is tested, unlike the intersects.h predicates that intersects.h:8 keeps "at whatever call count". The static angle(vec) also duplicates the member angle().
findings.suggested_fix: Delete them, or, if they are meant as vocabulary, give each a behavioural test, as the project rule for public primitives requires.
findings.verify_reason: A fixed-string grep of engine, samples, tests, bench, tools, website and cmake, plus ColourWars outside external/ and docs, finds only the definitions of sq_dist_point_AABB, Vector2F::clamp/clamped, static angle(vec) and set_position_from_top_right. The other hits were std/scalar clamp, the member angle() in rectangle_rotated.cpp:277, and the website test fixture 'object.clamp()'. tests/math has no tests for any of them. The finding holds, but unused public library vocabulary is not a correctness risk: medium, not high.

findings.title: RectangleF::set_position_from_top_right survived the unused-member removal with no caller and no test
findings.evidence: `void set_position_from_top_right(const Vector2F& position);` and `void set_position_from_top_right(float x, float y);`. The only hits for `set_position_from_top_right` in Labrador (engine, samples, tests, website) and ColourWars are the declaration and definition. CHANGES.md:326 removed its siblings `set_position_from_bottom_left` and `set_position_from_bottom_right` for exactly this reason.
findings.why: Removing the bottom-left and bottom-right setters while keeping top-right leaves an odd, untested corner of the API that a reader would expect to have a purpose.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove both overloads, and add them to a CHANGES.md source-break entry beside the other RectangleF removals.
findings.verify_reason: set_position_from_top_right appears only at rectanglef.h:73-74 and rectanglef.cpp:187/192. ColourWars has no hits apart from the different removed UiTexture member. CHANGES.md:326 removed the bottom-left/bottom-right siblings. Real, but dead setters with no behavioural impact are medium at most.

findings.title: Vector2F::clamp, Vector2F::clamped and the Vector2F-t lerp overload have no caller and no test
findings.evidence: :57 `void clamp(const Vector2F& min, const Vector2F& max);` :58 `Vector2F clamped(const Vector2F& min, const Vector2F& max) const;` :71 `static Vector2F lerp(const Vector2F& a, const Vector2F& b, const Vector2F& t);`. A search for `.clamp(`, `clamped(` and `lerp(` across engine, samples, tests and bench finds only the vector2f.cpp definitions. ColourWars uses only the float-t `Vector2F::lerp` (game/carried/removed_members.h:28) and neither clamp form. No test exercises any of the three.
findings.why: These are public primitives with no user and no behavioural test, which is the same criterion the 2026-10-27 removal applied. clamp() and clamped() also duplicate the same min/max arithmetic.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove clamp, clamped and the Vector2F-t lerp overload, with a CHANGES.md source-break entry. Alternatively, keep any that a documented consumer need justifies and add a test for it.
findings.verify_reason: clamped( appears only at vector2f.h:58 and vector2f.cpp:99, and .clamp( has no engine/sample/test hit. The Vector2F-t lerp is vector2f.h:71 / cpp:157 with no caller. ColourWars removed_members.h:28 uses only the float-t lerp. No tests cover them. Real dead API, but high is inflated.

findings.title: Vector2F::to_unit_vector and Vector2F::unit_vector have no caller and no test anywhere
findings.evidence: vector2f.h:66 `void to_unit_vector();` and :123 `static Vector2F unit_vector(const Vector2F& vec);`; normalized()'s comment at :50-52 still points at them: "Note this is deliberately NOT the same contract as to_unit_vector() and unit_vector(), which substitute (1, 0) for a zero vector." Searched `to_unit_vector` and `unit_vector(` across engine, samples, tests, bench, tools, website and ColourWars (game, scripts, editor). The only hits are vector2f.cpp's definitions and a comment at tests/math/vector2_tests.cpp:154. No call and no test.
findings.why: These are a second normalisation API with a deliberately different zero-vector contract that invents a direction. They are used by nothing, and normalized() carries a paragraph warning against them. That is the 'no caller, no test' class CHANGES.md 2026-10-27 removed, and AGENTS.md requires a test for every public primitive.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove both members and their definitions. Cut the 'Note this is deliberately NOT the same contract...' paragraph from normalized()'s comment and the 'See normalize()' cross-reference. Add a CHANGES.md source-break entry in the 2026-10-27 table style.
findings.verify_reason: git grep in Labrador and ColourWars (excluding the submodule copy) shows to_unit_vector/unit_vector only in vector2f.h:66/123, vector2f.cpp:112/191, a comment at vector2f.cpp:220 and the comment at tests/math/vector2_tests.cpp:154. No caller and no test, and normalized()'s comment at :50-52 does refer to them. This is the same class CHANGES.md 2026-10-27 removed, and it is not in code-hygiene.md or TODO. It is real, but unused API with no runtime effect is not high severity.

findings.title: Three of the four calculate_view_rectangle overloads have no callers and repeat the same arithmetic
findings.evidence:
"void calculate_view_rectangle(
			RectangleF& rectangle) const;" / "static RectangleF calculate_view_rectangle(
			const RectangleF& world_rectangle,
			const Camera& camera);" / "static void calculate_view_rectangle(... RectangleF& view_rectangle);". Searched engine, samples, tests, bench, website and tools, plus C:/Projects/ColourWars, for `calculate_view_rectangle(`. The only callers are the const member returning RectangleF (sprite_geometry.h:199, tests/render/camera_tests.cpp:130,152, and ColourWars). No call to the in-place form or either static exists, and none of them has a test.
findings.why: This is untested public API. camera.cpp carries the world-to-view transform four times, so a fix to one copy can miss the others. The repo's rule is that a public primitive ships with behavioural tests.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the in-place overload and both static overloads, keeping the const member that returns RectangleF. Record the removal in CHANGES.md.
findings.verify_reason: camera.h:43,47,52 declare the in-place overload and two statics, and camera.cpp:29-62 repeats the transform four times. git grep finds callers only of the const RectangleF-returning member: sprite_geometry.h:199 and camera_tests.cpp:130,152. ColourWars' game/ tree has no calls outside its external/labrador copy. The three overloads are dead and untested.

findings.title: By-name texture lookup has no caller, and its 'parity' justification is false
findings.why: Nothing calls this public member, and the comment's reason for keeping it says something untrue: no other backend has this overload, so removing it is what would bring D3D11 into line with the rest. SEAM.md §4 also describes this file as 'two lookups', which this dead overload makes look right.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the declaration at backend.h:79-84 and the definition at d3d11/render_resources.cpp:41-45, and check that SEAM.md §4's description of render_resources.cpp still holds.
findings.verify_reason: backend.h:79-84 and render_resources.cpp:41-45 are as quoted. git grep shows no caller of the by-name texture() anywhere: not in engine, tests, samples or website, and ColourWars doesn't reach Impl. No other backend's backend.h or render_resources.cpp declares a by-name texture overload; d3d12, gl, null and vulkan each have only texture(TextureHandle). So 'kept for parity with the other four backends' is false. The finding is real, but it is an unused member of a backend-internal Impl with a wrong comment and no runtime effect. That is medium, not high.

findings.title: set_resolution(string) and set_resolution(Vector2F) have no callers and silently coerce unknown input to 720p
findings.why: This is dead public API with a silent-failure contract: any unrecognised string or vector becomes s_1280_720 with no error, the same coercion this header warns against for window sizes. It is untested and widens the surface the website publishes.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove both overloads, the three helpers that serve only them, and ScreenResolution::max, with a CHANGES.md entry. If a string form is wanted for options files, make it throw on an unknown name (T6) and test it.
findings.verify_reason: The set_resolution(std::string) and set_resolution(Vector2F) overloads (resolution_manager.h:32-33) have no callers in Labrador. ColourWars calls only the enum form (main_menu_options.cpp:412, presentation_validation_options.cpp:127). convert_string_to_resolution and convert_vec_to_resolution serve only those overloads, and they do coerce unknown input to 720p. But ScreenResolution::max is used heavily by ColourWars (main_menu_options.cpp:379, display_settings_trial.cpp:16, presentation_validation_options.cpp:125, scripts/acceptance/display_trial.cpp), so removing it would break the consumer. The finding is partly wrong, and high severity is inflated.

findings.title: Quad::triangle_0/triangle_1 and Triangle::calculate_gradient are public but only used internally
