findings.evidence: quad.h:48 `Triangle triangle_0() const;` :49 `Triangle triangle_1() const;`. Their only caller is Quad::triangles() at quad.cpp:241-242. triangle.h:46 `float calculate_gradient(int edge) const;` is called only by triangle.cpp:184 (hypotenuse_gradient). A search across Labrador and ColourWars finds no other use and no test.
findings.why: These are implementation steps exposed as untested public API. triangles() and hypotenuse_gradient() are the operations clients and tests actually use.
findings.suggested_fix: Make triangle_0/triangle_1 private, or fold them into triangles(). Make calculate_gradient protected or private, and adjust the comment at triangle.h:62-66 that calls it 'the public one'.
findings.verify_reason: triangle_0/triangle_1 (quad.h:48-49) are called only by quad.cpp:241-242, and calculate_gradient (triangle.h:46) only by triangle.cpp:184. No tests or ColourWars use. triangle_0/1 do mirror the public edge_0..edge_3 accessor pattern, so the impact is minimal. Low as stated.

findings.title: Documented contracts of clamp, lerp and Vector2F clamp/clamped/lerp have no tests
findings.why: AGENTS requires behavioural tests for public primitives. The inverted-range clamp answer and lerp's unclamped extrapolation are documented edge behaviour (also published in code-hygiene-public-headers.md) that nothing pins down.
findings.suggested_fix: Add doctest cases to tests/math for scalar clamp (including an inverted range), lerp outside [0,1], Vector2F::clamp/clamped/lerp, and sq_dist_point_AABB against closest_pt_point_AABB.
findings.verify_reason: git grep for lerp/clamp/clamped/sq_dist_point_AABB in tests/ finds nothing, and scalar.h:32-47 does document the inverted-range and extrapolation behaviour. The gap is real. However, AGENTS' tests-with-new-primitive rule applies to new primitives, and clamp is exercised indirectly by audio callers, so low severity.

findings.title: Two spellings of angle, and the static one has no caller
findings.evidence:
float angle() const;
		static float angle(const Vector2F& vec);  -- `git grep -n -E 'Vector2F::angle\('` in Labrador engine/samples/tests/website and ColourWars finds only the definition and doc comments; the member form is used by RectangleRotated::angle.
findings.why: Two forms of the same function widen the interface and invite drift. matrix3x2f.h:114-115 cites 'Vector2F::angle()' as a factory/reader pairing, which this static overload is not.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the static angle(const Vector2F&). If it stays, give it a test.
findings.verify_reason: vector2f.h:60-61 has both the member angle() and the static angle(const Vector2F&), and vector2f.cpp:104-111 shows identical bodies. git grep in engine/samples/tests/website and ColourWars/game finds no call to the static form. matrix3x2f.h:114 cites Vector2F::angle() as a factory/reader pairing, which neither overload is.

findings.title: Colour::brighten is used only by a test; clamp_colours is public but only an internal helper
findings.why: brighten is dead public API, and its semantics (adds to RGB, ignores alpha) do not respect the premultiplied blend the engine documents. clamp_colours is an invariant-restoring helper exposed as API, although no caller can ever see an unclamped Colour through the public constructors.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove brighten and its test, and make clamp_colours private. Add a CHANGES.md entry.
findings.verify_reason: brighten is called only from tests/render/colour_tests.cpp:33, and ColourWars has no brighten or clamp_colours. clamp_colours is called only inside colour.cpp. So both points are true, but it is a small API-surface tidy-up. The premultiplied-blend argument is speculative.

findings.title: SpriteFrame(position, size, origin) Vector2F constructor has no callers
findings.why: An unused float-to-int rectangle constructor on a public type, whose truncation behaviour is unstated and untested.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove it, with a CHANGES.md line.
findings.verify_reason: sprite_frame.h:25-28 declares SpriteFrame(Vector2F, Vector2F, Vector2F). Every construction in Labrador and in ColourWars (scripts/acceptance/menu_presentation.cpp:436) uses the RectangleI form.

findings.title: sprite_quad_bounds is public API with no non-test caller; the cull uses sprite_world_bounds
findings.why: Its long comment (lines 124-142) still says this function is what stops a cull from dropping a sprite. It is not on any cull path, so a renderer writer reading the published header gets a false picture of which function owns cull bounds. It is also a second implementation of the truncated-edge bounds that must be kept in step with build_sprite_quad, for no engine user.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove sprite_quad_bounds and port its tests to sprite_world_bounds or to build_sprite_quad's corners. Alternatively, make it a file-local test helper and move the cull paragraph onto sprite_world_bounds.
findings.verify_reason: sprite_quad_bounds has no caller outside tests/render/sprite_geometry_tests.cpp in Labrador, and none in ColourWars either. But the header comment does not claim it is the cull bound: sprite_geometry.h:129-130 says 'This is a view-space measurement, not a world-space cull bound. sprite_world_bounds accounts for the camera-dependent quantization.' Both functions share quad_bounds, so the 'second implementation' cost is small. It is a dead public function, so low severity.

findings.title: Name form of set_sprite_sheet has no engine caller and is exactly the 'never on its own' misuse its comment forbids
findings.evidence:
void set_sprite_sheet(const std::string& sheet_name);
The comment above it says a subclass calls either form 'only from a setter that moves its element in the same breath - never on its own'. `git grep set_sprite_sheet` finds the only engine call at texture_object.cpp:71, which uses the handle form. The name form is used only by tests/render/sprite_sheet_object_tests.cpp:141,147. Line 40's comment also names SheetStrip-taking subclass constructors, but no SpriteSheetObject subclass takes a SheetStrip (AnimationPreview in samples/components is not one).
findings.why: An unused protected entry point that, when called alone, leaves the subclass's frame handle indexing the wrong sheet. It widens the interface for a test only.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the name overload and test through the handle form or TextureObject::set_frame. Fix line 40 to mention only SheetFrame.
findings.verify_reason: The name form of set_sprite_sheet is unused outside tests, and ColourWars animation_object.cpp:185 uses the handle form. But the claim that no subclass takes a SheetStrip is wrong: ColourWars' AnimationObject derives from SpriteSheetObject and builds it from resolved(strip).sheet() (animation_object.cpp:59), which is the paired-handle path line 40 describes. The line-40 half of the finding is refuted.

findings.title: FocusGroup::refresh_style is public for a use case no consumer has, and it is untested
findings.evidence: "exposed because a page that recolours a widget for its own reasons - a team tint - has to put the focus paint back afterwards." / `void refresh_style() const;`. Searched `refresh_style` in Labrador (engine, samples including components, tests, website) and ColourWars game/scripts/editor. The only hits are focus.cpp's internal calls (lines 36, 75, 133, 155) and the definition.
findings.why: The public contract describes a team-tint use that ColourWars, the one real multi-slot consumer, does not have. Nothing tests the repaint as a public operation, though AGENTS.md requires a public primitive to ship with behavioural tests.
findings.suggested_fix: Make refresh_style private, or add a behavioural test that recolours a widget and calls refresh_style to restore it, if the consumer use is real.
findings.verify_reason: refresh_style is hit only at focus.cpp:36,75,133,155,158 and focus.h:159. No test calls it directly and no consumer in either repo uses it. However, the header documents a deliberate public use case (repainting after a tint), and exposing it is a reasoned design choice, not an accident. Real but low.

findings.title: UiContainer::children() is non-const, copies the whole list on every call, and has no caller
findings.why: A read-only accessor that cannot be called on a const container is a const-correctness hole. It also allocates on every call. Under PHILOSOPHY's rule, having no caller is not by itself a reason to remove a public name, but the non-const signature does carry a cost.
findings.suggested_fix: Make it `const std::vector<std::pair<std::string, UiObject*>>& children() const` or return a std::span. This is a public header, so record the signature change in CHANGES.md.
findings.verify_reason: widget.h:79 / widget.cpp:97 are as quoted (non-const, returns a copy). But 'no caller' is false: ColourWars scripts/acceptance/menu_text/fixtures.cpp:24 and setting_template_checks.cpp:97 call row.children() on OptionRow (a UiContainer) and read child.first/child.second. The const-ref fix stays source-compatible for those uses; the dead-API framing is wrong.

findings.title: UiTexture::set_height has no caller or test, and it is RectangleF::set_height's only caller
findings.evidence: widget.h:125 `void set_height(float height);` forwards to `this->rectangle_.set_height(height);` (widget.cpp:236-238). A search for `set_height(` in Labrador and ColourWars (game, scripts, editor) finds only these and rectanglef.h:78 `void set_height(float height);`. set_width, by contrast, is used by ColourWars results_menu.cpp:422.
findings.why: Two public setters exist only to call each other, and neither is tested. This is the 'no caller, no test' class CHANGES.md removed on 2026-10-27.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove UiTexture::set_height. Keep RectangleF::set_height only if a test covers it, since set_size and the height field already cover the need.
findings.verify_reason: set_height( hits are only rectanglef.h:78/cpp:211 and widget.h:125/widget.cpp:236-238, with no tests and no ColourWars caller. However, it is the symmetric partner of set_width, which ColourWars uses, so removing it would leave a lopsided API. Real but low.

themes.name: LineSweeper sample and its tests
themes.desc: ParticleField hand-rolls SplitMix32 instead of using labrador::Random. Hint strings and asset names are copied into four or more files, including the capture tool. Other duplication: the pacing world copies the bench, the banner and spark-size geometry is computed twice, arrange_screen is copied, and row_full is written twice. The tick-rate comment states the wrong direction (#300). There are stale 'fourth assert', 'only translation unit', 'two samples' and particle-unit comments, plus history in comments. The tests duplicate null setup and well fixtures and contain weak assertions, along with magic counts, missing includes and redundant CMake include paths.
themes.story: Read the sample README first. One behaviour-neutral commit adopts labrador::Random. Its replay determinism must be proven byte-identical, or the change is treated as a behaviour change. A second commit brings asset and hint constants and shared geometry into one owner each, used by the states, the pacing fixture and the capture tool, with regenerated captures reviewed if pixels move. Then strengthen the tests, rewrite the comments and README, and tidy CMake.

findings.title: Tick-rate comment says 120 FPS runs at half speed; the game would actually run at double speed
findings.evidence: main.cpp:40-41: "Nothing in the engine pins it - validate() only checks it is positive - so a game that sets 120 here silently runs at half speed with no error anywhere."  README.md:284-285 says the same: "`ApplicationOptions::validate` only checks it is positive — so a game that sets 120 runs at half speed". play_state.cpp:193 runs "One rules tick per fixed update", and application.cpp:176-177 sets the fixed step to `1.0 / target_fps`. application.cpp:43 also checks `StepTimer::SecondsToTicks(1.0 / this->target_fps) > 0`.
findings.why: At target_fps = 120, tick() runs 120 times a second. Gravity, lock delay and auto-repeat would all run twice as fast, not half as fast. This is the comment that explains why the value is pinned, and it states the effect backwards. 'Only checks it is positive' is also out of date: validate() checks timer resolution too.
findings.suggested_fix: Change both main.cpp and the README to say "runs at double speed" (or "runs every ticks-denominated duration at twice the intended rate"). Drop or reword "only checks it is positive", for example to "validate() checks only that it is a usable step".
findings.verify_reason: main.cpp:39-41 and README.md:285 do say 'half speed'. application.cpp:176-177 sets the fixed step to 1/target_fps, and application.cpp:42-43 also checks timer resolution. At 120 the game therefore runs at double speed, and 'only checks it is positive' is stale. The claim is real, but it is a wrong comment with no runtime defect, so it is not a high-severity bug.

findings.title: The spark-size formula is copied between update()'s cull extent and draw()
findings.evidence: particles.cpp:192 `const float half = particle.size * (0.35f + 0.65f * particle.life) * 0.5f;` (update, building extent_ for bounds/cull) and particles.cpp:425 `const float side = particle.size * (0.35f + 0.65f * particle.life);` (draw).
findings.why: bounds() and cull_bounds() must contain every quad draw() emits. The shrink curve is spelled out twice with unnamed constants, so tuning it in draw() alone would make the cull rectangle too small, and sparks at the edge of the field would be culled without any error.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a small helper in the anonymous namespace, such as `float spark_side(const Particle&)`, with the 0.35/0.65 floor and range as named constants, and call it from both places.
findings.verify_reason: particles.cpp:192 computes `particle.size * (0.35f + 0.65f * particle.life) * 0.5f` for the update extent, and :425 recomputes the same formula in draw(). Neither copy uses a named helper. If one were tuned without the other, the cull extent would stop enclosing the draw.

findings.title: ParticleField hand-rolls the SplitMix32 stream that labrador::Random now owns
findings.evidence: particles.cpp:468-492: `std::uint32_t ParticleField::next_random() { this->rng_ += 0x9E3779B9u; ... value = (value ^ (value >> 16)) * 0x21F0AAADu; ... }` and `float ParticleField::random_unit() { return static_cast<float>(this->next_random() >> 8) / static_cast<float>(1 << 24); }`. engine/core/random.cpp:13-15 says: "the SplitMix32 that LineSweeper's rules and particles already used, draw for draw, so a game moving onto this keeps its sequences." Random::unit() is the same `next() >> 8` / 2^24. I grepped `labrador::Random|core/random.h` across the repo: only tests use it, and no sample does.
findings.why: Presentation is allowed to depend on the engine, so this is now a second copy of an engine primitive. The rules layer cannot link the engine and must keep its own copy, but the particle field has no such restriction. The engine comment presents LineSweeper as the motivating client of an API that the sample never adopted.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `rng_`, next_random(), random_unit() and random_signed() with a `labrador::Random random_` member. Use unit(), and uniform_float(-1, 1) or `unit() * 2 - 1`. Keep the 'second stream, never World::rng' rationale in particles.h. Leave tick.cpp's copy, because the rules layer may not include the engine.
findings.verify_reason: particles.cpp:468-492 has the identical SplitMix32 constants and the >>8 / 2^24 unit as engine/core/random.cpp:10-22, whose comment names LineSweeper's particles as a source. git grep finds no sample include of core/random.h. particles.h:336-341 justifies only a separate stream from World::rng, which a labrador::Random member would still be. Not tracked in TODO or code-hygiene.md.

findings.title: Particle units are documented as back-buffer pixels, but sparks live in board space
findings.evidence: particles.h:143 "// Back-buffer pixels, and pixels per second."; particles.h:162 "// The side of the quad, in pixels, at a heat of one."; particles.cpp:17 "// Pixels per second squared, downward." Sparks are born at layout.h's cell_centre(), which is "in board space: the 1280x720 ... which the camera fits to whatever buffer there is" (layout.h:26-27). arrangement.h scales board space to the buffer.
findings.why: Since the arrangement camera was added, positions, speeds, sizes and gravity are board units that the camera scales. They match pixels only at exactly 1280x720. A reader tuning sizes for a phone would be misled.
findings.suggested_fix: Say "board units" (and board units per second, or per second squared) in particles.h:143 and :162 and particles.cpp:17, as board_view.cpp:53-54 does for shadow_edge_width.
findings.verify_reason: particles.h:143 says 'Back-buffer pixels', :162 says 'in pixels', and particles.cpp:17 says 'Pixels per second squared'. layout.h:23 puts cells in board space, which the camera fits to the buffer, and arrangement.h:16-19 says the camera is the identity only at exactly 1280x720. board_view.cpp:53 already says 'board units'.

findings.title: The banner computes its panel rectangle and text origin twice, once for drawing and once for bounds
findings.evidence: draw(): `const float middle = well_origin_y + well_height * 0.5f;` (97), `RectangleF(well_origin_x, middle - banner_padding, well_width, this->text_size_.y + banner_padding * 2.0f)` (104-105), `std::floor(well_origin_x + (well_width - this->text_size_.x) * 0.5f)` (113-114). panel_bounds() repeats the rectangle (133-136), and update() repeats the floored x (81).
findings.why: bounds() and cull_bounds() are built from panel_bounds() and text_bounds_, but draw() works the same geometry out again on its own. SM-48 already filed a banner-extent defect (SRL-21), so these values need to stay in agreement, and a change to one copy would not reach the others.
findings.suggested_fix: Have draw() call this->panel_bounds() for the quad. Store the text origin in update(), or derive it from text_bounds_, so draw, bounds and cull all read one value.
findings.verify_reason: top_out_banner.cpp:97-105 (draw) and :131-136 (panel_bounds) compute the same rectangle independently. The floored text x appears both in update (:80-81) and in draw (:112-114). SRL-21 is closed (BACKLOG.md:1058), so this is not tracked, and extents that drift apart are exactly the defect class SRL-21 fixed.

findings.title: The 'fourth assert' that comments and the README point to is actually the third
findings.evidence: world.h:152 "THE FOUR ASSERTS, AND THE FOURTH IS THE INTERESTING ONE." The text then calls the next part "The first three" and goes on to describe has_unique_object_representations_v, which is the third static_assert (lines 170, 173, 176, 181; the fourth is `sizeof(World) == 276`). tables.h:329 "(world.h, the fourth assert)" cites it for the float ban. README.md:264 "The fourth assert is the one worth reading:" quotes the has_unique trait. world.h:196 "an invariant three asserts up": counting up from identical(), the third assert is is_trivially_destructible. world.cpp:12 "which world.h asserts three lines above this function's declaration": the assert is about 22 lines above it.
findings.why: Three files send the reader to the wrong assert, the sizeof check. These comments exist to say which line enforces the no-padding and no-float invariant.
findings.suggested_fix: Refer to the assert by name, not by position: "the has_unique_object_representations_v assert". Update world.h:152 and :196, tables.h:329, README.md:264 and world.cpp:12 to match.
findings.verify_reason: world.h:152 says 'the fourth is the interesting one', then describes has_unique_object_representations_v, which is the third static_assert (lines 170/173/176/181). tables.h:329 and README.md:264 repeat 'fourth'. world.cpp:12 says 'three lines above', but the assert is many lines above. Counting up from identical(), has_unique is two asserts up, so world.h:196 is wrong as well.

findings.title: pacing_world() is a verbatim copy of the frame bench's build_workload World

findings.title: Null-renderer setup copy-pasted three times in one file and again in two harnesses

findings.title: Subcase claims a per-cell comparison with a clear but asserts none
findings.why: The name states a policy, that a shattered row out-sparks a cleared row per cell, which nothing checks. If shatter tuning dropped below clear tuning, this subcase would still pass while claiming to guard against exactly that. The neighbouring case at line 273 does make the equivalent lock-versus-clear comparison.
findings.suggested_fix: Add CHECK(field.live() / well_columns > one_row_cleared() / well_columns) (move one_row_cleared above this case), or rename the subcase to what it asserts: 'a topped-out row shatters every one of its cells'.

findings.title: The content-copy rationale says "Two samples" but the repo has six

findings.verify_reason: CMakeLists.txt:201-203 says 'Two samples is few enough'. samples/ contains six sample directories.

findings.title: The build comment sends readers to board_view.cpp for the draw_rect rationale, which is not there

findings.title: The engine's premultiplied-blend contract is explained through DirectXTK internals that only one backend uses
findings.why: The rationale names one backend's implementation detail as the reason, although four of the five backends do not use DirectXTK SpriteBatch. A comment that can cite a named contract should cite it instead of re-deriving it (CONVENTIONS, Comments).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the DirectXTK paragraph with a citation, e.g. "draw_sprite blends premultiplied (engine/render/SEAM.md#5): dst = src.rgb + dst.rgb * (1 - a)", and keep the consequence for callers.
findings.verify_reason: palette.h:177-180 explains the blend through DirectXTK CommonStates::AlphaBlend. renderer.h:196-197 and SEAM.md#5 (line 181) state the premultiplied contract for every backend. CONVENTIONS asks for a rationale to be cited rather than re-derived, so this is valid. The equation the comment gives is still true for every backend, though, so it misleads only about the mechanism. Low.

findings.title: row_full() is written twice: in tick.cpp over a World and in particles.cpp over a cell array
findings.evidence: particles.cpp:108 `bool row_full(const std::array<std::uint8_t, well_columns * well_rows>& cells, int y)` and rules/tick.cpp:434 `bool row_full(const World& world, int y)`. The loop bodies are identical (`if (cells[...cell_index(x, y)] == cell_empty) return false;`).
findings.why: The particle field rebuilds the board as it was at lock to decide which rows the rules cleared. If the two definitions of 'full' ever diverge, the sparks come from the wrong rows, which is exactly the class of bug the TickResult change (G6-11) was made to remove. world.h already hosts pure cell queries that presentation may call (in_well, cell_index).
findings.suggested_fix: Declare one `constexpr bool row_full(const std::array<std::uint8_t, well_columns * well_rows>& cells, int y)` in world.h beside in_well, and call it from both tick.cpp and particles.cpp.
findings.verify_reason: particles.cpp:108-122 and tick.cpp:434-446 have the same loop, over a cell array and over World::cells respectively. Both use cell_index and cell_empty from world.h.

findings.title: Presentation headers explain themselves through history and predictions instead of current rationale
findings.evidence: particles.h:17 "THIS IS THE HALF OF THE SAMPLE THE README SAID WAS MISSING."; :27 "Nothing in this repository stood at that end until this file did."; :35-37 "IT ASKED THE ENGINE FOR NOTHING. ... the one verb renderer.h already had"; :42-44 "WHAT IT COSTS, PRICED BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN. bench/render_bench.cpp puts the engine's quad arithmetic at 35.4 ns a sprite on this desktop". palette.h:198-199 "the one the README spent a section predicting would need an atlas" and :213-215 "the sample predicted the glow would arrive as an atlas of soft radial dots and it did not". particles.cpp:32-34 "six sparks of three and a half pixels for a third of a second was invisible on screen". particles.cpp:422-424 "records that the atlas the sample predicted it would need turned out not to be needed". arrangement.h:18-20 "draws byte for byte what it drew before there was a camera here". touch_controls.h:19-23 "which is what README, Still open, said the pad's pricing had settled ... The engine gained a touch device".
findings.why: CONVENTIONS forbids history in comments, and SM-48 did not cover these files. The 35.4 ns per sprite is a machine-specific measurement embedded in a header, and it will go stale without anyone noticing.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite in the present tense: keep the rationale (one object for the whole field, no engine change needed, the cost is about a fiftieth of a frame) and cite README sections for the history and measurements. Remove the 'predicted', 'until this file did' and 'before there was a camera' narration.
findings.verify_reason: The cited text is present: particles.h:16 'THE HALF OF THE SAMPLE THE README SAID WAS MISSING', :26 'until this file did', :41-43 '35.4 ns a sprite on this desktop'. Also present are palette.h:198-215 'predicted', particles.cpp:32-34 and :419-422, arrangement.h:18-19 'before there was a camera', and touch_controls.h:19-23. SM-48's targets (code-hygiene.md:171-173) did not include these files. This is a CONVENTIONS archaeology violation in comments only, so low.

findings.title: ParticleField says BoardView needs the resource table to measure text; BoardView measures nothing
findings.evidence: "BoardView needs the table because it measures text, and measuring walks a font atlas." `grep -rn measure_text samples/linesweeper` matches only top_out_banner.cpp:63, touch_controls.cpp:151 and pause_state.cpp:72. BoardView's constructor only resolves a texture and a font handle (board_view.cpp:62-63).

findings.suggested_fix: Say BoardView takes the table to resolve its font and texture by name (and draws text), or contrast with TopOutBanner, which does measure text.

findings.title: try_move() returns a bool that no caller reads
findings.evidence: `bool try_move(World& world, int dx)`. I grepped `try_move` repo-wide: the only calls are tick.cpp:348 `try_move(world, dx);` and tick.cpp:360 `try_move(world, dx);`, and both discard the result.
findings.why: The unused return value suggests that a blocked move matters to the caller, but it does not. That is a small cost in reading the code that teaches the rules.
findings.suggested_fix: Make it `void`, or use the result if a blocked shift is meant to affect the shift timer.
findings.verify_reason: tick.cpp:197 'bool try_move(World& world, int dx)' returns false or true. The only callers (348, 360) discard the result.

findings.title: world.cpp claims to be the rules layer's only translation unit and says tick.cpp is still to come
findings.why: This is history left in an implementation comment, and it is now false: there are three translation units and tick.cpp has existed for a long time.

findings.title: Rules and state comments narrate past bugs and the review that found them
findings.evidence: world.h:241-245 "The presentation reconstructed both from shadow(before) ... and the field then found a full row at the wrong height and threw its sparks there (docs/review/gpt6/README.md, G6-11)." resume_gate.h:13-15 "the piece the player was looking at when they paused went through the floor the instant they chose RESUME ... (docs/review/gpt6/README.md, G6-07)." resume_gate.h:35 "the leak there was a hard drop on the first dealt piece." resume_gate.h:39-40 "which is where the review found the leak in the first place."
findings.why: These describe what the code used to do and how a review found it, which belongs in git history (CONVENTIONS, Comments). The present-tense rationale (a tick locks and clears in one step; a held key is a press after resume) is enough without the narrative.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite as conditions: "Reconstructing from shadow(before) is wrong whenever a piece moves on its locking tick" and "Without the mask, a key held through RESUME is a press to tick()". Drop the review citations and the 'found the leak' sentences.

findings.title: The COLOURS row carries a placeholder PauseChoice::resume that is never used
findings.evidence: `struct Row { std::wstring text; PauseChoice choice; };` with `{ colours_text(*this->palette_), PauseChoice::resume },`. The loop then special-cases `index == colours_row_index` and ignores `entry.choice` for that row.
findings.why: The table suggests that activating COLOURS resumes the game, but it actually cycles the palette. A reader, or a later edit that drops the index special case, would wire up the wrong behaviour.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the choice optional (`std::optional<PauseChoice>`, std::nullopt for COLOURS) and branch on that instead of on colours_row_index.
findings.verify_reason: The placeholder PauseChoice::resume on the COLOURS row is real (pause_state.cpp:157). The comment at 146-148, however, says COLOURS 'never submits its placeholder choice', so readers are told, which weakens the misleading-table argument. std::optional would be marginally clearer.

findings.title: arrange_screen() is copied identically into PlayState, PauseState and PacingState
findings.evidence: pause_state.cpp:216-224 `this->arrangement_ = arrange(this->app_->resolution_manager()->resolution_vec()); this->scene_->clear_views(); this->scene_->add_view(this->arrangement_.viewport, this->arrangement_.camera);`. The same body is at states/play_state.cpp:192-200 and web/pacing_state.cpp:22-28.

findings.suggested_fix: Add one free function, for example `Arrangement arrange_scene(labrador::Scene&, const labrador::Application&)` in arrangement.h/.cpp, that returns the arrangement after installing its view, and call it from all three states.
findings.verify_reason: Identical arrange/clear_views/add_view bodies at play_state.cpp:192-200 and pacing_state.cpp:22-28. pause_state's copy is cited at 216-224; I did not re-open it, but the pattern matches.

findings.title: Asset-name constants are copied into five files, and the comment that lists the copies names only one
findings.evidence: play_state.cpp:29 "Spelt here as well as in board_view.cpp for the reason font_name is". `const std::string block_texture_name = "white";` and `font_name = "jetbrains_mono_bold_16"` also appear in top_out_banner.cpp:19-20, touch_controls.cpp:16-17 and pause_state.cpp:31-32. pacing_state.cpp:36/42/46 writes the same literals inline.
findings.why: Renaming the white texture or the font means editing six files, and the comment that lists the copies is out of date.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare `inline const` asset names once in a presentation header (e.g. layout.h or a small assets header) and use them everywhere, or at least fix the comment so it does not list copies.
findings.verify_reason: The 'white' and 'jetbrains_mono_bold_16' constants are declared in board_view.cpp:20-21, top_out_banner.cpp:19-20, touch_controls.cpp:16-17, pause_state.cpp:31-32 and play_state.cpp:26/33, and pacing_state.cpp:36/41 has them inline. play_state.cpp:29 names only board_view.cpp.

findings.title: Include order breaks the sample's own sorted pattern; main.cpp uses std::move without <utility>
findings.evidence: play_state.h:13-15 `#include "samples/linesweeper/states/pause_state.h"` / `"samples/linesweeper/states/resume_gate.h"` / `"samples/linesweeper/rules/world.h"`: rules/ comes after states/, while every other file sorts its project includes. main.cpp:15-16 `#include <exception>` then `#include <cstdio>`, and main.cpp:44 `Application app(std::move(options));` with no <utility>, which main_web.cpp:33 does include.
findings.why: Small inconsistencies with sibling files. The missing <utility> relies on a transitive include.
findings.suggested_fix: Move rules/world.h above the states/ includes in play_state.h. Sort main.cpp's standard headers and add <utility>.
findings.verify_reason: play_state.h:13-15 lists rules/world.h after the states/ includes. main.cpp:15-16 has <exception> before <cstdio>, and main.cpp:44 uses std::move without <utility>, which main_web.cpp:33 does include. These are trivial inconsistencies.

findings.title: The fixture's failure message hard-codes 9,600 instead of using pacing_particle_count
findings.evidence: `"The browser pacing top-out must have exactly 9,600 live particles "` while the check right above it compares against `pacing_particle_count`.
findings.why: If the constant changes, the error message will state a different expected value from the one actually checked.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the message with std::to_string(pacing_particle_count).
findings.verify_reason: pacing_fixture.cpp:51 message hard-codes '9,600' while the check at line 49 compares against pacing_particle_count.

findings.title: pacing_mode() casts an unchecked page integer straight into PacingMode
findings.evidence: `PacingMode pacing_mode() { return static_cast<PacingMode>(linesweeper_pacing_mode()); }`, which is fed by `return Module["labradorPacingMode"] || 0;` (line 19). tools/web_pacing/page.js:130 sets `Module['labradorPacingMode'] = modes[modeName];`.
findings.why: Any value other than 0-3 becomes an unnamed enumerator. main_web.cpp treats every value except `disabled` as a request to start the pacing observer, so a mistyped mode silently runs the instrument against ordinary play instead of failing. The engine's stated contract (T6) is that a broken contract fails loudly.
findings.suggested_fix: Range-check the integer and throw std::runtime_error (which main_web reports through Module.onError) for unknown values, or map them explicitly with a switch.
findings.verify_reason: The unchecked static_cast is at pacing_observer.cpp:67-70. The claimed failure (a mistyped mode silently runs the instrument) is prevented upstream: tools/web_pacing/page.js:8-9 throws unless the mode name is play, topout or topout-frozen, and only then sets 1, 2 or 3. What remains is a defensive range check on a test-only path.

findings.title: pacing_state.cpp uses std::ignore and std::uint64_t without their headers
findings.evidence: `std::ignore = this->scene_.add(...)` (lines 33, 38, 39, 43) and `const std::uint64_t completed = ...` (line 56). The includes are only `<memory>` and `<utility>`. std::ignore is declared in <tuple> and std::uint64_t in <cstdint>.
findings.why: Both rely on transitive includes from libc++ that the standard does not guarantee.
findings.suggested_fix: Include <tuple> and <cstdint>.
findings.verify_reason: pacing_state.cpp uses std::ignore with no <tuple>, while every other std::ignore user in engine/ includes <tuple>. The std::uint64_t half is weaker: the file's own header pacing_state.h includes pacing_observer.h, which includes <cstdint>.

findings.title: Web test hooks hard-code counts that already have a named source
findings.evidence: test_input.cpp:49 `pending.code_index >= 9 || typeof pending.down !== "boolean") {` validates against `constexpr std::array<labrador::Key, 9> sampled_keys` (line 111). pacing_fixture.cpp:51 writes "The browser pacing top-out must have exactly 9,600 live particles" in the error text instead of using pacing_particle_count. pacing_state.cpp:57 `++this->warmup_updates_ >= 300` duplicates the "waits 300 fixed steps" in pacing_state.h:18.
findings.why: Adding a key to sampled_keys without editing the JavaScript literal would reject valid phases. The error text and the warm-up length can drift from the constants they describe.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass sampled_keys.size() into linesweeper_test_input_begin, build the message from std::to_string(pacing_particle_count), and name the warm-up as a constexpr next to PacingState.
findings.verify_reason: test_input.cpp:49 has `pending.code_index >= 9` while :111 declares `std::array<labrador::Key, 9> sampled_keys`. pacing_fixture.cpp:51 hard-codes '9,600' beside pacing_particle_count (pacing_fixture.h:12). pacing_state.cpp:57 has a literal 300 that mirrors pacing_state.h:18.

findings.title: Repository-root include directories duplicate what LineSweeperRules already exports PUBLIC
findings.evidence:
# The tests include their own fixtures header from the repository root, the
# same way everything else does.
target_include_directories(LineSweeperTests PRIVATE
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../.."
)
The same block appears again for LineSweeperViewTests at lines 63-65. samples/linesweeper/CMakeLists.txt:33-35 has `target_include_directories(LineSweeperRules PUBLIC "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../..")`, and both test targets link LineSweeperRules through labrador_add_test_suite (tests/CMakeLists.txt:14, `target_link_libraries(${name} PRIVATE ${suite_LINKS} ...)`).
findings.why: Both targets already get the repository root through LineSweeperRules' PUBLIC usage requirement, so the explicit blocks are dead configuration. The comment explaining them suggests they are needed, which misleads anyone trimming the build.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete both PRIVATE repository-root include blocks and the comment, or keep one comment noting that the root comes from LineSweeperRules.
findings.verify_reason: tests/linesweeper/CMakeLists.txt:19-23 and 63-65 add the repository root PRIVATE. samples/linesweeper/CMakeLists.txt adds it PUBLIC on LineSweeperRules, which both suites link through labrador_add_test_suite's target_link_libraries. So the blocks are redundant.

findings.title: rapidjson include path added unconditionally, but only the WIN32-only sources use it
findings.evidence:
target_include_directories(LineSweeperViewTests SYSTEM PRIVATE
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../../external/rapidjson/include"
)
Grep for `rapidjson` in tests/linesweeper/ and in the sources this target compiles finds only frame_result_tests.cpp and bench/linesweeper_frame_result.cpp. Both are added inside `if(WIN32)` at lines 72-79. LabradorEngine keeps rapidjson PRIVATE (engine/CMakeLists.txt:384).
findings.why: On wasm builds the target gets a third-party include path that none of its sources use. That hides which sources actually depend on rapidjson, the opposite of what the engine's 'PRIVATE and SYSTEM' rationale is trying to achieve.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the SYSTEM rapidjson include into the existing `if(WIN32)` block, next to the frame-result sources that need it.
findings.verify_reason: The SYSTEM rapidjson include is at CMakeLists.txt:66-68, unconditional. Within the test sources, only frame_result_tests.cpp and bench/linesweeper_frame_result.cpp include rapidjson, and both are added inside if(WIN32) at 72-79.

findings.title: Seven-kind array duplicated and magic 7 used instead of kind_count/size()
findings.evidence:
constexpr std::array<Kind, 7> kinds = { Kind::i, Kind::j, Kind::l,
		Kind::o, Kind::s, Kind::t, Kind::z };  (identical in palette_tests.cpp:42-43) and later `for (int index = 0; index < 7; ++index)` (line 114) and `std::array<int, 8> drawn` (line 151).
findings.why: world.h provides linesweeper::kind_count. The literal 7 and 8 and the copied array would drift silently if the kinds changed, and the loop bound repeats the array's size instead of reading it.
findings.suggested_fix: Size the array with linesweeper::kind_count, loop to kinds.size(), and use kind_count + 1 for `drawn`. Optionally share the array through well_fixtures.h.

findings.title: Uses std::invalid_argument/std::runtime_error without <stdexcept>
findings.why: The file compiles only through transitive includes. Siblings frame_statistics_tests.cpp and pacing_fixture_tests.cpp include <stdexcept> for the same assertions.
findings.suggested_fix: Add #include <stdexcept>.
findings.verify_reason: frame_result_tests.cpp includes chrono/filesystem/string/system_error/utility/vector, no <stdexcept>, yet uses std::invalid_argument (102,109) and std::runtime_error (201). Siblings frame_statistics_tests.cpp:5 and pacing_fixture_tests.cpp:9 include it.

findings.title: "benchmark's exact" world is checked against hand-copied literals, not against the benchmark
findings.why: The same world is built twice: by pacing_world() (samples/linesweeper/web/pacing_fixture.cpp:12-37) and by LineSweeperFrameBench::build_workload() (bench/linesweeper_frame_bench.cpp:190-213). The test restates the values a third time as literals and never compares against the bench. If either builder changes, the claimed parity breaks silently, or the test simply goes on pinning whatever pacing_world() returns. It also spells the kind count as a bare `% 7` instead of kind_count.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the bench call linesweeper::pacing_world() (or a shared helper both include), so parity holds by construction. Then reduce this test to the properties that matter and use kind_count, or rename it so it no longer claims to match the benchmark.
findings.verify_reason: The test is at lines 25-62, not 93-130. Its claim holds. pacing_world() (pacing_fixture.cpp:12-37) and the bench's build_workload() (linesweeper_frame_bench.cpp:190-213) build the same world independently. The test pins literals with a bare '% 7' and never compares against the bench, and pacing-method.md:210 only says the fixture 'reproduces' build_workload. The bench is a Release tool outside ctest and the values are fixed fixture constants, so drift risk is real but the impact is low.

findings.title: std::function wraps local lambdas where the unit elsewhere uses `const auto`; `size_t` used unqualified without <cstddef>
findings.why: std::function adds type erasure (and possibly an allocation) only to avoid writing `auto`, which the conventions explicitly allow here, and it makes this file inconsistent with its siblings. The unqualified `size_t` and the missing standard headers depend on transitive includes, against the include-what-you-use style the rest of the unit follows.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `const auto draw_at = [&](float fraction)` and `const auto draw = [&]()`, then drop <functional>. Write std::size_t and include <cstddef> in particle_draw_tests.cpp, and include <stdexcept> in frame_result_tests.cpp.
findings.verify_reason: The std::function lambdas are at particle_draw_tests.cpp:99 and 166, not 338/405. CONVENTIONS.md:62-69 says a lambda held in a variable is held in an auto, and siblings use const auto (touch_controls 285/324, view_tests 788). The file uses unqualified size_t (34, 88, 116, ...) with no <cstddef> include. frame_result_tests.cpp uses std::invalid_argument (102, 109) and std::runtime_error (201) with no <stdexcept> include. The line numbers are wrong but the substance holds.

findings.title: Comment names the wrong static_assert as the padding guarantee
findings.evidence:
"is defined only because World has no padding bits, which is what the
	// fourth static_assert in world.h is for."  In samples/linesweeper/rules/world.h the asserts are, in order: is_trivially_copyable_v (169), is_trivially_destructible_v (172), has_unique_object_representations_v (175), sizeof(World) == 276 (181). The no-padding assert is the third; the fourth is the size pin.
findings.why: This comment explains why the test's memcmp is well-defined. A reader who follows it lands on the size assert, which is not the assert that makes memcmp legal. (world.h's own heading, 'THE FOUR ASSERTS, AND THE FOURTH IS THE INTERESTING ONE', has the same miscount, outside this unit.)
findings.suggested_fix: Name the trait instead of a position: "...which is what world.h's has_unique_object_representations_v assert is for." Fix world.h's heading in the same change.
findings.verify_reason: replay_tests.cpp:68-71 says 'fourth static_assert in world.h'; world.h:170-181 has has_unique_object_representations_v third, sizeof==276 fourth. Real miscount (world.h:152 heading shares it, though its own prose names the trait), but a comment miscount whose trait is named right beside it in world.h is not high.

findings.title: Test name and comment claim more than the assertion proves
findings.evidence: TEST_CASE("the seed is the only thing that changes the deal") ... for (std::uint32_t seed = 1; seed <= 4; ++seed) { ... if (seeded.current.kind != fresh.current.kind) any_different = true; } // Zero is a legal seed and a different game from one ... CHECK(any_different);
findings.why: The case shows only that at least one of seeds 1..4 deals a different first piece from seed 0. It shows neither that the seed is the only input that changes the deal, nor that seed 1 specifically differs from seed 0, which is what the comment says.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to what is asserted, e.g. 'a different seed can deal a different first piece, and zero is a working seed'. Also assert that a seed-0 World deals a piece (current.kind != Kind::none) to back the xorshift remark.
findings.verify_reason: replay_tests.cpp:131-153 confirmed: name says 'only thing that changes the deal', assertion is any of seeds 1..4 differs from seed 0. Overclaiming test name, low impact.

findings.title: Comments narrate review provenance and backlog IDs instead of the contract
findings.evidence:
// What it pins is the leak the review found and the policy that closes it
// (docs/review/gpt6/README.md, G6-07), ... the first case is the review's reproduction  ; also view_tests.cpp:292-294 "gives a burst from the wrong row (docs/review/gpt6/README.md, G6-11): this is the review's board", view_tests.cpp:718 "// BDP-22: a player who asked for reduced motion ...", touch_controls_tests.cpp:99 "so the window main.cpp opens draws as it always did".
findings.why: CONVENTIONS forbids comments about how the code came to be. 'The leak the review found', 'the review's board' and a backlog ticket tag are provenance that git log answers. The present-tense policy each test pins is already stated beside them.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the present-tense policy sentences and drop the review/backlog provenance ('the review found', 'the review's board', 'BDP-22:', 'as it always did').
findings.verify_reason: Cited 172-177 wrong; text is at resume_gate_tests.cpp:19-21. CONVENTIONS 'Archaeology' forbids how-code-came-to-be comments; 'the leak the review found'/'the review's reproduction' and view_tests 'BDP-22:'/'G6-11 ... the review's board' are partly provenance, though a doc citation is also a checked citation form. touch_controls 'as it always did' is mild. Low.

findings.title: Unsigned score narrowed into int and compared signed/unsigned
findings.why: World::score is std::uint32_t. The implicit narrowing and the mixed-sign comparison compile only because doctest's expression decomposition moves the comparison into a system header, where /W4's C4018 and clang's -Wsign-compare are not reported. It goes against the explicit-type rule (declare the type the value has).
findings.suggested_fix: const std::uint32_t score_before = world.score;
findings.verify_reason: Cited 202-207 is wrong (resume_gate_tests.cpp is 150 lines). Line 47 'const int score_before = world.score;' with world.h:117 'std::uint32_t score'; line 52 compares. Real narrowing/sign mix.

findings.title: Score expectations hard-coded where sibling subcases use the tables
findings.why: A retune of tables.h fails this case with bare numbers when the formula is right there. The file is also inconsistent: other subcases express expectations through line_score/spin_score/mini_spin_score.
findings.suggested_fix: line_score[4], then line_score[4] + line_score[4] * back_to_back_numerator / back_to_back_denominator + combo_score.
findings.verify_reason: scoring_tests.cpp ~90 REQUIRE(world.score == 800) and CHECK(world.score == 800 + 1200 + 50) confirmed, while line 62 uses line_score[4]. Literal expectations are a defensible independent oracle; inconsistency is cosmetic.

findings.title: Reason given for not constructing TouchControls contradicts the CMake comment
findings.evidence:
// ... TouchControls itself measures its
// labels through a font a device filled and is not constructed here.  vs tests/linesweeper/CMakeLists.txt: "the TouchControls object beside them is constructed by the native-null state cases, where the sample font can be loaded without a graphics device."
findings.why: The test says a device has to fill the font. The CMake file, and board_view_tests.cpp's header ('A BOARDVIEW NEEDS A FONT, NOT A DEVICE'), say the null backend loads fonts without a device. A reader gets the wrong idea of why the object is absent here.
findings.suggested_fix: Say it is not constructed here because measuring needs a loaded font, which only the null-render configurations provide (focus_pause_tests.cpp constructs it).
findings.verify_reason: touch_controls_tests.cpp:39-40 says TouchControls measures 'through a font a device filled'; tests/linesweeper/CMakeLists.txt says it is constructed by the native-null cases 'where the sample font can be loaded without a graphics device'. Mild inconsistency.

findings.title: Local `inside` predicate re-implements RectangleF::contains
findings.why: A helper that duplicates a public engine predicate can drift silently, and the unit itself uses both spellings for the same question. (`overlaps` differs from RectangleF::intersects on whether touching edges count, so it has a reason to exist. It would be clearer with a comment saying that strictness is the point.)
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `inside(a, b)` with `b.contains(a)`. Comment `overlaps` to say it deliberately treats shared edges as not overlapping, which is why it is not RectangleF::intersects.
findings.verify_reason: touch_controls_tests.cpp:65-70 inside() is logically identical to RectangleF::contains at engine/math/rectanglef.cpp:118-124 (the same four comparisons, reordered). It is used at lines 155 and 245, and top_out_banner_tests uses bounds.contains.

findings.title: Literals duplicate arrangement.h constants, and the comment misnames the 620
findings.why: 620 is linesweeper::portrait_width (arrangement.h:49), not 'the block': the file's own board_block (line 46) is 550 units wide. The same applies to 1280.0f/720.0f (landscape_width exists) and 640.0f (the centre) throughout the file. If arrangement.h changes, these tests fail with numbers that do not say which constant they mirror.
findings.suggested_fix: Use linesweeper::portrait_width, landscape_width and the like, or name local constants after them. Reword the comment to 'the portrait frame's 620 units (portrait_width)'.
findings.verify_reason: touch_controls_tests.cpp:162-176 literal 620/1170/620 confirmed; arrangement.h:49 portrait_width=620, board_block is 550 wide so 'block's 620 units' is loose wording. Hard-coded expected values are a legitimate independent oracle in tests; only the comment wording is a real defect.

findings.title: View tests re-implement the well fixtures under a clashing name
findings.why: Both binaries can include well_fixtures.h: it depends only on rules headers, and LineSweeperViewTests links LineSweeperRules. Yet the view tests keep a second fill_row with different semantics (no holes, kind 1) under the same name. particle_draw_tests.cpp (lines 273, 327, 392), pacing_fixture_tests.cpp (295) and board_view_tests.cpp (116) also hand-write the same `world.cells[static_cast<size_t>(cell_index(...))] = ...` that set_cell exists to replace.
findings.suggested_fix: Include tests/linesweeper/well_fixtures.h in the view-side tests. Use set_cell/fill_row(world, y, {}), add a clear_row there if needed, and delete the local copies.
findings.verify_reason: view_tests.cpp:61-82 has local fill/fill_row/clear_row; well_fixtures.h is included only by the five LineSweeperTests files. But the cited particle_draw_tests.cpp lines 273/327/392 do not exist (file is 221 lines; real sites 34, 88, 153). Three tiny helpers in an anonymous namespace; low.

findings.title: about_to_clear's comment cites assertions the function does not contain
findings.why: The function has no assertions. The 'proof' at line 236-237 is REQUIRE(landed.kind == Kind::o), which checks that a piece exists, not where shadow() puts it. Only the later REQUIRE(world.lines == 1) shows the row completed, so the comment overstates what is verified.
findings.suggested_fix: Point the comment at the case that checks the setup and what it checks (the row clears: world.lines == 1). Or make the shadow check real, e.g. REQUIRE(landed.y == ...) and REQUIRE(landed.x == well_columns - 2).
findings.verify_reason: about_to_clear() (view_tests.cpp ~103-122) contains no assertions despite the comment; the caller's 'setup's own proof' is only REQUIRE(landed.kind == Kind::o). Real stale comment, but it is a comment inaccuracy in a test helper.

findings.title: A capture line with too many words gets a misleading arity message
findings.evidence: expected = words.size() == 3 ? 3 : 2;  ...  refuse(path, line, "'" + verb + "' takes " + std::to_string(expected - 1) + " argument" + (expected == 2 ? "" : "s") + ", not " + std::to_string(words.size() - 1));
findings.why: `capture a.png paused extra` is refused with "'capture' takes 1 argument, not 3". In fact capture takes one or two arguments (the file and an optional `paused`). The script's stated design goal is an error that tells the editor exactly what is wrong on that line.
findings.suggested_fix: For capture, refuse sizes other than 2 and 3 with their own message: "'capture' takes a file name and optionally paused".
findings.verify_reason: capture_script.cpp is 233 lines (the cited 314-349 is wrong). Line 184 sets expected = 2 when words.size() is not 3, and lines 214-219 then say "'capture' takes 1 argument, not 3" for a four-word line, although capture accepts an optional 'paused'. Real, low.

findings.title: "Same objects in the same order" omits PlayState's TouchControls
findings.evidence: main.cpp:19 "the tool owns the World and registers the same objects in the same order" and :135-137 "PlayState::init's objects, in PlayState::init's order, which is the sample's whole depth system: the board, the sparks over it, the banner over the sparks, then the hints." But samples/linesweeper/states/play_state.cpp:155-156 also registers `this->controls_ = this->scene_->add(std::make_unique<TouchControls>(resources));` after the hints. tools/linesweeper_capture/README.md:21-23 repeats the same list.
findings.why: The capture is described as a faithful copy of PlayState's scene, but it leaves out one registered object. It happens to draw nothing until a finger is seen, and that is exactly the assumption a maintainer needs written down when PlayState's scene changes.
findings.suggested_fix: Say that TouchControls is deliberately left out because it draws nothing until touch is seen and the captures are desktop frames, both in main.cpp and in the README paragraph.
findings.verify_reason: main.cpp:19 says 'registers the same objects in the same order', and :135-137 list the board, sparks, banner and hints. play_state.cpp:154-156 also adds TouchControls ('Touch controls draw over the other objects once a finger is seen'). Neither main.cpp nor tools/linesweeper_capture/README.md:21-23 mentions TouchControls (a grep for 'touch' finds nothing in either file). The omission is real and undocumented, though harmless for desktop frames.

findings.title: main.cpp includes <Windows.h> but uses nothing from it
findings.evidence: #include <Windows.h>
findings.why: Nothing in main.cpp calls a Win32 API. wmain and wchar_t need no header, and the only Windows work is WIC, which is in png_file.cpp. Including <Windows.h> in the translation unit that also pulls in engine and sample headers brings in its macros (min/max, near/far and so on) for no use, against the convention that a file includes only what it needs.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the include. Confirm with an x64-release build of LineSweeperCapture.
findings.verify_reason: main.cpp:46 includes <Windows.h>. A grep of main.cpp finds no Win32 type, macro or call; wmain needs no header, and png_file.h includes only <filesystem> and <vector>. The include arrived with eac9721 and appears unused. A build would confirm it, which I did not run.

findings.title: The 60 Hz rate and the 1280x720 size are re-typed as literals next to the constants that name them
findings.evidence: main.cpp:76 `constexpr float tick_seconds = 1.0f / 60.0f;` and :69-70 `frame_width = 1280; frame_height = 720;`, but :183-184 `std::printf("Sequence: %zu frames at 60 fps (%.3f seconds).\n", this->frames_, static_cast<double>(this->frames_) / 60.0);` and :388 `", not 1280x720, so these would not be the sample's frames."`. The usage text at :255 also hard-codes "every 60 Hz update".
findings.why: Each value has a named constant a few lines away, yet the printed duration and the refusal message re-type the numbers. If either constant changes, the output contradicts the behaviour.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `constexpr int ticks_per_second = 60;`, derive tick_seconds from it, and format the messages from ticks_per_second, frame_width and frame_height.
findings.verify_reason: main.cpp:76 defines tick_seconds = 1.0f/60.0f and :69-70 define frame_width and frame_height. :183-184 still print 'at 60 fps' and divide by the literal 60.0, :388 hard-codes 'not 1280x720', and the usage text at :255 says '60 Hz'. All as described.

themes.name: Small samples and components gallery
themes.desc:
Problems in minimal, collision, audio, local_multiplayer and components:
- Four differently-behaved --smoke-test parsers.
- Every browser main re-declares the onError bridge.
- local_multiplayer has an unreachable input mode.
- The minimal template re-measures its labels every frame, against Label's contract.
- Collision and audio pages lack touch-action: none.
- The collision sample reads only pad slot 0.
- Deadzones, route ticks and start positions are magic numbers.
- Bindings and font names are duplicated.
- verify_content.py relies on assert.
- The components layout and camera are duplicated, and the slider tail is repeated.
- A Python generator and an asset README disagree.
- Some comments are stale.
themes.story: Template-facing fixes go first: label measurement, the pad policy, touch-action and the onError bridge exported once by the engine. Each gets a samples/minimal README change-list line. Then unify the smoke-test argument parsing, remove the dead input mode, name the constants and fix the comments. Run each sample's PageTests and smoke tests.

findings.title: Collision and audio pages omit touch-action: none, which the published page contract requires
findings.evidence: collision/web/shell.html:23 `canvas { display: block; width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; background: #000; outline: none; }` and audio/web/shell.html:29 has the same rule. Compare minimal/web/shell.html:26 and local_multiplayer/web/shell.html:23 `... outline: none; touch-action: none; }`. The browser guide (website/.../guides/browser.mdx:622-623) says: `Keep tabindex="0" on the canvas ... and touch-action: none so a finger on it does not scroll the page.`
findings.why: Four sibling pages split two against two on a rule the website states as part of the page contract. On a touch device, a finger on the collision or audio canvas scrolls or zooms the page. Collision's header comment also says the page owes 'what LineSweeper's page owes', which includes touch-action: none.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `touch-action: none;` to the canvas rule in both pages, and mention it in their header comments as minimal's and local_multiplayer's comments do.
findings.verify_reason: collision/web/shell.html:23 and audio/web/shell.html:29 lack touch-action: none, while minimal and local_multiplayer have it. browser.mdx:622-623 tells pages to keep touch-action: none. samples/components/web/shell.html:23 also lacks it, so the fix should cover three pages.

findings.title: Comment says ComponentsTests checks the gallery's pointer rules without a browser, but nothing native tests them
findings.why: The rules for a release off the pressed row, stepping by left or right half of a value, Quit-by-release, the 20-unit grab margin, and keys cancelling a contact all live in GalleryState::update_pointer (gallery_state.cpp:326-411). ComponentsTests only covers PointerCapture, hit_target and Slider::drag_to/value_at. Its one GalleryState case (gallery_animation_tests.cpp) checks only the animation overlay. These rules run only in ComponentsPointerPageTests, which is registered only when configure finds a Chromium, so a regression there passes every native configuration.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the comment to say which pieces ComponentsTests covers (PointerCapture, hit_target, Slider), or add a native-null GalleryState case. That case would feed app.mouse()/app.touch() synthetic events, as gallery_animation_tests.cpp already does for the keyboard, and assert the status lines for release-off-row, value-half stepping and key-cancels-drag.
findings.verify_reason: pointer_input.mjs:10-11 says 'ComponentsTests holds each rule headlessly'. ComponentsTests covers PointerCapture (pointer_capture_tests.cpp), hit_target and Slider::value_at/drag_to. Its only GalleryState case (gallery_animation_tests.cpp) drives keyboard R and the preview overlay. GalleryState::update_pointer (gallery_state.cpp:325-411) is not exercised natively: release-off-row, value-half stepping, grab_margin and Quit-on-release run only in the Chromium page test.

findings.title: Three samples' --smoke-test modes, with real assertions, are run by hand only; only minimal's is in ctest
findings.evidence: Only `add_test(NAME MinimalSmokeTests COMMAND MinimalSample --smoke-test)` (samples/minimal/CMakeLists.txt:89) exists. The other smoke modes are checked by hand: local_multiplayer README "the existing null smoke run exits 0", collision README:83 "This is a device test, separate from CTest", audio README:47 `start "" /wait ...AudioSample.exe --smoke-test`. They call `state.verify_smoke_test()` (throws "LocalMultiplayerSample: scripted players or views diverged") and `audio_sample::smoke_test()`.
findings.why: local_multiplayer's smoke test needs no device under null render ('null records the draws without pixels'), and audio's needs no graphics device. Both could run in CI the way the null-backend view tests do. As things stand, their assertions only catch regressions when someone remembers to run them.
findings.suggested_fix: Register LocalMultiplayerSmokeTests (null render and native) and an AudioSmokeTests under null audio, plus CollisionSmokeTests where MinimalSmokeTests already runs. Update tests/ctest_inventory.json and the READMEs in the same commit.
findings.verify_reason: Only MinimalSmokeTests is registered (samples/minimal/CMakeLists.txt:89). ctest_inventory.json has no other smoke entry. The collision README calls its smoke run 'a device test, separate from CTest', but minimal's device smoke test is in CTest, so that reason does not hold. Local_multiplayer's null-render smoke run and audio's null-audio smoke run need no device and assert real behaviour (verify_smoke_test, audio_sample::smoke_test), but they are run only by hand. The gap is not tracked in TODO or code-hygiene.

findings.title: PlayState's unbound, non-smoke input mode is unreachable; its quit and stick-reading code computes values that are always thrown away
findings.evidence: play_state.cpp:50-53 `else { quit = quit || pads.pressed(0, GamepadButton::b) || pads.pressed(1, GamepadButton::b); }` and :61-64 `const std::array<Vector2F, Arena::player_count> sticks = { pads.state(0).left_stick, pads.state(1).left_stick }; std::array<Vector2F, Arena::player_count> directions = read_directions(keyboard, sticks);`; play_state.h:17 `explicit PlayState(labrador::Application* app, bool smoke_test = false);`. Grepped `PlayState(` across samples, tests, tools and website: the only constructions are main.cpp:77 `multiplayer::PlayState state(&app, true);` and JoinState's `std::make_unique<PlayState>(this->app_, sources)`, which delegates to PlayState(app) and then sets bound_sources_ = true.
findings.why: Nothing ever builds bound_sources_ == false with smoke_test_ == false. In the smoke path, `if (!this->smoke_test_ && quit)` ignores the quit and `directions = { ... }` overwrites the directions. The 'pad 0 and pad 1 quit' branch and the read_directions(keyboard, sticks) call therefore only compute values nobody reads. A reader of this teaching sample sees a third input policy, fixed to slots 0 and 1, that the README never describes.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the two real modes explicit: a smoke constructor (or a scripted-directions flag) and a bound-sources constructor. Drop the default `smoke_test = false` argument, and remove the else-quit branch and the unconditional read_directions call. The smoke title can stay as the scripted mode's label.
findings.verify_reason: play_state.cpp:50-64 matches. git grep shows PlayState constructed only at main.cpp:77 (smoke, true) and join_state.cpp:160 (bound sources); main_web.cpp does not construct it. read_directions' result at :64 is always overwritten by the bound branch or the smoke override, and the else-quit branch is ignored in smoke mode. Not tracked in code-hygiene.md or TODO.md.

findings.title: The template re-measures ten labels every frame, against Label's stated contract
findings.evidence:
hello_state.cpp:164-178 `for (size_t i = 0; i < this->touch_markers_.size(); ++i) { ... marker->set_text(L"+" + std::to_wstring(points[i].id)); ... else { marker->set_text(L""); } }`
engine/render/label.h:31-33 `set_text(L"") is the supported way to hide it; it re-measures on every call, so a caller that would do it every frame gates it on a change, as LineSweeper's play state does.`
The same applies to samples/audio/audio_state.cpp:84 `this->refresh_status();`, which runs every tick and at :94-99 builds a std::wostringstream and calls `this->status_->set_text(text.str());`.
findings.why: TouchState::capacity is 10 (engine/input/touch.h:59). So the new-project template allocates a string and walks the font for ten labels on every tick, even with no finger down. This is the pattern the Label header tells callers to avoid. Since minimal is the file people copy, the wasteful pattern spreads into new games. The audio sample does the same with a stringstream, every tick.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the last shown id or empty state per marker and call set_text only when it changes. In AudioState, refresh the status only after an input changed the board or the loop state changed.
findings.verify_reason: hello_state.cpp:164-178 calls set_text on all touch_markers_ (capacity 10, touch.h:59) every update, including set_text(L""). TextObject::set_text (text_object.cpp:74-78) always remeasures. label.h:31-33 tells callers to gate this on a change. audio_state.cpp:84 calls refresh_status every tick, and that builds a wostringstream and calls set_text. Neither is listed in code-hygiene.md or TODO. Because this is the template people copy, medium fits.

findings.title: Three samples, three namespace styles; audio_sample is not one lowercase word
findings.evidence: audio_state.h:11 `namespace audio_sample`; collision/body.h:6 `namespace collisiondemo`; local_multiplayer/arena.h:9 `namespace multiplayer`; collision/CMakeLists.txt:5 `add_library(CollisionExample STATIC body.cpp arena.cpp)` beside target `CollisionSample`.
findings.why: CONVENTIONS' table says a namespace is 'one lowercase word', and audio_sample breaks that. The collision sample alone uses three names for itself (demo, Example, Sample). Readers moving between samples meet naming that differs for no reason.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose one pattern, for example `audiosample`/`collisionsample`/`multiplayer`, or the plain folder word `audio`/`collision`/`multiplayer`. Rename CollisionExample to CollisionSampleLibrary or similar so it matches the target.
findings.verify_reason: CONVENTIONS.md:24 says namespaces are 'one lowercase word'. audio/*.h use `audio_sample`, collision uses `collisiondemo`, and the collision CMakeLists has CollisionExample beside the CollisionSample target.

findings.title: The audio-only manifest filter is duplicated between the Windows smoke test and the Web Audio test
findings.evidence: smoke_test.cpp:52-61 `AssetManifest audio_manifest; audio_manifest.source_path = manifest.source_path; for (const AssetEntry& entry : manifest.entries) { if (entry.kind == "sound_bank") { ... audio_manifest.entries.push_back(entry); } }` and tests.cpp:150-155 has the same loop
findings.why: tests.cpp:137-142 says this test takes 'The same steps smoke_test.cpp takes on Windows'. Those steps are copied by hand, so the two can drift (they already differ: only the smoke test requires `!entry.optional`).
findings.suggested_fix: Move a small `audio_entries(const AssetManifest&)` helper next to SoundBoard, which both targets already link, and call it from both.
findings.verify_reason: smoke_test.cpp:52-61 and tests.cpp:150-155 have the same filter loop; only the smoke test has the require(!entry.optional). The comment at tests.cpp:138 says 'The same steps'. The loop is four lines in test and smoke code, so the impact is trivial.

findings.title: Drone re-implements tone()'s sinusoid and full-scale literal inline; fade length is a bare literal
findings.evidence:
round(32767 * (0.15 * math.sin(2 * math.pi * 220 * index / SAMPLE_RATE)
                       + 0.075 * math.sin(2 * math.pi * 330 * index / SAMPLE_RATE)))
findings.why: The full-scale 32767 and the sine expression are repeated rather than shared with tone() (line 22-24), and `fade = round(0.012 * SAMPLE_RATE)` at line 19 is an unnamed 12 ms constant. The README's amplitude claim depends on these values, but they are scattered across three expressions.
findings.suggested_fix: Add FULL_SCALE = 32767 and FADE_SECONDS = 0.012 constants, plus a `sine(frequency, index)` helper that both tone() and the drone use.
findings.verify_reason: generate_waves.py:19 has the bare 0.012 fade, and lines 22 and 46 repeat 32767 and the sine expression. The drone is a two-partial sum with no fade, so it cannot just call tone(). This is real but trivial in a 55-line one-shot generator.

findings.title: Content verifier relies on assert statements, so running it under python -O checks nothing and still prints success
findings.evidence: verify_content.py:21 `assert header[:3] == (0x444E4257, 46, 44), "unexpected XWB header"` ... :57 `assert data[pcm_offset + start:pcm_offset + start + length] == pcm` ... :61 `print(f"{expected}: {len(values)} samples; source PCM matches named XWB entry")`
findings.why: Python strips assert statements under -O or PYTHONOPTIMIZE. The README presents this script as the check that 'checks format, durations, names, signal levels and every payload byte'. In an optimized interpreter every check vanishes and the script still prints 'source PCM matches named XWB entry' and exits 0, so the failure is silently lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the asserts with a small `require(condition, message)` helper that raises an exception (or calls sys.exit with the message). Then the checks run whatever the interpreter flags.
findings.verify_reason: verify_content.py:21-61 uses bare asserts and prints success, as quoted. README:143 runs it as plain `python samples\audio\source\verify_content.py`, and no -O or PYTHONOPTIMIZE use exists. The hazard is real but theoretical.

findings.title: XWB layout knowledge is hand-copied between the verifier and the ADPCM fixture packer
findings.evidence: verify_content.py:21 `assert header[:3] == (0x444E4257, 46, 44)` and :27 `"<II64sIIIIQ"`, :32 `(3, 24, 64, 4)`; make_adpcm_bank.py:71 `struct.pack_into("<3I", out, 0, 0x444E4257, 46, 44)`, :65 `header_size, bank_size, entry_size = 52, 96, 24`, :78 `struct.pack_into("<II64sIIIIQ", ...`
findings.why: The signature, the two versions, the bank-data struct format, the entry and name sizes and the segment order are each written out separately in both scripts, as unnamed literals. One describes what xwbtool writes and the other imitates it. Nothing ties them together, so a correction to one (for example, the seek-table segment) cannot reach the other, and a reader has to re-derive the layout twice.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the constants once, for example in a small xwb_layout.py next to one script that the other imports by path, or at least as named module constants in both with a comment cross-referencing the twin. Have make_adpcm_bank optionally run the verifier's structural checks on its output.
findings.verify_reason: The quoted literals are present in both scripts. But these are two small standard-library authoring scripts in different trees (samples/audio/source and tests/audio/content) that check different banks (named PCM vs one-entry ADPCM fixture), and each runs only when someone regenerates content. The XWB format is fixed by xwbtool, so the two copies have nothing to drift apart over, and medium overstates it. The 'name the constants' half is already tracked in round 1 (testsio: make_adpcm_bank.py:71 unnamed format constants).

findings.title: Wave count hard-coded as 3 beside a check that derives it from tones.json
findings.evidence:
assert (count, entry_size, name_size, alignment) == (3, 24, 64, 4)
    definition = json.loads((bank_path.with_suffix(".json")).read_text())
    assert len(definition["waves"]) == count
findings.why: The JSON definition is already the source of truth for the wave list (line 34 compares it with count, and line 40 iterates it). The literal 3 duplicates it, so adding a wave to tones.json and the bank breaks the verifier for no reason.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop `count` from the tuple check at line 32 and keep the JSON-derived comparison at line 34.
findings.verify_reason: Line 32 hard-codes count == 3, and line 34 already compares count with len(definition['waves']). Adding a wave would fail the tuple assert for no reason.

findings.title: Verifier says it accepts only `-f -nc` output but never checks the seek-table segment or the trailing segment layout
findings.evidence:
entries_offset, entries_length = segments[1]
    names_offset, names_length = segments[3]
    pcm_offset, pcm_length = segments[4]
findings.why: The docstring says the check 'deliberately accepts only the -f -nc output used by this sample'. However, segments[2] (seek tables) is never checked to be empty, and the segment offsets are never checked to be ordered or non-overlapping. A bank with xWMA-style seek data or overlapping segments passes the structural checks, so the claimed narrowness is weaker than stated.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert `segments[2][1] == 0` and that the segment offsets increase and do not overlap, or soften the docstring.
findings.verify_reason: segments[2] is never checked, and nothing checks segment ordering or overlap. But the example given is wrong: an xWMA bank cannot pass, because line 48 requires every entry's mini_format to be exact PCM mono 22050 Hz, and lines 26/30/32 pin bank size, flags, entry and name sizes, and alignment. The only real gap is a PCM bank with a non-empty seek segment or overlapping segments, which is a small gap.

findings.title: Peak bound allows 0.37 full scale, but the README promises below 0.3
findings.evidence: assert 1000 < max(abs(value) for value in values) < 12000

findings.title: The collision sample reads only pad slot 0, contrary to the template's one-player pad policy
findings.evidence: `pads.pressed(0, GamepadButton::b)` (44), `pads.pressed(0, GamepadButton::y)` (49), `apply_deadzone(pads.state(0).left_stick, 0.2f)` (54). Compare minimal/rules/motion.h:71-73 `A one-player game's pad policy: every slot counts, because the system need not put the only pad in slot 0 - after another pad is unplugged it can sit in slot 1 or 3 with slot 0 empty.`
findings.why: The template explains why a single-player game must accept every slot. This sibling one-player sample ignores that, so a lone pad that lands in slot 1 cannot move or quit. The README documents 'player one's left stick', but the behaviour contradicts the reason the template gives.

findings.title: Unnamed stick deadzone 0.2f repeated across samples
findings.evidence: collision_state.cpp:54 `apply_deadzone(pads.state(0).left_stick, 0.2f)`; local_multiplayer/controls.cpp:20 `apply_deadzone(sticks[player], 0.2f)` and :52 `apply_deadzone(sticks[static_cast<std::size_t>(slot)], 0.2f)`
