findings.title: Smoke route tick counts and the expected end position are bare numbers repeated across three files
findings.evidence: collision_state.cpp:57-60 `if (this->ticks_ < 120) { direction = Vector2F(1.0f, 0.0f); } else if (this->ticks_ < 180) ... else if (this->ticks_ < 280) ... else { direction = Vector2F(0.0f, -1.0f); }`; :78 `std::abs(player.x - 968.0f) > 0.01f || std::abs(player.y - 420.0f) > 0.01f`; main.cpp:74 `for (int tick = 0; tick < 315; ++tick)`, :81 `if (tick == 314 && !capture_path.empty())`, :76 `state.update(1.0f / 60.0f);`; arena_tests.cpp:112-117 repeats the same 120/60/100/35 route.
findings.why: The verified end point (968, 420) only holds if main.cpp runs exactly 315 ticks and the segment boundaries stay 120/180/280. These three facts sit in separate files, and only README prose ('315 fixed steps') links them. Changing any one makes the smoke test throw with no hint of which number moved.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare the route once as named constants or a small table (segment directions and lengths, total ticks, expected end), for example in collision_state.h. Use it in update(), verify_smoke_test() and main.cpp's loop and capture tick. Use a named step_time instead of 1.0f / 60.0f.
findings.verify_reason: collision_state.cpp:57-60 has 120/180/280, :78 has 968/420, and main.cpp has 315/314 with 1.0f/60.0f, as quoted. The coupling is real. The route is a fixed smoke script, and a drift fails loudly in a smoke test, so this is low, not medium.

findings.title: Four hand-rolled, differently-behaved `--smoke-test [--capture]` parsers and a copied capture loop across samples
findings.evidence: samples/collision/main.cpp:23 `trim_arguments` plus `arguments.starts_with(L"--smoke-test --capture ")` with manual quote stripping; samples/local_multiplayer/main.cpp:22 `command_arguments()` via `CommandLineToArgvW` and `arguments[0] == L"--smoke-test" && arguments.size() == 3 && arguments[1] == L"--capture"`; samples/audio/main.cpp:24 a second `CommandLineToArgvW` parse with `std::wcscmp(arguments[1], L"--smoke-test")`; samples/minimal/main.cpp:28 `asks_for_smoke_test` trimming only `L" \t"` (collision trims `L" \t\r\n"`). The read-back/write_png block `std::vector<unsigned char> pixels; app.renderer()->read_back_buffer(pixels); const Vector2F size = app.renderer()->back_buffer_size(); capture::write_png(capture_path, ...)` is duplicated at collision/main.cpp:82-88 and local_multiplayer/main.cpp:87-93.
findings.why: The same command-line contract (used by ctest entries and READMEs) behaves differently per sample. For example, a quoted path with a space works through argv in local_multiplayer, but collision only strips quotes that wrap the whole remaining string. A reader learning from the samples sees four idioms for one job.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one parser (the CommandLineToArgvW form is the correct one) and one capture helper. Put them in a small shared sample helper, as samples already share minimal's manifest and fonts, or at least make the four copies identical.
findings.verify_reason: collision/main.cpp:23 trim_arguments with a ' \t\r\n' trim and the '--smoke-test --capture ' prefix with quote stripping; local_multiplayer/main.cpp:22 command_arguments via CommandLineToArgvW; audio/main.cpp a second CommandLineToArgvW parse with wcscmp; minimal/main.cpp:28 asks_for_smoke_test trimming ' \t'. The capture read-back block is duplicated at collision/main.cpp:82-88 and in local_multiplayer. All as described, and low is right.

findings.title: Collision and local_multiplayer hand-drive frames with a smoke flag in the state, contradicting minimal's stated pattern
findings.evidence: collision: `for (int tick = 0; tick < 315; ++tick) { state.update(1.0f / 60.0f); app.renderer()->begin_frame(); state.draw(*app.renderer()); app.renderer()->submit(); ... if (tick == 314 && !capture_path.empty())`. local_multiplayer/main.cpp:79 repeats the loop with `tick < 120` and `tick == 14`. Both states take a flag (`CollisionState(Application* app, bool smoke_test)`, `explicit PlayState(labrador::Application* app, bool smoke_test = false)`). minimal/main.cpp:48 says: "It wraps the state rather than adding a flag to it, so HelloState has no test code in it and a copy wraps its own first state the same way." Also collision main.cpp:95 `return app.run(std::make_unique<CollisionState>(&app, smoke_test));` is reached only when smoke_test is false.
findings.why: The same begin/draw/submit/read-back/end loop is copied twice. Its tick counts and capture frames are bare literals, and its dt of 1.0f/60.0f is not tied to target_fps. The loop skips Application::run, so the smoke test checks less of the shell than minimal's does. Passing `smoke_test` where the value is always false suggests a path that does not exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Either follow minimal's wrapper-state approach, or move the frame loop into one helper with named tick and capture constants. Pass `false` explicitly at collision main.cpp:95, or drop the parameter once the flag leaves the state.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: collision main.cpp:74-93 and local_multiplayer main.cpp:77-97 contain the same hand-driven loop with bare tick literals, and collision line 95 passes smoke_test, which is always false there. However, the loop has a reason: --capture has to read the back buffer between submit() and end_frame(), and Application::run cannot do that. Minimal's comment at :48 describes its own wrapper, not a rule for every sample. Samples are self-contained by design, so two copies of a 15-line loop is minor.

findings.title: The interactive path passes smoke_test, which is always false there
findings.evidence: `return app.run(std::make_unique<CollisionState>(&app, smoke_test));` comes after `if (smoke_test) { ... return 0; }` at lines 70-94
findings.why: The variable can only be false on this line. Passing it suggests that the interactive run can follow the scripted route, which it never does.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass `false` explicitly, or give CollisionState a default/named factory for interactive play.
findings.verify_reason: collision/main.cpp:95 passes smoke_test after the if(smoke_test){...return 0;} block at lines 70-94, so the value is always false there.

findings.title: Startup and usage failures are invisible when any argument is given to the WIN32 samples
findings.evidence:
collision/main.cpp:99-103 `std::fprintf(stderr, "CollisionSample: %s\n", error.what()); if (arguments.empty()) { MessageBoxA(...); }`
audio/main.cpp:19 `const bool interactive = command_line[0] == L'\0';` with :62 `if (interactive) { MessageBoxA(...) }`
local_multiplayer/main.cpp:46 `const bool interactive = *command_line == L'\0';` with :105 `if (interactive)`
findings.why: All three are `WIN32` subsystem executables (see each CMakeLists `add_executable(... WIN32 ...)`). Run from a console without redirection, they have no stderr. A mistyped flag (`CollisionSample.exe --smoketest`) or a failure during a `--smoke-test` run that nobody redirected exits 1 with no output at all. The usage message thrown at collision/main.cpp:59, audio/main.cpp:35 and local_multiplayer/main.cpp:62 is effectively never seen. The minimal template uses a different rule (`if (!smoke_test)`), so the four samples disagree on when a failure is shown.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate the message box on 'not a smoke test' as minimal does, so a usage error is always shown. Alternatively, attach to the parent console (AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS)) before writing stderr. Use the same rule in all four samples.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: collision/main.cpp:100 uses arguments.empty(), and audio/main.cpp:19 and local_multiplayer/main.cpp:46 use an interactive flag based on an empty command line. Minimal gates on !smoke_test (minimal/main.cpp:151). All are WIN32 executables, so a mistyped flag fails silently. But smoke tests run under ctest/CI, which captures stderr, so the effect is limited to a mistyped flag in a hand-run sample. Low, not medium.

findings.title: Four test files open with the subject header instead of <doctest/doctest.h>
findings.evidence: animation_preview_tests.cpp:1 `#include "samples/components/animation_preview.h"` (doctest at line 4). The same applies to animation_preview_content_tests.cpp:1, animation_preview_null_tests.cpp:1 and gallery_animation_tests.cpp:1 (`#include "samples/components/gallery_state.h"`). The siblings nine_slice_tests.cpp, option_row_tests.cpp, pointer_capture_tests.cpp and slider_tests.cpp all start with `#include <doctest/doctest.h>`.
findings.why: CONVENTIONS (Files) says: "A test has no header of its own, so it opens with <doctest/doctest.h> and then follows the same order." Half of this folder's tests follow that rule and half do not, and a reader copying a test into a game gets whichever style they happened to pick.
findings.suggested_fix: Move `#include <doctest/doctest.h>` to the first line of the four files, followed by the sample headers, then engine, external and standard headers, as the other four tests do.
findings.verify_reason: CONVENTIONS.md line 139-140: 'A test has no header of its own, so it opens with <doctest/doctest.h>'. animation_preview_tests.cpp, animation_preview_content_tests.cpp, animation_preview_null_tests.cpp and gallery_animation_tests.cpp open with the subject header and include doctest at lines 4/13/10. nine_slice_tests.cpp and slider_tests.cpp open with doctest.

findings.title: Most of the gallery's layout is bare literals sitting next to the named layout constants

resources->resolve_texture("panel"), RectangleI(0, 0, 16, 16),

findings.title: The reason given for building the status text before the rows is wrong
findings.evidence: // Built before the rows, because every row's callback writes to it.
findings.why: The row callbacks only run from adjust()/drag_to() during update(), never while the rows are being built. Slider's constructor fires nothing, and the window_mode_->set_index at line 158 is silent by contract. The callbacks read this->status_ when they run, so the order in which init() builds things does not matter to them. A maintainer could be misled into preserving or debugging an ordering that has no effect.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the comment, or replace it with the real constraint if there is one (for example, draw order in the scene).
findings.verify_reason: Row callbacks fire only from adjust()/drag_to() (option_row.cpp:93-95, slider.cpp adjust). No constructor fires them, and set_index at :158 is silent. Each lambda reads this->status_ when it is called, after init() returns, so the stated reason for building the status before the rows does not hold.

findings.title: "Index 1 means full screen" is written three times, tied to the order of the window_modes list
findings.evidence:
this->app_->set_fullscreen(index == 1);   // :154
this->app_->fullscreen() ? 1 : 0);          // :159
this->app_->fullscreen() ? 1 : 0);          // :268
findings.why: The mapping between window_modes and fullscreen is repeated as bare literals in the callback, in init and in every update. Reordering or extending window_modes silently breaks all three places. The website's settings-and-saves.mdx excerpts end on this exact text, so it is also quoted.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the index once, for example `constexpr size_t fullscreen_choice = 1;`, next to window_modes. Use it in all three places and update the website excerpt bounds in the same commit.
findings.verify_reason: index == 1 at :154, and fullscreen() ? 1 : 0 at :159 and in update (~:268), are bare literals tied to the order of the local window_modes list. The website's settings-and-saves.mdx quotes the ':159/:268' text as excerpt bounds, as the finding says.

findings.title: Pointer-row bookkeeping uses a hard-coded count, and treats the last row as Quit by position
findings.why: The loop bound repeats the array length by hand, and update_pointer decides which row is Quit by its position in the list. This gallery is meant to be copied and extended, and adding a row after Quit, or a row without updating the 5, quietly breaks hit-testing or the Quit action.
findings.suggested_fix: Loop with `std::size(rows)` (or a range-for that tracks the row number). Keep a `UiWidget* quit_` member and compare `pressed == this->quit_` instead of using pointer_widgets_.back().
findings.verify_reason: gallery_state.cpp:194-200 loops `for (int row = 0; row < 5; ++row)` over the rows[] array with a hand-written count. Line 407 uses `pressed == this->pointer_widgets_.back()` to identify Quit, and gallery_state.h has no quit_ member. Both are fragile in code that is meant to be copied and extended. The fix is cheap, and the issue is not tracked.

findings.title: The window row's text is rewritten and re-measured every tick, even when nothing changed
findings.evidence:
"this->window_mode_->set_index(
			this->app_->fullscreen() ? 1 : 0);" inside GalleryState::update; OptionRow::set_index does "this->value_.set_text(this->choices_[index]);" and TextObject::set_text (engine/render/text_object.cpp:74-77) copies the string and calls remeasure() unconditionally.
findings.why: Every tick copies a wstring and re-walks the glyphs to re-measure text that has not changed. The README (lines 156-158) presents this as the pattern to copy, so a game with many rows that follow outside state would repeat that work on every row, every tick.
findings.suggested_fix: Only call set_index when the value differs: `const size_t wanted = fullscreen ? 1 : 0; if (window_mode_->index() != wanted) window_mode_->set_index(wanted);`. Alternatively, make OptionRow::set_index return early when index == index_.
findings.verify_reason: gallery_state.cpp:267-268 calls window_mode_->set_index every tick. OptionRow::set_index (option_row.cpp:116-126) calls value_.set_text unconditionally, and TextObject::set_text (text_object.cpp:74-77) copies the string and calls remeasure() every time. The README's 'every update use fullscreen() and set_index()' paragraph presents this as the pattern. The cost is trivial for one row, so low is the right severity.

findings.title: The 1280x720 layout rectangle and viewport/camera derivation is written twice and must stay in sync
findings.evidence: world_point (lines 417-421): `const Viewport viewport(RectangleF(Vector2F::zero, resolution)); return Camera::frame(RectangleF(0.0f, 0.0f, 1280.0f, 720.0f), viewport).world_position(client, viewport);` and refresh_view (lines 447-453): `const Viewport viewport(RectangleF(Vector2F::zero, resolution)); ... Camera::frame(RectangleF(0.0f, 0.0f, 1280.0f, 720.0f), viewport));`
findings.why: Pointer hit-testing works only if world_point uses exactly the camera refresh_view gave the scene; the comment at line 415 says so. Two literal copies of the layout size and the viewport construction can drift silently, and the 1280/720 literals are the gallery's one layout constant beside the named label_x/row_spacing set. pointer_input.mjs also mirrors these numbers.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `const RectangleF layout_bounds(0.0f, 0.0f, 1280.0f, 720.0f);` to the anonymous namespace next to the other layout constants, and a small helper that returns the (viewport, camera) pair. Have both refresh_view and world_point use it.
findings.verify_reason: gallery_state.cpp 413-421 (world_point) and 446-453 (refresh_view) both build Viewport(RectangleF(zero, resolution)) and Camera::frame(RectangleF(0,0,1280,720), viewport) as quoted. The duplication is real, but both copies are in one file about 30 lines apart, and world_point's comment names refresh_view. Drift is unlikely and would be caught by the pointer page test. Low, not medium.

findings.title: The gallery's set_filter(point) does nothing, and the test that claims to cover it cannot fail
findings.evidence:
list.set_filter(TextureFilter::point);  // gallery_state.cpp:437
CHECK(first[index].filter == TextureFilter::point);  // gallery_animation_tests.cpp:66
"overlay, point filter and R press/hold behavior"  // README.md:128
findings.why: engine/render/sprite_geometry.h:325 resets every view's filter to TextureFilter::point at the start of each frame, and nothing in engine/scene or engine/ui sets linear. Deleting the gallery's call would change nothing, and the test's filter assertion would still pass. The README's claim that the hidden-window case checks the point filter is therefore not evidence of anything.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove the no-op call along with the assertion and the README phrase, or make the test meaningful: draw the scene with linear filtering first (for example, have the panel or a test overlay set linear) so that the overlay's set_filter has something to override, then assert point.
findings.verify_reason: This is real. DrawList reset() sets the filter to point (sprite_geometry.h ~325), and nothing in engine scene/ui sets TextureFilter::linear (a grep finds it only in backend translation). So set_filter(point) at gallery_state.cpp:437 does nothing today, and the test's filter CHECK cannot tell whether the call is there. It is still a harmless explicit statement in copyable sample code, and the assertion does pin the observable result, so medium is inflated.

findings.title: "Told every line the status shows" is false for the starting line
findings.evidence:
// Told every line the status shows, for a page that reports it;
// main_web.cpp writes each to the console.
findings.why: The first status line is built directly into the UiText at gallery_state.cpp:129-131 (L"Window mode applies; difficulty and volume sliders are examples.") and never goes through set_status(). on_status_ therefore never hears it, and the browser console never shows it.
findings.suggested_fix: Construct the UiText with an empty string and call set_status() with the starting text once on_status_ is set. Alternatively, change the comment to "every line set after init".
findings.verify_reason: The starting status text is passed straight to the UiText constructor (gallery_state.cpp:129-131) and never goes through set_status (:424-430). on_status_ never hears it, so the header comment 'Told every line the status shows' is false for the first line.

findings.title: NineSlice::draw and Bar::draw (the hidden check and skipping empty pieces) have no test
findings.why: nine_slice_tests.cpp checks only the geometry and the pieces() accessor. Bar::draw (slider.cpp:60-71) is not covered either. Neither component's draw is recorded under the null backend, although animation_preview_null_tests.cpp already shows how. The hidden() early return, skipping zero-area pieces, and the texture, source and colour actually submitted are all unchecked.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a native-null recording case: draw a NineSlice with a zero border and a squeezed destination, and assert the recorded sprite count and their source and destination. Draw it again after set_hidden(true) and assert nothing was recorded. Do the same for a Slider's track and fill.
findings.verify_reason: nine_slice_tests.cpp covers geometry and pieces only, with no draw case. slider_tests does not record Bar::draw. The gallery null case keeps only atlas sprites (gallery_animation_tests.cpp draw_previews), so the hidden() early return and the zero-area skip in NineSlice::draw (:131-153) and Bar::draw (slider.cpp:60-71) are unrecorded.

findings.title: adjust() and drag_to() repeat the same set-value / show / notify step
findings.why: The header promises that drag_to calls the callback "as adjust() does". Two copies of that step can drift apart in a game's edited copy, for example if one copy gets a sound or a clamp and the other does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a private `bool change_to(int next)` that compares, assigns, calls show_value(), notifies and returns, and call it from both adjust() and drag_to().
findings.verify_reason: slider.cpp:147-155 (adjust) and 189-197 (drag_to) contain the same assign / show_value / on_change_ / return true block. slider.h:102 says drag_to changes the value 'as adjust() does'. It is a small real duplication in copyable sample code. Neither code-hygiene.md nor TODO tracks it.

findings.title: A track with zero or negative width is accepted silently and turns dragging into a no-op
findings.why: The constructor checks minimum, maximum, step and value (checked_minimum) but never the track. A degenerate track makes value_at always return the current value, so drags quietly do nothing, and fill_rectangle produces a zero or negative fill width. The value_at contract in slider.h:95-99 does not mention this case. T6 would have the constructor throw, naming the slider, as it does for the other arguments.
findings.suggested_fix: Check `track.width > 0` (and height >= 0) in the constructor's validation and throw std::invalid_argument naming the slider. Then the guard in value_at can become an assertion of the invariant.
findings.verify_reason: checked_minimum (slider.cpp:28-39) validates only minimum, maximum, step and value. The track is not checked, and value_at silently returns the current value when track.width <= 0 (:161-164). The constructor contract in slider.h does not mention the track. It is sample code, so the impact is low.

findings.title: Bar's comment says it is "twenty lines", and the comment is broken mid-sentence
findings.why: Bar's declaration is about 22 lines and its definitions in slider.cpp are about 45 more, so the count is false and will drift further. The orphaned `A leaf` line break looks like a leftover from an edit.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the line count (for example, "...when the engine's set does not fit, and this one is small.") and reflow the paragraph.
findings.verify_reason: slider.h 17-21 has the mid-sentence break 'A leaf' and the words 'this one is twenty lines'. Bar's definitions in slider.cpp run from line 43 to about 95, so the count is false for the whole widget.

findings.title: Slider::minimum() and maximum() are never called, not even by tests
findings.evidence:
int minimum() const;
int maximum() const;
findings.why: A whole-repo grep for `.minimum()`/`.maximum()` on a Slider finds no caller in samples, tests or website, and slider_tests.cpp never asserts them. The copyable surface carries untested accessors, while OptionRow's matching choice_count() is tested.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove them (a game that copies the slider can add them), or add a CHECK in slider_tests that they return the constructor's range.
findings.verify_reason: A grep of Labrador and ColourWars for .minimum()/.maximum()/->minimum()/->maximum() in cpp/h/mdx/ts/astro finds no caller, and slider_tests does not assert them.

findings.title: std::move is used without including <utility>
findings.evidence: `&content.resources, std::move(on_change));` while the includes are `<climits>`, `<stdexcept>`, `<vector>`
findings.why: It compiles only through a transitive include. The sibling sources that call std::move (option_row.cpp, slider.cpp, gallery_state.cpp, animation_preview_null_tests.cpp) all include <utility> explicitly.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `#include <utility>` to the standard-library block.
findings.verify_reason: slider_tests.cpp includes only <climits>, <stdexcept> and <vector> from the standard library, and uses std::move at line 37 without <utility>.

findings.title: The asset record says the diamond is centred, but the generator centres it at texel 7 of a 16-texel frame
findings.evidence: README: `four 16x16 frames are a centred cyan diamond`. Generator lines 22-23: `for x in range(16):` and `distance = abs(x - 7) + abs(y - 7)`.
findings.why: The centre of a 16-texel frame is 7.5. Centring at 7 makes the radius-6 frame span texels 1..13, which leaves one texel of margin on the left/top and two on the right/bottom. Either the prose is false, or the asymmetry is unintended and only shows in the reviewed previews.
findings.suggested_fix: Either say the diamond is centred on texel (7, 7), or change the rule to be symmetric. Changing the rule changes the checked-in DDS, so regenerate and review it.
findings.verify_reason: README line 4: 'four 16x16 frames are a centred cyan diamond'. The generator uses `abs(x - 7) + abs(y - 7)` over range(16), so the centre is texel 7 and the true centre of the frame is 7.5. The prose is slightly inaccurate.

findings.title: "Unicode-source policy remains untouched" narrates a change rather than stating a fact
findings.evidence:
`All source
and JSON text is ASCII; Unicode-source policy remains untouched.`
findings.why: "Remains untouched" describes what this change did not do, which is review-time history (CONVENTIONS, Comments: the test is the tense). It tells someone reading the content's record nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the clause and keep "All source and JSON text is ASCII."
findings.verify_reason: source/README.md ends that paragraph with 'All source and JSON text is ASCII; Unicode-source policy remains untouched.' The clause describes what a change did not do, which is change narration.

findings.title: The generator repeats the frame size 16 and centre 7 as bare literals beside named WIDTH/HEIGHT/RADII
findings.evidence: `WIDTH = 64` ... `for x in range(16):` / `distance = abs(x - 7) + abs(y - 7)` / `offset = (y * WIDTH + frame * 16 + x) * 4`, and `"w": 16, "h": 16` / `"frame_count": 4` in sheet_text
findings.why: WIDTH (64) is really len(RADII) * frame size, and the frame size and frame count are repeated in both the pixel and JSON halves. Changing the frame size or count means finding every literal, and the two outputs can disagree.
findings.suggested_fix: Define `FRAME = 16` and derive `WIDTH = FRAME * len(RADII)`, `HEIGHT = FRAME`, and a centre constant. Use them in atlas_bytes and in sheet_text (`len(RADII)` for frame_count).
findings.verify_reason: The generator defines WIDTH=64, HEIGHT=16 and RADII, but repeats `range(16)`, `x - 7`, `frame * 16`, `"w": 16, "h": 16` and `"frame_count": 4` as literals.

findings.title: The strip's frame_count and frame size are literals instead of being derived from RADII
findings.evidence: "frame_count": 4, "frame_time": 0.25, "looping": looping}
findings.why: The atlas has one frame per entry in RADII (atlas_bytes loops over enumerate(RADII)), but sheet_text() hard-codes 4. Adding a radius would make a wider atlas while the JSON still describes four frames. This is separate from the known finding about the 16 and 7 literals at line 22.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `len(RADII)` for frame_count and a named FRAME_SIZE for the w/h fields and WIDTH (WIDTH = FRAME_SIZE * len(RADII)).
findings.verify_reason: sheet_text() hard-codes frame_count 4 while atlas_bytes iterates over RADII. The known item at :22 covers the 16/7 literals in the pixel loop, not the JSON frame_count, so this is a distinct but adjacent nit.

findings.title: The mirrored layout uses an unexplained `- 1` and mixes constant naming styles
findings.why: The `- 1` turns the text middle (row_y + 10) into the track's middle (row_y + track_inset 4 + height 10 / 2 = 9), but nothing says so. The row origin 240 and spacing 50 are inline while the x values are named. `FRAMES` is a function in SCREAMING case beside the lower-case function `row_middle`. A layout change in gallery_state.cpp would break this driver in ways that are hard to trace.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the mirrored values (FIRST_ROW_Y, ROW_SPACING, TEXT_MIDDLE, TRACK_MIDDLE = 4 + 10 / 2) with a comment linking each to gallery_state.cpp, use `track_middle(row)` for the drag, and give the frame-wait builder a lower-case name such as `frames_script`.
findings.verify_reason: pointer_input.mjs 49-56: the constants have a header comment naming gallery_state.cpp and 1280x720 world units, so the mirror is documented. The unexplained `row_middle(2) - 1` at line 100 is real: the track middle is row_y+4+5=9 and the text middle is +10. 240/50 are inline, and FRAMES is a function in caps. The findings are real but minor, and the 'hard to trace' claim is exaggerated given the header comment.

findings.title: The page's help line leaves out pointer input and R, both of which the gallery supports
findings.evidence: "Up and down choose a row, left and right change it. Escape quits.";
findings.why: The gallery now takes clicks, taps and slider drags (README.md:144-152, ComponentsPointerPageTests), and R or gamepad X restarts the previews. The page's own instructions describe the keyboard-only version.
findings.suggested_fix: Mention click/tap/drag and R, or point to the in-canvas help line that gallery_state.cpp already draws.
findings.verify_reason: shell.html:44 sets 'Up and down choose a row, left and right change it. Escape quits.' The in-canvas help (gallery_state.cpp:116-121) and the README control table include click/tap/drag and R.

findings.title: Font asset name repeated as a literal three times in one function
findings.evidence: join_state.cpp:31 `this->font_ = resources->resolve_sprite_font("jetbrains_mono_bold_16");` :34 `"ready", L"READY", "jetbrains_mono_bold_16", ...` :36 `"leave", L"LEAVE", "jetbrains_mono_bold_16", ...`; play_state.cpp:29 repeats it again.
findings.why: The template teaches spelling an asset name once and resolving it once. This sample repeats the string four times across two files, so a font change means a search-and-replace.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one `const std::string font_name` in an anonymous namespace (or a shared sample header) used by both states.
findings.verify_reason: join_state.cpp:31,34,36 and play_state.cpp:29 each spell "jetbrains_mono_bold_16" as a literal.

findings.title: Keyboard bindings for the two keyboard players are written out four times
findings.evidence: controls.cpp:12-15 `{ Key::a, Key::d, Key::w, Key::s }, { Key::left, Key::right, Key::up, Key::down }`; join_state.cpp:55-65 `if (keys.held(Key::w)) return Direction::up; ... if (keys.held(Key::up)) return Direction::up; ...`; join_state.cpp:76-85 `pressed(Key::f)` / `pressed(Key::enter)` / `pressed(Key::g)` / `pressed(Key::backspace)`; join_state.cpp:103,105 `input[0].join_pressed = keyboard.pressed(Key::f); ... input[1].join_pressed = keyboard.pressed(Key::enter);`
findings.why: Movement keys appear in both controls.cpp's table and join_state's held_direction. The join and confirm keys (F and Enter) appear in both confirm_pressed and the join-input fill. Changing one binding means editing several functions in two files, plus the hint strings at join_state.cpp:193-197. This sample exists to show per-game binding policy (T1), so it should keep each binding in one place.
findings.suggested_fix: Make one per-InputSource binding table (move/confirm/leave/join keys) in controls.h. Derive held_direction, confirm_pressed, leave_pressed, the join inputs and read_directions from it.
findings.verify_reason: Real duplication: the movement keys are in controls.cpp:12-15 and again in join_state.cpp:55-65. F/Enter appear in confirm_pressed (76-77) and again in the join fill (103,105). G/Backspace appear once, and the hint strings are display text. 'Four times' is an exaggeration; each binding appears at most twice in code. Small sample duplication, so low.

findings.title: JoinInput array indexed with literal 0, 1 and +2 instead of the InputSource enumerators
findings.evidence: join_state.cpp:102 `input[0].connected = true;` :104 `input[1].connected = true;` :108 `JoinInput& source = input[static_cast<std::size_t>(slot) + 2];`
findings.why: join_rules.h defines the order (keyboard_left = 0, keyboard_right, pad_0..pad_3) as the simultaneous-join priority. Here the order is re-encoded as bare offsets, so reordering the enum silently mis-binds sources. The static_assert only checks the count.
findings.suggested_fix: Index with `static_cast<std::size_t>(InputSource::keyboard_left)`, `...keyboard_right` and `...pad_0) + slot`. A small `source_index(InputSource)` helper would also do.
findings.verify_reason: join_state.cpp:102-108 indexes input[0], input[1] and slot+2. join_rules.h:12-21 defines the order keyboard_left=0, keyboard_right, pad_0..pad_3. The static_assert checks only the count.

findings.title: Sample failure reporting differs in stderr prefix, message-box title and condition, capitalisation, full stops, and doubles a prefix
findings.evidence:
stderr prefixes: minimal/main.cpp:150 and linesweeper `"startup failure: %s
"`, but minimal/main_web.cpp `"MinimalSample: %s
"`; other samples use their program name. Box titles: "Sample - startup failure", "CollisionSample failure", "AudioSample failure", "Local multiplayer - failure", "ComponentsGallery failure", "LineSweeper - startup failure". When the box shows: `!smoke_test` (minimal), `arguments.empty()` (collision), `interactive` (audio, local_multiplayer), always (components, LineSweeper). Text: "usage: CollisionSample ..." vs "Usage: AudioSample.exe ..."; "AudioSample could not read its command line." (full stop) vs "Could not read command-line arguments" (none). The throw here, `"LocalMultiplayerSample: scripted players or views diverged"`, is printed by main.cpp:104 `"LocalMultiplayerSample: %s
"` as "LocalMultiplayerSample: LocalMultiplayerSample: ...".
findings.why: These six files present themselves as parallel examples of one pattern, and a reader copying one picks up arbitrary differences. The doubled prefix shows the thrower and the catcher each assume the other adds the context.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one form in all six: '<Target>: <message>' on stderr, '<Target> failure' as the box title, and the box shown exactly when the command line is empty. Use the same 'usage:' capitalisation everywhere, and no full stop in exception text, as the engine's messages do. Remove the self-prefix from the thrown smoke-failure messages.
findings.verify_reason: play_state.cpp:130 throws "LocalMultiplayerSample: scripted players or views diverged", and main.cpp:104 prints it with a "LocalMultiplayerSample: %s\n" prefix, so the prefix is doubled. The box titles, conditions and 'usage:'/'Usage:' differences quoted are accurate.

findings.title: Comment points to rules/motion.h for 'what moved there', which that header does not describe
findings.evidence: CMakeLists.txt:22-23 `MinimalTests below runs them with none of those (rules/motion.h says what moved there to make that true).`; rules/motion.h's header comment says `HelloState reads the devices and draws the result; everything between the two is here.` and nothing about a move.
findings.why: The pointer is archaeology (the move is in README's change list for cc56ddd). It sends a reader to a file that does not answer it.
findings.suggested_fix: Say what the library holds now, for example '(rules/motion.h says what the rules take and why they take plain values)'.
findings.verify_reason: minimal/CMakeLists.txt:22-23 says 'rules/motion.h says what moved there'. motion.h's header describes why the library takes plain values and links no engine, but says nothing about a move. The pointer is archaeology wording.

findings.title: Template content-copy comment talks about an optional sound bank the template does not have
findings.evidence: CMakeLists.txt:99-100 `so a required file goes on loading here and is missing only from a clean build, and an optional bank is never replaced by the silent one.`
findings.why: The minimal manifest holds only a font. The comment is copied into every new project, and its bank clause describes the audio sample's situation, which confuses a reader trying to understand the template's own copy step.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the bank clause, or make it explicitly conditional ('a game that adds an optional sound bank ...').
findings.verify_reason: minimal/CMakeLists.txt:99-100 has the optional-bank clause. minimal/content/manifest.json lists only the font.

findings.title: Every sample's browser main re-declares the engine's private Module.onError bridge
findings.evidence: engine/app/web/window.cpp:139 `EM_JS(void, labrador_tell_page_error, (const char* message), { if (typeof Module.onError === "function") { Module.onError(UTF8ToString(message)); } });` is repeated with only the name changed in samples/minimal/main_web.cpp:25 (`minimal_tell_page_error`), samples/audio/main_web.cpp:31, samples/collision/main_web.cpp:30, samples/components/main_web.cpp:28, samples/linesweeper/main_web.cpp:55 and samples/local_multiplayer/main_web.cpp:28. Each also carries its own `EM_JS_DEPS(..., "$UTF8ToString")` and the same `catch` block that prints and calls it. The minimal copy is shipped to every consumer in the starter ZIP.
findings.why: window.h documents onError as the engine's page contract (window.h:254-274), but only failures from inside the loop use the engine's bridge. Startup failures depend on each game re-implementing the same JS call correctly, so a page-contract change (argument shape, a new callback) must be made in seven places, six of them copied into users' projects.
findings.suggested_fix: Expose one engine function for the browser build (for example in engine/app, `report_fatal_error(const char*)` or a helper that runs a startup callable and reports what it throws) that reuses labrador_tell_page_error. Reduce each main_web.cpp to calling it, and update the minimal README's change list.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: engine/app/web/window.cpp:139 labrador_tell_page_error, and identical EM_JS bridges at minimal/main_web.cpp:25, audio:31, collision:30, components:28, linesweeper:55 and local_multiplayer:28, each called from a catch block. Not tracked. The copies are five-line JS shims in sample entry points. The fix adds a new public engine primitive, which is design work rather than hygiene, and a contract change would not silently break them. Low.

findings.title: The template's font name is spelt in two files despite a comment saying it is spelt once
findings.evidence: hello_state.cpp:19-22 `// Asset names, matching content/manifest.json. They are spelt once and resolved to handles once ... const std::string font_name = "jetbrains_mono_bold_16";` and confirm_state.cpp:14 `const std::string font_name = "jetbrains_mono_bold_16";`
findings.why: The comment's 'spelt once' claim is false for the copy-from template. Renaming the font, which the collision and multiplayer READMEs tell adapters to do, means finding both copies.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare the asset name once (for example an inline constexpr std::string_view in a small samples/minimal/states/assets.h) and use it from both states, or reword the comment.
findings.verify_reason: hello_state.cpp:19-22 says the names are 'spelt once', and confirm_state.cpp:14 declares font_name = "jetbrains_mono_bold_16" again. The comment could be read as applying only within its own file, but the template still spells the name twice.

findings.title: Test writes a two-pad state and overwrites it before anything observes it
findings.evidence: motion_tests.cpp:73 `slots[0] = PadReading{ Vector2F(-1.0f, 0.0f), false };` :74 `slots[2] = PadReading{ Vector2F(0.0f, 1.0f), true };` :75 `slots[0] = PadReading{};`
findings.why: The comment says 'Two pads, then the one in slot 0 unplugged', but combine_pads is pure and is called only after the overwrite. The first write is never asserted and has no effect, so the 'two pads' half of the scenario is not tested.
findings.suggested_fix: Either assert combine_pads on the two-pad array before clearing slot 0 (summed stick (-1, 1), quit requested), or delete the first write and reword the comment as 'slot 0 empty, a pad in slot 2'.
findings.verify_reason: motion_tests.cpp:73-75 writes slots[0] and then overwrites it before combine_pads is called. combine_pads is pure, so the two-pad state is never observed.

findings.title: Sample tests are built four different ways; local_multiplayer recompiles sample sources by relative path
findings.evidence: tests/local_multiplayer uses labrador_add_test_suite with `"${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../../samples/local_multiplayer/arena.cpp"`, controls.cpp, join_rules.cpp, and later join_state.cpp/play_state.cpp. collision builds `add_library(CollisionExample STATIC body.cpp arena.cpp)` and links it into `CollisionSampleTests arena_tests.cpp`. minimal, collision and audio each `find_package(doctest CONFIG REQUIRED)` and define `DOCTEST_CONFIG_IMPLEMENT_WITH_MAIN` inside their single test file. samples/components/test_main.cpp is a byte copy of tests/test_main.cpp. samples/audio/tests.cpp is not named for its subject (CONVENTIONS: "Tests are named for their subject: `vector2_tests.cpp`").
findings.why: Which sample's tests live in tests/ and which in the sample folder, and whether sample code reaches its test through a library or as a list of source paths, follows no rule. local_multiplayer's two lists of the same .cpp files can drift (a file added to the sample but not to the test), and each .cpp is compiled twice.
findings.suggested_fix: Give local_multiplayer a static library like CollisionExample and link it from both the sample and the test. Document where sample tests live (in the sample folder unless they need the shared harness). Rename samples/audio/tests.cpp to sound_board_tests.cpp.
findings.verify_reason: tests/local_multiplayer/CMakeLists.txt compiles samples/local_multiplayer/*.cpp by relative path, while collision has add_library(CollisionExample) and its tests in the sample folder. samples/components/test_main.cpp is byte-identical to tests/test_main.cpp (cmp). samples/audio/tests.cpp breaks CONVENTIONS:143 'Tests are named for their subject'.

themes.name: Engine mechanical cleanup outside render: naming, duplication, includes
themes.desc: Behaviour-neutral tidying in math, core, ui, collision, assets, input, audio and app. The naming problems are camelCase Ericson locals, uppercase operator parameters, AABB_intersects, off-allowlist abbreviations such as horiz/vert, num_ and min_num_threads, lowercase nested types, and asset_details breaking the one-namespace rule. The duplication covers the orthonormal check written four times, the Quad validation, the GamepadButton bit encoding, the second UTF-8 encoder, Registry/NameTable bookkeeping, the modifier-side tracking, on_resuming and content_root. Missing and unused includes, widget.cpp's using-directive and pragma regions, Partitioner's folder, and commented-out Ericson code complete the list.
themes.story: Mechanical commits only. First, private and implementation renames and dedupe that are not consumer-visible. Second, public renames (AABB_intersects, find_hypotenuse, parameter names) with a CHANGES entry and the sample migration. Third, moving Partitioner out of collision as a pure move with its CMake source lists updated. Run include and website checks.

findings.title: Partitioner is filed under collision but only splits the scene's per-view draw fan-out; its published comment uses ColourWars vocabulary
findings.evidence:
engine/collision/partitioner.h has no type comment on "class Partitioner". Its only engine callers are engine/scene/scene.cpp:239 "this->partitioner_->partition(count, this->thread_pool_->max_num_threads());" (views) and engine/app/application.cpp:226. Comment: "a zero in a config file is an integer
// divide-by-zero on the first frame of the first match."
findings.why: ARCHITECTURE describes collision/ as "contacts, the broad phase that prunes the pairs, the narrow phase, manifolds, resolution", and the partitioner is none of these. Its consumers are scene and app (searched for "partitioner.h" in engine, samples, tests and bench: application.h, scene.cpp, fanout tests, local_multiplayer draw tests, fanout bench). The header is published in website/src/lib/published.ts under 'collision', and 'match' is one game's word in an engine contract that is published word for word.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the class a type comment that states its role (splits an index range across worker threads). Replace 'first match' with neutral wording, for example 'the first frame that fans out'. Consider moving it next to ThreadPool or scene in a commit that also updates ARCHITECTURE and published.ts.
findings.verify_reason: partitioner.h has no type comment on `class Partitioner`, and :24-27 says 'the first frame of the first match'. Its engine users are scene.cpp and application.h. ARCHITECTURE:168-171 lists collision/ as contacts, broad phase, narrow phase, manifolds and resolution, and puts 'the per-view draw fan-out' under scene/. published.ts:138 lists it. It is used only by the fan-out benches and tests, and by the ColourWars submodule copy of the bench.

findings.title: on_resuming copies reset_elapsed_time's body
findings.why: The public call and the resume handler mean the same discontinuity. If FrameTimings gains another discontinuity-sensitive field, or the step position needs resetting, only one copy may get the change, and FrameTimings::interval's documented zero-after-resume would no longer hold.
findings.suggested_fix: Have on_resuming call this->reset_elapsed_time().
findings.verify_reason: application.cpp:523-527 on_resuming repeats timer_.ResetElapsedTime(); frame_timer_.discontinuity(); exactly as reset_elapsed_time() at 349-353. Trivial duplication.

findings.title: application.h includes <vector> but uses no std::vector
findings.evidence: #include <vector>
findings.why: I grepped application.h for 'vector': the only matches are this include and engine/math/vector2i.h. No std::vector appears in the public header, which is published word for word to the website and included by every game.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the include. Build the samples and tests afterwards, in case any of them relied on the transitive include.
findings.verify_reason: application.h:28 is '#include <vector>'; grep for 'vector' in application.h finds only that line and engine/math/vector2i.h at 22. No std::vector in the header.

findings.title: Platform guard mismatch and separator logic written twice in content_root.cpp
findings.why: Windows.h is included under _WIN32, but the GetModuleFileNameW branch is chosen by `#else` of __EMSCRIPTEN__. Any other target fails with an undeclared-identifier error, not a clear message, although AGENTS.md treats Vulkan on Linux and Android as a port path. The trailing-separator test is also written twice, and the two copies already differ on an empty string: executable_directory appends a separator to an empty directory and resolved_under does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `#elif defined(_WIN32)` with an `#else #error "executable_directory has no implementation for this platform"`. Factor out a small `with_trailing_separator(std::string)` helper and decide once what an empty directory gets.
findings.verify_reason: content_root.cpp guards Windows.h with _WIN32 but selects GetModuleFileNameW by #else of __EMSCRIPTEN__, and the trailing-separator test appears twice (lines 54-58 and 72-76). But the 'differ on empty string' point is not a defect: an empty directory in resolved_under correctly yields the relative path unchanged, while executable_directory's parent_path is never meaningfully empty. Every other app file is platform-foldered (win32/web only), so a third platform fails far earlier than here. Minor tidy, not a real duplication bug.

findings.title: Modifier-side bitfield duplicated between Win32 and web, with magic bit layout and re-derived scan code
findings.why: The same encoding (shift=bits 0-1, control=2-3, alt=4-5, mask 3u) is written twice with unnamed numbers. Web's copy is a tested class (DomModifiers), but Win32's is inline in Impl with a bool return whose meaning ("forward this event") the name update_modifier does not say. The scan-code extraction (>>16 & 0xff) and the extended bit (1LL << 24) also repeat keyboard_input.cpp:45-46, which SM-50 made the owner of scan-position translation.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract a shared ModifierSides helper (side enum in, forward-or-withhold out) with named bit offsets, used by DomModifiers and the Win32 Impl. Have keyboard_input.h expose the scan/extended decoding or the right-side test so window.cpp stops re-deriving it.
findings.verify_reason: The encoding is the same in both: update_modifier at win32/window.cpp:654-678 and DomModifiers::update at dom_events.cpp:173-193 (first = 2/4, 3u << first). But each copy is about 10 lines, and the side detection differs (scan code and extended bit on Win32, a code ending in 'Right' on the web). SM-50 in code-hygiene.md deliberately keeps modifier ownership in the Win32 window. A shared helper would also need a neutral home outside both backend folders. Real but minor duplication.

findings.title: read_json_file hand-rolls a second whole-file reader with a different missing-file exception type
findings.why: engine/core/byte_reader.h already exports read_file_bytes, which every other content reader uses. JSON alone reads in 64 KB stack chunks and throws runtime_error for a missing file, while textures, fonts and banks throw out_of_range for the same fact. The ResourceLoader's optional-asset logic and callers therefore have to know which reader a file went through.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement read_json_file as parse over read_file_bytes(path), keeping the 'read_json_file' message prefix. Either adopt the out_of_range missing-file convention and update json.h:16, or state why JSON differs.
findings.verify_reason: Real: read_json_file (json.cpp:78-95) hand-rolls a chunked reader instead of read_file_bytes and throws runtime_error for missing files (documented in json.h:16). But the claimed consequence is weak: ResourceLoader reads definitions outside its optional catch and the optional path catches runtime_error anyway; the different type is documented, not silent. Low duplication.

findings.title: `labrador::asset_details` breaks the one-namespace rule, whose only exception is `detail`
findings.evidence: "namespace labrador::asset_details"
findings.why: CONVENTIONS, Namespaces: "No deeper nesting, with one exception: `detail` wraps internals that headers must expose but users must not touch." This is exactly that case, under a second invented name.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename it to `labrador::detail` and update the ten call sites in asset_manifest_loader.cpp and sprite_sheet_loader.cpp.
findings.verify_reason: CONVENTIONS:94-98: 'No deeper nesting, with one exception: `detail`'. json_object_keys.h:13 is `namespace labrador::asset_details`, the only non-`detail` nested namespace in engine/; inflate.h, colour.h and xaudio2/device_recovery.h all use `detail`.

findings.title: Formatting outliers: an unbraced if, double blank lines, and engine/standard includes not separated
findings.why: Every other if in the unit is braced, and every other file puts one blank line between include groups and before the namespace. The whitespace lint does not catch any of these.
findings.suggested_fix: Brace the if, collapse the double blank lines, and separate the include groups with one blank line.
findings.verify_reason: json_object_keys.h:30-31 has an unbraced if. There are double blank lines at contacts.cpp:8-9, resolve.cpp:6-7 and narrow_phase.cpp:15-16 (awk confirmed). resource_loader.h has '#include "engine/render/renderer.h"' directly followed by '#include <functional>', and sprite_sheet_loader.h:3-4 has the same with <memory>.

findings.title: Public header includes four full headers where pointers need only forward declarations
findings.why: Every includer of resource_loader.h gets the registry, font, sprite sheet, sound bank and sound group headers transitively, though the class touches these types only by pointer. ARCHITECTURE explains that this header once carried a backend type to every client; keeping it minimal is how that stays fixed.
findings.suggested_fix: Forward-declare RenderResources, Renderer, AudioResources and AudioDevice in the header, and move the includes into resource_loader.cpp.
findings.verify_reason: resource_loader.h:4-7 includes audio_device.h, audio_resources.h, render_resources.h and renderer.h. The class uses those types only as pointers, in the constructor parameters and private members (lines 74-76, 116-119). Forward declarations would do. A caveat: removing the includes could break consumers such as application.h users that depend on them transitively. The cited lines were wrong.

findings.title: Include groups not separated as CONVENTIONS and every sibling file do
findings.why: CONVENTIONS requires engine, then external, then standard library, and every other file in the unit separates the groups with a blank line. These two run the groups together, and audio_resources.h lists core before audio unlike sound_bank.h.
findings.suggested_fix: Add blank lines between the engine, external and standard groups, and order the engine includes as sound_bank.h does.
findings.verify_reason: audio_resources.h:3-9 runs the engine and standard includes together with no blank line. xinput/gamepad_reader.cpp has <GamePad.h> and <memory> in one block. CONVENTIONS:138 requires group order, which both files follow, but not blank lines, and it sets no order within the engine group. The finding stands only as a local blank-line style inconsistency.

findings.title: Seven SoundBank method definitions run together without blank lines
findings.why: The rest of this file and the whole unit separate function definitions with a blank line. This one block of the effect verbs does not, which makes the run hard to scan. The whitespace lint does not catch it.
findings.suggested_fix: Put a blank line between each pair of definitions from play_effect through is_effect_looping.
findings.verify_reason: cat -A of sound_bank.cpp:160-200 shows '}' followed directly by 'void SoundBank::stop_effect', then pause_effect, resume_effect and set_effect_volume, with no blank line between definitions.

findings.title: Null and Web Audio duplicate the whole name-table and handle bookkeeping
findings.evidence: webaudio Impl::bank/voice (553-574), wave_index (664-673), and the create_voice/play_wave range checks (678-684, 696-702) match null/audio_device.cpp 54-78, 111-125, 130-136 and 149-155 word for word, error strings included. WebVoice (520-526) is NullVoice (39-45) with a different name. The comments then state the agreement by hand: web 564 "The same words the other two backends use for the same mistake", null 65-68.
findings.why: The only thing keeping the behaviour (and the error text T6 relies on) identical across backends is copy-paste plus comments asserting it. The null play_voice divergence above is that drift already happening.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the name-table bank list, the bounds-checked bank()/voice() lookups and the three-state voice record into a shared headless helper in engine/audio/ (as vibration_output.h does for pads). Both backends would use it, leaving only the API calls in each backend.
findings.verify_reason: The duplication is real: Impl::bank and Impl::voice in null (54-78) and webaudio (553-574) are identical, error strings included, and NullVoice and WebVoice have the same shape. It is about a dozen lines of bounds-checked lookup per backend, and AGENTS keeps backend data inside each folder. Worth noting, but low.

findings.title: `num_elements`/`num_partitions` use an abbreviation that is not on the allowlist
findings.evidence: "partition(int num_elements, int num_partitions) const;"
findings.why: CONVENTIONS: "The allowlist of short forms is small and closed: dt, id, src, dst, min, max." 'num' is not on it, and these are published parameter names.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename them `element_count` and `partition_count` in partitioner.h and .cpp, including the error messages.
findings.verify_reason: CONVENTIONS:59-61 lists a closed allowlist (dt, id, src, dst, min, max). partitioner.h:29-32 uses num_elements and num_partitions. The same pattern also appears in thread_pool.h's min_num_threads and max_num_threads, so a rename should cover both.

findings.title: NameTable and Registry duplicate their name-to-index bookkeeping verbatim
findings.evidence: name_table.h:29-49 and registry.h:68-90 both implement: find in std::map<std::string,int>, overwrite slot if present, else emplace index then push_back in try { } catch (...) { this->indices_.erase(inserted); throw; }. resolve() (name_table.h:55-65, registry.h:99-109) and contains() repeat the same map lookup.
findings.why: The headers explain why the storage differs (by value versus a nullable owner), but the strong-exception-guarantee insert and the resolve lookup are the same logic in two places. A fix to one, such as the rollback-on-throw that both now carry, has to be remembered in the other.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract a small `NameIndex` helper in core that owns the std::map<std::string,int>, with a guarded `claim(name, push)` and a `find(name)` returning an optional index. Both tables would keep their own element storage and error wording.
findings.verify_reason: name_table.h add/resolve and registry.h add/resolve do share the same map-claim-with-rollback and lookup (~20 lines). name_table.h:11-20 deliberately presents NameTable as a parallel of Registry with different storage, and docs/code-hygiene.md 'Rules for the work' says not to introduce public API or a helper framework merely to shorten code; error wording also differs. Small, intentional parallel; a NameIndex helper is optional at best.

findings.title: Lowercase type names: Registry::handle and Registry::entry, plus ThreadPool::Impl::task_item
findings.why: CONVENTIONS: 'Types — classes, structs, enums, aliases' are PascalCase. The sibling private struct StateContext::Frame/PendingOp follows the rule. The public `handle` alias is used by engine/audio/sound_bank.h:71, tests and website/src/content/docs/docs/guides/assets.mdx:205, so renaming it is a source break. The private `entry` and `task_item` cost nothing to fix.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename `entry` to `Entry` and `task_item` to `TaskItem`. For `handle`, either document it as a deliberate exception (a PascalCase `Handle` would shadow the class template) or add a PascalCase alias such as `HandleType` and deprecate the old one through CHANGES.md.
findings.verify_reason: registry.h:57 has `using handle = Handle<Resource>;`, registry.h:166 has `struct entry`, and thread_pool.cpp:39 has `struct task_item`. CONVENTIONS:18 makes types, aliases included, PascalCase. sound_bank.h:71 uses Registry<SoundEffect>::handle, so renaming that alias is a source break. The two private structs are free to fix.

findings.title: ThreadPool::min_num_threads/max_num_threads use an off-allowlist abbreviation and disagree with ApplicationOptions::min_threads/max_threads
findings.why: CONVENTIONS keeps the short-form allowlist closed (dt, id, src, dst, min, max), and 'num' is not on it. The same quantity is spelled two ways one call apart: application.cpp:208 passes options_.max_threads into the constructor, and Scene reads it back as max_num_threads().
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the accessors to min_threads()/max_threads() to match ApplicationOptions, recording it in CHANGES.md because thread_pool.h is public. Update scene.cpp, bench and thread_pool_tests.
findings.verify_reason: thread_pool.h:36 and :56-57 use min_num_threads/max_num_threads. CONVENTIONS:59-60 closes the short-form allowlist to dt, id, src, dst, min and max, and :213 lists off-allowlist abbreviations as a defect. ApplicationOptions spells the same values min_threads/max_threads. ARCHITECTURE.md:569 also cites ThreadPool::max_num_threads and would need updating. Renaming is a public source break.

findings.title: DirectionRepeat's default intervals are written twice
findings.why: The members are always set by the constructor, so their initialisers are redundant copies of the defaults. Changing one place and not the other makes the reader wonder which value applies.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the defaults once, for example `static constexpr float default_first_delay = 0.4f`, and use them for the default arguments. Alternatively, drop the member initialisers or set them to 0.
findings.verify_reason: direction.h:105-106 gives default arguments 0.4f and 0.1f, and lines 149-150 repeat them as member initialisers. It is real but trivial.

findings.title: The GamepadButton bit encoding is written out in three places
findings.why: GamepadState::buttons' layout ('one bit each') belongs to gamepad.h, yet each backend re-derives it. A change to the layout would have to be made in three files with no compiler help.
findings.suggested_fix: Expose one inline helper beside GamepadState (e.g. `constexpr uint16_t gamepad_button_bit(GamepadButton)`) or a `set_down(GamepadButton)` member, and use it in is_down and both backends.
findings.verify_reason: The three sites exist (gamepad.cpp:11-12, xinput_gamepad.cpp:10-14, standard_gamepad.cpp:81-82), plus a mouse.cpp analogue. Each is a one-expression 'enum value is the bit index' idiom that gamepad.h documents ('one bit each'). The proposed fix adds public API to dedupe a single shift, which code-hygiene.md's rules discourage. Marginal.

findings.title: Edit artifacts left unreflowed comment paragraphs in public headers
findings.evidence:
gamepads.h:176 "// - a controller that comes back in a different slot is a different slot. Binding a player" is one overlong line among normally wrapped ones. sound_bank.h:115-116 "// Under the null audio backend every bank here is
// audible and none of them makes a noise" breaks mid-sentence.
findings.why: Public header comments are published word for word on the website, so a visibly half-edited paragraph ships as published reference text.
findings.suggested_fix: Reflow both paragraphs.
findings.verify_reason: The gamepads.h overlong line is at line 25 (119 characters), not 174-179. sound_bank.h:115-116 does break mid-sentence ('every bank here is / audible'). Both artifacts exist in published headers.

findings.title: Second UTF-8 encoder duplicates render/text_encoding.cpp's
findings.evidence:
keyboard.cpp:35  void append_utf8(std::string& text, char32_t codepoint) { ... text.push_back(byte(0xF0u | (value >> 18))); ... }
render/text_encoding.cpp:71  void append_utf8(std::string& utf8, char32_t code_point) { ... utf8 += static_cast<char>(0xF0 | (code_point >> 18)); ... }
findings.why: There are two anonymous-namespace copies of the same four-branch encoder. keyboard.h's contract already says it matches render/text_encoding.h's replacement rule, so the two are meant to agree, but nothing makes them. input may not include render, so the shared owner would be core.
findings.suggested_fix: Move one append_utf8, including the surrogate/out-of-range to U+FFFD substitution, into an engine/core helper (e.g. core/utf8.h). Have both keyboard.cpp and render/text_encoding.cpp call it, and keep the existing tests for each caller.
findings.verify_reason: keyboard.cpp:35-74 and render/text_encoding.cpp:71-94 both have an anonymous-namespace four-branch encoder. They are not identical: keyboard's substitutes U+FFFD for surrogates and out-of-range values, while text_encoding's leaves that to its callers. The duplication is real but small, and a core home would need the substitution reconciled.

findings.title: Focus loss clears key words by literal index
findings.evidence:
this->live_.keys[0] = 0;
			this->live_.keys[1] = 0;
findings.why: keyboard.h:121's static_assert invites extending the array ("A key set past 128 needs a third"). This clear would then leave the third word set, which reintroduces the stuck-key bug the comment above it describes.
findings.suggested_fix: Clear the whole array, e.g. `std::fill(std::begin(this->live_.keys), std::end(this->live_.keys), 0)`, or loop over its extent.
findings.verify_reason: keyboard.cpp:377-378 clears keys[0] and keys[1] by literal index. keyboard.h:121-122's static_assert message says 'A key set past 128 needs a third.'

findings.title: Slot table initialised with a hand-written count of four instead of max_count
findings.evidence: GamepadSlots slots = { no_gamepad, no_gamepad, no_gamepad, no_gamepad };  (GamepadSlots is std::array<int, Gamepads::max_count>)
findings.why: If Gamepads::max_count grows, the extra slots are zero-initialised. Zero is a valid browser pad index, not no_gamepad, so the reader would claim pad 0 occupies them. The whole file otherwise follows max_count.
findings.suggested_fix: Initialise from the constant, for example a constructor or helper that calls `slots.fill(no_gamepad)`, or a constexpr factory in standard_gamepad.h that returns a filled GamepadSlots.
findings.verify_reason: web/gamepad_reader.cpp:107 has `GamepadSlots slots = { no_gamepad, no_gamepad, no_gamepad, no_gamepad };`. standard_gamepad.h:33 defines GamepadSlots as std::array<int, Gamepads::max_count>. If max_count grows, the extra slots zero-initialise.

findings.title: camelCase locals in the Ericson ports
findings.why: CONVENTIONS: variables are snake_case. The header's "keeping its names" rationale (ericson_math.h:15) covers public routine names, not book-style locals. Neighbouring code already uses snake_case (ab_length_squared, twice_area).
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to radius_sum and squared_distance, and dist2 to distance_squared.
findings.verify_reason: Line 50 has radiusSum and line 161 has sqDist, and CONVENTIONS:20 says variables are snake_case. However, ericson_math.h:15-16 says the routines are ported 'keeping its names and its comments where they still apply', and the same functions keep book locals such as d1, vc and dist2. Whether that exception covers locals is unclear. The camelCase is still inconsistent, but the case is weak: low.

findings.title: Commented-out code and integer returns from a bool function
findings.why: The header (ericson_math.h:25-29) rejects commented-out book code. `return 1/0` in a bool function is leftover from the book's int-returning C listing.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the commented-out line (the a4 identity comment above it says the same thing) and return true/false.
findings.verify_reason: ericson_math.cpp:459 declares bool test_2D_segment_segment, but the body returns 1 and 0 (lines ~490 and 494). The commented-out line 'float a4 = Signed2DTriArea(...)' is at ~479, which ericson_math.h:25-29's no-commented-out-book-code stance argues against.

findings.title: quad_point_intersect triangulates although the convex-polygon test applies directly
findings.evidence:
// check if the point is contained within any of the quad's triangles
		const std::array<Triangle, 2> triangles = quad.triangles();
findings.why: The neighbouring quad_segment_intersect (385-388) and point_rectangle_rotated_intersect (488) use the one convex-polygon definition of inside, which ericson_math.h:220 says the engine should have. Splitting into two triangles does twice the work for the same answer. Quad also lacks a points() accessor like RectangleRotated::points(), which forces the local copy at 385-386.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `std::span<const Point2F, 4> points() const` (or a const std::array&) to Quad and use point_in_convex_polygon(quad.points(), point). Use the same accessor in quad_segment_intersect.
findings.verify_reason: intersects.cpp:391-404 loops over quad.triangles() and calls triangle_point_intersect, while quad_segment_intersect (385-388) builds a local points[4] for the convex-polygon routine and point_rectangle_rotated_intersect uses point_in_convex_polygon directly. Quad has no points() accessor (quad.h has triangles() and points_ only). Since triangles() returns std::array, the cost is extra work, not an allocation.

findings.title: The 'bounding boxes' pre-check runs a full shape-vs-box intersection, not a box test
findings.evidence:
// check if the rectangles' bounding boxes intersect
		if (!rectangle_rotated_rectangle_intersect(b.bounding_box(), a))
findings.why: rectangle_rotated_rectangle_intersect does an AABB test, eight containment tests and four segment-AABB tests, so the early-out costs nearly as much as the full query and the comment misdescribes it. triangle_rectangle_rotated_intersect (line 322) does the same thing by calling the whole rectangle_triangle_intersect as its pre-filter.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `a.bounding_box().intersects(b.bounding_box())` here, and `triangle.bounding_box().intersects(rect_rotated.bounding_box())` at line 322, so each pre-check is the cheap test its comment describes.
findings.verify_reason: intersects.cpp:494-495 calls rectangle_rotated_rectangle_intersect(b.bounding_box(), a). That function begins with the cheap rect.intersects(bbox) test (line 99), so separated boxes still exit cheaply. The extra cost appears only when the boxes overlap. The filter is valid and tighter, not wrong, so this is a minor efficiency and comment-accuracy issue. Line 322 has the same pattern.

findings.title: The same rotated-rectangle parameter has three spellings across sibling predicates
findings.why: The sibling functions use `rectangle` for RectangleF (line 33) but `rect` here, and `rotated_rect` in one predicate but `rect_rotated` in six others. `rect` is off the allowlist. These are published declarations.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `rectangle` and `rotated_rectangle` (or `rectangle_rotated`) consistently in intersects.{h,cpp}.
findings.verify_reason: intersects.h:51-52 uses rect/rotated_rect while line 33 and nearby use 'rectangle', and the header has 5 uses of rect_rotated (the finding says 6). The inconsistency is real; 'rect' is off the allowlist. Low.

findings.title: Quad(const RectangleRotated&) validates twice and copies through accessors
findings.why: rectangle.quad() already constructs a validated Quad (and throws if it is invalid), so the second is_valid() can never fail and the four copies are boilerplate.
findings.suggested_fix: Delegate: `Quad::Quad(const RectangleRotated& rectangle) : Quad(rectangle.quad()) {}`.
findings.verify_reason: quad.cpp:43-56 copies rectangle.quad() through four accessors and then calls is_valid() again. The Quad returned by quad() was already validated by its constructor, so delegation would be equivalent.

findings.title: Quad promises a clockwise-from-top-left order that nothing enforces, and constructor parameters are numbered 1-4 while accessors are 0-3
findings.why: Quad::is_valid (quad.cpp:81-120) tests only convexity and accepts either winding and any start vertex. ericson_math.h:145 says "nothing in this library constrains the order a caller lists vertices in". The header comment reads like a contract but is not one. The declaration names point1..point4, while the definition (quad.cpp:14-17) uses point0..point3 and the accessors are point_0..point_3.
findings.suggested_fix: State the real contract: any convex order of either winding; the RectangleF form produces top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left. Name the parameters point_0..point_3 in both files.
findings.verify_reason: quad.h:14-15 says 'ordered clockwise starting from the top left', and quad.cpp:81-120 is_valid checks only that the diagonals cross strictly, so either winding and any start vertex pass. The declaration names point1..point4 (quad.h:21-22) while the definition uses point0..point3 (quad.cpp:14-17). Real inconsistency, but low impact: low.

findings.title: The orthonormal-axes check is written out four times
findings.evidence:
set_axes: if (!are_equal(new_x.length(), 1.0f, default_epsilon) ||
			!are_equal(new_y.length(), 1.0f, default_epsilon) ||
			!are_equal(Vector2F::dot(new_x, new_y), 0.0f, default_epsilon))
-- repeated at set_x_axis (175-176), set_y_axis (188-189) and axes_valid (340-346); the half-width rule (<= 0.0f) is likewise repeated in inflate (90), set_half_extents (199), set_half_x_width (209), set_half_y_width (219) and half_widths_valid (331).
findings.why: Validity is the type's invariant. With four copies, a tolerance change, for example scaling as edges_valid does, has to be made consistently in four places.
findings.suggested_fix: Add file-local helpers `axes_orthonormal(const Vector2F&, const Vector2F&)` and `half_widths_positive(const Vector2F&)`, and have the setters and the *_valid members all call them.
findings.verify_reason: The repetitions exist at rectangle_rotated.cpp:160-162, 175-176, 188-189 and 340-346, and the <=0 checks at 90, 199, 209, 219 and 331. However, the single-axis setters check a different predicate (the candidate against the current partner), so the copies are not fully equivalent. Each is a two-line check in one file, which is low severity.

findings.title: Axes and half extents are exposed as Point2F although they are directions and extents
findings.why: The same struct names its storage Vector2F and its API Point2F. The library uses the alias to say 'position', and Matrix3x2F's transform_point/transform_vector split depends on that distinction.
findings.suggested_fix: Spell the axis and extent accessors and setters as Vector2F. Keep Point2F for center and the corners.
findings.verify_reason: rectangle_rotated.h:30-58 returns and takes Point2F for the axes and half extents, while the storage is Vector2F. Point2F is a typedef of Vector2F (vector2f.h:148), so the issue is cosmetic and CONVENTIONS has no rule about the alias. The inconsistency inside one type is still real and visible.

findings.title: Off-allowlist abbreviations in public parameters (horiz/vert, hw_extents)
findings.why: CONVENTIONS keeps a closed list of short forms (dt, id, src, dst, min, max), and these names are published on the website reference. `hw_extents` / `hw_extents_` also differs from the accessor half_extents(), and half_y_width() calls a height a width.
findings.suggested_fix: Use half_width/half_height and half_extents throughout. Rename the private hw_extents_ to half_extents_.
findings.verify_reason: rectanglef.h:28-29 has horiz_half_width/vert_half_height. rectangle_rotated.h:20, 56 and 102 have hw_extents, :89 has hw_extents_, and :35 is half_y_width(), which names a height as a width. CONVENTIONS:59-60 keeps a closed allowlist (dt, id, src, dst, min, max). Low.

findings.title: Shape::AABB_intersects breaks the snake_case rule and has a pointer overload
findings.evidence:
bool AABB_intersects(const Shape* other) const;
		bool AABB_intersects(const Shape& other) const;
findings.why: CONVENTIONS: functions are snake_case, and acronyms are cased as words. Ericson's "keep the book's names" rationale covers ported routines, not this engine-authored member. Its one production caller (engine/collision/contacts.cpp:24) uses the pointer overload, which dereferences without a contract on null. The reference overload just forwards to it.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to `bounding_boxes_intersect(const Shape&)`, keep the reference form only, and update contacts.cpp, with a CHANGES.md entry.
findings.verify_reason: shape.h:15-16 declares both overloads, shape.cpp:13-15 forwards the reference form to the pointer form, and contacts.cpp:24 is the only caller (pointer form). The 'acronyms are cased as words' rule sits in CONVENTIONS' Types section (line 38), and the Ericson routines use AABB throughout, so the naming break is arguable. docs/file-length-audit.md:102 deliberately keeps this member. Renaming it would be a public API break. Low.

findings.title: Unused and missing includes in triangle.cpp, intersects.cpp and inflate.cpp
findings.evidence: triangle.cpp:6 #include "engine/math/ericson_math.h" (no ericson symbol used; grep for signed_area/strictly/test_/closest in triangle.cpp finds only the include); intersects.cpp:9 #include "engine/math/shape.h" (already reached through every shape header); inflate.cpp:50 `const std::span<const Point2F> outline(points, static_cast<size_t>(count));` with no <span> include
findings.why: Own-header-first only proves headers compile alone if each file includes what it uses. inflate.cpp gets std::span only through ericson_math.h, and triangle.cpp pays for a heavy header it does not use.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove ericson_math.h from triangle.cpp and shape.h from intersects.cpp. Add <span> and <cstddef> to inflate.cpp.
findings.verify_reason: I checked every function declared in ericson_math.h against triangle.cpp: none is used there, so line 6's include is unused. intersects.cpp:9 includes shape.h but never names Shape, and rectanglef.h:3 already includes it. inflate.cpp:50 uses std::span, and its includes (inflate.h, scalar.h, ericson_math.h, cmath) have no <span>; it arrives only through ericson_math.h. Low.

findings.title: find_hypotenuse returns the right-angle vertex and takes a redundant Triangle parameter
findings.why: The name and its comment say it finds the hypotenuse, but it returns a vertex index. That confusion already produced the leg-instead-of-hypotenuse bug described at lines 150-159. It is also a const member that ignores `this` and reads its argument instead.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename it to right_angle_vertex() and drop the parameter (read this->angle_N()), or make it a file-local free function taking the Triangle. Delete the 'find the hypotenuse' comment.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: triangle.h:66 declares a public int find_hypotenuse(const Triangle&) const. It returns the right-angle vertex index, and both callers (triangle.cpp:168, 178) pass *this. The vertex/edge confusion is now explained by the anonymous-namespace comment at 150-159 and fixed by edge_opposite_vertex. What remains is a naming and interface cleanup, not a live hazard.

findings.title: Uppercase parameter names on the free vector operators
findings.why: Parameters are snake_case per CONVENTIONS. Uppercase single letters read like macros or types. vector2i.h:38-44 and both .cpp files repeat the pattern, and every other function in the module uses a/b or other.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to a/b (and `scale` for the scalar) in vector2f.{h,cpp} and vector2i.{h,cpp}.
findings.verify_reason: vector2f.h:153-161 and vector2i.h:38-44 use the parameter names V, V1, V2 and S. CONVENTIONS:20 says parameters are snake_case. Cosmetic: low.

findings.title: navigation.cpp uses std::min without including <algorithm>
findings.why: The file compiles only through a transitive include. Under the clang/libc++ wasm build, or after an unrelated header cleanup, this can break. Engine files include their standard headers explicitly elsewhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Add #include <algorithm>.
findings.verify_reason: navigation.cpp includes navigation.h, widget.h, vector2f.h, <cmath>, <vector> and no <algorithm>, while using std::min at ~line 101. Relies on transitive include.

findings.title: widget.cpp is the only engine source using namespace-scope `using namespace labrador;` and MSVC `#pragma region`
findings.why: CONVENTIONS allows `using namespace labrador;` only in a .cpp outside the engine. Every sibling .cpp puts its anonymous namespace inside `namespace labrador`. The region pragmas are IDE folding markers no other engine file uses, and they are mis-nested against the namespace braces.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the anonymous namespace (with Children) inside `namespace labrador`, drop the using-directive and remove the #pragma region/endregion lines.
findings.verify_reason: widget.cpp:10 has `using namespace labrador;`, and CONVENTIONS:101-103 allows that only in a .cpp outside the engine. git grep shows it is the only engine hit. The anonymous namespace at :12-16 sits outside namespace labrador, and widget.cpp is the only engine file with `#pragma region` (5 hits). The first region opens at :18, before `namespace labrador` at :20.

findings.title: UiContainer caches each child's name beside the pointer although UiObject's name is immutable
findings.why: The pair stores a second copy of data the child already owns and can never change. Every add_child allocates a string, and the public children() type exposes the redundancy. remove_child(name) could compare child->name() directly.
