findings.why: README.md:63 says CHARACTERS.md 'separates owner-supplied traits from invented dialogue and records the copy rules', and it is presented as the copy record. One of the five fictional exchanges shown on the page is missing from it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the dry Examples exchange to CHARACTERS.md's 'Proposed exchanges' section, or delete the study.
findings.verify_reason: CHARACTERS.md's proposed exchanges cover the warm Home exchange and two alternate Examples exchanges (duo and guides). The dry examples exchange from data.ts:16-21 ('I saved you a place.' ... 'That'll do.') is absent.

findings.title: QA record names a heading the browser test does not check
findings.evidence:
QA.md:47-48 "Chrome accessibility tree: hidden dog asides and footer are absent when off;
  the active Get Started heading remains present." vs browser-review.mjs:101 "node.name?.value === 'Pick a sample'"
findings.why: The recorded evidence does not match the assertion actually run (the Examples context heading is "Pick a sample"). The record has drifted from the code it describes.
findings.suggested_fix: Change QA.md to say the active Examples heading "Pick a sample" remains present.
findings.verify_reason: QA.md:47-48 says 'the active Get Started heading remains present'. browser-review.mjs:101 actually asserts the heading 'Pick a sample', and its own report string says 'active Examples heading present'.

findings.title: QA.md says the regular website check/build is broken, citing a path that no longer exists
findings.evidence:
"The regular `npm run check` and `npm run build`, with the original untouched
`astro.config.ts`, stop while loading that config:
...
C:/VSProjects/Labrador/website/node_modules/source-map-js/lib/source-map-generator.js:11:17
...
Its normal production build must be restored and rechecked before any future integration"
findings.why: CI's website workflow runs `npm run gate` (check, tests and build) on every PR, so the production build works. The checkout is now C:/Projects/Labrador. Anyone reading this record would believe the site's build is broken and needs restoring before integration.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the 'Existing website verification limit' section, or reduce it to a dated note that the failure was local to that environment and has since been resolved.
findings.verify_reason: The quote is at QA.md:73-87 and cites C:/VSProjects/Labrador. CI's website gate passes, so the claim is stale. However, QA.md is the study's own verification record, written in the moment, not a live site document, and its readers are limited to the study. Low.

findings.title: Whole study directory is orphaned: nothing builds, runs, links or tracks it
findings.evidence: README.md:10 "No production page, navigation, site setting, dependency or engine file is changed."; astro.config.mjs:3 "// A separate entry point: the regular website build never includes this study." A whole-repo grep for explorations|labradors|labrador-dog-concepts outside the directory returns nothing. website/package.json has no script for it. git log -- website/explorations shows only 9162f44 (2026-10-21).
findings.why: It has 1,077 lines in the public repo, including personal family copy, and nothing keeps them in step with the site: no CI job, no TODO/BACKLOG item, no mention in website-plan.md. Its scripts depend on run_page.mjs's --input contract and on transitive packages, so they can break silently. The site's own tsconfig `include: ["**/*"]` probably also pulls its .astro/.ts files into `npm run check`, which would make an orphan a potential gate failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose one of two options. (a) Delete website/explorations/ if the owner has no further use for the voice study. (b) Keep it, but record it as an owner decision in docs/website-plan.md or TODO.md, add `explorations` to website/tsconfig.json's exclude (or confirm that the check is wanted), and add a package.json script for its build and verify steps.
findings.verify_reason: The facts check out: nothing outside website/explorations references it, and there is no package.json script, TODO item or website-plan entry for it. But it is not dead code. README.md:16-20 presents it as a deliberate owner design study that is still awaiting a decision (constraint confirmed 20 October 2026, 'no tone has been chosen'). The tsconfig gate-failure risk is speculative: tsconfig does include **/*, yet CI's npm run gate passes with these files present. It is untracked work, not a medium defect.

findings.title: README keeps agent-session process history rather than the study's content
findings.evidence:
"- There is no repository `.agents/` directory. The user-level synced skills
  inventory contains document/workflow skills and no additional relevant design
  skill. The available Sites skill's local-only workflow was used."
findings.why: This is a transcript of how one agent session worked, including its tooling environment and the skills available to it. It says nothing about the study, and the repo's own reading rules keep history out of living documents.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the 'Context consulted' section, or reduce it to the design documents that informed the study.
findings.verify_reason: README.md:101-103 describes agent-session tooling (the absence of a .agents directory, the skills inventory, the Sites skill workflow). That is process provenance, not study content.

findings.title: README claims nothing was committed, but the study is on master
findings.evidence: "Nothing is committed, pushed, published or deployed by this exploration."
findings.why: This is false: commit 9162f44 "feat: add Labrador design study components and pages" committed all 16 files and they are on master in a public repository. A reader relying on this sentence would think the directory is local scratch.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the sentence, or replace it with a dated statement that the study is committed for reference only and is not part of the site build or deployment.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: README.md:116 says 'Nothing is committed, pushed, published or deployed by this exploration.', yet git ls-files lists all 16 files on master. It is one false sentence in a study README outside every build, so low.

findings.title: The route/file list is hard-coded in four places instead of derived from data.ts
findings.evidence: export-review.mjs:12 "[['', 'index.html'], ['duo', 'duo.html'], ['guides', 'guides.html']]"; export-review.mjs:27 "[['/', 'index.html'], ['/duo/', 'duo.html'], ['/guides/', 'guides.html']]"; prepare-browser-review.mjs:9 "['index.html', 'duo.html', 'guides.html']"; verify-review.mjs:59 "['index.html', 'duo.html', 'guides.html']"
findings.why: data.ts `directions` is the source of truth for the routes, and the `dry` → '/' special case is repeated in [...direction].astro:7 and ConceptPreview.astro:41. Adding or renaming a direction requires five coordinated edits, and missing one of them fails silently.
findings.suggested_fix: Export a `route(direction)` / `offlineFile(direction)` helper from data.ts (or a small shared .mjs), and derive the lists from it.
findings.verify_reason: The route/file lists are hard-coded at export-review.mjs:12 and :27, prepare-browser-review.mjs:9 and verify-review.mjs:59. The dry->'/' special case is repeated in [...direction].astro and ConceptPreview.astro:41.

findings.title: Generated offline README promises screenshots this script never produces, in a folder it never creates
findings.evidence:
'Seven screenshots and three rendered Chrome test reports are included in the screenshots folder.',
'Full screen-reader review, all-control keyboard traversal and actual 200% browser zoom remain outstanding.',
findings.why: export-review.mjs writes offline/README.txt unconditionally, before any browser review runs. The screenshots are written by browser-review.mjs to out/labrador-dog-concepts/screenshots (browser-review.mjs:9), which is a sibling of offline/ and not inside it. So the README asserts evidence that may not exist, at a location the reader of offline/ cannot see. The status text is also hard-coded rather than derived.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the evidence claims from the generated README.txt. If they are kept, write them from browser-review.mjs after the screenshots exist, and use the correct relative path ../screenshots.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: export-review.mjs writes offline/README.txt unconditionally, saying the screenshots are 'included in the screenshots folder'. browser-review.mjs:9 writes them to out/labrador-dog-concepts/screenshots, a sibling of offline/. The file is ignored generated output from an exploration script, so low.

findings.title: Element lookup and double-rAF wait copied across evaluate strings and scripts
findings.evidence: framed-captures.mjs:24 and :29 "const el = [...document.querySelectorAll(${JSON.stringify(selector)})].find(candidate => candidate.getClientRects().length && !candidate.closest('[hidden]'));"; 'new Promise(resolve => requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(resolve)))' at framed-captures.mjs:21,27,42 and browser-review.mjs:13
findings.why: Identical page-side snippets are pasted as string literals. browser-review.mjs already wraps the rAF wait in `ready()`, but framed-captures.mjs repeats the raw string three times. framed-captures.mjs also duplicates browser-review.mjs's theme/presence selection logic (lines 14-18 vs browser-review.mjs:14).
findings.suggested_fix: Do the scroll and the rect measurement in a single evaluate in framed-captures.mjs, add a local `ready()` helper, or share a small helpers module between the two driver scripts.
findings.verify_reason: framed-captures.mjs repeats the element lookup on lines 24 and 29 and the double-rAF string on lines 21, 27 and 42. browser-review.mjs:13 already wraps the same wait in a ready() helper.

findings.title: `long-form` condition is always true, so the `.guides .conversation` grid rule is dead
findings.evidence:
<div class:list={['conversation', { 'long-form': lines.length > 2 }]}>  // every exchange in data.ts has 4 or 5 lines
concepts.css:106 ".conversation.long-form, .guides .conversation.long-form { grid-template-columns: 1fr; ...}"
concepts.css:139 ".guides .conversation { grid-template-columns: 1fr 1.45fr; }"
findings.why: Every `home` and `examples` array in data.ts has more than two lines, so `long-form` is always applied. The more specific rule at line 106 then always overrides line 139's two-column grid, which can never take effect. Both the branch and the rule mislead a reader.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the `long-form` conditional and apply the single-column rule unconditionally, then delete concepts.css:139 (and simplify line 166).
findings.verify_reason: Every home/examples array in data.ts has 4 or 5 lines, so long-form is always applied. '.guides .conversation.long-form' at concepts.css:106 always outranks '.guides .conversation' at :139 in specificity, so :139 never takes effect.

findings.title: The same 'has this dog spoken before' scan is computed twice per line
findings.evidence:
<div class:list={['speaker', { reply: lines.slice(0, index).some((earlier) => earlier.dog === line.dog) }]}>
	{lines.slice(0, index).some((earlier) => earlier.dog === line.dog)
findings.why: The same predicate is duplicated inline, and the name mapping `line.dog === 'vader' ? 'Vader' : 'Ani'` is repeated on lines 16 and 18 and again in DogPortrait.astro:4. Changing one copy and not the others would desynchronise the portrait/reply logic.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute `const reply = ...` once per line, for example with a map to `{ ...line, reply }` in the frontmatter, and export the display-name mapping from data.ts.
findings.verify_reason: DogAside.astro:14-15 computes the same lines.slice(0,index).some(...) predicate twice, and the vader->Vader/Ani mapping is repeated on lines 16 and 18.

findings.title: Unused CSS classes `.feature-line` and `.guide-links`
findings.why: No .astro or .ts file in the study emits class feature-line or guide-links (grep over src/components, src/pages and data.ts). They are left over from an earlier layout. Line 95's selector list also carries `.feature-line p`.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete lines 99-100 and 149, and remove `.feature-line p` from line 95.
findings.verify_reason: A grep over src finds feature-line and guide-links only in concepts.css (lines 95, 99, 100 and 149). No component emits them.

findings.title: Script imports domhandler and css-select, which are not declared in website/package.json
findings.evidence:
import { Document, Element, Text } from 'domhandler';
import { selectAll, selectOne } from 'css-select';
findings.why: Neither package is listed in website/package.json (devDependencies has parse5 but not these two). They resolve only because another package's dependency tree, through package-lock.json's node_modules/css-select and node_modules/domhandler, hoists them to the top level. Any upstream bump or dedupe change can break the script without warning. The README (line 113) presents this as a virtue rather than a risk.
findings.suggested_fix: Either declare both packages as website devDependencies, or delete the script along with the study.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: verify-review.mjs:7-8 imports domhandler and css-select, and website/package.json declares only parse5 (line 33). The script is in an optional study that no CI job runs, so breakage affects only the study. Low.

themes.name: Live document drift
themes.desc: Live documents whose checkable claims no longer match the tree: README and docs/verification.md browser ctest counts, SEAM.md's golden-frame count and its statement that only Direct3D rasterises on CI, ARCHITECTURE's module table and tree diagram, and sample README claims.
themes.story: One documentation commit correcting each claim against ctest_inventory.json, ci.yml and the tree, preferring statements that do not decay over counts. Run the website gate where a page quotes the changed text.

findings.title: README's wasm ctest counts are one short and leave out the Firefox entries
findings.evidence: README.md:295-298: "A `wasm-*` build has 19 without a Chromium and, where one is found, 32 in Debug and 33 in Release, the extra ones being pages run in headless Chrome". tests/ctest_inventory.json lists 24 entries only some configurations get for wasm-release; 18 every-configuration entries plus those 24 make 42. Take away the 8 Firefox* entries and 34 remain with Chromium, and Debug lacks only LineSweeperPacingPageTests, so 33. AGENTS.md:58 already says "33 Debug / 34 Release with Chromium, 8 more with Firefox, 19 without", and website samples.mdx:268-269 says a tree after 4 November "ends `out of 33`".
findings.why: README tells a reader to check that ctest's last line says 'out of N'. A correct wasm build reports a number that differs from README's, because ComponentsPointerPageTests was added and the README was not updated. On a machine with Firefox the number is 8 higher again, and README never mentions those entries.
findings.suggested_fix: Change this to 33 in Debug and 34 in Release with a Chromium, add that a found Firefox registers eight more Firefox* entries, or point to AGENTS.md's table instead of repeating the numbers.
findings.verify_reason: README.md:295-297 says 19 / 32 Debug / 33 Release. AGENTS.md says 33/34 with Chromium plus 8 Firefox entries, and ci_gap_report's BROWSER_TESTS has 14, so 19+14=33 for Debug. README is a live document and does not mention the Firefox entries.

findings.title: Tree diagram says docs/review/ holds findings against the current code
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md:277: "├── review/             findings against the current code". AGENTS.md says: "`docs/review/` holds historical reviews: do not rewrite findings as fixes land or trust their line numbers as current." README.md:325-327 says: "Their findings are not updated as they are fixed."
findings.why: The design document tells readers the review folder describes the current tree, which is the opposite of the rule in the brief and the README. A reader who trusts it would act on findings that have already been fixed.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the annotation to say what the folder is: dated reviews kept as written, with INDEX.md and each folder's STATUS/README giving current disposition.
findings.verify_reason: ARCHITECTURE.md:277 reads 'review/             findings against the current code'. That contradicts AGENTS.md ('historical reviews ... do not trust their line numbers as current') and README's statement that findings are not updated as fixed.

findings.title: Module table leaves out the browser input and audio backends and the lodepng dependency
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md:377: "| `input` | core, math — XInput inside `xinput/` only |". :378: "| `audio` | core, math — XAudio2 inside `xaudio2/`, nothing inside `null/` |". The tree has engine/input/web/ (the browser Gamepad API) and engine/audio/webaudio/, and the same document's tree diagram (lines 186-205) lists both. Line 375's `render` row names only graphics APIs, but since 2026-11-04 render links lodepng (engine/render/png_file.h; vcpkg.json lists "lodepng"). Line 110 still says vcpkg.json "names DirectXTK and the XAudio2 redistributable" and leaves out doctest and lodepng.
findings.why: The dependency table is the stated authority for which external APIs each module may use. 'XInput inside xinput/ only' is now false, and the new engine-wide third-party dependency is missing from both the table and the 'bought edge' bullet.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'browser Gamepad API inside web/' to input, 'Web Audio inside webaudio/' to audio, and lodepng to render (as rapidjson is listed for assets). List doctest and lodepng in the vcpkg.json bullet.
findings.verify_reason: ARCHITECTURE.md:377-378 name only XInput in xinput/ and XAudio2 in xaudio2/ plus null. engine/input/web and engine/audio/webaudio exist. engine/render/png_file.cpp uses lodepng, which engine/CMakeLists.txt:407-411 links PRIVATE. Line 110 names only DirectXTK and XAudio2 in vcpkg.json, which also lists lodepng. Web backends belong to the documented destination, so ARCHITECTURE's destination framing does not excuse this.

findings.title: verification.md says wasm-debug has 13 browser tests; ci_gap_report.py requires 14
findings.evidence: docs/verification.md:268-270: "The required tests are the GL/Vulkan pixel and smoke tests and `wasm-debug`'s 13 browser tests, which configure registers only when it finds a Chromium". tools/ci_gap_report.py:40-45 BROWSER_TESTS has 14 names: RenderPixelTests, RenderPixelTestsWithoutS3tc, RenderContextLossTests, WebWindowTests, Minimal/Collision/Audio/LocalMultiplayer/Components/ComponentsPointer/LineSweeper PageTests, LineSweeperReducedMotionPageTests, LineSweeperPalettePageTests, LineSweeperBundlePageTests. 19 headless entries plus 14 makes the 33 that AGENTS.md gives for wasm-debug.
findings.why: This document defines the gap-report contract. Its count no longer matches the tool's list, so a reader checking a record against the document will see a mismatch even when the tool is right.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the count to 14, or drop the number and refer to BROWSER_TESTS in tools/ci_gap_report.py.
findings.verify_reason: verification.md:269 says "`wasm-debug`'s 13 browser tests". tools/ci_gap_report.py:40-45 BROWSER_TESTS lists 14 names, including ComponentsPointerPageTests.

findings.title: SEAM.md says there are sixty-three golden frames; there are sixty-four
findings.evidence: SEAM.md:364-367: "Sixty-three frames, four of which fill more than one view ... `d3d11`, `d3d12`, `gl` and `vulkan` reproduce all sixty-three exactly." `ls tests/render/golden | wc -l` gives 64. The sentence came in with ac58ca1, when the folder held 63 images. d5b24ce (2026-10-27, "Pin additive blending with a pixel test") added contract-a-tint-with-zero-alpha-adds-its-colour.png afterwards. website/src/content/docs/why.mdx:203 repeats "sixty-three reference images".
findings.why: The seam charter's statement that all backends reproduce the golden set exactly now quotes a count that is wrong, and it is copied onto the public site.
findings.suggested_fix: Change both places to sixty-four, or state the property without a count, as SEAM §4 already does for line counts.
findings.verify_reason: SEAM.md:364-367 says sixty-three twice. tests/render/golden holds 64 files, all PNG. why.mdx:203 repeats "sixty-three reference images".

findings.title: SEAM.md says only the two Direct3D backends rasterise on CI; GL and Vulkan now draw there too
findings.evidence: SEAM.md:370-374: "Two of the four happen on the build machine as well, which is the reason the fourth backend is a Direct3D one: a runner has no GPU and Direct3D gets a device there anyway, where OpenGL falls back to GDI 1.1 and Vulkan has no in-box fallback at all." .github/workflows/ci.yml:329 and :333 set `software_device: llvmpipe` and `software_device: SwiftShader` for the GL and Vulkan entries, and line 490 is "Point the Vulkan loader at Chrome's SwiftShader". AGENTS.md says "CI's GL job draws on Mesa's llvmpipe and its Vulkan job on Chrome's SwiftShader, and fails if `RenderPixelTests` names another device".
findings.why: The present-tense description of which backends CI holds to the golden set is wrong. A reader would think GL and Vulkan golden regressions are only caught locally.
findings.suggested_fix: Say that all four rasterising backends run RenderPixelTests on CI (GL on llvmpipe, Vulkan on SwiftShader). If the Direct3D rationale for the fourth backend is worth keeping, state it as a reason, not as a description of CI today.
findings.verify_reason: SEAM.md:371-374 says only two of the four rasterising backends run on the build machine, and that OpenGL/Vulkan get no device there. ci.yml:329/333 set software_device llvmpipe for GL and SwiftShader for Vulkan, and lines 402/491 configure those devices. AGENTS.md also says CI's GL and Vulkan jobs draw.

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE says the include wall covers subfolders of render/ and audio/ only; it covers every module's subfolders
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md:518-521: "The rule `cmake/check_engine_includes.cmake` enforces is the *folder* ... a subfolder of `render/` or of `audio/` **is** a backend and its headers are its own". The check matches any `engine/<module>/<sub>/...h` (`if(engine_relative MATCHES "^([^/]+)/([^/]+)/.+[.]h$")`), which also walls input/xinput, input/web, app/win32 and app/web. AGENTS.md says: "The wall covers render, audio, input and app platform folders."
findings.why: The design document understates what the check enforces. The earlier paragraph about the window move relies on app/win32 being walled, which this sentence does not cover.
findings.suggested_fix: Say that any subfolder of an engine module (render, audio, input, app) is a platform/backend folder whose headers are its own.
findings.verify_reason: ARCHITECTURE.md:519-520 limits the wall to subfolders of render/ or audio/. check_engine_includes.cmake:73 matches '^([^/]+)/([^/]+)/.+[.]h$' for any module. engine/CMakeLists.txt's comment also says it guards the audio, input and app backend folders.

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE says the shell asks the machine 'exactly one question'; APPLICATION.md says two
findings.evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md:565-566: "**The shell asks the machine exactly one question, once, and what the answer sizes is one thing.**" engine/app/APPLICATION.md:16-18: "The shell asks the machine two questions, and this is one of them; the other is where the executable is (`content_root.h`)." engine/app/content_root.h exists, and CHANGES records manifest paths resolving against the executable's directory.
findings.why: Two authoritative design documents contradict each other on the same claim. The one in ARCHITECTURE became false when content_root was added.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the ARCHITECTURE sentence to match APPLICATION.md §1: two questions, the processor count and the executable's location, each sizing or deciding one thing.
findings.verify_reason: ARCHITECTURE.md:565 says 'exactly one question', and APPLICATION.md:16-18 says 'two questions ... the other is where the executable is (content_root.h)'. The contradiction is real. It is a rhetorical framing in a paragraph whose actual subject is thread-pool sizing, and that subject is still correct, so the impact is low.

findings.title: Docs say end_not_comparable covers three frames; six call sites use it
findings.evidence: SEAM.md:377: "`Harness::end_not_comparable` holds the three frames that are not 64x64". AGENTS.md:152: "`Harness::end_not_comparable` names the three backend/resize-specific frames". It is called at tests/render/pixel_tests.cpp:309, 370, 433 and tests/render/view_pixel_tests.cpp:180, 208, 501. The header comment in tests/render/pixel_test_harness.h:83-86 says: "Three resize cases use this ... The analytic composition and viewport regressions also use it, asserting every pixel against known colours."
findings.why: Both briefs describe the exemption from golden comparison as a closed set of three resize frames. It now also covers three analytic 64x64 cases, so a reviewer counting exemptions would be misled.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe it as the harness header does: three resize frames plus the analytic composition and viewport cases, each asserted pixel by pixel.
findings.verify_reason: SEAM.md:377 says end_not_comparable 'holds the three frames that are not 64x64'. It has six call sites (pixel_tests.cpp:309,370,433; view_pixel_tests.cpp:180,208,501). pixel_test_harness.h:83-86 says the analytic composition and viewport regressions also use it. The sentence is literally true about non-64x64 frames but understates what the function covers.

findings.title: BlendMode rationale still describes DirectXTK SpriteBatch's Begin
findings.evidence: samples/linesweeper/README.md:632-635: "`set_filter` closes and reopens the batch on every change, because a sprite batch cannot swap state mid-`Begin`; a blend selector would inherit exactly that". The renderer no longer uses SpriteBatch: SEAM.md:106 says "DirectXTK is no longer on the render path at all". engine/render/d3d11/renderer.cpp:350-360 shows set_filter returning early when the filter is unchanged, and otherwise `flush()` because there is "One sampler per draw call". No Begin is involved.
findings.why: The reason given for declining BlendMode cites a library constraint the engine no longer has. The real cost, a flush per state change because each draw call binds one state, is not stated.
findings.suggested_fix: Restate it in terms of the engine's own batch: a state change flushes the view's batch (renderer.h: 'Changing it mid-list is legal and costs a flush'), so a per-particle blend toggle would multiply draw calls.
findings.verify_reason: samples/linesweeper/README.md:632-634 still gives 'a sprite batch cannot swap state mid-`Begin`' as the reason. d3d11/renderer.cpp:351-360 returns early when the filter is unchanged and otherwise flushes because there is 'One sampler per draw call'. The conclusion (a flush per change) still holds; only the stated mechanism is stale.

findings.title: Capture README says the tool is built in every rasterising preset; it is Windows-only
findings.evidence: tools/linesweeper_capture/README.md:36-38: "The tool needs a device, so it is not a ctest entry. It is built in every preset with a rasterising backend. The `-null` presets do not build it at all". The root CMakeLists.txt:98-102 adds it only under `if(WIN32)` ("Windows only until it has a reason not to be"), so wasm-debug and wasm-release (GL/WebGL2, rasterising) never build it.
findings.why: A reader looking for LineSweeperCapture in a rasterising browser build will not find it, and the README gives the wrong reason.
findings.suggested_fix: Say it is built in every Windows preset with a rasterising backend, and not in -null or wasm presets.
findings.verify_reason: tools/linesweeper_capture/README.md:36-37 says the tool is built in every preset with a rasterising backend. Root CMakeLists.txt:98-102 adds it only under if(WIN32), so the rasterising wasm presets never build it.

themes.name: Engine comment truth outside render (math, core, ui, collision, assets, input, audio, app)
themes.desc: False or stale claims and archaeology in non-render engine comments. Examples: comments that point to rationale SM-45/SM-46 removed, gamepad.h quotations that no longer exist, a broad-phase contract naming bounds(), 'seven' SAT axes, backend censuses, 'EIGHT FORWARDERS' over thirteen, and polling 'once per frame'. Some are in public headers that the website publishes word for word.
themes.story: A comments-only SM-47-style batch over engine/{math,core,ui,collision,assets,input,audio,app}. Check each claim against the code and the cited passage. Rewrite false contracts to describe current behaviour; where a contract needs a behaviour decision (for example #126's polling cadence), file it in the behaviour theme instead. Remove history and keep the one owner of duplicated rationale. Change no tokens. Run citation, whitespace and website checks, and review the published header pages.

findings.title: Devices are polled once per update step, not once per frame as the contract says
findings.why: Application::update (application.cpp:410-413) polls gamepads/keyboard/mouse/touch, and it runs once per fixed step inside timer_.Tick. A rendered frame can run 0, 1 or several updates; FrameTimings::updates in this same header says so. A catch-up frame polls several times, and a zero-update frame polls none. In this header "frame" means the rendered frame, so the contract is wrong in the place a caller reads it. The input headers (keyboard.h:146,172, mouse.h:140, touch.h:128, gamepads.h:19) repeat the wording.
findings.suggested_fix: Say "once per fixed update, before that update's states". Correct the input headers' "once per frame" in the same change.
findings.verify_reason: application.h:345-348 says the devices are polled 'once per frame before any state updates'. Polling happens inside Application::update (application.cpp:410-413), which timer_.Tick calls once per fixed step (line 374). FrameTimings::updates in the same header says a frame runs 0, 1 or several steps. The same wording is in gamepads.h:19, keyboard.h:146 and 172, mouse.h:140 and touch.h:128. These are public header comments that the website publishes word for word.

findings.title: Seam says audio suspends on foreground loss under GamepadReader's contract; it does neither
findings.why: An alt-tabbed game keeps playing sound, which contradicts the clause. "Same contract as GamepadReader's" is also wrong on substance. GamepadReader's suspend stops output and 'resume replays nothing'. XAudio2's Suspend/Resume (StopEngine/StartEngine) and Web Audio's context.suspend/resume resume every voice where it stopped. A reader of the seam cannot tell when audio actually goes quiet or what comes back.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the clause to state the actual trigger: minimised, power-suspended or page hidden, and not foreground loss. State that resume continues persistent voices from where they were. Drop the GamepadReader equivalence, or change Application if foreground loss really should silence audio.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed: audio_device.h:154-157 says suspend/resume follow foreground loss under GamepadReader's contract. But Application::settle_presence (application.cpp:479-497) suspends only the gamepad reader, input focus and touch. AudioDevice::suspend is called only from on_suspending (line 519) and teardown (lines 95, 563). An alt-tabbed game therefore keeps its sound. This is real contract drift in a comment, not a crash or corruption, so medium.

findings.title: Claim that the AudioDevice releases a replaced bank's voices is false; replaced looping voices keep sounding
findings.evidence:
"// A bank holds only handles: the voices and the wave bank behind them
// belong to the AudioDevice, which releases them itself." The AudioDevice seam (audio_device.h:112-142) has no release/destroy verb. All three backends append to `banks`/`voices` vectors that are freed only in ~AudioDevice. add_sound_bank (audio_resources.h:39-42) explicitly supports re-adding a name, which 'destroys its previous bank'.
findings.why: Suppose a bank is replaced or emptied while one of its effects is playing with loop=true. The SoundBank and its EffectHandles are gone, but the device voice keeps looping, and nothing in the engine can stop it until the device dies. The wave bank memory is also held for the device's lifetime. The comment presents this as handled. (The known finding at this line is only about the block being attached to no declaration.)
findings.suggested_fix: Either stop every effect voice in ~SoundBank (it holds the device pointer and the voice handles) or add a release verb to the seam. At minimum, state in add_sound_bank's contract that replacing a bank does not stop or free its voices.
findings.verify_reason: No ~SoundBank exists, and sound_bank.cpp never stops voices on destruction. A replaced or emptied bank's looping effect voice therefore keeps sounding until the AudioDevice dies, and add_sound_bank's contract (audio_resources.h:39-44) does not say so. The comment is literally true, though: the device does release the voices, at its own destruction. The real gap is the undocumented consequence of replacement, and the block's placement is already tracked. Medium.

findings.title: Web Audio says its non-immediate stop matches the null backend, but null keeps answering playing
findings.why: The comment tells a maintainer that null and Web Audio agree on this transition. In fact null behaves like XAudio2 here: it answers playing indefinitely. Someone writing a cross-backend test from this comment would expect `stopped` under null and get `playing`.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the clause about null, or replace it with an accurate one: null has no clock, so it keeps answering playing as XAudio2 does, and only Web Audio reports the natural end.
findings.verify_reason: The webaudio/audio_device.cpp comment at about lines 72-79 says the natural-end outcome 'is also the one engine/audio/null/ describes'. null/recording.h:20-22 says the opposite: 'a non-looping voice does not finish by itself, and stop_voice(false) does not stop its tail'. null/audio_device.cpp:186-201 sets stopped only on immediate.

findings.title: Contract says the broad phase indexes GameObject::bounds(); BroadPhase reads shape()->bounding_box()
findings.evidence:
"// The fine half of the pair GameObject::bounds() opens. bounds() is
// the coarse extent a broad phase indexes;" vs broad_phase.cpp:120 "this->boxes_.push_back(object->shape()->bounding_box());"
findings.why: This is a published public-header contract. A game could reasonably make bounds() larger or smaller than its shape, expecting the broad phase to follow it, but the broad phase ignores bounds() entirely, and so does contacts.cpp's AABB filter, which uses shape()->AABB_intersects.
findings.suggested_fix: Say that the broad phase and the AABB filter both index shape()->bounding_box(), and that bounds() is GameObject's extent for culling and layout, which collision does not read.
findings.verify_reason: collision_object.h:27-29 says bounds() is 'the coarse extent a broad phase indexes'. But broad_phase.cpp:119 pushes object->shape()->bounding_box(), and contacts.cpp:24 uses shape()->AABB_intersects. Nothing in engine/collision reads bounds(). game_object.h:46-47 makes the same false claim ('bounds() remains the unsnapped geometry used by layout and collision'). Both are published headers.

findings.title: Polygon rationale says Shape::edges() returns a std::vector; Shape has no edges() and each shape's edges() returns std::array
findings.why: The comment justifies the Polygon struct with an allocation that does not exist and a virtual function that was deliberately removed. A reader who trusts it learns something false about the math module's API.
findings.suggested_fix: Restate the rationale in present terms: Shape exposes no virtual edge list, so the narrow phase copies each shape's corners into one fixed-size Polygon and treats every shape type the same way. Drop the claim about std::vector and heap allocation.
findings.verify_reason: narrow_phase.cpp:21-25 does say Shape::edges() returns a std::vector. engine/math/shape.h:70-77 says there is no virtual edges() and that each shape returns a std::array. The comment is false, but it is a comment in an anonymous namespace and changes no behaviour, so high is inflated.

findings.title: direction.h quotes gamepad.h text that no longer exists, and direction.cpp points to a warning 'two lines above'
findings.why: A verbatim quotation in a published header that matches nothing in the cited file misleads more than a paraphrase does. The .cpp pointer sends a maintainer to the wrong place. Both broke when SM-45 rewrote gamepad.h.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the quotation with a paraphrase of what gamepad.h now says (edge queries are free functions over two snapshots; Gamepads forwards to them). Point direction.cpp at GamepadState's stick comment rather than at 'two lines above'.
findings.verify_reason: direction.h:66-69 quotes 'free functions over two values, and Gamepads' methods of the same names are forwarders...'. A grep of gamepad.h finds neither 'free functions' nor 'forwarder'. direction.cpp:16-19 says the warning is 'two lines above the function this calls', but gamepad.h:131-140 (apply_deadzone) carries no such warning. The second-deadzone warning is at gamepad.h:47-49, in GamepadState's stick fields.

findings.title: mouse.h and touch.h defer to keyboard.h reasoning that SM-45 removed
findings.evidence:
mouse.h:9 "// Fed, not read, for the reason keyboard.h gives at length and will not"; mouse.h:50 "// are all up when it is false, for the reason keyboard.h documents -"; mouse.h:145-146 "// THE FEEDING SIDE, public for the reasons keyboard.h gives: `input`
		// may not name a class in `app` to friend it"; touch.h:10 "// Fed, not read, for the reason keyboard.h gives"; touch.h:132 "// THE FEEDING SIDE, public for the reasons keyboard.h gives." keyboard.h now has a three-line summary (lines 10-12) and nothing about friending `app`. `git show 86eaed7^:engine/input/keyboard.h` lines 227-233 held the removed "public rather than friended" argument and the long fed-versus-read section.
findings.why: These are published public headers. They point readers at keyboard.h for an explanation "at length" that SM-45 deliberately cut. mouse.h and touch.h were outside SM-45's six-header scope, so their references were left dangling.
findings.suggested_fix: Either state each reason in a sentence where it is cited (feeding is public because `input` cannot friend an `app` class, and test or replay feeders need it; focus loss clears buttons because the up event goes to another window), or cite only what keyboard.h still says. Remove "at length and will not repeat".
findings.verify_reason: mouse.h:9-11 ('at length and will not repeat'), mouse.h:49-50 and mouse.h:145-146 (the friend-`app` reason), touch.h:10 and touch.h:132 all defer to keyboard.h. Current keyboard.h has only the three-line summary at lines 10-12. grep for friend/app finds nothing. 86eaed7^ keyboard.h:230-231 held the 'public rather than friended' argument, so the references dangle in published headers.

findings.title: test_AABB_AABB is documented as a sphere-vs-AABB test
findings.why: This comment was copied from test_circle_AABB (line 124). It names a sphere and a parameter `s` that this function does not have. The function is the box-vs-box filter behind RectangleF::intersects, used by the broad phase and the view cull, so the false description sits on one of the most-read functions in the file.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace it with "Whether boxes a and b overlap, boundary included", or delete it and rely on the in-body NaN note.
findings.verify_reason: ericson_math.cpp:17 really reads 'Returns true if sphere s intersects AABB b' above test_AABB_AABB(a, b), and ericson_math.h:16 keeps the book's comments only 'where they still apply', so this one is wrong. It is not tracked (SM-47 left this file out). It is medium, not high: the function name and the detailed body comment beside it make the error obvious, so no reader is actually misled.

findings.title: Ericson ports narrate former code and past bugs
findings.evidence: line 29: "so the rejecting form fell through to `return true` and one NaN coordinate produced a box that intersected everything"; line 74: "Unguarded, that divided 0/0 and returned (NaN, NaN)"; line 79: "Falling through is the fix, NOT returning a."; line 251: "The rejecting form was three comparisons that are all false against NaN, falling through to `return 1`"; line 264: "is still added after the two axis tests have been decided, exactly as before."; lines 368-373: "The disagreement was not academic. A default-constructed Triangle ... made Triangle().contains(p) true for every point in the plane"
findings.why: These comments describe what the code was, which CONVENTIONS says belongs in `git log`. Lines 368-373 also cite `Triangle().contains(p)`, a member that no longer exists (shape.h:93 says there is no contains(const Point2F&)). SM-47 cleaned rectangle_rotated.cpp but not this file.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the present-tense rationale: the accepting form makes NaN report no hit; the guard prevents 0/0 for a degenerate edge; an all-zero polygon encloses nothing. Remove the then/now narration and the stale contains() reference.
findings.verify_reason: I checked each quoted line: 29 'fell through to `return true`', 74 'Unguarded, that divided 0/0', 79 'Falling through is the fix', 251 'The rejecting form was...', 264 'exactly as before', and 368-373 'The disagreement was not academic... Triangle().contains(p)'. shape.h:93 confirms there is no contains(const Point2F&). CONVENTIONS:161-163 classes this kind of comment as archaeology. SM-47's targets did not include ericson_math.cpp, so it is not tracked.

findings.title: test_point_triangle says it computes barycentric coordinates; it deliberately does not
findings.why: The header (ericson_math.h:220-224) says explicitly that this is NOT the barycentric form, because that form divides by zero on collinear triangles. The .cpp comment states the opposite of the contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the two-line comment. The header owns the contract.
findings.verify_reason: ericson_math.cpp:496-497 says it computes barycentric coordinates. The body calls point_in_convex_polygon, and ericson_math.h:220-224 says explicitly that it is not the barycentric form. The comment directly contradicts the published contract.

findings.title: Comment says narrow_phase.cpp uses signed_area; it does not
findings.why: The comment backs a design decision with a cross-module usage that does not exist. A reader who goes looking in narrow_phase for agreement will not find it, and someone changing signed_area may think collision depends on it.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the narrow_phase clause. Keep the justification that signed_area is ericson_math's definition of 'encloses nothing', shared with point_in_convex_polygon and test_segment_convex_polygon.
findings.verify_reason: inflate.cpp:45-47 says narrow_phase.cpp uses signed_area. git grep finds signed_area only in inflate.cpp and ericson_math. narrow_phase.cpp:178-217 answers 'encloses anything' with its own double-precision area accumulation, deliberately not signed_area, so the claimed agreement is false.

findings.title: point_rectangle_rotated_intersect cites allocations that no longer exist, plus history
findings.why: Quad keeps its points in fixed storage, Quad::triangles() returns std::array<Triangle, 2>, and RectangleRotated::quad() builds from cached corners. Building and triangulating a Quad allocates nothing, so the "allocate twice" argument is false today. "now answers false rather than throwing" is history.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the reason that still holds: Quad's constructor throws on a default-constructed rectangle's coincident corners. Drop the allocation claim and the "now" clause.
findings.verify_reason: intersects.cpp:476-487 says building a Quad 'would allocate twice' and 'A degenerate rectangle now answers false'. But quad.h:58 stores points_[4] as a fixed array, quad.h:50 returns std::array<Triangle,2> from triangles(), and rectangle_rotated.cpp:265 builds the Quad from 'Quad's fixed-storage constructor'. So the allocation argument is false, and 'now' is history. The throwing rationale still holds.

findings.title: View cost stated in D3D11-only terms
findings.evidence:
every view costs a deferred context and a sprite batch's
dynamic vertex buffer, built eagerly at `create_device` and rebuilt after every
device restore
findings.why: Deferred contexts and SpriteBatch are D3D11 mechanisms. D3D12, Vulkan and GL record per-view state differently, and the null backend builds no device objects. The shell's rationale document should state the seam-level cost, since application.h:90-93 already says it generically.
findings.suggested_fix: "every view costs the backend's per-view recording state (SEAM.md), built eagerly..."
findings.verify_reason: APPLICATION.md:28-31 says every view costs 'a deferred context and a sprite batch's dynamic vertex buffer'. Those are D3D11 terms, while application.cpp:139 says 'the backend's per-view recording state'.

findings.title: "four panes at the very most" contradicts the configurable view_capacity
findings.why: view_capacity is any value of at least 1 (validate()). Four is only its default. Calling four a hard maximum misstates the option the comment cites.
findings.suggested_fix: "...to draw a frame whose pane count the game states in view_capacity."
findings.verify_reason: application.cpp:139-142 says 'four panes at the very most'. view_capacity defaults to 4 (application.h:97) and validate() requires only at least 1, so four is a default, not a maximum.

findings.title: Comment points to gamepads.h for detectors "this replaced"
findings.why: This is history (what the code replaced). gamepads.h:14-21 gives the present-tense rationale and mentions no "two" detectors that were replaced, so the pointer is also inaccurate.
findings.suggested_fix: "...true - gamepads.h says why the engine polls and a game does not."
findings.verify_reason: application.cpp:401-403 says '...the two hand-primed edge detectors this replaced'. That is past-tense archaeology, which CONVENTIONS.md:161-169 forbids. gamepads.h:14-21 gives the present-tense reason (a game's own detector needs priming, and a second one drifts). The pointer is roughly apt; the wording is history.

findings.title: Says frame arithmetic is create_window's job, but Window does it
findings.why: Application::create_window (lines 180-203) only copies options into WindowOptions. The client-to-outer conversion is outer_size_for_client/Impl::outer_size in engine/app/win32/window.cpp, and window.h:144 says "Turning one into the other is this class's job and nobody else's". The comment sends the reader to the wrong file.
findings.suggested_fix: Say "that is the Window's job (window.h, WindowOptions::client_size)".
findings.verify_reason: application.cpp:598-601 says it. Application::create_window (180-203) only copies options into WindowOptions; outer_size_for_client in win32/window.cpp does the frame conversion. The pointer names the wrong place, but the comment's actual point (no frame arithmetic belongs in on_window_size_changed) is still correct.

findings.title: on_device_lost narrates a past bug
findings.why: "left every object holding a freed SoundBank*" describes what an earlier version did. CONVENTIONS forbids archaeology comments, and the present-tense reason (audio is not device-owned, and banks are borrowed by objects) fits in one clause.
findings.suggested_fix: "Only the resources the device holds; audio is not one, and objects hold borrowed SoundBank pointers across a device loss."
findings.verify_reason: application.cpp:615-617: 'tearing down the sound banks here left every object holding a freed SoundBank*'. That describes what an earlier version did, which is archaeology under CONVENTIONS.md:161.

findings.title: "EIGHT FORWARDERS" comment heads a block of thirteen
findings.evidence: // EIGHT FORWARDERS AND NOT ONE DECISION IN THEM, which is the point.
findings.why: The block below has on_key_down, on_key_up, on_text, on_mouse_move, on_mouse_button_down, on_mouse_button_up, on_mouse_capture_lost, on_mouse_wheel, on_mouse_wheel_horizontal and four touch forwarders: 13 in all. The count went stale as text, capture-loss, horizontal-wheel and touch handlers were added. The comment also sits between partitioner() and the forwarders, while keyboard(), mouse(), touch() and gamepads() are defined after them, so the accessor block is split in two.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the number ("THE FORWARDERS, AND NOT ONE DECISION IN THEM") and move the keyboard(), mouse(), touch(), gamepads() and window() accessors up to sit with the other accessors.
findings.verify_reason: application.cpp:679 reads 'EIGHT FORWARDERS AND NOT ONE DECISION IN THEM'; the block that follows defines 13 forwarders (on_key_down through on_touch_cancel), then keyboard() at 794, mouse, touch, and window() at 813, separated from partitioner() at 675.

findings.title: Citation APPLICATION.md#5 does not support the privacy claim
findings.why: APPLICATION.md §5 argues why the callbacks stay on Application rather than moving into Window. It says nothing about why the overrides are private or about reaching them through a base pointer. The citation check passes because the section exists, but the claim has no source.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the citation, since the sentence is self-contained, or add the private-override rationale to §5.
findings.verify_reason: APPLICATION.md §5 (lines 88-99) argues why the callbacks stay on Application rather than Window, plus set_input_focus. It says nothing about private overrides or reaching them through a base pointer, so the citation at application.h:420-422 does not support the claim.

findings.title: Points to win32/window.cpp for translation that SM-50 moved to helpers
findings.evidence:
// What the DOM's input events mean to the engine: the browser half of the
// message translation engine/app/win32/window.cpp does for Win32.
findings.why: Key-position and UTF-16 translation now live in win32/keyboard_input.cpp, and touch translation in win32/pointer_input.cpp, the direct counterparts of dom_events. The pointer names the dispatcher, not the counterpart.
findings.suggested_fix: "...the browser half of engine/app/win32/keyboard_input.h and pointer_input.h."
findings.verify_reason: dom_events.h:12-13 cites win32/window.cpp as the counterpart translation. Per SM-50 (code-hygiene.md:244-249) scan-position and UTF-16 translation live in win32/keyboard_input.h/.cpp. pointer_input.h:7-9 says it holds the touch half of the translation. window.cpp keeps dispatch and modifiers, so the pointer is only partly stale.

findings.title: Constructor comment repeats outer_size_for_client's rationale as history
findings.why: outer_size_for_client (lines 70-77) already gives the same 1264x681 rationale in the present conditional. This copy is in the past tense ("came out", "nothing said so"), so it is archaeology and a duplicate that can drift.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut it to "CreateWindowExW takes an outer rect; outer_size_for_client says why the conversion is needed" and keep the part about the WS_POPUP branch and the system DPI.
findings.verify_reason: window.cpp:340-348 says 'a windowed 1280x720 came out as roughly 1264x681 ... and nothing said so' in the past tense. It repeats outer_size_for_client's present-tense rationale at lines 70-77.

findings.title: Win32 window comment names D3D11's private DeviceResources as the renderer's behaviour
findings.why: The Win32 window drives all four Windows render backends. The contract it depends on is Renderer::window_size_changed answering false before create_device, which renderer.h:340-343 states. DeviceResources::WindowSizeChanged exists only in engine/render/d3d11/device_resources.cpp:331. The window's justification therefore cites one backend's internals, which do not describe D3D12, GL or Vulkan.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the seam instead: "Renderer::window_size_changed rebuilds nothing before create_device and answers false (renderer.h)". Describe the stretch generically, as a back buffer created at the preset and scaled to the monitor.
findings.verify_reason: win32/window.cpp:373-383 cites 'DeviceResources::WindowSizeChanged returns early with no window set' and DXGI_SCALING_STRETCH; the Win32 window serves D3D11/D3D12/GL/Vulkan, and renderer.h:340-343 states the seam contract ('BEFORE create_device IT REBUILDS NOTHING AND ANSWERS false') that the comment should cite.

findings.title: WM_MOVE rationale counts backends as if there were three
findings.why: There are five backends now. Vulkan answers back_buffer_size from its engine-owned colour target (vulkan/renderer.cpp:1243-1253, "for a reason no other backend has"), and null answers from stored width/height. "Two of the backends" plus GL was the D3D11/D3D12/GL era, so the comment now misdescribes which backends behave which way.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the count. Either say "the D3D backends answer from a swap chain and Vulkan from its colour target; GL answers from the window" or cite SEAM.md#6, which renderer.h already names as owning each backend's answer.
findings.verify_reason: window.cpp:705-713 says 'Two of the backends answer it from a swap chain'. Vulkan's back_buffer_size (renderer.cpp:1243) answers from its colour target, which is also the size it was last told, and null stores width/height. So the grouping 'GL answers from the window, the others answer what they were told' still holds. Only the count and the 'swap chain' mechanism are stale.

findings.title: Default justified by what "every existing manifest already meant"
findings.evidence:
"// Absent means required, which is the safe default and the one
// every existing manifest already meant."
findings.why: 'already meant' refers to manifests that existed before `optional` did, which is history. The contract is stated in asset_manifest.h and asset_manifest_loader.h.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut it to 'Absent means required (asset_manifest.h).' or remove the comment.
findings.verify_reason: asset_manifest_loader.cpp:34-35 reads verbatim: 'the one every existing manifest already meant'. It justifies the default by history.

findings.title: "both of this tree's" audio backends: the tree has three
findings.why: This is a stale count. The engine has three audio backends selected by LABRADOR_AUDIO_BACKEND (xaudio2, webaudio, null), so the claim that the branch is unreachable is made about a backend set that no longer exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Write 'which every backend in this tree does', or name the three backends, after confirming that each one checks the list on open.
findings.verify_reason: The text is at sound_bank_loader.cpp:113-117, and engine/audio has null, webaudio and xaudio2, so 'both' is a stale count. The unreachability claim still holds for all three. XAudio2 (audio_device.cpp:139-147) and webaudio (:630-635) check the list on open. Null stores the definition's own wave_names as the bank (null/audio_device.cpp:95-108), so wave_index cannot miss a listed wave. Only the number is wrong, and it changes no conclusion.

findings.title: Comment narrates a removed SpriteFrame member, using a non-root path
findings.why: 'already existed ... is gone too' describes what the code used to be, which CONVENTIONS says is never a comment. The citation `render/sprite_frame.h` is also not written from the repository root, unlike every other path in this unit (for example `engine/render/sprite_geometry.h` in the same comment).
findings.suggested_fix: Write it in the present tense: 'SpriteFrame has no member to hold it (engine/render/sprite_frame.h).'
findings.verify_reason: sprite_sheet_loader.cpp:71-73: 'arrive through a member that already existed, so the member is gone too (render/sprite_frame.h)'. That is history, and the path is not written from the root, while the same comment cites engine/render/sprite_geometry.h.

findings.title: A comment block in a public header is attached to no declaration
findings.why: It sits between add_sound_bank and the SOUND GROUPS block, separated from both by blank lines, so the website reference reader and a maintainer cannot tell which declaration it qualifies. Its last sentence repeats add_sound_bank's own contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Fold the first two sentences into add_sound_bank's comment (or the class comment) and delete the repeated last sentence.
findings.verify_reason: audio_resources.h:53-56 is a free-standing comment block, separated by blank lines from add_sound_bank above and from the SOUND GROUPS block below. Its last sentence restates the replacement rule that belongs to add_sound_bank.

findings.title: null backend cites an argument in recording.h that SM-46 removed, and still counts two backends
findings.why: SM-46 rewrote recording.h, and this pointer in its sibling .cpp now leads to text that is not there. The "two backends" wording predates engine/audio/webaudio/.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the "recording.h carries the argument" sentence, or state the rationale here. Change line 147-150 to "the same words every backend uses", as webaudio's comment does.
findings.verify_reason: Both texts exist, but at different lines from those cited. 'recording.h carries the argument for why that mattered enough to build' is at null/audio_device.cpp:18-19, and the 'two backends disagreeing' remark is at lines 65-67. recording.h:8-28 has no such argument, and webaudio:564 says 'the other two backends'. The defect is real, but it is in a non-published .cpp pointer, so low rather than medium.

findings.title: "in every build now" implies an earlier state
findings.why: "now" contrasts the code with a previous version. CONVENTIONS' tense test says that belongs in history, not a comment.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop "now": "every play below rejects an unresolved handle in every build".
findings.verify_reason: sound_bank.cpp:41-43 reads 'rejects an unresolved handle in every build now'. CONVENTIONS' Comments section (lines 160-170) says to test the tense: 'now' contrasts the code with a previous state.

findings.title: "four or five things an audio API actually does" understates the seam
findings.evidence:
"It calls audio_device.h for the four or five things an
// audio API actually does." SoundBank calls wave_index, play_wave, play_voice, stop_voice, pause_voice, resume_voice, set_voice_volume/pitch/pan, voice_state and is_voice_looping: eleven seam methods.
findings.why: The count misdescribes the seam's width to a reader deciding what a new backend must implement.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the count, for example 'for what an audio API actually does (audio_device.h)'.
findings.verify_reason: sound_bank.h:26-27 says 'the four or five things an audio API actually does'. SoundBank calls roughly eleven AudioDevice methods, including wave_index, play_wave, the play, stop, pause and resume voice verbs, volume, pitch, pan, voice_state and is_voice_looping.

findings.title: XAudio2 backend's file comment narrates what the code used to be
findings.why: CONVENTIONS' Comments section says history ("what it used to be") is never a comment. android.md §3.2 is now headed "BUILT, 2026-08-27", so the quoted "provably false today" describes a past state. The include-check name is also missing its `.cmake` extension, so the path cannot be checked.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep only the present-tense constraint: this is the only file that includes <Audio.h>, and cmake/check_engine_includes.cmake forbids backend includes from outside this folder. Drop the android.md narrative.
findings.verify_reason: xaudio2/audio_device.cpp:15-20 is quoted correctly. android.md:182 is headed '3.2 ... BUILT, 2026-08-27', so 'provably false today' is a narrative of a past state, and 'cmake/check_engine_includes' lacks .cmake. The comment's present-tense claims are still accurate: it is the only <Audio.h> includer, and the include wall exists. It is a private .cpp, so this is a low archaeology cleanup.

findings.title: "six lines from the library" line count is false
findings.evidence:
//    themselves from it. It is Impl's declaration order, six lines from the
//    library that requires it, rather than a paragraph in the shell's member
findings.why: `#include <Audio.h>` is at line 5 and Impl's ordered members are at lines 55-61, about fifty lines apart. This is the kind of fragile line-count claim SM-47 removed elsewhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Say "in Impl's declaration order, in this file" and drop the count.
findings.verify_reason: xaudio2/audio_device.cpp:33 says 'six lines from the library'. #include <Audio.h> is line 5, and the Impl members begin at about line 55-60.

findings.title: "The one place the container's spelling appears" is said in two places
findings.evidence: xaudio2:47 "// The one place the container's spelling appears." `return directory + name + ".xwb";`, repeated at webaudio/audio_device.cpp:502-507 "// The one place the container's spelling appears, as in xaudio2/." with the same body.
findings.why: The comment is false by its own count. Both backends depend on the same spelling, and nothing ties the two copies together.
findings.suggested_fix: Put the container path helper beside read_xwb_file in engine/audio/xwb_file.h (the format's owner) and call it from both backends.
findings.verify_reason: xaudio2/audio_device.cpp:47-52 and webaudio/audio_device.cpp:502-507 both define container_path returning directory+name+".xwb", each claiming to be 'the one place the container's spelling appears'.

findings.title: "The loops this replaces did neither" is history
findings.evidence:
"// From i + 1, so every pair is considered once and no object is
// tested against itself. The loops this replaces did neither."
findings.why: It describes code that no longer exists. git log answers that question; the first sentence is the whole rationale.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the second sentence.
findings.verify_reason: contacts.cpp:71-72 reads verbatim: 'The loops this replaces did neither.' It describes code that no longer exists.

findings.title: Benchmark figure is restated in contacts.h as well as broad_phase.h
findings.why: The same measured number lives in two published headers, so a re-measurement has to find both. CONVENTIONS prefers citing over re-deriving.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the numbers in broad_phase.h only, and in contacts.h say 'all-pairs, O(n^2); broad_phase.h gives the measured cost'.
findings.verify_reason: contacts.h:43-44, '106 ms for four thousand objects, six times a 60 Hz frame', restates broad_phase.h:19-21. The same measured figure is in two published headers.

findings.title: Engine comment refers to "this game's collision traffic"
findings.why: The engine has no game, and this is the only 'this game' in engine/ (git grep "this game" -- engine). It is a leftover from before the ColourWars split and asserts a workload the engine cannot know.
findings.suggested_fix: Write 'on rectangle pairs, the commonest pairing in tile-based content', or drop the clause.
findings.verify_reason: narrow_phase.cpp:42-44 says 'essentially all of this game's collision traffic'. git grep 'this game' in engine/ finds only this line, a leftover from before the split.

findings.title: Claims the Quad constructor allocates; Quad has fixed storage
findings.why: The allocation claim is false (Quad stores `Point2F points_[4]` and is_valid says "no allocation"). Only the double validation is real, so the stated reason for this code shape is half wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep only the true reason: building a Quad would validate convexity twice, through quad() and then the converting constructor, while the corners and axes are already valid. Remove 'allocates'.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed at narrow_phase.cpp:133-137: 'that constructor allocates and validates twice over'. Quad stores `Point2F points_[4]` (quad.h). Quad(const RectangleRotated&) in quad.cpp:43-52 calls rectangle.quad() and then is_valid(), so only the double validation is real. This is a wrong half-rationale in a private comment, so low.

findings.title: Early-out comment says "all seven" axes; quad against quad tests eight
findings.why: Polygon::max_points is 4 and a quad contributes four axes (fill_axes(polygon, 4)), so a quad-quad pair has eight candidate axes. A rectangle pair has four. 'Seven' matches only triangle against quad, so the number misleads anyone reasoning about worst-case cost.
findings.suggested_fix: Say "rather than every axis of both shapes" instead of quoting a count.
findings.verify_reason: narrow_phase.cpp around line 459-462 reads '...cost one projection pair rather than all seven.' Polygon::max_points is 4 (line 28), and fill_axes(polygon, 4) at line 128 gives a quad four axes, so quad against quad tests up to eight. 'Seven' fits only triangle against quad.

findings.title: Zero-normal fallback gives a reason that measurable() has already ruled out
findings.why: measurable() already returns early when a shape has no axes or no interior, and every non-separated axis test produces a unit normal of ±axis. The stated reason therefore cannot hold here. The only remaining way in is a penetration that is not below FLT_MAX. The same check at line 429 in circle_polygon has the same problem.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite both comments to state the real residual case (no axis produced a penetration below the sentinel), or remove the guard and assert that least was updated.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed at :474-478: measurable() (:296-299) already requires axis_count>0 and an interior. fill_axes skips zero-length edges (:63-65), and test_intervals sets the normal to ±axis for any overlap. So the comment's reason cannot occur, and the guard is defensive. But the circle_polygon check at :429 has no comment, so the claim that it has 'the same problem' is wrong. Low.

findings.title: Precondition bullet for min_axis_alignment is garbled
findings.evidence: "//   - `axis` is no more than min_axis_alignment away from being useless."
findings.why: The checked condition (resolve.cpp:51) is `std::abs(dot(normal, axis)) >= min_axis_alignment`. 'no more than X away from being useless' reads as the opposite of a lower bound on the cosine and does not say what is measured.
findings.suggested_fix: Write: '|dot(normal, axis)| is at least min_axis_alignment.'
findings.verify_reason: resolve.h:50: '`axis` is no more than min_axis_alignment away from being useless.' The check at resolve.cpp:48-49 is std::abs(dot(normal, axis)) < min_axis_alignment → throw. The bullet does not say what is measured.

findings.title: The comment credits the mixing constants to Mulberry and frames them as migration history
findings.why: As far as I know, Mulberry32 uses the 0x6D2B79F5 increment and an imul-based mixer. 0x21F0AAAD/0x735A2D97 look like the two-round 32-bit integer hash from Chris Wellons' hash-prospector, so the comment sends a reader who checks the provenance to the wrong source. 'Already used' and 'a game moving onto this' are migration history. LineSweeper has not moved onto it either: samples/linesweeper/rules/tick.cpp:51 and presentation/particles.cpp:473 still carry their own copies.
findings.suggested_fix: State the algorithm and its source in present tense, e.g. "Weyl increment 0x9E3779B9, then the hash-prospector two-round 32-bit mixer. These are the same draws as LineSweeper's rules-side generator." Drop the migration framing.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed. random.cpp:12-14 credits 'Mulberry's mixing constants', but the code is a 0x9E3779B9 Weyl increment followed by the 16/0x21F0AAAD/15/0x735A2D97/15 two-round mixer. That mixer is from Wellons' hash-prospector. Mulberry32 uses 0x6D2B79F5 and an imul/|1/|61 mixer. The comment's 'already used' and 'a game moving onto this' are migration framing. LineSweeper keeps its own copies at rules/tick.cpp:51 and presentation/particles.cpp:473, and rules cannot link the engine anyway. The provenance is wrong but the behaviour is unaffected, so low.

findings.title: State::update points at a rationale in GameObject::update that the SM-45 audit removed
findings.why: The reader is sent to a declaration that no longer gives any reason. The citation checker cannot catch this because the pointer is prose, not a document path.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite only the source that still holds the reason: "Frame time is a parameter, not shared state (docs/design/PHILOSOPHY.md, Services and lifetimes)."
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed. state.h:17-19 still says 'for the reason GameObject::update gives', but game_object.h:23-25 now reads only 'Steps the object by dt seconds, once per tick on one thread. Changes to object state belong here rather than in draw().' The comment also cites PHILOSOPHY Services and lifetimes, so the reader still reaches a real rationale. This is a stale pointer, low severity.

findings.title: The public State header uses 'frame' for a stack entry, a term defined only in StateContext's private section
findings.why: In a header whose neighbouring comments talk about drawing frames, 'every frame is told' reads as 'every rendered frame'. The meaning intended is every state on the stack, and StateContext::Frame is private. state_context.h:52, 61 and 66 do the same in public comments ('which frame is being replaced', 'after this frame is popped').
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'every state on the stack is told' and 'the state that most needs to hear this'. In state_context.h's public comments, prefer 'stack entry' or 'pushed state' over 'frame'.
findings.verify_reason: state.h:88-91 says 'EVERY FRAME IS TOLD' and 'the frame that most needs to hear this', meaning stack entries. The type for those is the private StateContext::Frame (state_context.h:126-147). The public comments at state_context.h:52, 61 and 66 use 'frame' the same way. It is a wording ambiguity in a header that also talks about drawing frames. Minor.

findings.title: ~StateContext comment narrates the former defaulted destructor and the bug it had
findings.why: CONVENTIONS and AGENTS say comments state current contract or rationale, not history. SM-45 cleaned the header and SM-47 cleaned scene.cpp, but this implementation comment still tells the story of the previous code.
findings.suggested_fix: Reduce it to the present-tense reason: the destructor calls clear() so that states are destroyed top-down, in dependency order, for every owner. Application also calls clear() earlier, before its own members are destroyed.
findings.verify_reason: state_context.cpp:32-39 narrates 'Defaulted, this let the vector destroy...' and what 'had no such line' - archaeology that CONVENTIONS.md#comments says 'is never a comment'. SM-47's target list (code-hygiene.md:150) did not include state_context.cpp, and SM-45 reviewed only the header, so it is not tracked.

findings.title: TouchState::cancelled defers to a reason Mouse::cancel_buttons does not give
findings.why: The cross-reference points at text that was trimmed. The rationale now exists only here, and it is attributed to the wrong place. (This is distinct from the known mouse/touch→keyboard.h deferral.)
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the attribution and keep the sentence's own reason, or point to wherever the cancel rationale now lives.
findings.verify_reason: touch.h:73-76 attributes its rationale to Mouse::cancel_buttons. mouse.h:152-154 gives no reason, only 'Clears buttons at the next poll without synthesizing normal release edges.' This is distinct from the tracked mouse/touch deferral to keyboard.h.

findings.title: Former-code narratives in math .cpp files not covered by SM-47
findings.evidence:
intersects.cpp:141 "already ported and already correct, and it had no callers anywhere
		// in the tree."; intersects.cpp:303 "That pair missed a segment entering at one vertex"; intersects.cpp:436 "It also did not fix the hole it sat in front of"; ericson_math.cpp:264 "is still added after the two axis tests have been decided, exactly as before."; ericson_math.cpp:368 "The disagreement was not academic. A default-constructed Triangle ..."; triangle.cpp:155 "Both accessors below used the vertex index as an edge index directly"; quad.cpp:95-96 "against six segment tests over a heap-allocated vector of edges."
findings.why: SM-47 cleaned this pattern out of rectangle_rotated.cpp only. These comments narrate removed code or past bugs, and AGENTS says to keep history out of the code. Some are already false, for example test_circle_circle now has a caller.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite each as a present-tense statement of the rule and its reason, for example 'closed clip so a vertex-to-vertex traversal is caught'. Drop the history; the commit log keeps it.
findings.verify_reason: Verified intersects.cpp:141-143 ('had no callers anywhere', now false because circles_intersect calls it), 303-304 and 436. Also verified ericson_math.cpp:263-264 ('exactly as before') and 368, triangle.cpp:155-159, and quad.cpp:95-96. SM-47's targets list only engine/math/rectangle_rotated.cpp among the math files, so these are not tracked.

findings.title: Comment's justification for translation() describes Vector2F::angle wrongly
findings.why: Vector2F::angle has no factory form. Its two overloads, `float angle() const` and `static float angle(const Vector2F& vec)` (vector2f.h:60-61), both read an angle. The factory is unit_vec_from_angle. The precedent the comment cites for overloading a factory and a reader under one name does not exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the Vector2F::angle sentence, or cite a real factory/reader pair.
findings.verify_reason: matrix3x2f.h:65 has the static translation(offset) factory and :116 the reader, and the comment at 112-115 cites Vector2F::angle() as the same factory/reader pairing. vector2f.h:60-61 shows angle() const and static angle(vec), and both read an angle; the factory is unit_vec_from_angle (matrix3x2f.h:73 says so itself). So the cited precedent is false, but it is a side remark in a comment: low.

findings.title: References to "scalar.h's ordering" of tolerances that scalar.h no longer presents as an ordering
findings.why: scalar.h:19-29 is a list of "Related thresholds [that] serve different purposes", not an ordering. It includes min_axis_alignment, which it says bounds a direction and "is not a rounding tolerance". So "every tolerance ... bounds a LENGTH" is false against the list it cites.
findings.suggested_fix: Refer to scalar.h's list of related thresholds, and say the default and segment tolerances are absolute lengths, without claiming every listed threshold is one.
findings.verify_reason: matrix3x2f.h:132-133 says 'Every tolerance in scalar.h's ordering bounds a LENGTH', and ericson_math.h:74-75 refers to 'where segment_parallel_epsilon sits in the ordering'. scalar.h:19-29 is a list of 'Related thresholds [that] serve different purposes', and it includes min_axis_alignment, which 'bounds the permitted separation direction; it is not a rounding tolerance'. So both cross-references are stale. Low.

findings.title: The comment refers to an angles() function that does not exist
findings.evidence:
// The INTERIOR angle at each vertex - the one a reader means by "the
	// angles of a triangle", and the one that makes angles() sum to pi.  -- `git grep -n -E '\bangles\(\)' -- engine tests` finds only this comment and a test comment; Triangle declares angle_0/1/2 only.
findings.why: A reader looking for angles() will not find it. The invariant is about the three angle_N() values.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'makes angle_0() + angle_1() + angle_2() sum to pi'.
findings.verify_reason: triangle.cpp:83 and 88 refer to angles(). git grep finds no angles() declaration, only those comments and tests/math/triangle_tests.cpp:19. Triangle has only angle_0/1/2.

findings.title: edge_opposite_vertex comment narrates a fixed bug
findings.why: This is past-tense bug narration in the code. Lines 150-153 already give the present-tense rationale (vertex index vs edge index). triangle.h:62-65 has the same kind of comment about a removed redeclaration: "A byte-for-byte copy would hide the public one".
findings.suggested_fix: Delete lines 155-159. Reduce triangle.h:62-65 to nothing, or to a contract statement.
findings.verify_reason: triangle.cpp:155-159 narrates the bug ('Both accessors below used the vertex index as an edge index... they returned...'), and lines 150-153 already give the present rationale. Real archaeology. triangle.h:62-65 explains why the base helper is not redeclared, which is rationale for an absence and is weaker evidence. A comment-only fix: low.

findings.title: Vector2F constructor comment says "explicit, all of them" above a non-explicit constructor, and argues from Quad
findings.why: The two-float constructor is not explicit, and the brace-initialised constants in vector2f.cpp rely on that. The comment also reasons about Quad's constructors, which belong in quad.h. A reader of Vector2F gets a false "all of them" and a rationale for a different type.
findings.suggested_fix: Say "every single-argument (converting) constructor is explicit" and move the Quad sentence to quad.h:23-24.
findings.verify_reason: vector2f.h:17 says 'explicit, all of them', but line 28 'constexpr Vector2F(float x, float y)' is not explicit. Lines 18-23 argue from Quad's constructors and their throws, which belongs to another type. Low.

findings.title: refresh_style comment says widgets are painted back to 'one of two colours', but FocusStyle has three
findings.why: The comment predates the disabled state and now misdescribes the repaint this published header documents.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'back to the style's focused, unfocused or disabled colour'.
findings.verify_reason: focus.h:155-158 says 'paints all of them back to one of two colours'; FocusStyle has focused/unfocused/disabled and focus.cpp:167-179 paints disabled rows with style_.disabled. Stale.

findings.title: The edges-not-centres rationale is written out twice, in navigation.h and navigation.cpp
findings.evidence:
navigation.h:39-43: "Edges and not centres, and that is the whole of why: a left-aligned column ... a centre test makes \"right\" from \"Standard\" find \"Team Deathmatch\" one row down. By edges, nothing in that column clears..."
navigation.cpp:33-38: "Edges, not centres. A left-aligned column of labels ... a centre-based test makes \"right\" from \"Standard\" find \"Team Deathmatch\" one row down. By edges, every row in that column starts..."
findings.why: The same paragraph in two places will drift. The header, which is published, is the owner of the rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut the .cpp copy to one line pointing at rule 1 in navigation.h.
findings.verify_reason: navigation.h:39-43 and navigation.cpp:33-38 re-derive the same edges-not-centres 'Standard'/'Team Deathmatch' rationale; CONVENTIONS#comments says rationale is cited rather than re-derived.

findings.title: UiContainer::draw and cull_bounds comments describe earlier behaviour and an earlier API
findings.why: Both comments narrate removed code: a container that ignored hidden(), and a 'predicate form' of bounds that no longer exists. That forces readers to reconstruct history to understand the current rule.
