findings.suggested_fix: State the current rule only: a hidden container draws nothing, and bounds are the union of children with positive area.
findings.verify_reason: widget.cpp draw comment ('this one did not, so set_hidden(true) on a container did nothing') and cull_bounds comment ('the predicate form could only approximate') both narrate prior code, per CONVENTIONS archaeology rule. widget.cpp was not an SM-47 target.

themes.name: Render comment truth and archaeology (shared seam and five backends)
themes.desc: Render-side comments that tell history or carry false censuses. Examples: 'both samples', the '41 of 43 .dds' and line-count tallies, 'CI skips RenderPixelTests' for Vulkan and GL, a texture-format rationale written before PNG support, add_texture_asset's 'only engine callers', frame_open() which no longer exists, sprite.hlsl's self-history, and D3D12 and Vulkan fix narratives.
themes.story: A comments-only batch over engine/render (an SM-46/SM-47 continuation). Replace censuses and line counts with statements that do not decay, or delete them. Correct the CI and seam claims against ci.yml and SEAM.md. Remove history and the commented-out function. Keep the D3D12/Vulkan synchronisation contracts intact and re-read them against the Vulkan review. Run all five native Debug builds to confirm no tokens changed.

findings.title: RenderResources::Impl class comment says fonts and sheets live here; the class body says they do not
findings.why: The class has exactly one member table, `textures`, and engine/render/render_resources.h:35-37 says the font and sheet tables are members of RenderResources. Lines 48-57 describe an earlier three-table layout. Line 64 contradicts them and adds archaeology ('now'). A reader of the backend's central header gets a false picture of where resources are stored.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace lines 48-57 and 63-64 with one present-tense statement: Impl holds only the texture table, keyed by D3D11 views; fonts and sheets are RenderResources' own members (render_resources.h). The null backend's equivalent comment at null/backend.h:54-56 has the right shape.
findings.verify_reason: Re-read d3d11/backend.h:48-71. Lines 52-57 say 'ONE OF THE THREE TABLES IS THIS BACKEND'S AND TWO ARE NOT. Fonts and sheets ... are here', but line 69 says 'so are their tables now - this holds one table, not three', and the class has only `textures`. null/backend.h:54-56 has the correct one-table wording. The contradiction is real. It sits in a backend-private header with no published reference page, and the header contradicts itself within 15 lines, so a careful reader is not actually misled. Medium, not high.

findings.title: Comment narrates what its own earlier sentence said
findings.why: CONVENTIONS' Never list says outright: "a comment narrating what the code used to be", and a sentence narrating what this comment used to say "has lost the thread twice". The tree-wide census ("the only NEGATIVE low-tier sentence") is also unverifiable.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep one present-tense rationale: feature level 11_0 is D3D12's minimum, so this backend excludes pre-D3D12 hardware that the D3D11 and GL backends still reach. The named low tier is 12_2. Drop the rest.
findings.verify_reason: device_resources.cpp:30-42 contains 'NOT A TARGET ON THE LOW TIER IS NO LONGER THE RIGHT SENTENCE, which is what naming the low tier cost this comment' and 'the only NEGATIVE low-tier sentence in the tree'. CONVENTIONS.md:161-169 explicitly forbids archaeology, including 'a sentence narrating what this very comment used to say'. Not tracked in docs/code-hygiene.md.

findings.title: WARP comment says CI skips GL RenderPixelTests and D3D12 is only the second CI-checked backend
findings.why: CI now runs GL RenderPixelTests on Mesa llvmpipe and Vulkan on SwiftShader (AGENTS.md says the same), so both halves of the claim are false. A reader would wrongly conclude that CI never checks GL pixels.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut it to the current rationale: debug builds fall back to WARP so a GPU-less machine can still run the D3D12 pixel contract. Drop the GL narrative and the backend ordinal.
findings.verify_reason: device_resources.cpp:231-239 does say ci.yml skips GL RenderPixelTests and that D3D12 is 'the second backend whose pixel contract CI can actually check'. AGENTS.md says CI draws GL on llvmpipe and Vulkan on SwiftShader, so the comment is false. It is a stale rationale comment inside a release-only #else block, not a behaviour defect, so medium rather than high.

findings.title: wait_for_gpu comment contradicts the resize comment about E_OUTOFMEMORY
findings.why: The two comments make opposite claims about the same function. The code's fallback to E_FAIL actually handles the non-removal case, so the first sentence of the wait_for_gpu comment is false.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite it as: "A failed wait is reported as the device-removed reason when the device has gone, else as E_FAIL; Signal/SetEventOnCompletion failures on a live device lose their own HRESULT here." Alternatively, keep the failing HRESULT and throw that.
findings.verify_reason: Lines 589-590 say 'The only way the wait above fails is a device that has gone'. Lines 335-339 say an E_OUTOFMEMORY from Signal/SetEventOnCompletion is a live device. The contradiction is real. The next sentence at 591-592 already covers the E_FAIL case and the code handles it correctly, so this is an inaccurate comment, not high.

findings.title: Resize comment argues against frame_open(), a function that no longer exists
findings.why: The comment describes the behaviour of removed code in the present tense, so a reader goes looking for frame_open(). That is the archaeology CONVENTIONS says to remove.
findings.suggested_fix: State the current rule only. Restart is keyed on Impl::frame_begun, the begin_frame..end_frame interval renderer.h names, because 'a list is recording' is false between begin_frame and the first set_view_count.
findings.verify_reason: d3d12/renderer.cpp:997-1001 discusses frame_open() in the present tense. git grep finds frame_open only there and in historical review docs (docs/review/d3d12), so the function is gone. Not tracked in code-hygiene.md.

findings.title: Hard-coded line counts and the cross-reference to renderer.h are false
findings.why: Current counts are vulkan 399, d3d12 346, gl 229, d3d11 116 and null 49. Three of the five numbers are wrong. Grepping renderer.h (and engine/, docs/design and website/src) for these counts or for a list of texture-factory sizes finds nothing, so 'renderer.h lists in one place and holds all five against' points at text that does not exist. Line counts in comments go stale on every edit.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the numbers and the renderer.h claim. Keep only the reason: no initial-data parameter, so the backend stages, copies and waits itself.
findings.verify_reason: Lines 94-98 quote 382, 342, 168, 116 and 49 lines. wc -l now gives vulkan 399, d3d12 346, gl 229, d3d11 116 and null 49. renderer.h contains no texture_factory size list: a grep for 382, 342 and 'longest' finds nothing there, and nothing in tests mentions one either. So the cross-reference points at text that does not exist.

findings.title: DDS census in comments is false against the current trees
findings.evidence: "Forty-one of the forty-three .dds between this repository and its client are block compressed" (l.132-134) and "it reaches only the two .dds in either client that are not block compressed" (l.50-51). `git ls-files '*.dds'` here lists samples/components/content/textures/animation_preview.dds, panel.dds, samples/linesweeper/content/textures/white.dds and tests/render/content/quad.dds, all with a zero fourCC at byte 84 (uncompressed); ColourWars alone tracks 46 .dds.
findings.why: Two fragile counts that drifted: this repo alone now has three uncompressed sample textures, so 'only the two' and '41 of 43' are both wrong, and they span a separate repository nobody updates this comment against.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the counts; state the rationale qualitatively (font atlases and most art are block compressed, so refusing would leave a no-S3TC context without text) and that the BGRA swap is a load-path cost only.
findings.verify_reason: texture_factory.cpp l.50-51 and l.132-134 carry the quoted counts. Reading byte 84 of every tracked .dds shows a zero fourCC, meaning uncompressed, for animation_preview, panel, linesweeper white and tests quad. findings.title: add_texture_asset's contract says only two engine callers exist and that a client never sees it; both claims are false
findings.evidence:
line 87: "// Every caller is one of the two above, and both of them are engine code -
// so a client never sees this and a backend never sees a file."  line 14: "// TWO OF THESE ARE THE ENGINE'S AND ONE IS THE BACKEND'S". Searched the repo for `add_texture_asset(`. Engine callers: load_texture_asset, add_white_texture and load_font_asset (resource_factory.cpp:92,99,109,128). Non-engine callers: about 40 test, sample and bench sites, e.g. tests/render/renderer_seam_tests.cpp:80, samples/components/animation_preview_null_tests.cpp:41, bench/fanout_bench_null.cpp:128. website/src/content/docs/docs/guides/testing.mdx:339 tells clients to call it. The header declares four functions, not three.
findings.why: Public header prose is published word for word on the website. This contract tells readers that a function is internal when the site's own testing guide teaches clients to call it. The 'two of these / one' census is also stale since add_white_texture was added.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite the class-level paragraph so it names three engine-side functions and one backend function. Change line 87 to say the engine's loaders call it, and that tests and tools may call it directly to install decoded TextureData. Update the website page in the same commit.
findings.verify_reason: resource_factory.h:14 says 'TWO OF THESE ARE THE ENGINE'S AND ONE IS THE BACKEND'S' and :87 says 'Every caller is one of the two above ... a client never sees this'. git grep add_texture_asset( finds engine callers at resource_factory.cpp:92,99,109,128 (texture/png, dds, white, font), and outside callers in bench/fanout_bench_null.cpp:128, samples/components/animation_preview_null_tests.cpp:41, tests/linesweeper/*, tests/assets/string_table_text_tests.cpp:165 and tests/render/d3d12/*. website testing.mdx:339 calls it. So the claim is false. Still, it is a prose inaccuracy in a comment and does not change behaviour, so medium, not high.

findings.title: sprite.hlsl explains what earlier versions of itself said and where it used to live
findings.why: CONVENTIONS lists exactly this in its Never section: 'a comment narrating what the code used to be', and 'a sentence narrating what this very comment used to say has lost the thread twice'. This file is outside SM-47's targets, so the case is not tracked.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the facts in the present tense: the D3D11 floor is 10.0, the shader is shared by three HLSL backends, and two multiply-adds replace a 4x4 matrix. Delete the 'used to', 'still did not move' and SpriteBatch clauses.
findings.verify_reason: sprite.hlsl:3-4 says 'WHICH IS WHERE IT USED TO LIVE', :15 says 'the source still did not move', :57-58 says 'AND THIS LINE USED TO SAY IT WAS', and :68 says 'A matrix is what SpriteBatch used'. findings.title: Worked example contradicts itself: claims x=10.9 gives 7, then says x=10.9 demonstrates nothing
findings.why: The comment backs a pixel-contract rule (edges first, then the difference) with an example that is false, and then admits it in a parenthetical. Width 8 at x=10.9 truncates to 8 either way. The comment also carries history ('the rectangle went through a RECT of four truncated longs'). A maintainer cannot tell which sentence to trust.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace it with a correct example, such as x=10.6 width=7.6: edges give 18-10=8 but trunc(width)=7. Alternatively, cite viewport.h's 721-row split, which is correct. Drop the RECT history and the parenthetical.
findings.verify_reason: sprite_geometry.cpp:158-167 says 'at x=10.9 the first gives 18 - 10 = 8 and rounding the size first would give 7', then ends with '(Pick the worked example with care: x=10.9 is answered 8 by both orders and demonstrates nothing.)'. With width 8, trunc(width) is 8, so the comment contradicts itself and neither example shows the two orders disagreeing. It also carries the 'RECT of four truncated longs' history, which CONVENTIONS' comments section treats as archaeology.

findings.title: TextureData says the engine loads only two things, which leaves out PNG
findings.why: This comment is false against the current loader and is part of the published renderer-writer reference. It gives the wrong count for the very point it makes: one creation function for every file kind.
findings.suggested_fix: Say: "Every texture source this engine reads - a .dds, a .png and the atlas inside a .spritefont - comes out as one of these."
findings.verify_reason: texture_data.h:37-39 reads 'Both of the two things this engine loads - a .dds and the atlas inside a .spritefont'. read_png_file returns TextureData, and resource_factory.cpp:92 loads it, so PNG is missing from the list.

findings.title: TextureFormat rationale was written before PNG support and is now false
findings.why: The engine now loads three file kinds, and a third reader (read_png_file/decode_png), plus block_decode, produces TextureFormat. Every PNG texture arrives as r8g8b8a8_unorm, so the claim that no file says it is false. This published header describes a format set that no longer exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Name PNG as a third source that states no DXGI number. Count the producers correctly (the .dds, .spritefont and .png readers, plus the block decoder). Say that r8g8b8a8_unorm is what every PNG and every decoded block texture becomes.
findings.verify_reason: texture_format.h:8-27 says 'Both file kinds this engine loads ... both say it as a DXGI number' and 'bc1_unorm and r8g8b8a8_unorm are here because they complete a switch ... rather than because a file says them'. png_file.cpp:62 (not :131) sets TextureFormat::r8g8b8a8_unorm, block_decode.cpp:200 produces it too, and resource_factory.cpp:78-92 loads .png. The comment is stale. It is prose only, so medium.

findings.title: Header says the Vulkan preset skips RenderPixelTests in CI, but CI draws them on SwiftShader
findings.evidence: "no in-box software\n// rasteriser the way Direct3D has WARP, so this preset skips RenderPixelTests\n// in CI exactly as the OpenGL one does." -- but .github/workflows/ci.yml:281 "THE VULKAN PRESET DRAWS ON SWIFTSHADER, WHICH THE RUNNER ALREADY HAS" and ci.yml:332-333 "- preset: x64-debug-vulkan / software_device: SwiftShader"; device_resources.cpp:558-559 itself says ".github/workflows/ci.yml points the loader at the SwiftShader Chrome carries".
findings.why: This is the backend's top-level rationale header. It states a false verification fact that contradicts CI, AGENTS.md ("its Vulkan job on Chrome's SwiftShader, and fails if RenderPixelTests names another device") and a comment in the same folder. A reader could conclude that Vulkan pixel regressions are not caught in CI.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the sentence: CI runs RenderPixelTests on Chrome's SwiftShader ICD, which is a software device and not a real driver, and ci_gap_report.py covers the real-driver run.
findings.verify_reason: backend.h:32-35 does say the preset 'skips RenderPixelTests in CI exactly as the OpenGL one does'. ci.yml:281-290 and the matrix entries at 329/333 contradict it: GL draws on llvmpipe, Vulkan on SwiftShader, and both are checked by name. The comment is stale. Its claim about GL is wrong too. It is still only a comment, so medium rather than high. Note that ci.yml:274 also still says 'GL and Vulkan do not' get a device.

findings.title: create_swapchain and create_window_size_dependent_resources narrate a past bug
findings.why: Both passages describe what the code used to do ("did not come across", "was not", "threw", "did not have") instead of the current contract, which CONVENTIONS bans.
findings.suggested_fix: State the current rule: a device loss from vkCreateSwapchainKHR, when a swapchain existed, answers false and recovers rather than throwing, because this path runs inside a window procedure. Delete the history clauses at 1196-1203 and 1409-1410.
findings.verify_reason: device_resources.cpp:1194-1203 says 'the half that did not come across from ... Here the wait was answered and this was not, so a TDR ... threw out of a window procedure'. Lines 1409-1410 say 'the one this file did not have'. Both are past-tense narration that CONVENTIONS bans.

findings.title: execute() comment narrates a lost line from the D3D12 transliteration
findings.why: The rationale (advancing the counter before a failed submit leaves waits hanging on a value nothing will signal) is present-tense and worth keeping. The story of what the transliteration lost is archaeology that belongs to git log.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut it to: the counter advances only after a successful submit, because a non-loss submit failure would otherwise leave timeline_value_ naming a value nothing signals, and wait_for_gpu would hang.
findings.verify_reason: device_resources.cpp:1529-1539 says 'which is the one line the transliteration from engine/render/d3d12/device_resources.cpp lost' and goes on to narrate that file. This is archaeology mixed with a valid present-tense rationale.

findings.title: Acquire-barrier comment narrates the old code and carries a stale barrier count
findings.why: "This was TOP_OF_PIPE" is archaeology. The 'five other' census is already wrong, and 'exactly one' is false because transition_colour can emit TOP_OF_PIPE. The real rationale (the barrier's source stage must equal the semaphore wait stage) is buried in it.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep only the present-tense rule: the source stage must be the acquire semaphore's wait stage, because a TOP_OF_PIPE source is not ordered after the presentation engine's read. Delete the history and the count.
findings.verify_reason: device_resources.cpp:1786-1799 says 'This was TOP_OF_PIPE, which exactly one of the five other hand-written barriers in this folder still says'. grep finds 7 vkCmdPipelineBarrier sites (dr.cpp 1802/1863/1987, renderer.cpp 602/1329, texture_factory.cpp 309/323), so there are six others. stage_of() returns TOP_OF_PIPE at line 74 for the transition_colour barrier, so 'exactly one' is also wrong.

findings.title: block_compression comment repeats the stale 41-of-43 .dds census and miscites texture_format.h
findings.why: The count is ColourWars-era and false here, and the cited document does not support it.

findings.title: Archaeology plus a false claim about a using-declaration
findings.why: "Counting them as one line was a claim texture_factory.cpp then cited" narrates what an earlier comment said, which CONVENTIONS' Never section bans. The using-declaration does not exist, and "fourteen-line" is a line census of another file.

findings.title: User-facing throw cites a stale '41 of the 43 .dds' content census
findings.evidence:
"compressed and this Vulkan device has no "
"textureCompressionBC. Desktop drivers all provide it; most "

findings.title: set_from_hex comment narrates former std::stoi implementation
findings.why: This describes code that no longer exists rather than the current rule: the digits are validated before any are read, so a malformed string becomes opaque black without throwing.

findings.title: Include-wall comment refers to 'how the wall was climbed last time', and line 274 refers to the replaced CommonStates

Line 274-275 ('This replaced DirectX::CommonStates, which offered twenty-odd and was asked for four') is the same kind of history.

findings.title: `bound` field comment tells the story of a past leak, and renderer.cpp repeats it
findings.why: The incident narrative and its numbers (sixteen views, 1,800 commands a second) describe an earlier begin_frame. The invariant is that a bound context must be finished or discarded, and set_view_count binds. renderer.cpp:855-863 tells the same history again ('that is the fix rather than an optimisation ... stranded two commands per idle view per frame'), so the backend carries two copies of it.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the invariant (a bound deferred context accumulates commands until finished, so only set_view_count binds and submit finishes every bound view) and delete the incident narrative from both places.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed at backend.h:164-175 ('exactly what happened while begin_frame bound all sixteen ... 1,800 stranded commands a second'). It is repeated at renderer.cpp:855-863 ('that is the fix rather than an optimisation ... stranded two commands per idle view per frame, permanently'). Both copies also keep the invariant, so the defect is narrative and duplication in comments, not a misleading contract. Low.

findings.title: UpdateColorSpace comment talks about a removed c_EnableHDR flag, and its same-size caller is unreachable
findings.why: c_EnableHDR no longer exists, so the first part is archaeology. The second part admits that the same-size UpdateColorSpace branch in WindowSizeChanged (lines 340-345) is unreachable, because Renderer::window_size_changed (renderer.cpp:757-762) makes the same comparison before calling. UpdateColorSpace is also public (device_resources.h:77), but `git grep UpdateColorSpace` finds only callers inside device_resources.cpp.
findings.suggested_fix: State only the current behaviour (sRGB always, refresh a stale factory). Move UpdateColorSpace to private. Either remove the unreachable same-size branch or stop describing it.
findings.verify_reason: device_resources.cpp:526-537 mentions the removed c_EnableHDR, which is archaeology. git grep UpdateColorSpace finds callers only inside device_resources.cpp (304, 342, 421), so making it public is unnecessary. The unreachable same-size branch is already-tracked: docs/review/d3d12/STATUS.md item 5 records 'Bypassed branch confirmed ... The current comment describes these paths'. Only the c_EnableHDR wording and the public visibility are new. Low.

findings.title: Accessor block comment is a census of what was removed
findings.why: A count of removed accessors is archaeology and is exactly the kind of method census SM-46 removed elsewhere. The no-depth-buffer point there is cited by sprite.hlsl:61 and sprite_vertex.h:24, so it is a rationale worth keeping, but it should be in the present tense.

The TRIMMED block at 30-50 is written in the past tense ('Three capabilities came from the upstream sample ... are gone'). The finding is real. The comments are accurate, though, and the rationale is useful, so low.

findings.title: RenderResources section comment tells the history of its own past restatements

findings.title: Unwrapped reflow lines in comments (also at 432, backend.h:213 and null/texture_factory.cpp:35)

findings.title: FinishCommandList comment cites ColourWars' former Level/MenuPage code
findings.why: Level and MenuPage are game classes from before the split. They exist nowhere in this repo; grep of engine/ and samples/ finds no such types. The sentence is archaeology a reader cannot follow up. The rationale for FALSE is already in the first three lines.

findings.title: Sampler and rasterizer comments are framed against removed DirectXTK CommonStates and SpriteBatch
findings.why: The "state cache" and SpriteBatch no longer exist in the tree. Both comments justify the current code against what it replaced, so a reader needs the history to follow the rationale. Round 1 flagged only backend.h:274 for CommonStates.
findings.suggested_fix: State the present rationale without the comparison, for example "Remade with the device in create_device_dependent_resources; nothing outside Impl holds one" and "No culling: a sprite quad's winding never changes, because a flip mirrors texcoords only."
findings.verify_reason: Line 416 says 'Held rather than demanded from a state cache', and line 505 says 'NO CULLING, WHERE SpriteBatch CULLED BACK FACES'. Both compare the code with DirectXTK code it replaced, and neither DirectXTK class is used in the engine any more. Round 1 covered only backend.h:274. The same SpriteBatch sentence also appears in d3d12/sprite_pipeline.cpp:156 and vulkan/renderer.cpp:416.

findings.title: 'both samples' is stale; there are six samples (same text in the d3d12, gl and vulkan blend comments)
findings.why: AGENTS.md lists six samples. The count comes from an earlier tree and is copied in d3d12/sprite_pipeline.cpp:135, gl/renderer.cpp:399 and vulkan/renderer.cpp:437. renderer.cpp:61 has a similar stale framing ('A second backend writes its own') when five backends exist.

findings.title: submit() comment tells the history of the protocol that was once hand-written in four places
findings.why: This is past-tense history of client code that has since moved out. Only the next sentence, about view order, is a contract.

findings.verify_reason: d3d11/renderer.cpp:975-978 reads 'the protocol that was hand-written in four places, each of which had to pre-size a vector...'. This is past-tense archaeology, and the following view-order sentence is the contract.

findings.title: The marker-guard comment tells the story of a past crash
findings.why: AGENTS.md and CONVENTIONS say comments state contract or rationale, not history. This comment narrates a bug that has been fixed rather than stating why the guard exists. It is a separate location from the round-1 history findings.
findings.suggested_fix: Reduce it to the rationale: the annotation object exists only with a device, and renderer.h makes markers legal before create_device, so these return early without a device.

findings.title: Device-null guard comment describes a past access violation
findings.why: The rationale (ThrowIfFailed cannot catch a null-device dereference) is useful, but it is told as a past incident ('was an access violation'). The same pattern is in renderer.cpp:1071-1077 ('a marker before create_device dereferenced a null ComPtr here').
findings.suggested_fix: State it in the present tense: 'GetD3DDevice() is null before create_device, and the calls below would dereference it before ThrowIfFailed could see an HRESULT.' Make the same change to the marker comment.
findings.verify_reason: texture_factory.cpp:73-80 says 'a load before the device existed was an access violation'. renderer.cpp:1071-1077 says 'a marker before create_device dereferenced a null ComPtr here'. Both are past-tense incident framing of a present-tense rationale.

findings.title: Destructor comment carries commit history and a destructor census
findings.why: "From the same commit" and "arrived with the fifth backend" are history, and the four-destructor count is a census nothing checks. The useful content is one sentence: wait for the GPU before releasing objects it may still be reading.
findings.suggested_fix: Reduce it to the contract: release must wait for queued work, the wait is non-throwing because the destructor is noexcept (T6), and ~Renderer::Impl does the same for the lists and pages it owns.
findings.verify_reason: ~DeviceResources at 62-73 does contain 'from the same commit' and 'arrived with the fifth backend', plus a four-destructor census. Both are real archaeology under CONVENTIONS. The surrounding rationale is accurate, so the harm is low.

findings.title: Resize-wait comment is written as a history of earlier bugs
findings.why: Past-tense narration of earlier defects and earlier wording is archaeology under CONVENTIONS. The present-tense rule (recover only when GetDeviceRemovedReason fails, otherwise throw) is buried in it.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite in the present tense: the wait must not throw, so device removal can reach handle_device_lost; a failed wait on a live device throws, because continuing would release a buffer in use. Drop the past-tense clauses at the other two sites.
findings.verify_reason: device_resources.cpp:330-346 narrates 'a throw here skipped handle_device_lost' and 'Recovering there ran handle_device_lost against exactly that'. renderer.cpp:989-990 has 'which is what this did before the rule was written down'. texture_factory.cpp:110-111 has 'which the sentence here has now had wrong in both directions'. All are past-tense archaeology.

findings.title: Says pixel_tests.cpp calls end_frame exactly once; it calls it three times
findings.why: This census of test code is false since the pixel-test reorganisation (SM-49), and nothing checks it.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the test census. Keep "flip-model presents discard the presented buffer, so read-back must precede end_frame".
findings.verify_reason: device_resources.cpp:395-398 claims pixel_tests.cpp calls end_frame 'exactly once'. grep shows three calls: 166 (in the set_vsync case's present lambda), 482 and 541. The claim is false. It is a stale cross-file census in a comment, so low.

findings.title: Slot-reuse rationale narrates history and repeats rationale held in three other places
findings.why: "Is now written there" and "Without it a re-load took a fresh slot" describe how the code got here. The same slot-lifetime rationale also appears in backend.h:207-210, texture_factory.cpp:311-320 and render_resources.h:97-109, so the four copies can drift apart.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the contract at backend.h (texture_capacity / descriptor_slot) and the seam's precondition in render_resources.h. Cut this block and texture_factory.cpp's paragraph to one-line citations of those.
findings.verify_reason: render_resources.cpp:70-85 has 'IS NOW WRITTEN THERE' and 'Without it a re-load took a fresh slot', which is archaeology. backend.h:207-210 and texture_factory.cpp:309-320 restate the slot-reuse rule. The duplication is real but the copies agree today, so low.

findings.title: Allocator-reset comment calls the resize wait a full wait_for_gpu; it is the non-throwing try_wait_for_gpu
findings.why: create_window_size_dependent_resources calls `this->try_wait_for_gpu()` (device_resources.cpp:348). That function returns false instead of throwing, and the resize then branches to handle_device_lost or ThrowIfFailed(E_FAIL). A reader checking the allocator-reset precondition follows the name to the throwing function and misses the branch where the wait did not complete.
findings.suggested_fix: Name try_wait_for_gpu and say that a failed wait never reaches open_frame: it either recovers through handle_device_lost or throws.
findings.verify_reason: renderer.cpp:316-323 calls the resize wait 'a full wait_for_gpu', but device_resources.cpp:348 calls try_wait_for_gpu() and branches on failure: handle_device_lost at 353, or ThrowIfFailed(E_FAIL) at 357. The comment names the wrong function. This is not the round-1 589 item, which is a different comment conflict.

findings.title: A second length-ranking claim about texture_factory.cpp is duplicated in renderer.cpp
findings.why: This file-size ranking across backends repeats the claim in texture_factory.cpp:94 and vulkan/texture_factory.cpp:114. Every such copy has to be kept true by hand whenever any of the five factories changes length. The index-buffer upload explanation does not need it.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the ranking sentences and keep the point that the index buffer follows the same staging-copy-wait steps as texture uploads.
findings.verify_reason: renderer.cpp:776-778 has the ranking sentence word for word. The claim is still true (d3d12 346 is second only to vulkan 399), but it repeats the claim in texture_factory.cpp and has to be kept true by hand. Low severity is right.

findings.title: The same comment is repeated on the class and its first member
findings.why: The repeated sentence adds nothing and can drift.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the class-level comment and drop the repeat on add_texture.
findings.verify_reason: gl/backend.h:102-104 (class comment) and :108-110 (add_texture comment) repeat the sentence 'The font and sheet tables are RenderResources' own members; engine/render/render_resources.h says why, and what it saved.' word for word.

findings.title: Comment explains a function by the comment it replaced
findings.why: 'a comment kept getting wrong' is the history CONVENTIONS forbids ('a sentence narrating what this very comment used to say'). Line 32 already states the point without history.
findings.suggested_fix: Reduce to 'How many entry points the list above declares, counted from the list (T5).'
findings.verify_reason: gl_functions.h l.141-143: 'The compiler answers a question a comment kept getting wrong (T5)'. CONVENTIONS l.168-169 names exactly this case: a sentence narrating what a comment used to say.

findings.title: Section comment's list of context-defined members is incomplete
findings.why: Both context files also define tell_host_lost, tell_host_restored and device_string (wgl_context.cpp l.232-246, web_context.cpp l.194-247; backend.h l.214 and l.291-292 say 'Defined by the context'). A reader looking for those in renderer.cpp is told they are not context members.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add the three missing members or replace the enumeration with 'every member backend.h marks "Defined by the context"'.
findings.verify_reason: The comment at renderer.cpp l.271-274 omits tell_host_lost, tell_host_restored and device_string. grep shows all three defined in both wgl_context.cpp (l.232-240) and web_context.cpp (l.194-239). The list is incomplete, but it is a stale comment in one section header, so low.

findings.title: Comment points to the wrong place for the run-length cap
findings.why: DrawList::View::draw (renderer.cpp:180-184) only forwards to record(). The cap `this->open.sprites < max_run_sprites` is in RunRecorder::record in engine/render/sprite_geometry.h:293, so the comment sends a reader to the wrong function.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite RunRecorder::record (engine/render/sprite_geometry.h) instead.
findings.verify_reason: renderer.cpp:325-328 cites DrawList::View::draw. That function (renderer.cpp:180-184) only calls this->record(...). The `open.sprites < max_run_sprites` cap is in RunRecorder::record in sprite_geometry.h (~line 293).

findings.title: Sampler comment narrates the backends' past disagreement on mip levels
findings.why: Chronology of a prior D3D11 behaviour; the current fact is only that these are the non-mipmap filters so level zero is sampled. texture_factory.cpp l.177 ('belt and braces since the seam settled on level zero') carries the same history.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep 'these are the non-mipmap min filters, which is this backend's share of the seam's level-zero term (d3d11/renderer.cpp argues it)' and drop the 'has always / until' narrative here and in texture_factory.cpp.
findings.verify_reason: renderer.cpp l.374-377: 'This backend has always answered level zero and the other one sampled the chain until its MaxLOD was set to 0' narrates past behaviour. texture_factory.cpp l.177, 'since the seam settled on level zero', is milder history.

findings.title: Comment records how the backend first failed
findings.evidence:
// keeps errors queued, so the next thing to check glGetError blames
		// itself for it. That is exactly how this backend first failed.
findings.why: The rationale (core profile rejects GL_TEXTURE_2D, errors queue) stands alone; the last sentence is history, which CONVENTIONS says is never a comment.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete 'That is exactly how this backend first failed.'
findings.verify_reason: renderer.cpp l.418-419 ends with 'That is exactly how this backend first failed.' That is archaeology, which CONVENTIONS l.161 forbids. The rationale before it stands on its own.

findings.title: 'a third copy' of forwarding calls dates from when there were fewer backends
findings.why: There are five backends, so a per-backend forwarding page would have five copies, not three. The sentence argues against a design that no longer exists and contradicts 'the other four' in the line before it. The paragraph is also mostly argument against a rejected alternative, which render_resources.h already owns.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace it with a one-line pointer: 'The same short list as every backend; render_resources.h states the rule.'
findings.verify_reason: null/render_resources.cpp:42-50 does say 'The same short list the other four keep' followed by 'a third copy of it'. The count is inconsistent with five backends, and the paragraph mostly argues against a rejected alternative. It is still only a stale count in a comment that is otherwise true: low, not medium.

findings.title: Claims a sentence appears 'in all four folders', but GL and Vulkan do not have it
findings.why: `git grep -n 'ONE TEXTURE PER\|one texture per' engine/render` finds the sentence only in d3d11/renderer.cpp:134 and d3d12/renderer.cpp:187, not in gl/ or vulkan/. Line 34 is also an unwrapped reflow, about 100 columns, against the file's roughly 78-column wrap.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete 'which is the same sentence in all four folders' and rewrap the paragraph.
findings.verify_reason: git grep -i 'one texture per' engine/render finds only d3d11/renderer.cpp:134 and d3d12/renderer.cpp:187 (plus null itself), so 'the same sentence in all four folders' is false. An awk length check confirms null/renderer.cpp:34 is 99 columns.

findings.title: Resize comment tells the story of a past bug under this backend
findings.why: 'got std::logic_error ... under this backend' is the history of a fixed bug. The current fact is that reset clears `touched`, so a relayout after a resize may lower the view count. null/backend.h:112-116 has the same kind of story ('This backend answered that correctly by accident').
findings.suggested_fix: State the invariant: 'reset() clears touched, so a shell that re-lays out after this returns true may lower the view count.' Delete the 'by accident' clause in backend.h.
findings.verify_reason: null/renderer.cpp:226-230 has '...got std::logic_error out of set_view_count under this backend and silence under the other four', and null/backend.h:112-116 has 'This backend answered that correctly by accident'. Both are past-tense narratives of fixed behaviour.

findings.title: The text-query comment refers to the three backend copies that no longer exist
findings.why: 'Having three copies' describes a past state in which each backend had its own copy. A reader of the one current copy gains nothing from it.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep only the present-tense rationale (measure_text is a term of the pixel contract and is computed once from Font). Re-wrap lines 17-22.
findings.verify_reason: render_resources.cpp:97-99 says 'which is what made having three copies of them survivable', which refers to a past per-backend state. Lines 17-19 show the ragged mid-paragraph wrap.

findings.title: Setter comment narrates history ('deliberately unchanged', 'has always meant', 'change of heart')
findings.why: The current contract (it coerces unknown sizes to 1280x720; use set_resolution_exactly for a live size) is already in the header. Framing it as 'unchanged' and 'always' is history.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut to a present-tense line, e.g. "Coerces to a preset, 1280x720 for an unknown size; set_resolution_exactly is the non-coercing path."
findings.verify_reason: resolution_manager.cpp:55-60 contains 'Still coercing, deliberately unchanged', 'has always meant' and 'change of heart', which is history framing under CONVENTIONS:161.

findings.title: 'Not a RECT*' comments argue against a DirectXTK-era signature that is long gone
findings.why: No RECT exists anywhere above the backends, so the comment argues with code that no longer exists. 'The conversion happens once, in the backend' no longer describes anything either: backends receive SpriteVertex corners, not a rectangle.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete both sentences, or replace them with the actual contract: the returned reference lives as long as the frame or strip.
findings.verify_reason: sprite_frame.h:30-33 and animation_strip.h:20 argue 'not a RECT*'. No RECT exists above the backends, and backends receive SpriteVertex corners built in shared sprite_geometry, so 'the conversion happens once, in the backend' is stale.

findings.title: Includer census and 'compiles in every configuration' are both false
findings.why: These are fragile census claims, and both are now wrong. The second overstates test coverage of the exception contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the per-backend count and say the test compiles in every Windows configuration, not in browser builds.
findings.verify_reason: throw_if_failed.h:11 says 'three translation units each', but git grep finds four D3D12 includers (device_resources, renderer, sprite_pipeline, texture_factory.cpp) against three for D3D11. tests/render/CMakeLists.txt:71-73 adds throw_if_failed_tests.cpp only if(WIN32), so 'compiles in every configuration' is false for wasm. It is a stale comment, so low severity.

findings.title: Commented-out function left in source
findings.why: Leftover code with no declaration in viewport.h. It is noise to every reader of the file.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the four lines.
findings.verify_reason: viewport.cpp:38-41 holds the commented-out rectangle(minDepth, maxDepth). CONVENTIONS.md:192 says 'Commented-out code is deleted.'

findings.title: Viewport-manager comments name calls and access that do not exist
findings.why: Three comments in a 183-line file describe behaviour that does not exist. The 'asking for *4*' note is left over from a fixed defect (tests/render/viewport_manager_tests.cpp:79 records it). That makes it archaeology dressed as a warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the note to say player_viewport(4) answers fullscreen. Reword the set_viewport sentence to say callers use these Viewports in index order. Drop the 'test can drive' rationale, or make calculate_viewport static and say only that it reads no member.
findings.verify_reason: viewport_manager.h:30-32: all_viewports() takes no argument and player_viewport(int) is the indexed call. DrawList::set_viewport(const Viewport&) at renderer.h:130 takes no index. calculate_viewport is private and non-static (viewport_manager.h:51), and the 'a test can drive' rationale does not hold for it. tests/render/viewport_manager_tests.cpp:80 records the fixed fall-through. All three comments are stale. These are comment defects, so low.

findings.title: Validation callback comment frames itself by backend authoring order
findings.evidence: "// THIS IS WHY THE FIFTH BACKEND IS CHEAPER TO GET RIGHT THAN THE\n// FOURTH WAS. Direct3D's debug layer says what is wrong through a"
findings.why: "Fifth" and "fourth was" refer to the order the backends were written, not to anything in the code.
findings.suggested_fix: Lead with the present-tense point: Vulkan's validation layers report through a callback and check every barrier, layout and descriptor, so this forwards them to the debugger.
findings.verify_reason: device_resources.cpp:124-125 reads 'THIS IS WHY THE FIFTH BACKEND IS CHEAPER TO GET RIGHT THAN THE FOURTH WAS', which refers to authoring order. The present-tense point follows it.

findings.title: create_render_pass comment records what the code had first
findings.evidence: "// The obvious shape is a render pass that clears, which is what every\n// tutorial writes and what this had first. It does not fit the seam:"
findings.why: "what this had first" is history. The weighed alternative (a clearing render pass) is a legitimate rationale without it.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop "and what this had first".
findings.verify_reason: device_resources.cpp:819-820 says 'what every tutorial writes and what this had first', a history clause inside an otherwise valid rationale.

findings.title: 'THREE OTHER SITES ... in the same words' undercounts the folder's put-it-back catch sites
findings.evidence: "// THREE OTHER SITES IN THIS FOLDER HAVE THAT SHAPE and say so in the\n// same words - the read-back buffer in renderer.cpp, the staging buffer\n// in texture_factory.cpp, and the image-and-memory pair beside it"  grep 'catch (...)' finds more release-and-rethrow sites: device_resources.cpp:345 (create_vulkan_buffer), 2135, 2155; renderer.cpp:335 (vertex shader), 608 (index staging buffer).
findings.why: The census is already stale; the index-buffer staging in renderer.cpp:566-612 has exactly this shape. The sites are not worded the same either.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the count and list: "VulkanBuffer and raw handles have no destructor, so every throwing path releases them by hand."
findings.verify_reason: device_resources.cpp:2207-2211 says 'THREE OTHER SITES ... in the same words'. grep catch (...) finds dr.cpp 345/2135/2155, renderer.cpp 335/608/1224/1370 and texture_factory.cpp 352. renderer.cpp:608 (the index staging buffer) has the same shape but is not among the three, so the census is stale.

findings.title: The comment cites renderer.h for a decision that SEAM.md §4 owns
findings.evidence: "THE PART OF AN API THAT IS NOT ABOUT DRAWING, which is what renderer.h says a\n// backend's fourth translation unit is for." -- grep for "translation unit" in engine/render/renderer.h finds nothing; SEAM.md:110-117 "Three translation units every backend has ... plus the part of its API that is not about drawing ... d3d11/, d3d12/ and vulkan/ each add device_resources.cpp."
findings.why: The cross-reference sends a reader to the caller-contract header, which does not contain the decision. AGENTS.md says SEAM.md holds the rationale and renderer.h holds the caller contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the citation to engine/render/SEAM.md#4.
findings.verify_reason: device_resources.h:22-23 says 'which is what renderer.h says a backend's fourth translation unit is for'. Grepping renderer.h for 'translation unit' and 'fourth' finds nothing. SEAM.md:111 holds the translation-unit decision.

findings.title: frame_count declaration carries a verification procedure and evidence caveats rather than a contract
findings.why: Test coverage, how to run validation and evidence limits are none of CONVENTIONS' contract or rationale categories at a constant. They belong in docs/review/vulkan or docs/verification.md, and here they will go stale against the tests.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the rationale (two frames, not the swapchain image count). Move the testing and validation guidance to docs/review/vulkan/README.md and cite it.
findings.verify_reason: device_resources.h:207-214 at frame_count lists which tests and benchmarks exercise the ring, how to run synchronization validation, and the limits of that evidence. This is verification guidance, not contract or rationale, and it will drift against the tests. It is a judgement call, so low.

findings.title: Index-upload barrier comment says 'The asymmetry was the finding'
findings.why: "The asymmetry was the finding" refers to a review event, not the code. The rationale before it stands on its own.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the final sentence; keep the reason that a host wait is not an availability operation.
findings.verify_reason: renderer.cpp:589 reads 'The asymmetry was the finding;', which refers to a review event. The rationale before it, that a host wait is not an availability operation, stands on its own.

findings.title: Marker comment says 'the other three backends that say it'; only D3D12 and GL do
findings.evidence: "// THE THREE MARKERS DO NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE HONEST ANSWER RATHER THAN A\n// GAP - which is worth arguing here rather than pointing at the other three\n// backends that say it"  d3d11/renderer.cpp:1078-1102 implements markers (PIXSetMarker); null/renderer.cpp:379-381 are bare no-ops with no comment; only d3d12/renderer.cpp:1281 and gl/renderer.cpp:885 argue no-op markers.
findings.why: The count is wrong; the same comment later admits D3D11 has working markers.
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'the D3D12 and GL backends', or drop the count.
findings.verify_reason: renderer.cpp:1388-1390 says 'the other three backends that say it'. d3d11/renderer.cpp:1084/1102 implements PIXBeginEvent/PIXSetMarker, and null/renderer.cpp:378-381 has a one-line comment rather than an argument. So only D3D12 and GL make the argument and the count is wrong.

findings.title: Comment says texture_format.h counts b4g4r4a4 uses; it does not
findings.evidence: "VK_FORMAT_B4G4R4A4_UNORM_PACK16 means. No file in either client uses\n// it (texture_format.h counts them), so the honest thing is to say so"  texture_format.h:24-25 says only "b4g4r4a4_unorm because MakeSpriteFont offers it" and counts nothing.
findings.why: The citation points at a document that does not carry the claim, so a reader cannot check it.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the parenthesis, or cite texture_format.h for what it actually says (present because MakeSpriteFont offers it).
findings.verify_reason: texture_factory.cpp:64-65 says '(texture_format.h counts them)'. texture_format.h:25 says only 'b4g4r4a4_unorm because MakeSpriteFont offers it' and counts nothing. The miscitation is real but it is a parenthesis, so low.
